# open_sol API reference

Regenerate with: python -m open_sol describe --update-reference (also writes api_templates.md)

Generated by describe() from the registry, the model spec, the expression vocabulary, the material library and the templates (their model JSON: api_templates.md beside this file); selftest fails while this file differs from it.

Workflow: write the closest template (Templates) to a model JSON file with python -m open_sol template KEY model.json, edit it, run python -m open_sol check model.json (check.json), then python -m open_sol run model.json --figures (summary.json, log.txt, figures/); --set NAME=EXPR changes a parameter for one check / run. Units are SI unless a unit says otherwise; every wavelength is a vacuum wavelength.

More worked model files, many with an analytic reference, are in examples/<physics area>/*.json beside the package (examples/README.md; not part of this reference).

Topics (describe(topic) or python -m open_sol describe <topic>): spec, expressions, geometry, materials, mesh, solvers, each physics type name, `<physics>.<feature>`, each coupling type name, each study type name, templates, results, selftests.

## Model spec

A model is one JSON object (ModelSpec.to_dict(); api.save / api.load) made of the dataclasses below. Unknown keys, missing required keys, a wrong list / dict / text type and another version fail on load; everything else is reported by validation (check) as issues at node paths.

### Spec dataclasses

#### `ModelSpec` - the model file (root object)

- `title` (str; default "Untitled"): Free-text name of the model, shown in reports and the GUI.
- `description` (str; default ""): Free text (may span lines) on what the model shows and how to read its results; shown in the GUI (model node, Examples menu tooltip), never used by build or run.
- `version` (int; default 2): Spec format version 2; version 1 files (2D only, no size_z / geometry z params) load unchanged and are saved as version 2; other versions are rejected on load.
- `parameters` (list; default []): Named scalar parameters (ParameterSpec); every numeric value may be an expression of them.
- `domain` (DomainSpec; default {"size_x": 4e-06, "size_y": 4e-06, "size_z": null, "coordinates": "cartesian", "radius_min": 0, "angle_min": 0, "angle_wrap": "none"}): Size of the physical domain (DomainSpec), whose lower-left corner is the origin, and its in-plane grid (Cartesian, or polar / spherical about the origin).
- `geometry` (list; default []): Geometry objects (GeometrySpec): domain objects, points and lines, in m.
- `selections` (list; default []): Named entity lists (SelectionSpec), usable wherever entities are selected.
- `materials` (list; default []): Material assignments (MaterialSpec); list order and background materials decide overlapping cells (see materials).
- `physics` (list; default []): Physics instances (PhysicsSpec) of registered physics types, each with its features.
- `couplings` (list; default []): Couplings (CouplingSpec) that feed a field of one physics into a source slot of another.
- `meshes` (list; default [{"name": "mesh", "kind": "tensor", "mode": "uniform", "dx": 2e-08, "max_ratio": null, "wavelength_min": null, "points_per_wavelength": null, "refinements": [], "outer_dx": null, "outer_ratio": null, "axes": [], "h_min": null, "curvature_factor": 0.3, "mesher": "builtin", "sweep_axis": "none", "pml_layers": 8, "mirror_x": false, "mirror_y": false, "size_points": [], "face_sizes": []}]): Named meshes (MeshSpec, at least one, unique names; the first is the default): tensor (uniform, nonuniform or auto cells plus refinements), triangles (2D) or tetrahedra (3D). Each physics runs on one (PhysicsSpec.mesh); see mesh. A legacy "mesh" object (one MeshSpec) loads as [that mesh]; ModelSpec(mesh=...) and spec.mesh in scripts mean meshes[0].
- `solvers` (list; default []): Solver nodes (SolverSpec), each a solver type with its settings, used by the physics roles that name it in PhysicsSpec.solvers; [] = every physics on Automatic (the default solver of each role). A node no physics uses is a warning.
- `solver_defaults` (SolverDefaultsSpec; default {"backend": "auto", "precision": "auto", "subpixel_smoothing": false, "conformal_boundaries": false, "memory_check": "error"}): Model-wide solver choices (SolverDefaultsSpec).
- `study` (StudySpec; default {"type": "time_dependent", "settings": {}, "stored_fields": [], "sweep": null, "stored_cuts": [], "adaptation": null, "estimation": null, "solved_physics": []}): What to compute (StudySpec): study type, its settings, stored fields and an optional sweep.
- `derived_values` (list; default []): Scalars evaluated at the end of the run (DerivedValueSpec), reported in summary.json derived (with derived_reference / derived_error when they have a reference).
- `analytic_curves` (list; default []): Analytic curves (AnalyticCurveSpec) the GUI draws dashed over a simulated curve (a feature result, the sweep plot or a line profile); figures=True draws them into the feature result figures and adds figures/curve_<name>.png per line curve and figures/<key>_vs_<x_column or row>.png per table target. They do not change the run.
- `derived_curves` (list; default []): Curves (DerivedCurveSpec) computed after the run from 1D feature results, e.g. several spectra on one plot, a sum or ratio of results or a result scaled to physical units; shown in the GUI Derived curves tab, in summary.json derived_curves and with figures=True in figures/derived_<plot>.png. They do not change the run.

#### `ParameterSpec` - items of ModelSpec.parameters

- `name` (str; required): Identifier; not a reserved expression name (function, constant, x, y, z, t, value) nor a physics field name.
- `expression` (float | int | str; required): Number or expression of other parameters and constants, e.g. "550*nm"; it must evaluate to a finite number.
- `description` (str; default ""): Free text, e.g. the meaning and unit.

#### `DomainSpec` - ModelSpec.domain

- `size_x` (float | int | str; default 4e-06): Width of the physical domain in m (> 0), x from 0 to size_x. A uniform mesh has ceil(size_x / dx) cells, so the meshed window (Domain.physical_extent) can be one cell wider; EM PML cells lie outside. Polar / spherical: the radial depth in m, r from radius_min to radius_min + size_x (exact: dr = size_x / ceil(size_x / dx)).
- `size_y` (float | int | str | None; default 4e-06): Height of the physical domain in m (> 0), y from 0 to size_y (window rounding as size_x). Polar / spherical: the angle span in rad (polar <= 2 pi; spherical angle_min + size_y <= pi). null = a 1D model (symmetry 2.20), invariant in both other directions: cartesian = a slab along x (totals per m^2), polar = a cylinder, r from radius_min (per m of length; geometry planar), spherical = a sphere (whole shells; geometry axisymmetric); size_z, angle_min and angle_wrap stay unset; only types whose dimensions include 1 (heat, electric_currents, electrostatics). Drawn on the x axis (y = 0): objects select the cells whose centres (x, 0) they hold, points sit and line curves run on y = 0; outer faces x_lo / x_hi only (x_lo at r = 0: no area). Mesh: uniform at dx, or graded by a mesh axis x entry (no axis y, object refinements or auto mode). Fields are (nx, 1); the Automatic linear solver is banded.
- `size_z` (float | int | str | None; default null): null (default) = a 2D model; a length in m (> 0) makes it 3D, z from 0 to size_z: the xy layout is extruded over each object's z0..z1 (layer stack), the outer faces gain z_lo / z_hi and only physics types whose dimensions include 3 are allowed. z cells: uniform at dx, or graded by the refinements' z extents (see mesh mode).
- `coordinates` (str; default "cartesian"): cartesian (default) | polar | spherical: the in-plane grid of a 2D model. polar = (r, phi) cells, x = r cos phi, y = r sin phi about the origin (planar per unit z, every physics with geometry 'planar'); spherical = (r, theta) cells of the meridional half plane, x = r sin theta the distance to the rotation axis y, y = r cos theta (every physics with geometry 'axisymmetric', whole shells). Circles about the origin, annuli, spheres, shells and cones (theta = const) are conformal; other shapes staircase on the cell centres. Outer faces: x_lo / x_hi = the inner / outer arc (r = 0: no area), y_lo / y_hi = the rays at angle_min / angle_min + size_y (spherical theta = 0 / pi: the axis, no area); insulated by default (a full 2 pi disk keeps a cut unless angle_wrap joins them). Only types whose coordinate_grids include polar (heat, electric_currents, electrostatics; 3D: heat); k_xx / k_yy (sigma_dc_*, eps_dc_*) are the radial / angular components and *_xy is refused; object perimeter flux features (heat_flux, convection, current_density, surface_charge) weight each exposed face by its metric area (2D; refused in 3D sectors and 1D); conformal_boundaries applies on 2D grids too (heat, potential). Mesh: uniform at dx radially and along the outer arc (angle cells = ceil(size_y r_max / dx)); nonuniform: mesh axis 'x' bands / edges / segments (in r - radius_min) grade the radius, axis 'y' edges / segments (rad) the angle; object refinements, mode 'auto' and EM PML are refused. Fields come as a containing-cell image over the sector's box (NaN outside), _x / _y components radial / angular; derived values integrate over the exact sector areas / shell volumes. With size_y null: a 1D slab / cylinder / sphere (see size_y). polar with size_z set = a 3D cylindrical (r, phi, z) sector (symmetry 2.21; heat only): z along the axis (uniform at dx, or graded by a mesh axis z entry), z_lo / z_hi the end faces, geometry z params as in Cartesian 3D (masks on the drawing-plane centres per cross-section), k_zz axial; fields are z cuts only (plane x / y, stored x / y cuts and 3D segment line curves refused), derived values integrate over r_c dr dphi dz; Session.volume gives (r, phi, z) centres.
- `radius_min` (float | int | str; default 0): Polar / spherical: r of the x_lo face in m (>= 0; 0 = the origin is in the domain, a face without area). Ignored (warning) on a Cartesian grid.
- `angle_min` (float | int | str; default 0): Polar: phi of the y_lo face in rad (from +x toward +y); spherical: theta of the y_lo face from the +y rotation axis (>= 0). Ignored (warning) on a Cartesian grid.
- `angle_wrap` (str; default "none"): Polar only: none (default) | periodic | antiperiodic. periodic joins the y_hi ray to the y_lo ray: a full 2 pi annulus or disk without a cut, or one C_N sector of size_y = 2 pi / N whose sources and conditions share the symmetry (warning when 2 pi / size_y is not whole). antiperiodic = u changes sign across the wrap (Bloch phase pi; needs an even N = 2 pi / size_y, else an error): sources alternating in sign between sectors; other Bloch phases are not available. y_lo / y_hi are then no boundary (features selecting them: error). Exact in the finite-volume operator; anchoring counts loops through the wrap (an antiperiodic loop anchors on its own).

#### `GeometrySpec` - items of ModelSpec.geometry

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among geometry objects and selections (one namespace); not x_lo, x_hi, y_lo, y_hi, z_lo, z_hi, all.
- `kind` (str; required): Geometry kind: rectangle, rounded_rectangle, circle, ellipse, polygon, point, line, union, intersection, difference, array, box, cylinder_z, sphere (see geometry).
- `params` (dict; default {}): Values of the kind params by name (numbers or parameter expressions, lengths in m); missing keys take the defaults.

#### `SelectionSpec` - items of ModelSpec.selections

- `name` (str; required): Identifier in the namespace shared with geometry objects.
- `kind` (str; required): Entity kind of the selection: domain | boundary | point | line | interface.
- `entities` (list; default []): Entity names: geometry objects, other selections of the same kind, outer faces (boundary) or all (domain). interface: domain objects (their outlines; composites: the outline of the result).
- `side` (str; default ""): Kind 'interface' only: 'inside' | 'outside' = the side of the outline its fields are read from; '' for the other kinds. An interface selection (2D models incl. polar / spherical; not 3D) is the outline of each listed object, sampled every half finest cell (parts on the window edge skipped); each sample reads its side 1.5 and 2.5 local cells deep along the outward normal from least-squares planes through 4 x 4 blocks of side cells (no average mixes materials), extrapolated linearly onto the outline: exact for fields linear on the side, error ~1.9 (k_n h)^2 for a wave of normal wavenumber k_n; a side thinner than ~4 cells gives no samples (a polar block does not cross an angle_wrap seam). Derived values reduce the samples (DerivedValueSpec.selection), line curves read them (AnalyticCurveSpec.interface): normal components one-sided (E_n jumps by eps_2 / eps_1), tangential ones continuous.

#### `MaterialSpec` - items of ModelSpec.materials

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among materials.
- `library` (str | None; default null): Library material name (see materials), or null / "" for none.
- `properties` (dict; default {}): Material properties of the present physics types {name: number or expression}, overriding the library values (see materials).
- `dispersion` (list | None; default null): EM dispersion poles [{"model": "drude" | "lorentz" | "nk_fit", ...}], plus at most one {"model": "crystal", ...} entry (piezoelectric crystal data, not a pole); null, [] and a list: see materials.
- `selection` (list; default []): Domain entities the material covers (all = a background material, PML included: see materials); an empty list assigns it nowhere (warning).

#### `PhysicsSpec` - items of ModelSpec.physics

- `name` (str; required): Instance name (identifier) used in field names <name>_<field>, stored fields <name>.<component> and couplings; usually the default instance name of the type.
- `type` (str; required): Registered physics type name (see the physics type sections).
- `settings` (dict; default {}): Values of the physics type settings by name; missing keys take the defaults.
- `features` (list; default []): Features (FeatureSpec) of this physics: sources, probes, monitors, boundary and domain conditions.
- `every` (int; default 1): Stride in runner ticks (int >= 1): the physics steps on every n-th tick over n * dt_sync, dt_sync being the smallest dt_limit of all physics (EM: its Courant step). EM must use 1; heat coupled to EM typically a few hundred.
- `solvers` (dict; default {}): Solver role (stepper, linear, shifted, eigen) -> SolverSpec name; a missing role = Automatic. The roles of each physics type and their Automatic types: see solvers. A misfit (role, operator, precision) is an error; a role the study does not use is a warning.
- `mesh` (str; default ""): Name of the MeshSpec this physics runs on; "" = the first mesh (ModelSpec.meshes[0]). Physics on different meshes exchange data only through couplings whose type transfers across meshes (see mesh).

#### `FeatureSpec` - items of PhysicsSpec.features

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique within its physics; its result key is <physics>.<feature>.
- `type` (str; required): Feature type of the physics type (see its Feature sections).
- `selection` (list; default []): Entities of the selection kind of the feature type (domain, boundary, point or line entities).
- `params` (dict; default {}): Values of the feature type params by name; missing keys take the defaults.
- `enabled` (bool; default true): false leaves the feature out of validation and build; it stays in the model.

#### `CouplingSpec` - items of ModelSpec.couplings

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among couplings.
- `type` (str; required): Registered coupling type name (see the coupling type sections).
- `source` (str; required): Name of the physics instance whose field is read.
- `target` (str; required): Name of the physics instance whose source slot is written; two enabled couplings writing the same target slot are an error.
- `every` (int | None; default null): Transfer stride in runner ticks (int >= 1); null = the larger every of the source and target physics.
- `params` (dict; default {}): Values of the coupling type params by name; missing keys take the defaults.
- `enabled` (bool; default true): false leaves the coupling out of validation and build.

#### `MeshSpec` - items of ModelSpec.meshes

- `name` (str; default "mesh"): Identifier, unique among meshes; PhysicsSpec.mesh names it; issues of the mesh sit at node ["mesh", name].
- `kind` (str; default "tensor"): Mesh kind (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `mode` (str; default "uniform"): Mesh mode (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `dx` (float | int | str; default 2e-08): Cell size (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `max_ratio` (float | int | str | None; default null): Maximum growth ratio (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `wavelength_min` (float | int | str | None; default null): Shortest wavelength (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `points_per_wavelength` (float | int | str | None; default null): Points per wavelength (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `refinements` (list; default []): Local refinements (RefinementSpec), used in nonuniform and auto modes (triangles / gmsh tetrahedra: maximum element sizes in / along / at the object, gmsh tetrahedra also along its edges or at its surface only (where); builtin tetrahedra: tensor bands, per-axis sizes included).
- `outer_dx` (float | int | str | None; default null): Outer cell size (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `outer_ratio` (float | int | str | None; default null): Outer growth ratio (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `axes` (list; default []): Per-axis options (MeshAxisSpec, at most one per axis), used in nonuniform and auto modes (tensor meshes and builtin tetrahedra).
- `h_min` (float | int | str | None; default null): Minimum element size (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `curvature_factor` (float | int | str; default 0.3): Curvature factor (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `mesher` (str; default "builtin"): Mesher (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `sweep_axis` (str; default "none"): Swept layers (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `pml_layers` (int | str; default 8): Absorbing layers (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `mirror_x` (bool; default false): Mirror-symmetric in x (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `mirror_y` (bool; default false): Mirror-symmetric in y (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `size_points` (list; default []): Element-size sources in m: [x, y, h] on triangles, [x, y, z, h] on tetrahedra (h > 0, mesher gmsh only: refused with builtin tetrahedra), each growing by max_ratio with the distance like an object size; adaptive mesh refinement writes them into adapted triangle meshes (convergence report adapted_meshes). [] = none.
- `face_sizes` (list; default []): Tetrahedra only: element sizes near plane faces (MeshFaceSizeSpec), every mode; gmsh: a size field over the face rectangle; builtin: a band [c - distance, c + distance] across the whole face plane (the plane an element face). [] = none.

#### `RefinementSpec` - items of MeshSpec.refinements

- `object` (str; required): Geometry object whose region is refined (domain object, line or point).
- `dx` (float | int | str; required): Target cell size in m in that region; it applies only when finer than the base size.
- `margin` (float | int | str | None; default null): Distance in m around the object that is refined too (3D: along z as well); null = 3 * the axis cell size.
- `dx_x` (float | int | str | None; default null): Cell size in m along x only (anisotropic refinement); null = dx. A value >= the base size leaves x unrefined, e.g. for a waveguide crossing the domain along x.
- `dx_y` (float | int | str | None; default null): Cell size in m along y only; null = dx (see dx_x).
- `dx_z` (float | int | str | None; default null): Cell size in m along z only (3D models); null = dx (see dx_x). dx_x / dx_y / dx_z: tensor meshes and builtin tetrahedra only.
- `automatic` (bool; default false): true = filled in from the auto-mode sizes (the GUI writes it when a mesh leaves auto mode, with dx = the auto base size); auto mode ignores such refinements and computes its own, so switching back to auto recalculates them. Default false.
- `where` (str; default "inside"): Where dx applies: 'inside' (default) = in the object; 'edges' = along the edges of its primitives (box 12 edges, z cylinder 2 rims, composite: every input, hole rims included; the physics' edge sizes path); 'surface' = at its surface only, dx + (max_ratio - 1) x |distance to the surface| on both sides (composites: the composite surface, a hole's inside stays coarse). 'edges' / 'surface': tetrahedron meshes with mesher gmsh only (validation error elsewhere); spheres have no edges, and objects gmsh gets no solid of (ellipses, polygons, x / y circles, tapers) get no size field (a warning).

#### `MeshAxisSpec` - items of MeshSpec.axes

- `axis` (str; required): 'x', 'y' or 'z' (z only in 3D models).
- `max_ratio` (float | int | str | None; default null): Maximum growth ratio of this axis (> 1; also its PML ramp); null = the mesh max_ratio.
- `bands` (list; default []): Coordinate bands (MeshBandSpec) refined along this axis only, without a geometry object.
- `edges` (list; default []): Custom cell edges in m (numbers or parameter expressions), increasing within [0, size]; 0 and the size are added when missing. They replace the graded cells of this axis (refinements and bands are then ignored along it); give edges or segments, not both.
- `segments` (list; default []): Custom cells as consecutive pieces (MeshSegmentSpec) from 0 to the axis size; they replace the graded cells of this axis like edges.

#### `MeshBandSpec` - items of MeshAxisSpec.bands

- `lo` (float | int | str; required): Band start in m along the axis.
- `hi` (float | int | str; required): Band end in m (> lo).
- `dx` (float | int | str; required): Cell size in m inside the band; applies only when finer than the base size (graded ramps outside, as for refinements).

#### `MeshSegmentSpec` - items of MeshAxisSpec.segments

- `cells` (float | int | str; required): Number of cells of the piece (whole number >= 1).
- `end` (float | int | str | None; default null): End of the piece in m (it starts at the previous end, the first at 0); null = the axis end (last piece only).
- `profile` (str; default "uniform"): 'uniform' (equal cells), 'geometric' (constant growth from the start, last / first cell = ratio; < 1 shrinks toward the end) or 'tanh' (two-sided clustering toward both ends of a gap, centre / end cell = ratio >= 1).
- `ratio` (float | int | str; default 1): Size ratio of the profile (see profile); 1 = uniform.

#### `MeshFaceSizeSpec` - items of MeshSpec.face_sizes

- `entity` (str; required): Outer face ('x_lo' ... 'z_hi') or a domain object (its bounding-box faces, clipped to the window).
- `size` (float | int | str; required): Element size in m at the face (> 0); applies only below dx, floored at h_min.
- `face` (str; default ""): Objects: one bounding-box face ('x_lo' ... 'z_hi'), '' = all six; outer faces: ''.
- `distance` (float | int | str; default 0): Half-thickness in m (>= 0) of the band held at size; beyond it the size grows by max_ratio up to dx.

#### `SolverSpec` - items of ModelSpec.solvers

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among solvers; PhysicsSpec.solvers refers to it.
- `type` (str; required): Registered solver type: pcg, line_block, sparse_direct, arpack_shift_invert, block_eigen, explicit_kernels (see solvers: roles, settings and which physics use them).
- `settings` (dict; default {}): Values of the solver type settings by name (see solvers); missing keys take the defaults.

#### `SolverDefaultsSpec` - ModelSpec.solver_defaults

- `backend` (str; default "auto"): auto (default) | gpu | cpu: where the run computes (api check / run backend=, CLI --backend override it); auto = gpu when cupy is installed, else cpu. cpu needs every physics type to list it in its backends (else a validation error per physics) and every solver to fit it (explicit_kernels and sparse_direct cusolver_qr do not); on cpu the device memory estimate counts against the host RAM.
- `precision` (str; default "auto"): auto (default) | single | double | mixed | half_storage: model-wide solver precision. auto = each solver's own default (pcg double, explicit_kernels single, ...). Otherwise every role solver whose type and role offer it takes it, unless its solver node sets its own precision; the others keep their default (a validation info names them), e.g. double makes pcg and the time steppers double (sparse_direct / arpack_shift_invert / banded are double anyway); mixed reaches only pcg nodes, Automatic pcg of heat, electric_currents, electrostatics and magnetostatics, and line_block / block_eigen nodes. A pcg node with preconditioner multigrid and no own precision fails with mixed. check.json / summary.json solvers record the precision each role resolved to.
- `subpixel_smoothing` (bool; default false): false (default) | true: anisotropic permittivity averaging at material interfaces (Kottke / Farjadpour): in cells two materials share, E_z and the component along the interface see the mean eps, the component across it the harmonic mean, from fill fraction and normal sampled once at build (64 x 4 and 4 x 64 per cell); reapplied after every eps change, so thermo-optic and other eps couplings keep working. Honoured by em_fdtd_ez / _hz, em_fdfd_ez / _hz, em_modes and em_fdtd_3d outside an optimization study (mode ports included); every other physics ignores it (validation info). em_fdtd_3d: exact for vertical walls of z prisms, tapers and spheres smoothed per layer (staircased along z), prism tops / bottoms sampled at 16 heights per half cell; the face eps cost 2 bytes per cell. Only the background eps is averaged: sigma_e, mu_r and Drude / Lorentz poles keep their cell membership, and expression-defined eps jumps inside one material stay staircased. Second order on curved E_z interfaces; on slanted H_z interfaces better than staircasing, not second order.
- `conformal_boundaries` (bool; default false): false (default) | true: curved walls at their drawn position instead of staircased (located once at build). em_fdtd_ez / _hz pec_domain: E_z = 0 at the exact wall distance along each link into a PEC cell; H_z (Dey-Mittra) from the free face lengths and area of each cut cell, only faces wholly in the metal PEC; each corrected cell is limited to stay stable at the unchanged time step (a very small cut is then partly staircased). Their Drude / Lorentz poles: each pole current is weighted by the share of its control area inside the drawn material instead of 0 / 1 (the Courant check uses the shares); the background eps keeps the cell mask (subpixel_smoothing averages it). em_fdfd_ez / _hz pec_domain: the same wall distances and free lengths / area (fractions >= 0.02), the operator stays reciprocal; mode ports, sources and FDFD poles keep the cell mask. laminar_flow: linear interpolated (Bouzidi) bounce-back at the drawn solid wall (a material is solid when most of its cells have viscosity 0); outer faces keep their face rules. heat, electric_currents, electrostatics (cut cells): held values on object perimeters (temperature / voltage, fixed_temperature_domain, terminal) sit on the drawn outline (Shortley-Weller, t >= 0.02); walls of non-conducting materials (most cells conduct neither) get fractional face apertures and merged cut cells (>= 0.02), re-located when the conducting cells change (k(T), sigma(T)); perimeter heat_flux / current_density / surface_charge feed value x outline chord into the owning cell, convection loses h L / (1 + h delta / k_n). em_modes pec_domain: Dey-Mittra on the projected Yee cell (fractions >= 0.02). em_fdtd_3d pec_domain (3D): Dey-Mittra H faces from the free lengths of their four E edges over their free area, floored for stability at the time step. Otherwise 2D Cartesian only; heat / potential also (r, z) and polar / spherical domains (links across an angle_wrap seam stay staircased); every other physics ignores it (validation info). Features thinner than 1/16 of a cell face, or that no cell centre sees, stay invisible.
- `memory_check` (str; default "error"): error (default) | warning: what a memory estimate over the budget does (the GPU estimate at its peak, cuDSS factors included, against the GPU budget; the host estimate against the available RAM; also per sweep value and refinement level). error refuses the model before the build (triangle / tetrahedron meshes are built first when the size-based estimate is over: the judgement uses the built element count); warning builds and runs it with a validation warning, for a model whose estimate is known to be high (cuDSS fill can only be modelled). Runtime guards stay: the GPU pool limit raises OutOfMemoryError; each cuDSS plan checks its own estimate against the free device memory before factorising (Automatic sparse_direct then falls back to SuperLU, an explicit cudss node raises); MUMPS / PARDISO check theirs against 80 % of the available RAM (an explicit node raises).

#### `StudySpec` - ModelSpec.study

- `type` (str; default "time_dependent"): Registered study type name (see the study type sections).
- `settings` (dict; default {}): Values of the study type params by name; missing keys take the defaults.
- `stored_fields` (list; default []): Output fields stored in snapshots, as 'physics.component' (e.g. 'em.ez'); [] (default) = every output field (primary first); snapshots past 1 GB keep only the final state.
- `sweep` (SweepSpec | None; default null): Optional parameter sweep (SweepSpec): one build and run per value; null = no sweep.
- `stored_cuts` (list; default []): 3D models only: extra cut planes [axis 'x' | 'y' | 'z', position in m (number or parameter expression)] each snapshot stores besides the mid-height z cut (window cell containing the position; same fields and 1 GB limit), e.g. [["y", 1e-6]] for an xz cut. Read with Results.snapshot_field(index, name, plane=(axis, position) or the cut index); summary.json stored_cuts lists them. [] = none.
- `adaptation` (AdaptationSpec | None; default null): Optional mesh refinement levels (AdaptationSpec): the study reruns on refined meshes until a derived value converges; null = none. Only study types that support it; no sweep or parity sectors.
- `estimation` (EstimationSpec | None; default null): Optional parameter estimation (EstimationSpec): the study reruns with the estimated parameters until the weighted misfit of measured derived values and curves is least, then once at the best point (summary estimation). null = one run. Any study type; no sweep or adaptation; parity_sectors run every sector per evaluation. A geometry parameter remeshes per evaluation (finite-difference noise): keep diff_step large or use nelder_mead.
- `solved_physics` (list; default []): Physics the study solves itself, e.g. ['membrane']; the others run first as stationary background physics (couplings from them into the listed ones allowed). [] = every physics whose solver has the study's solve. frequency_domain, mode_analysis, eigenfrequency, frequency_response and optomechanics only.

#### `SweepSpec` - StudySpec.sweep (or null)

- `parameter` (str; required): Name of the parameter that takes each value.
- `values` (list; default []): spacing 'list': numbers (or parameter expressions) the parameter takes, run in list order (kept but unused for the other spacings).
- `keep_fields` (bool; default true): true (default): every sweep value keeps its snapshots (summary sweep snapshot_times / snapshot_labels, results.npz sweep_snapshot/..., Results.sweep_field); past 1 GB in total only each value's final snapshot (a warning). false: only the last value keeps snapshots, earlier ones their derived values and results.
- `spacing` (str; default "list"): 'list' (default: the values), 'linear' (count evenly spaced points from lower to upper) or 'log' (count geometrically spaced points; lower and upper non-zero, same sign).
- `lower` (float | int | str | None; default null): spacing 'linear' / 'log': first value (number or parameter expression); may exceed upper (a descending sweep).
- `upper` (float | int | str | None; default null): spacing 'linear' / 'log': last value (number or parameter expression).
- `count` (int; default 5): spacing 'linear' / 'log': number of values including both end points (1 = lower only).
- `reuse_build` (bool; default false): true: build once and run every value on that build. The swept parameter (and its dependants) may then reach, with parameters only (no x / y / z / t), only: feature values and physics settings whose help says so (loads, held values, voltages, doping, em_eme wavelength, ...), material values read by no EM type (repainted; not on 3D tensor meshes), derived values, curves and study settings; any other use (geometry, mesh, other materials, dispersion, physics / solver / coupling settings, stored cuts), time_dependent, optimization and parity_sectors are validation errors. Each value reruns from the previous state (nonlinear solids start Newton from it; summary sweep builds = 1); followed material values are range-checked per value, followed feature values and settings only where their setter checks them. A physics that cannot rerun rebuilds per value (info). false (default): one build per value.

#### `AdaptationSpec` - StudySpec.adaptation (or null)

- `target` (str; required): Derived value name whose relative change between levels stops the refinement (required).
- `method` (str; default "adaptive"): 'adaptive' (error indicator marks where to refine) or 'uniform' (every mesh size x growth^(-1/2) per level).
- `tolerance` (float | int; default 0.001): Converged when |v_k - v_k-1| <= tolerance |v_k| (> 0).
- `max_levels` (int; default 2): Levels after the model meshes (integer >= 1); reaching it unconverged warns.
- `growth` (float | int; default 1.7): Cell / element count growth per level (> 1).
- `meshes` (list; default []): Mesh names refined ([] = every mesh the physics use).
- `max_cells` (int | None; default null): Stop before a level above this cell / element count (null = no cap; the memory budget always applies).
- `anisotropic` (bool; default true): Tensor meshes: refine x and y bands separately by the dominant indicator part (true) or both axes alike.
- `keep_levels` (bool; default false): true: keep every level's snapshots, not only the last level's.

#### `EstimationSpec` - StudySpec.estimation (or null)

- `parameters` (list; default []): Estimated parameters (EstimatedParameterSpec, >= 1), set as numbers per evaluation; dependent parameters follow.
- `targets` (list; default []): Measured derived values (EstimationTargetSpec); residual (model - value) / sigma.
- `curves` (list; default []): Measured curves (EstimationCurveSpec); residual per point (model interpolated onto x - y) / sigma.
- `method` (str; default "least_squares"): 'least_squares' (scipy TRF within the bounds, finite-difference Jacobian: n + 1 runs per step; standard errors from J^T J) or 'nelder_mead' (bounded simplex for noisy misfits; no standard errors).
- `max_evaluations` (int; default 50): Study runs of the search (integer >= 1; the final run at the best point is extra); reaching it ends the search at the best point so far.
- `diff_step` (float | int; default 0.01): least_squares: finite-difference step relative to each parameter scale (> 0; default 1e-2: far above solver / mesh noise).
- `tolerance` (float | int; default 1e-06): Stop when the cost and the step change by less than this (> 0; relative, nelder_mead: absolute in the scaled parameters and the cost).

#### `EstimatedParameterSpec` - items of EstimationSpec.parameters

- `name` (str; required): Model parameter name (ParameterSpec.name).
- `initial` (float | int | str | None; default null): Start value (number or expression of the base parameters); null = the parameter's own value. Strictly between lower and upper; |initial| (else upper - lower, else 1) is the search scale.
- `lower` (float | int | str | None; default null): Lower bound (number or expression); null = unbounded.
- `upper` (float | int | str | None; default null): Upper bound (number or expression); null = unbounded.

#### `EstimationTargetSpec` - items of EstimationSpec.targets

- `derived` (str; required): Derived value (DerivedValueSpec.name) compared with the measured value (parity sectors: the combined value).
- `value` (float | int | str; required): Measured value (number or expression of the base parameters).
- `sigma` (float | int | str | None; default null): Measurement uncertainty (> 0, same unit); null = |value| (relative; 1 when value is 0). Standard errors are absolute only when every target and curve gives sigma, else scaled by the reduced chi-square.

#### `EstimationCurveSpec` - items of EstimationSpec.curves

- `source` (str; required): Model curve: 'physics.feature:sample' of a 1D feature result (as a derived curve input) or a derived curve name.
- `x` (list; default []): Measured abscissa values (source abscissa unit), inside the model curve's range (the run fails otherwise).
- `y` (list; default []): Measured values, one per x.
- `sigma` (float | int | str | list | None; default null): Uncertainty: one number or expression (> 0), a list with one value per point, or null = the RMS of y.

#### `DerivedValueSpec` - items of ModelSpec.derived_values

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among derived values; its key in summary.json derived.
- `expression` (str; required): source null: expression of parameters, x, y (3D: z), t and output fields (<physics>_<field>, or <field> when one physics alone provides it); over an interface selection also normal_x, normal_y, tangent_x, tangent_y (outward unit normal of the outline, tangent = the normal turned +90 deg; polar / spherical: radial / angular components; they shadow parameters), e.g. "em_ex_re*normal_x + em_ey_re*normal_y". Operation 'expression': one number of parameters, scalar outputs and t (no fields, x, y, z or selection), e.g. c_eff = "sqrt(N_int / rho_int)". With a source: an expression of the result sample names and parameters per sample, e.g. "power" or "1 - fraction_positive" (see Derived values). All may use the derived values listed before this one (evaluated in float64 in list order; NaN when they failed). Examples: stored electric energy W_E = integral of eps0_const*em_eps_r*em_e_intensity/4 (J/m in 2D); V = mode_volume of em_eps_r*em_e_intensity; Purcell F = 3/(4*pi**2)*(lam/n)**3*Q/V in 3D, (Q/(pi**2*V))*(lam/n)**2 for an E_z line emitter in 2D (twice that for H_z), lam and Q from a resonance_table source (operation at, at = the row); small-inclusion shift d_omega/omega = -alpha*E2_at/(2*eps0_const*eps_int) with E2_at = |E|^2 at the point (operation at), eps_int = integral of eps_r*|E|^2 and alpha [F m^2; 2D: F] = 4*pi*eps0_const*eps_b*a**3*(eps_s - eps_b)/(eps_s + 2*eps_b) (sphere), eps0_const*(eps_s - eps_b)*area (2D rod, E_z), 2*eps0_const*eps_b*area*(eps_s - eps_b)/(eps_s + eps_b) (2D rod, in-plane E).
- `selection` (list; default []): Domain entities to reduce over; [] = the whole physical window; or exactly one 'interface' selection: its one-sided outline samples (see SelectionSpec.side; operations mean, max, min, integral: mean / integral weighted by outline length, integral per unit z length, axisymmetric times 2 pi r). Must be [] with a source and for operation 'expression'.
- `operation` (str; default "mean"): mean | max | min | integral | last | at | argmax | fwhm | polyfit | exp_fit | lorentz_fit | two_exp_fit | two_wave_fit | richardson | multi_lorentz_fit | pole_fit | mode_volume | expression. Over fields (mean, max, min, integral, mode_volume, at): mean is area-weighted, integral = sum of value * cell area (per unit z length; geometry axisymmetric: ring volume 2 pi r * cell area), mode_volume = integral / (maximum over the selection, or the value at point) [m^3; 2D: m^2], at = the value in the cell containing point; integral and mode_volume count each mirror face the selection reaches twice (the unfolded structure), max / min (and the mode_volume maximum) include the mirror image. expression: see expression. Over a source (the finite samples inside window): mean, max, min, integral = trapezoid over the abscissa (window edges interpolated), argmax = abscissa of the maximum (parabola through it and its neighbours), fwhm = full width at half the largest peak (linear crossings; baseline 0: subtract one in the expression), the fits = the quantity fit (see fit), last = the last sample (the final time of a timeseries), at = linear interpolation at the abscissa value at. far_field angles wrap (at, window, a peak at 0 rad; argmax in [0, 2 pi) without a window).
- `source` (str | None; default null): null = fields over the selection (operation 'expression': no fields, the other values); 'physics.feature' = the 1D result of that enabled feature (kinds timeseries, flux_spectrum, far_field, xy, table), reduced over its samples; the name of a derived curve = that curve (sample names: the curve name and x), e.g. a reduction or fit of a gradient / cumtrapz of results. Evaluated with the other derived values at the end of each run, so a sweep reports it per value.
- `at` (float | int | str | None; default null): Operation 'at' over a source only (fields: point): abscissa value of the source result, number or parameter expression in the abscissa unit (wavelength in m for a flux_spectrum, t in s for a timeseries, x in the x unit of an xy result, the 0-based row of a table); outside the sampled range the value is NaN plus a warning.
- `reference` (float | int | str | None; default null): Optional analytic value (number or expression of parameters only, in the unit of the derived value); summary.json derived_reference and derived_error = |value - reference| / |reference| (|value - reference| for a zero reference); the GUI shows both beside the value and dashes it over the sweep plot.
- `tolerance` (float | int | None; default null): Optional number >= 0 or null: largest accepted derived_error (relative, absolute for a zero reference; a sweep: at every value). Used only by selftest --examples, which fails the example above it; null = reported, never failed.
- `window` (list; default []): Source only: [lo, hi] (numbers or parameter expressions in the abscissa unit, e.g. ["1540*nm", "1560*nm"]) limiting the samples every operation but last / at reduces; [] = every sample. No finite sample inside gives NaN plus a warning. far_field: angles in rad, a window may cross 0 (e.g. [-0.3, 0.3]), at most 2 pi wide.
- `wavelength` (float | int | str | None; default null): far_field sources only: wavelength [m] (number or parameter expression) of the pattern reduced, the recorded one nearest to it; null = the first. Derived curve inputs of a far_field result use the first.
- `fit` (str; default ""): Fit operations only: the fitted quantity. polyfit: 'c0' .. 'c<degree>' (coefficient of x**k, in the abscissa unit); exp_fit (y = amplitude exp(rate x), log-linear least squares weighted by |y|, samples of one sign): amplitude, rate, decay (decay = -1 / rate, the e-folding length or time); lorentz_fit (y = offset + amplitude / (1 + (2 (x - center) / fwhm)**2), least squares, a peak or a dip; window it around one line): center, fwhm, amplitude, offset, q (q = |center| / fwhm, the quality factor of a line versus frequency or wavelength); two_exp_fit (y = amplitude_start exp(-kappa (x - x_first)) + amplitude_end exp(kappa (x - x_last)), kappa > 0, amplitudes at the outermost samples; an evanescent field between two ends): kappa, decay_length, amplitude_start, amplitude_end, r_squared (decay_length = 1 / kappa); two_wave_fit (complex y = A_f exp(-j beta x) + A_b exp(+j beta x), beta > 0; the expression is one bare '<name>_re' series, paired at run time with '<name>_im' of the same result and x samples; A_f travels toward +x in the exp(+j omega t) convention, phases at x = 0): beta, wavelength, forward_abs, forward_phase, backward_abs, backward_phase, reflection_abs, r_squared (reflection_abs = |A_b| / |A_f|); richardson (y = extrapolated + coefficient x**order, x > 0: a step size or cell count; samples monotone): extrapolated, order, coefficient, error_estimate, relative_error_estimate (order > 0 converges as x -> 0, order < 0 as x -> infinity; error_estimate = |y - extrapolated| of the sample nearest the limit). Peak fits (degree = number of lines K, quantities generated per line k = 1 .. K numbered by ascending position, then the shared ones; spacing = least-squares slope of the line positions vs k, degree >= 2 only): multi_lorentz_fit (y = offset + sum_k amplitude_k / (1 + (2 (x - center_k) / fwhm_k)**2), joint least squares seeded from the K most prominent maxima, or minima for dips): center_<k>, fwhm_<k>, amplitude_<k>, q_<k>, offset, spacing, r_squared (q_k = |center_k| / fwhm_k); pole_fit (complex y = sum_k r_k / (x - nu_k) + d0 + d1 x, vector fitting by pole relocation; the expression is one bare '<name>_re' series as for two_wave_fit; x is usually frequency, a nearby line outside the window is absorbed by d0 + d1 x only roughly: window around the K lines): frequency_<k>, q_<k>, fwhm_<k>, residue_abs_<k>, spacing, r_squared (frequency_k = Re nu_k, fwhm_k = 2 |Im nu_k|, q_k = |Re nu_k| / (2 |Im nu_k|), residue_abs_k = |r_k|; either sign convention of Im nu). A fitted line outside the samples is an error (lower the degree or move the window).
- `degree` (int; default 1): Operation 'polyfit': polynomial degree 0 .. 10 (default 1); multi_lorentz_fit / pole_fit: number of lines (peaks / poles) 1 .. 10.
- `point` (str; default ""): Field operations only: point object of 'at' (required: the value in the window cell containing it) and of 'mode_volume' (integral / the value there; '' = integral / maximum over the selection).

#### `AnalyticCurveSpec` - items of ModelSpec.analytic_curves

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among analytic curves.
- `target` (str; required): Simulated curve to draw over: 'physics.feature' of an enabled feature with a timeseries, flux_spectrum, far_field, xy, table result, 'sweep' (the Sweep tab: versus the swept parameter) or 'line' (a profile of field along line).
- `expression` (str; required): Expression of parameters and the target variable: wavelength [m] (flux_spectrum, xy versus wavelength), t [s] (timeseries; iteration = the 1-based sample index when every sample shares one t, e.g. stationary iterations), frequency [Hz] (timeseries with series 'fft'), x (xy, in its x unit; table: the x_column value in its unit, or the 0-based row), angle [rad from +x] and wavelength [m] of the shown frequency (far_field, normalised to its peak like the simulated pattern), the swept parameter (sweep: every parameter is re-evaluated per point), x, y [m], z [m, the cut height or the 3D segment point; 3D models only] and s [m from the line start] (line). Variables shadow parameters of the same name.
- `series` (str; default ""): Simulated quantity the curve belongs to (drawn in its colour): an xy series or table column name, 'ratio' (Spectra ratio-to-reference plot of a flux_spectrum / wavelength xy target), 'fft' (probe FFT of a timeseries: |FFT| * dt, value unit times s); for sweep the derived value name, 'physics.feature' of a timeseries (its final value) or '<column>_<k>' of a per-value table (band k: the k-th smallest value, as Results.sweep_xy); '' = every quantity of the target.
- `line` (list; default []): Target 'line' only: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in m (numbers or parameter expressions), two distinct points (the Line profile tab plots field along it). 3D models also take a 3D segment [x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1] in any direction, sampled from the final state of the whole volume (see sampling; no mirror unfolding; live Results only; plane stays null); every snapshot also stores its profile, so snapshot works with it (saved runs too).
- `field` (str; default ""): Target 'line' only: output field 'physics.component' (e.g. 'heat.T') sampled along the line from the final state (or the snapshot) in the containing cells (on a cell edge: the upper cell).
- `x_column` (str; default ""): 'table' targets only: numeric column used as the abscissa x of the curve and the plot (rows sorted by it); '' = the 0-based row index. series names the plotted column.
- `plane` (float | int | str | None; default null): Target 'line' in 3D models only: height z [m] (number or parameter expression) of the horizontal cut the line [x0, y0, x1, y1] lies in; null = the GUI cut-plane choice (when a z cut), headless the mid-height cut. Not with snapshot (snapshots hold the mid-height cut) or a 3D segment (side planes: give a 3D segment).
- `snapshot` (int | str | None; default null): Target 'line' only: sample field from a stored snapshot instead of the final state: an index into Results.snapshots() (negative from the end) or a snapshot label, whole or its text before ':' (e.g. 'mode 2', 'resonance 1', 'lambda = 1550 nm'), also without its mirror parity tag ('mode 2' for 'mode 2 [x_lo symmetric]'); it must match one snapshot; null = the final state. field must be stored (a 3D segment: any field).
- `tolerance` (float | int | None; default null): Optional number >= 0 or null: largest accepted summary.json curve_error max (max |simulated - analytic| / ptp(analytic) at the simulated samples: an absolute temperature is judged against its rise; target sweep: relative per swept value; a feature target in a sweep: at every value). Used only by selftest --examples, which fails the example above it or when the curve cannot be compared; null = reported, never failed.
- `interface` (str; default ""): Target 'line' in 2D models only: name of an 'interface' selection; '' = the containing cells. Each line sample (two per finest cell) then reads the side along the outward normal of the nearest outline sample and extrapolates onto itself (see SelectionSpec.side); draw the line along the outline (e.g. a slot-waveguide sidewall). field is one component, or with projection the x component of an in-plane vector. Polar / spherical: live Results read the (r, angle) cells, saved ones and snapshots the image over the sector box (first order at the outline).
- `sampling` (str; default "nearest"): Target 'line' with a 3D segment only: 'nearest' (default: the containing cell, curve_error at those cell centres) or 'trilinear' (between the 8 surrounding cell centres, constant in the outer half cells; curve_error at the sample points, so an oblique segment shows no staircase). Other lines: 'nearest' only (validation error).
- `projection` (str; default ""): With interface only: '' (field as it is) | normal | tangential: field names the x component of an in-plane vector (e.g. em.ex_re; its y partner em.ey_re by x -> y), both read one-sided and projected on the nearest outline normal or the tangent = normal turned +90 deg (polar / spherical: radial / angular components). A snapshot curve needs both stored.

#### `DerivedCurveSpec` - items of ModelSpec.derived_curves

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among derived curves; its key in summary.json derived_curves.
- `expression` (str; required): Expression of the input aliases (arrays on the curve abscissa, or numbers for scalar samples), x (the abscissa, in its unit) and parameters, evaluated per abscissa point, e.g. "eta*S*P_top/(h_const*c_const/lambda0)". Aliases shadow parameters of the same name. Besides the expression functions it may call (here only): gradient(y): dy/dx along the curve abscissa x (second-order differences, also at the ends), over the finite samples of y (NaN ones stay NaN); cumtrapz(y): running trapezoid integral of y over x, 0 at the first finite sample; NaN samples (outside an interpolated input's range) are skipped and stay NaN, so it integrates over the overlap.
- `inputs` (dict; default {}): {alias: 'physics.feature:sample'}: an identifier (not a reserved name) per input, the sample a sample name of that enabled 1D feature result as for derived values (xy series, table column, timeseries values, flux power, or a numeric scalar such as variance). The first array input sets the abscissa (sorted); later ones are interpolated linearly onto it (NaN outside their range) and must share its abscissa label and unit.
- `plot` (str; default ""): Plot the curve is drawn in, shared with the other curves naming it (an identifier; '' = a plot of its own named after the curve); figures/derived_<plot>.png. Curves of different unit go to separate panels of the plot.
- `label` (str; default ""): Legend text; '' (or a label already used in the plot) = the curve name.
- `unit` (str; default ""): Unit of the values, free text ('' = none); panels group by it.
- `log_x` (bool; default false): Logarithmic abscissa; the first drawn curve of a plot sets it for the plot.
- `log_y` (bool; default false): Logarithmic value axis; the first drawn curve of a plot sets it for the plot.
- `reference` (float | int | str | None; default null): Optional analytic curve: number or expression of x (the curve abscissa) and parameters, drawn as series '<series> reference' in the plot; summary.json derived_curves <name> curve_error {max, rms, n_points} = |curve - reference| / ptp(reference) on the curve abscissa (as AnalyticCurveSpec.tolerance) and y_reference.
- `tolerance` (float | int | None; default null): Optional number >= 0 or null: largest accepted curve_error max against the reference. Used only by selftest --examples, which fails the example above it or when the curve fails; null = reported, never failed.

### Param kinds

- `float`: a number or an expression string (see expressions)
- `int`: a whole number, or an expression of parameters that evaluates to one
- `bool`: true or false
- `choice`: one of the listed choices (text)
- `str`: text
- `expression`: expression text kept as written and evaluated at run time (its help names the allowed names)
- `ref`: the name of a model node of the given kind (material, geometry object, physics or parameter); null or "" = none where optional
- `float_list`: a list of numbers or parameter expressions
- `points`: a list of [x, y] pairs of numbers or parameter expressions, in m
- `names`: a list of node names (of the given kind)
- `table`: a list of rows, each a list of one number or parameter expression per column, in the column order and units listed with the param (range bounds apply to every entry)

### Param lines

- Param lines read "- `name` [unit] (facts) - Label", the help indented below ([1] = dimensionless). Facts: the kind unless float (a choice lists its choices a | b); default <value>, or required; the range (> a, >= a, <= b, [a, b], (a, b]); nullable = null allowed; may use x, y / fields / t = names an expression may use beyond parameters (expressions: Names available where); visible when ... = used and checked only then; writes = the material arrays set. Material properties may use x, y and physics fields and write the array of their own name unless marked "no x, y", "no fields" or "writes ...". Consecutive params differing only in name and label share one line.

### Names

- Node names (parameters, geometry objects, selections, materials, physics, features, couplings, meshes, derived values, analytic and derived curves) are Python identifiers, unique within their kind (features: within their physics).
- Geometry objects and selections share one namespace and may not use the reserved entity names x_lo, x_hi, y_lo, y_hi, z_lo, z_hi, all.
- Parameter names may not be reserved expression names (functions, constants, x, y, z, t, value) or physics field names (see expressions).

### Entities and selections

- Selection kinds: domain | boundary | point | line | interface. An entity list (MaterialSpec.selection, FeatureSpec.selection, DerivedValueSpec.selection, SelectionSpec.entities) holds geometry object names, named selections of the same kind (expanded recursively) and reserved entity names.
- Domain entities: domain objects and all (the whole domain; build masks include the PML ring). Boundary entities: the outer faces x_lo (left), x_hi (right), y_lo (bottom), y_hi (top) and domain objects = their perimeter cells inside the object (the window edge is no perimeter). Point and line entities: point and line objects.
- 3D models (DomainSpec.size_z set) add the outer faces z_lo and z_hi; the 2D domain kinds become prisms over z0 / z1 (null = full height), points and lines sit at their z (null = mid-height), and box, cylinder_z and sphere are 3D-only. Fields are cut planes (the mid-height z cut unless an x / y / z plane is chosen).
- Inputs of a composite (union, intersection, difference, array) cannot be selected on their own.

### Values

- Numeric fields and float / int params take a number or an expression string of parameters, e.g. "2*r_disk + 50*nm" (see expressions).
- Settings and params dicts (PhysicsSpec.settings, FeatureSpec.params, CouplingSpec.params, StudySpec.settings, GeometrySpec.params) hold values by param name: a missing key takes the default, an unknown key is an error.
- A param is checked only while visible (visible when ...); an invisible param whose value fails keeps its default.
- Validation range-checks values that evaluate over the parameters. Material properties using x, y, z are range-checked on their cells at build time; those using physics fields at every update (FDTD / transient fields: at update 1, 2, 4, 8, ... and every 100th, so a run fails late and a range left after the last check is not reported), naming material, property and range. Other expressions of x, y, z are checked for finite values only.

### Physics, couplings and study

- Snapshots (StudySpec.stored_fields): time_dependent at the output interval plus the final state, stationary the final state, frequency_domain one per wavelength ("lambda = <nm> nm"), mode_analysis one per mode ("mode <k>: n_eff = <value>"), eigenfrequency one per resonance ("resonance <k>: lambda = <nm> nm, Q = <value>"). A snapshot holds the native window cells (x_centers / y_centers set) up to 250,000 cells; a larger window is nearest-cell resampled on square pixels of max(finest cell, sqrt(window area / 250,000)) (native_shape set, x_centers None), which can skip features finer than a pixel. 3D: the mid-height z cut plus each StudySpec.stored_cuts plane.
- A physics type lists the studies it supports; a study with a background study (e.g. frequency_domain: stationary) also accepts the physics that support only that one and solves them first as background physics. Heat is solved as a steady state in every study except time_dependent.
- A 2D type's geometry setting axisymmetric solves a body of revolution about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z; x_lo is the axis, r = 0 a symmetry): field derived values of the whole model are then ring-weighted by 2 pi r dx dy ('integral' a whole-body total, 'mean' a volume mean), and a coupled planar physics (no geometry setting, e.g. EM, or set to planar) solves a planar cut per unit z length whose fields are applied per cell as rings (validation warns).
- StudySpec.sweep {"parameter": name, "values": [...]} builds and runs the model once per value ({"spacing": "linear" | "log", "lower", "upper", "count"} for a range); summary.json sweep holds the derived values and feature result digests per value.
- Physics type entries: the default study is the one the GUI applies when the physics is the first; backends = SolverDefaultsSpec.backend values it runs on, mesh kinds = MeshSpec.kind values, refinement indicator fields = what StudySpec.adaptation reads when its solver has no error indicator of its own, dispersion poles = whether MaterialSpec.dispersion is read; each feature is also a topic `<physics>.<feature>`. State fields are the solver state: expressions name them <physics>_<field>, or <field> when one physics alone provides it; field_transfer source_field. Output fields are what Results.field, study stored_fields (<physics>.<field>) and derived values read; [] stored_fields stores all. Scalar outputs are numbers after a run; derived-value expressions name them <physics>_<name>.
- Source slots (physics type entries) are the coupling targets (CouplingSpec.target; field_transfer target_slot), with unit and meaning; a slot takes one overwriting coupling, or several additive ones whose contributions are summed (see the coupling types).
- Feature entries (params in FeatureSpec.params): "result kind `<kind>`" = Results.result(physics name, feature name) returns a dict with the keys under Result kinds (topic results; a feature topic lists them inline); "requires a uniform mesh" = nonuniform and auto modes fall back to a uniform grid at the finest target (see mesh); "stepper precisions ... only" = another resolved stepper precision is a validation error at the feature.
- Coupling entries: "across meshes" = what happens when source and target run on different meshes.
- Study entries: "solution feedback" = couplings from a physics the study solves into background physics are allowed (feedback rounds); "coupled points" = couplings and material properties may read a physics the study solves, each point of the study axis then a stationary fixed point of every physics; "StudySpec.adaptation allowed" = mesh refinement levels are supported.

### Derived values

- A derived value that fails for any reason, including running out of GPU memory, becomes NaN plus a warning (summary.json warnings); the run itself is not failed by it.
- DerivedValueSpec.source 'physics.feature' reduces a 1D result (timeseries, flux_spectrum, far_field, xy, table) instead of fields. Its sample names (they shadow parameters): every numeric scalar and every numeric array with one entry per sample of the result dict by key (timeseries t, values; flux_spectrum wavelength, frequency, power, power_per_cw (FDTD only); xy x and extras such as wavelength, n_eff), plus the xy series by name and the numeric table columns by name (one sample per row, abscissa row = 0, 1, ...). xy series and table column names are known only at run time: a missing one gives NaN plus a warning. far_field: the pattern at one wavelength (DerivedValueSpec.wavelength): angle [rad], power, power_norm (power over its peak), power_per_cw (when the result has it), and that wavelength and frequency as numbers.
- Far-field examples: beam direction {"name": "theta_peak", "source": "em.ff", "expression": "power", "operation": "argmax"}, beam width {"name": "theta_fwhm", "source": "em.ff", "expression": "power", "operation": "fwhm"}, value at an angle {"name": "p_up", "source": "em.ff", "expression": "power_norm", "operation": "at", "at": "pi/2"}; a line width {"name": "Q_line", "source": "em.trans", "expression": "power", "operation": "lorentz_fit", "fit": "q", "window": ["1545*nm", "1555*nm"]}.
- A sample name may equal an expression function name (e.g. the xy series abs of an FDFD probe): written without "(" it is the sample ("abs**2"), with "(" the function ("abs(phase)"); one expression may not use the same name both ways. Analytic curve series match series names as plain text, so any name works there.
- Example: {"name": "T_1550", "source": "em.trans", "expression": "power", "operation": "at", "at": "1550*nm", "reference": "T_film"}.

### Analytic curves

- ModelSpec.analytic_curves never change the run: they are drawn over the results and compared with them (summary.json curve_error; with a tolerance, selftest --examples fails the model above it). The GUI evaluates them with numpy on its own thread over the parameters of the last built session (a sweep: its last value) on 501 points spanning the sampled range (timeseries: the own sample times when there are 501 to 20000, else 501 or 20000 points, so a ring-down does not alias; fft: the FFT frequency bins; sweep: 201 points over the swept values) and draws them dashed in the colour of the simulated curve they belong to; a failing curve is reported in the Results panel message line.
- Sweep tab: each numeric column of a per-value table result is offered as bands vs the swept parameter ('<column>_<k>', sorted per value as Results.sweep_xy); the per-value result overlays also draw the curves targeting that result, evaluated at each swept value. Curves & tables: a table result is also plotted versus a chosen numeric column (x_column of its curves). Headless figures (figures=True) draw feature curves except series 'ratio' and 'fft' (no FFT figure; a flux spectrum only series '' and 'power', its one panel), a table's curves into figures/<key>_vs_<x_column or row>.png and line curves into figures/curve_<name>.png.
- Examples: {"name": "T_fp", "target": "em.trans", "expression": "1 / (1 + F*sin(2*pi*n_f*d_f/wavelength)**2)", "series": "ratio"}; {"name": "T_line", "target": "line", "expression": "T0 + q*s*(L - s)/(2*k_s)", "line": [0, "H/2", "L", "H/2"], "field": "heat.T"}; {"name": "R_sweep", "target": "sweep", "expression": "R0*(1 + alpha*w)", "series": "R"}; {"name": "ring", "target": "em.probe", "expression": "A*exp(-pi*f0*t/Q)*cos(2*pi*f0*t)"}; {"name": "ring_fft", "target": "em.probe", "expression": "A/(2*sqrt((2*pi*(frequency - f0))**2 + (pi*f0/Q)**2))", "series": "fft"}; {"name": "band_2", "target": "sweep", "expression": "c0*k_b/(2*pi*n_eff)", "series": "frequency_2"}; {"name": "Q_fit", "target": "em.res", "expression": "Q0", "x_column": "frequency", "series": "Q"}; {"name": "mode_2", "target": "line", "expression": "A*sin(2*pi*s/L)", "line": [0, "H/2", "L", "H/2"], "field": "em.ez", "snapshot": "resonance 2"}; {"name": "T_top", "target": "line", "expression": "T0", "line": [0, 0, "L", 0], "field": "heat.T", "plane": "h_top"}.

### Derived curves

- ModelSpec.derived_curves are evaluated with numpy after the run (GUI: on its own thread, re-evaluated when edited, no rerun) over the final feature results and the parameters of the last built session (a sweep: its last value). A failing curve (missing result or sample, other abscissa, expression error) is left out of its plot and reported: GUI message line, summary.json derived_curves {name: {plot, error}}.
- Example (heterodyne signal over shot noise, P_LO cancels: eta S / (h nu), S scaled from 1 V/m to a beam power): {"name": "snr_trn", "inputs": {"S": "heat.top_x:psd"}, "expression": "eta*S*E0sq/(h_const*c_const/lambda0)", "plot": "snr", "label": "TRN", "unit": "1", "log_x": true, "log_y": true} with E0sq a parameter.
- Calculus example (a capacitance dQ/dV from an xy result whose x is a voltage and whose series Q is a charge, against a constant): {"name": "C_V", "inputs": {"Q": "<physics>.<feature>:Q"}, "expression": "gradient(Q)", "unit": "F/m", "reference": "eps_ox*eps0_const/t_ox", "tolerance": 0.05}; a derived value with source "C_V" (expression "C_V") then reduces or fits the curve like a 1D result.

### Validation issues

- Levels: error, warning, info; errors block build and run. A build error becomes one issue at the node path of the failing build step.
- Node paths: ["parameters"] (each message names the parameter), ["geometry", name] (the domain size at ["geometry"]), ["selection", name], ["material", name], ["physics", name], ["feature", physics, feature], ["coupling", name], ["mesh"], ["study"], ["derived", name], ["curve", name], ["model"] (invalid file content and failures not tied to one node).
- Reports add node, the label of the path: [] -> model, ["mesh"] -> mesh, ["feature", "em", "source"] -> feature em/source.

## Expressions

Numeric values are numbers or expression strings, evaluated by a safe evaluator. Which names an expression may use depends on where it sits (Names available where).

### Syntax

- Arithmetic: + - * / // % ** and unary + -; ** is the power (^ is not allowed).
- Comparisons < <= > >= == != give 1 or 0, e.g. "(x > 1*um) * 2"; chained comparisons, and / or / not and if / else are not allowed: use where, min and max.
- Integer literals become floats (1/2 = 0.5). Only numbers, names and positional calls of the functions below (no attributes, indexing, strings or keywords). A function name without "(" is an ordinary name, which only a result sample name can supply (see Derived values).
- At most 2000 characters. Results must be real: a complex result (e.g. (-8)**(1/3)) is an error; a value outside a function domain (log(-1)) gives nan, which fails where a finite number is needed.
- With numbers and parameters only an expression gives one float; with x, y, z or fields it is evaluated per cell.

### Functions

- abs(x): absolute value
- acos(x): inverse cosine in rad, for x in [-1, 1]
- asin(x): inverse sine in rad, for x in [-1, 1]
- atan(x): inverse tangent in rad, in (-pi/2, pi/2)
- atan2(y, x): angle of the point (x, y) in rad, in [-pi, pi], counter-clockwise from +x
- ceil(x): smallest whole number >= x (a float)
- cos(x): cosine of an angle x in rad
- cosh(x): hyperbolic cosine
- erf(x): error function (2/sqrt(pi)) * integral of exp(-u**2) from 0 to x, in (-1, 1)
- erfc(x): complementary error function 1 - erf(x), accurate where erf(x) is close to 1
- exp(x): e to the power x
- floor(x): largest whole number <= x (a float)
- hypot(a, b): sqrt(a**2 + b**2) without intermediate overflow
- i0(x): modified Bessel function of the first kind I_0 (overflows to inf above x ~ 700)
- i1(x): modified Bessel function of the first kind I_1 (overflows to inf above x ~ 700)
- j0(x): Bessel function of the first kind J_0 (real x)
- j1(x): Bessel function of the first kind J_1 (real x)
- k0(x): modified Bessel function of the second kind K_0, for x > 0 (inf at 0, nan below)
- k1(x): modified Bessel function of the second kind K_1, for x > 0 (inf at 0, nan below)
- log(x): natural logarithm, for x > 0
- log10(x): base-10 logarithm, for x > 0
- max(a, b, ...): element-wise maximum of 2 or more arguments
- min(a, b, ...): element-wise minimum of 2 or more arguments
- pow(a, b): a to the power b, same as a**b
- sign(x): -1, 0 or 1 by the sign of x
- sin(x): sine of an angle x in rad
- sinh(x): hyperbolic sine
- sqrt(x): square root, for x >= 0
- tan(x): tangent of an angle x in rad
- tanh(x): hyperbolic tangent
- where(condition, a, b): element-wise a where condition is true (non-zero), else b; both a and b are evaluated everywhere
- y0(x): Bessel function of the second kind Y_0, for x > 0 (-inf at 0, nan below)
- y1(x): Bessel function of the second kind Y_1, for x > 0 (-inf at 0, nan below)

### Constants

- `pi` = 3.14159: ratio of circumference to diameter of a circle
- `c_const` = 2.99792e+08: speed of light in vacuum [m/s]
- `eps0_const` = 8.85419e-12: vacuum permittivity [F/m]
- `mu0_const` = 1.25664e-06: vacuum permeability [H/m]
- `h_const` = 6.62607e-34: Planck constant [J s]
- `hbar_const` = 1.05457e-34: reduced Planck constant [J s]
- `e_const` = 1.60218e-19: elementary charge [C]
- `kB_const` = 1.38065e-23: Boltzmann constant [J/K]
- `NA_const` = 6.02214e+23: Avogadro constant [1/mol]
- `nm` = 1e-09: length unit 1e-9 (m)
- `um` = 1e-06: length unit 1e-6 (m)
- `mm` = 0.001: length unit 1e-3 (m)
- `cm` = 0.01: length unit 1e-2 (m)
- `fs` = 1e-15: time unit 1e-15 (s)
- `ps` = 1e-12: time unit 1e-12 (s)
- `ns` = 1e-09: time unit 1e-9 (s)
- `us` = 1e-06: time unit 1e-6 (s)
- `ms` = 0.001: time unit 1e-3 (s)
- `THz` = 1e+12: frequency unit 1e12 (Hz)
- `GHz` = 1e+09: frequency unit 1e9 (Hz)
- `MHz` = 1e+06: frequency unit 1e6 (Hz)
- `kHz` = 1000: frequency unit 1e3 (Hz)

### Reserved names

Not usable as parameter names: every function and constant above and t, value, x, y, z (t, x, y, z: time and coordinates; value: the source field in coupling expressions).

### Names available where

- ParameterSpec.expression: numbers, constants and other parameters in any order (unknown names and cycles are errors).
- Domain size, geometry params, mesh values, refinement dx / margin, sweep values, dispersion pole values and every param not marked "may use x, y": parameters only.
- Settings, feature params and material properties that may use x, y: also x and y, the cell centres in m (EM PML cells take the nearest window centre), and in 3D models z [m] (z in a 2D model is a validation error). 3D materials using z are written one z cell plane at a time, feature values using z cover the bounding box of their selection.
- Material properties that may use fields: also the state fields of the physics in the model as <physics>_<field>, or <field> when one physics alone provides it (e.g. T); such a property is rewritten right after each step of the physics it reads (the one with the largest every), so physics stepping on later ticks see it, but only when one of them solved or stepped since the last rewrite (a quasi-static physics that did not re-solve rewrites nothing), and once more after the final solves of a time-dependent run (a stationary study iterates it; frequency_domain allows only fields of its background physics). They may also use t [s] (with or without fields and x, y): rewritten at the start of every runner step (t = the step start time; t = 0 in every other study).
- Feature params that may use t: also the time t [s] with parameters only (no x, y, z), re-evaluated at the start of every runner step of the physics (an implicit step, e.g. transient heat, sees the start value, a first-order lag); t = 0 at the build and in every other study.
- Coupling params of kind expression (field_transfer expression): value (the source field), x, y (3D: z) and parameters; no other field names and no t.
- Derived values: parameters, x, y (3D: z), t (the final time), the output fields as <physics>_<field> or a unique <field> and the scalar outputs of a physics (e.g. em_modes n_eff_1) as <physics>_<name> only (a name the solver did not report gives NaN plus a warning); with a source the sample names of that result instead (a derived curve source: the curve name and x; see Derived values). Derived value at / reference / window / wavelength: parameters only.
- Analytic curves: parameters and the variables of their target (AnalyticCurveSpec.expression).
- Derived curves: parameters, their input aliases and x, plus gradient / cumtrapz (DerivedCurveSpec.expression); reference: parameters and x.
- A parameter may not have the name of a physics state or output field or scalar output (validation error).

### Physics field names by physics type

- `drift_diffusion`: state fields V, N, P, E_x, E_y, J_x, J_y, Jn_x, Jn_y, Jp_x, Jp_y, phi_n, phi_p, net_doping, space_charge, recombination, generation, generation_ext; output fields: the state fields
- `elastic_waves`: state fields pressure, sxx, syy, sxy, vx, vy; output fields: the state fields, plus stt, v_abs, elastic_strain_xx, elastic_strain_yy
- `electric_currents`: state fields V, E_x, E_y, J_x, J_y, q_joule, current_source, current_source_ext, sigma_dc_xx, sigma_dc_yy; output fields: the state fields, plus E_z, J_z, sigma_dc_zz
- `electrostatics`: state fields V, E_x, E_y, D_x, D_y, rho_free, rho_free_ext, rho_ion, eps_dc_xx, eps_dc_yy; output fields: the state fields, plus c_ion_1, c_ion_2, c_ion_3, c_ion_4, E_z, D_z, eps_dc_zz
- `em_eme`: state fields ez_re, ez_im, hz_re, hz_im, e_intensity, eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy, sigma_e; output fields: the state fields, plus ez_abs, ez_phase, e_abs, h_abs, absorbed_power, eps_sensitivity, design_density, hz_abs, hz_phase, eps_xy
- `em_eme_3d`: state fields eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy; output fields: the state fields, plus e_abs, e_intensity, ex_re, ex_im, ey_re, ey_im, ez_re, ez_im, absorbed_power, eps_sensitivity
- `em_fdfd_3d`: state fields eps_r; output fields: the state fields, plus ex_re, ex_im, ex_abs, ey_re, ey_im, ey_abs, ez_re, ez_im, ez_abs, hx_re, hx_im, hx_abs, hy_re, hy_im, hy_abs, hz_re, hz_im, hz_abs, e_abs, e_intensity, h_abs, w_e
- `em_fdfd_bor`: state fields e_intensity, eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy, sigma_e, q_abs; output fields: the state fields except q_abs, plus er, ephi, ez, hr, hphi, hz, er_abs, ephi_abs, ez_abs, hr_abs, hphi_abs, hz_abs, e_abs, h_abs, absorbed_power
