## Geometry

ModelSpec.geometry objects are named shapes in m (Params: GeometrySpec.params); selections, materials, features and mesh refinements refer to them by name.

- Geometry kinds by entity kind: domain: rectangle, rounded_rectangle, circle, ellipse, polygon, union, intersection, difference, array, box, cylinder_z, sphere; point: point; line: line.
- Coordinates are physical, in m, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the physical domain: x from 0 to size_x (to the right), y from 0 to size_y (up); EM PML cells lie outside.
- Masks test cell centres: rectangles, polygons and boxes are half-open ([x0, x1) x [y0, y1), corners in any order: a centre on x0 / y0 is inside, on x1 / y1 outside), circles, ellipses and spheres closed; rounded rectangles are half-open along their straight sides, closed on their corner arcs; a point or line end exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell.
- Validation's material preview uses float64 cell centres while the build tests float32 centres clamped into the window, so cells exactly on a boundary can differ: avoid material edges exactly on cell centres.
- Composite inputs (union, intersection, difference, array; composites included) are consumed: they can no longer be selected on their own and may feed only one composite.
- An array repeats its base object on an nx x ny (x nz) grid of copies moved by multiples of pitch_x / pitch_y / pitch_z, the base being the first copy: one GeometrySpec for thousands of holes or pillars. It acts as one domain object (a union of its copies) in selections, materials, features and refinements; meshes follow every copy's outline. Copies are internal shapes named '<array>[i,j]' (never selectable); overlapping copies get a validation warning.
- 3D extrusion of the 2D domain kinds (params z0, z1, axis, sidewall_angle; 3D models only: in 2D they must stay null / 'z' / 0): the shape is extruded along axis between z0 and z1, centres with min(z0, z1) <= coordinate < max(z0, z1) inside. axis 'x' / 'y': the shape's (x, y) are the model's (y, z) / (x, z), the ellipse angle turns from the first toward the second, and z0 / z1 (both required, beyond the domain to run into the PML) are its ends along x / y: a circle with axis 'x' is a cylinder along x. Faces parallel to the mesh axes become snap nodes on refined meshes; curved faces are staircased. sidewall_angle (deg, -90 < angle < 90, needs z0 and z1): the shape as given sits at min(z0, z1) and is offset inward by (s - min(z0, z1)) tan(angle) toward the other end (positive narrows: etched ridges, tapers; negative widens: undercuts, V-grooves as a widening hole); rectangles shrink on every side, circles become cones, ellipses frusta (both semi-axes by the same offset), polygons are offset per vertex (mitred; simple polygons only); a collapsing or self-intersecting offset is an error. Slanted walls are staircased per z cell; along x / y each cross-section is sampled in 256 steps.

### Geometry kind `rectangle` - Rectangle

Axis-aligned rectangle (domain object) between two opposite corners, half-open [x0, x1) x [y0, y1) (corners sorted).

- Entity kind domain

Params:
- `x0` [m] (default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, x
  x of one corner (corners in any order).
- `y0` [m] (default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, y
  y of the same corner as x0.
- `x1` [m] (default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, x
  x of the opposite corner.
- `y1` [m] (default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, y
  y of the opposite corner.
- `z0` [m] (nullable) - Extrusion start
  Lower end of the extrusion along axis; null = the domain bottom (full height, PML included; axis z only). 3D models only (null in 2D).
- `z1` [m] (nullable) - Extrusion end
  Upper end of the extrusion along axis; null = the domain top (axis z only). 3D models only (null in 2D).
- `axis` (default "z"; z | x | y) - Extrusion axis
  Extrusion axis; 'x' / 'y' read the shape's (x, y) as (y, z) / (x, z) and need z0 and z1. 3D models only ('z' in 2D).
- `sidewall_angle` [deg] (default 0) - Sidewall angle
  Side-wall tilt from the axis, -90 < angle < 90: positive narrows the shape toward z1, negative widens it; needs z0 and z1. 3D models only (0 in 2D).

### Geometry kind `rounded_rectangle` - Rounded rectangle

Axis-aligned rectangle (domain object) between two opposite corners with its corners rounded to quarter circles of radius r (a union of two rectangles and four circles). Triangle meshes follow the arcs exactly (P2 curved edges); gmsh tetrahedra export an untapered z prism as two boxes and four z cylinders, other axes and tapers are tagged per element.

- Entity kind domain

Params:
- `x0` [m] (default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, x
  x of one corner of the enclosing rectangle (corners in any order).
- `y0` [m] (default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, y
  y of the same corner as x0.
- `x1` [m] (default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, x
  x of the opposite corner.
- `y1` [m] (default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, y
  y of the opposite corner.
- `r` [m] (default 1e-07; >= 0) - Corner radius
  Radius of the four quarter-circle corners, <= half the shorter side (0 = a plain rectangle; half the shorter side = a stadium).
- `z0` [m] (nullable) - Extrusion start
  Lower end of the extrusion along axis; null = the domain bottom (full height, PML included; axis z only). 3D models only (null in 2D).
- `z1` [m] (nullable) - Extrusion end
  Upper end of the extrusion along axis; null = the domain top (axis z only). 3D models only (null in 2D).
- `axis` (default "z"; z | x | y) - Extrusion axis
  Extrusion axis; 'x' / 'y' read the shape's (x, y) as (y, z) / (x, z) and need z0 and z1. 3D models only ('z' in 2D).
- `sidewall_angle` [deg] (default 0) - Sidewall angle
  Side-wall tilt from the axis, -90 < angle < 90: positive narrows the shape toward z1, negative widens it; needs z0 and z1. 3D models only (0 in 2D).

### Geometry kind `circle` - Circle

Circle (domain object) of radius r around (cx, cy), closed.

- Entity kind domain

Params:
- `cx` [m] (default 2e-06) - Centre x
  x of the centre.
- `cy` [m] (default 2e-06) - Centre y
  y of the centre.
- `r` [m] (default 5e-07; > 0) - Radius
  Radius.
- `z0` [m] (nullable) - Extrusion start
  Lower end of the extrusion along axis; null = the domain bottom (full height, PML included; axis z only). 3D models only (null in 2D).
- `z1` [m] (nullable) - Extrusion end
  Upper end of the extrusion along axis; null = the domain top (axis z only). 3D models only (null in 2D).
- `axis` (default "z"; z | x | y) - Extrusion axis
  Extrusion axis; 'x' / 'y' read the shape's (x, y) as (y, z) / (x, z) and need z0 and z1. 3D models only ('z' in 2D).
- `sidewall_angle` [deg] (default 0) - Sidewall angle
  Side-wall tilt from the axis, -90 < angle < 90: positive narrows the shape toward z1, negative widens it; needs z0 and z1. 3D models only (0 in 2D).

### Geometry kind `ellipse` - Ellipse

Ellipse (domain object) with semi-axes a and b about (cx, cy), closed.

- Entity kind domain

Params:
- `cx` [m] (default 2e-06) - Centre x
  x of the centre.
- `cy` [m] (default 2e-06) - Centre y
  y of the centre.
- `a` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - First semi-axis
  Semi-axis along +x before the rotation.
- `b` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Second semi-axis
  Semi-axis along +y before the rotation.
- `angle` [deg] (default 0) - Rotation
  Rotation of semi-axis a about the centre, counter-clockwise from +x.
- `z0` [m] (nullable) - Extrusion start
  Lower end of the extrusion along axis; null = the domain bottom (full height, PML included; axis z only). 3D models only (null in 2D).
- `z1` [m] (nullable) - Extrusion end
  Upper end of the extrusion along axis; null = the domain top (axis z only). 3D models only (null in 2D).
- `axis` (default "z"; z | x | y) - Extrusion axis
  Extrusion axis; 'x' / 'y' read the shape's (x, y) as (y, z) / (x, z) and need z0 and z1. 3D models only ('z' in 2D).
- `sidewall_angle` [deg] (default 0) - Sidewall angle
  Side-wall tilt from the axis, -90 < angle < 90: positive narrows the shape toward z1, negative widens it; needs z0 and z1. 3D models only (0 in 2D).

### Geometry kind `polygon` - Polygon

Polygon (domain object) through its vertices, even-odd fill rule (overlapping parts of a self-intersecting polygon are holes), half-open like rectangles (a centre on a left / bottom edge is inside, on a right / top edge outside).

- Entity kind domain

Params:
- `points` [m] (points; default [[1.5e-06, 1.5e-06], [2.5e-06, 1.5e-06], [2e-06, 2.5e-06]]) - Vertices
  Vertices [(x, y), ...]: at least 3, not all on one line; implicitly closed.
- `z0` [m] (nullable) - Extrusion start
  Lower end of the extrusion along axis; null = the domain bottom (full height, PML included; axis z only). 3D models only (null in 2D).
- `z1` [m] (nullable) - Extrusion end
  Upper end of the extrusion along axis; null = the domain top (axis z only). 3D models only (null in 2D).
- `axis` (default "z"; z | x | y) - Extrusion axis
  Extrusion axis; 'x' / 'y' read the shape's (x, y) as (y, z) / (x, z) and need z0 and z1. 3D models only ('z' in 2D).
- `sidewall_angle` [deg] (default 0) - Sidewall angle
  Side-wall tilt from the axis, -90 < angle < 90: positive narrows the shape toward z1, negative widens it; needs z0 and z1. 3D models only (0 in 2D).

### Geometry kind `point` - Point

Zero-area point entity for sources, probes and monitors (point source, field probe, temperature probe).

- Entity kind point

Params:
- `x` [m] (default 2e-06) - x
  x of the point.
- `y` [m] (default 2e-06) - y
  y of the point.
- `z` [m] (nullable) - z
  Height of the point / the plane holding the line; null = mid-height. 3D models only (null in 2D).

### Geometry kind `line` - Line segment

Zero-area line segment for sources, probes and monitors (line source, gaussian beam, flux monitor); lines used by EM features must be horizontal or vertical.

- Entity kind line

Params:
- `x0` [m] (default 1e-06) - Start x
  x of the start point.
- `y0` [m] (default 2e-06) - Start y
  y of the start point.
- `x1` [m] (default 3e-06) - End x
  x of the end point; x1 = x0 makes a vertical line.
- `y1` [m] (default 2e-06) - End y
  y of the end point; y1 = y0 makes a horizontal line.
- `z` [m] (nullable) - z
  Height of the point / the plane holding the line; null = mid-height. 3D models only (null in 2D).

### Geometry kind `union` - Union

Union of domain objects: a cell centre inside any input is inside. Inputs (domain objects, composites included) are consumed.

- Entity kind domain; composite

Params:
- `inputs` (names: geometry names; default []) - Input objects
  Domain objects combined by this operation (at least one); each is consumed.

### Geometry kind `intersection` - Intersection

Intersection of domain objects: a cell centre must be inside every input. Inputs (domain objects, composites included) are consumed.

- Entity kind domain; composite

Params:
- `inputs` (names: geometry names; default []) - Input objects
  Domain objects combined by this operation (at least one); each is consumed.

### Geometry kind `difference` - Difference

The base object minus the subtracted objects: a cell centre inside the base and outside every subtracted object is inside. Inputs (domain objects, composites included) are consumed.

- Entity kind domain; composite

Params:
- `base` (ref: geometry name; required) - Base object
  Domain object the others are subtracted from; consumed.
- `subtract` (names: geometry names; default []) - Objects to subtract
  Domain objects removed from the base (may be empty); each is consumed.

### Geometry kind `array` - Array

Rectangular array of nx x ny (x nz in 3D) copies of the base object, copy (i, j, k) moved by (i pitch_x, j pitch_y, k pitch_z); a union of the copies, acting as one domain object (see the array note). Meshes follow every copy (triangles: curved edges on circles, ellipses and rounded-rectangle arcs; gmsh tetrahedra: the solids of each copy). Composite bases are copied whole (a hole with a ring cut out, nested arrays). At most 200000 copies. Inputs (domain objects, composites included) are consumed.

- Entity kind domain; composite

Params:
- `base` (ref: geometry name; required) - Base object
  Domain object repeated (a primitive or a composite); the first copy, at its own position; consumed.
- `nx` [1] (int; default 2; >= 1) - Copies along x
  Number of copies along x, the base included.
- `ny` [1] (int; default 2; >= 1) - Copies along y
  Number of copies along y, the base included.
- `pitch_x` [m] (default 1e-06; > 0) - Pitch x
  Displacement between neighbouring copies along x: copy (i, j) is the base moved by (i pitch_x, j pitch_y). Copies whose bounding boxes overlap get a validation warning (they merge into one region).
- `pitch_y` [m] (default 1e-06; > 0) - Pitch y
  Displacement between neighbouring copies along y.
- `nz` [1] (int; default 1; >= 1) - Copies along z
  Number of copies along z, the base included; above 1 it needs pitch_z. 3D models only (1 in 2D).
- `pitch_z` [m] (> 0; nullable) - Pitch z
  Displacement between neighbouring copies along z; needed when nz > 1. A base with an open z end (z0 / z1 null) reaches the domain top / bottom in every copy, so such copies overlap. 3D models only (null in 2D).

### Geometry kind `box` - Box

Axis-aligned box (3D domain object) between two opposite corners, half-open on every axis; the same as a rectangle with z0 / z1. 3D models only.

- Entity kind domain

Params:
- `x0` [m] (default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, x
  x of one corner (corners in any order).
- `y0` [m] (default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, y
  y of the same corner as x0.
- `z0` [m] (default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, z
  z of the same corner as x0.
- `x1` [m] (default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, x
  x of the opposite corner.
- `y1` [m] (default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, y
  y of the opposite corner.
- `z1` [m] (default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, z
  z of the opposite corner.

### Geometry kind `cylinder_z` - Cylinder (z axis)

Cylinder with its axis along z (3D domain object): a circle extruded from z0 to z1 (a circle with axis 'x' / 'y' gives a cylinder along x / y, sidewall_angle a cone). 3D models only.

- Entity kind domain

Params:
- `cx` [m] (default 2e-06) - Centre x
  x of the axis.
- `cy` [m] (default 2e-06) - Centre y
  y of the axis.
- `r` [m] (default 5e-07; > 0) - Radius
  Radius (closed test).
- `z0` [m] (default 1.5e-06) - Bottom z
  One end along z (ends in any order; half-open in z).
- `z1` [m] (default 2.5e-06) - Top z
  The other end along z.

### Geometry kind `sphere` - Sphere

Sphere (3D domain object) of radius r around (cx, cy, cz), closed; the 2D canvas draws its cross-section at the shown layer. 3D models only.

- Entity kind domain

Params:
- `cx` [m] (default 2e-06) - Centre x
  x of the centre.
- `cy` [m] (default 2e-06) - Centre y
  y of the centre.
- `cz` [m] (default 2e-06) - Centre z
  z of the centre.
- `r` [m] (default 5e-07; > 0) - Radius
  Radius (closed test).

## Materials

Materials assign properties to domain entities: a library material, explicit properties of the present physics types and EM dispersion poles.

- MaterialSpec.library takes a library material name below; properties override its values (a null property keeps the library value); dispersion null inherits the library poles, [] removes them, a list replaces them.
- Materials apply in list order, later materials winning overlapping (whole) cells. A material whose selection contains all is a background material: it fills only the cells no other material covers, wherever it sits in the list (of several, the later wins). Cells under no material keep the type defaults: vacuum for EM, k = 0 for heat, sigma_dc = 0 for electric_currents, eps_dc = 1 for electrostatics.
- Only the properties of the physics types present, and only those the merged material sets, are written. A table property (e.g. magnetostatics bh_curve) is one constant table per material region, written to no array.
- eps_r is isotropic; eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_zz are components written after it (a component wins): the E_z types (em_fdtd_ez, em_fdfd_ez) see eps_zz (their eps_r array), the H_z types (em_fdtd_hz, em_fdfd_hz) eps_xx and eps_yy, em_modes all three.
- Library optical values (eps_r, sigma_e) are for 1.55 um; without dispersion poles the index is the same at every wavelength. Thermal data use the model property names (cp = specific heat). sigma_dc / eps_dc are static values for electric_currents / electrostatics, distinct from the optical sigma_e / eps_r.
- Dispersion poles are dicts {"model": "drude" | "lorentz", ...} with the params below (EM only); for a Drude material that sets no permittivity property for an array (eps_r or that component) the first Drude eps_inf is the background permittivity of that array.
- An {"model": "nk_fit", ...} entry (one per material; library materials with tabulated n, k only: their description names the data set) is replaced by eps_inf (>= 1) + an optional Drude pole + Lorentz poles fitted to the table over [wavelength_start, wavelength_stop] (passive: all pole values >= 0); the library optical values are then dropped, eps_inf is the Drude eps_inf or, without a Drude pole, eps_r. Validation reports the fit error (max |eps error| / |eps|, loss error / (|Im eps| + 0.03 |eps|)) as info, a warning above 2 % / 10 % or when the study band leaves the fit range. FDTD steps the fitted poles; FDFD, em_modes and slab-mode ports use their exact chi(omega).
- A {"model": "crystal", "crystal": <name>, "euler_deg": [phi, theta, psi], "plane": "sagittal"} entry (one per material; crystals aluminum_nitride, gallium_arsenide, lithium_niobate, quartz, zinc_oxide) is no pole: it is removed from the list and sets the rotated crystal data in model axes: c11, c12, c22, c66 (c16 / c26 when non-zero), rho, piezo_e11 .. piezo_e26 and the clamped eps_dc_xx / _yy / _xy; with optical data (not every crystal) also photoelastic_p11 / _p12 (+ photoelastic_p16 .. _p66 for elastic_waves when the cut is not isotropic in them; row 6 = xy, the eps_xy of em_fdfd_hz) and the clamped Pockels pockels_r11 .. _r62 when non-zero (precedence: library < crystal < explicit properties, also beside nk_fit). The optical index is not set. euler_deg in degrees, SAW convention: passive Rz(psi) Rx(theta) Rz(phi), rows X1' = propagation, X3' = surface normal (YZ = 0, 90, 90); sagittal = model (x, y, z) = (X1', X3', -X2'). The anti-plane couplings and the off-diagonal photoelastic / Pockels index change are dropped (validation reports the sagittal values as info and warns when not negligible; the acousto-optic and Pockels couplings warn). A 3D model needs "plane": "full" (2D: 'sagittal', the default; else validation errors): model (x, y, z) = (X1', X2', X3'), the surface normal along z; it sets all 21 c11 .. c66 (Voigt 1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz, 4 yz, 5 xz, 6 xy), the 18 piezo_e11 .. piezo_e36, eps_dc_xx / _yy / _zz / _yz / _xz / _xy and rho (no optical entries).

### Library materials

#### Library material `air`

Air at room temperature with vacuum optics; heat conduction only (no convection inside the gas: use a convection boundary feature).

- Properties: {"eps_r": 1, "k": 0.026, "rho": 1.225, "cp": 1005, "dndT": 0, "alpha": 0, "eps_dc": 1}; dispersion poles: none

#### Library material `aluminum`

Aluminium for EM, heat and electric currents (room temperature). The Drude pole is fitted to Rakic 1998 at 1.55 um (eps -244 - 49.6j), folding the 0.83 um interband band in: near-IR only, wrong in the visible / UV. For other bands use an nk_fit entry on its table (Rakic 1995 evaporated films, 207-1771 nm; a Lorentz pole takes the interband band).

- Properties: {"k": 237, "rho": 2700, "cp": 897, "dndT": 0, "alpha": 2.31e-05, "youngs_modulus": 7e+10, "poisson_ratio": 0.35, "sigma_dc": 3.8e+07}; dispersion poles: [{"model": "drude", "omega_p": 1.94e+16, "gamma": 2.46e+14, "eps_inf": 1}]

#### Library material `ce_yig`

Polycrystalline Ce:YIG (Ce1Y2Fe5O12) film, sputtered or pulsed-laser deposited on silicon or silicon nitride and saturated by a small in-plane field. The gyration is not set (the magnetisation direction is the model's): set g yourself, |g| ~ 0.009 from theta_F ~ -4500 deg/cm (g = theta_F lambda n / pi in magnitude; films ~ -2000 to -6000 deg/cm; g changes sign with the magnetisation), as gyration_z (em_fdfd_hz, magnetisation out of plane) or gyration_x / gyration_y (em_modes, transverse magnetisation). Loss ~40 dB/cm as sigma_e (films ~20-60 dB/cm). Typical literature values (Bi et al., Nat. Photonics 5, 758 (2011); Zhang et al., Optica 6, 473 (2019)), unverified; thermal data rough (YIG bulk).

- Properties: {"eps_r": 4.93, "sigma_e": 5.4, "k": 6, "rho": 5200, "cp": 570}; dispersion poles: none

#### Library material `gold`

Gold for EM, heat and electric currents (room temperature). The Drude pole fits Johnson & Christy 1972 over about 0.6-2 um (eps ~ -116 - 10.6j at 1.55 um; evaporated films have |Im eps| ~7, single crystals ~4); no interband absorption, so below ~550 nm |Im eps| is up to ~5x low. Resolve the ~25 nm field decay into the metal with several cells. Its table (Johnson & Christy 1972, 188-1937 nm) serves an nk_fit entry, whose Lorentz poles add the interband absorption.

- Properties: {"k": 317, "rho": 19300, "cp": 129, "dndT": 0, "alpha": 1.42e-05, "youngs_modulus": 7.9e+10, "poisson_ratio": 0.42, "sigma_dc": 4.1e+07}; dispersion poles: [{"model": "drude", "omega_p": 1.37e+16, "gamma": 1.02e+14, "eps_inf": 9.84}]

#### Library material `gst_225_amorphous`

Ge2Sb2Te5 phase-change alloy, amorphous (as deposited). Optical data at 1.55 um only, absorption as sigma_e (exact there, sigma_e = 2 n k omega eps0); non-dispersive. Thermal data: room-temperature conductivity of the phase (Lyeo et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 89, 151904 (2006)), density (Njoroge et al., J. Vac. Sci. Technol. A 20, 230 (2002)), a typical specific heat; no latent heat, no temperature dependence. For switching give its domains a phase_change_medium feature (its defaults are these optical constants plus the crystalline ones and the crystallisation kinetics). GST-225 data: n, k at 1.55 um as used for sputtered films in integrated photonics (e.g. Rios et al., Nat. Photonics 9, 725 (2015); film dependent by ~10 %); crystallisation onset ~150 C and activation energy 2.24 eV from Friedrich et al., J. Appl. Phys. 87, 4130 (2000); melting point 616 C from Yamada et al., J. Appl. Phys. 69, 2849 (1991). The Avrami exponent 2.5 is typical of nucleation-dominated GST (2-4 reported); the cap of 50 ns above 650 K is an illustrative calibration (100 s at the 150 C onset with 2.24 eV, tens of ns in laser / electrical SET pulses): fit both to the device.

- Properties: {"eps_r": 15.5216, "sigma_e": 3815.5, "k": 0.19, "rho": 5870, "cp": 210}; dispersion poles: none

#### Library material `gst_225_crystalline`

Ge2Sb2Te5 phase-change alloy, crystalline (face-centred cubic, the phase a short anneal or SET pulse gives). Optical data at 1.55 um only, absorption as sigma_e (exact there, sigma_e = 2 n k omega eps0); non-dispersive. Thermal data: room-temperature conductivity of the phase (Lyeo et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 89, 151904 (2006)), density (Njoroge et al., J. Vac. Sci. Technol. A 20, 230 (2002)), a typical specific heat; no latent heat, no temperature dependence. GST-225 data: n, k at 1.55 um as used for sputtered films in integrated photonics (e.g. Rios et al., Nat. Photonics 9, 725 (2015); film dependent by ~10 %); crystallisation onset ~150 C and activation energy 2.24 eV from Friedrich et al., J. Appl. Phys. 87, 4130 (2000); melting point 616 C from Yamada et al., J. Appl. Phys. 69, 2849 (1991). The Avrami exponent 2.5 is typical of nucleation-dominated GST (2-4 reported); the cap of 50 ns above 650 K is an illustrative calibration (100 s at the 150 C onset with 2.24 eV, tens of ns in laser / electrical SET pulses): fit both to the device.

- Properties: {"eps_r": 36.6432, "sigma_e": 109136, "k": 0.57, "rho": 6270, "cp": 210}; dispersion poles: none

#### Library material `heavy_water`

Heavy water (D2O) at 20 C, n = 1.3170, its absorption (extinction 4.47e-6, ~0.36 /cm) as sigma_e (an optical loss proxy valid near 1.55 um only, as water). dndT is estimated from water; alpha = 0 as water.

- Properties: {"eps_r": 1.735, "sigma_e": 0.127, "k": 0.589, "rho": 1105, "cp": 4219, "dndT": -7e-05, "alpha": 0, "eps_dc": 78.1, "viscosity": 0.00125}; dispersion poles: none

#### Library material `lithium_niobate_x_cut`

X-cut lithium niobate film at 1.55 um and room temperature in top view, optic axis (crystal z) along model x: eps_xx = n_e^2 is seen by E_x (em_fdtd_hz, em_fdfd_hz, em_modes), eps_r = n_o^2 by E_y and E_z. Lossless and non-dispersive. dndT_xx is dn_e/dT, dndT_yy = dndT_zz dn_o/dT (approximate); k and alpha are a-axis values, alpha_xx the c-axis expansion along x, both the free crystal (a film bonded to Si follows the substrate: set alpha and alpha_xx; an alpha override alone keeps the library alpha_xx). eps_dc_xx = eps_c and eps_dc = eps_a are clamped values (eps^S, as for RF / electro-optic electrodes). Pockels coefficients for an applied field along the optic axis (electrostatics_em_pockels with field_component 'x'): r_xx = r33 (n_e, E_x of the H_z types), r = r13 on r_yy and r_zz (n_o), both clamped (r^S, consistent with the clamped eps_dc; the unclamped r13 / r33 of a free crystal at low frequency are 10 / 32.2 pm/V). An applied field along y acts through r22 / r51 terms, not modelled (keep field_component 'x').

- Properties: {"eps_r": 4.889, "eps_xx": 4.571, "k": 4.6, "rho": 4640, "cp": 628, "dndT_xx": 3.3e-05, "dndT_yy": 3e-06, "dndT_zz": 3e-06, "alpha": 1.5e-05, "alpha_xx": 7.5e-06, "youngs_modulus": 1.7e+11, "poisson_ratio": 0.25, "eps_dc": 43, "eps_dc_xx": 28, "r": 8.6e-12, "r_xx": 3.08e-11}; dispersion poles: none

#### Library material `lithium_niobate_z_cut`

Z-cut lithium niobate film at 1.55 um and room temperature, optic axis z (out of plane): eps_zz = n_e^2 (n_e = 2.138) is seen by E_z (em_fdtd_ez, em_fdfd_ez), and the isotropic xy plane has eps_r = n_o^2 (n_o = 2.211), seen by E_x / E_y (em_fdtd_hz, em_fdfd_hz). An eps_r override therefore does not change E_z: set eps_zz. Lossless and non-dispersive. dndT_zz is dn_e/dT, dndT_xx = dndT_yy dn_o/dT (approximate). For an x-cut film (optic axis along x) use lithium_niobate_x_cut. k and alpha are a-axis values, alpha_zz the c-axis expansion (solid_mechanics only); alpha is the free crystal (a film bonded to Si follows the substrate: set alpha and alpha_zz to 2.6e-6; an alpha override alone keeps the library alpha_zz). eps_dc = eps_a, the in-plane z-cut permittivity, clamped (eps^S, valid above the acoustic resonances, as for RF / electro-optic electrodes; the unclamped DC eps_a of a free crystal is ~85: override eps_dc for that case). No Pockels coefficients: an in-plane applied field of a z-cut film acts through r22 with opposite signs on n_xx and n_yy, which the diagonal r_xx / r_yy / r_zz of electrostatics_em_pockels cannot express.

- Properties: {"eps_r": 4.889, "eps_zz": 4.571, "k": 4.6, "rho": 4640, "cp": 628, "dndT_xx": 3e-06, "dndT_yy": 3e-06, "dndT_zz": 3.3e-05, "alpha": 1.5e-05, "alpha_zz": 7.5e-06, "youngs_modulus": 1.7e+11, "poisson_ratio": 0.25, "eps_dc": 43}; dispersion poles: none

Fused silica (SiO2 glass), n = 1.444 lossless (about 1.46 in the visible). Elastic data of bulk fused silica (deposited oxide films are often softer, 60-70 GPa).

#### Library material `silicon`

Crystalline silicon, n = 3.476 lossless (real silicon absorbs below ~1.1 um: an nk_fit entry on its table gives dispersive, absorbing silicon; Green 2008, intrinsic, 300 K, 250-1450 nm, band-to-band only). Intrinsic: no sigma_dc (set it for doped silicon, e.g. 1e4 S/m). k: the common engineering value, below the ~148 W/(m K) of pure bulk silicon. Elastic data: an isotropic average (E 130 GPa along <100>, 169 GPa along <110>). Drift-diffusion data: 300 K, lightly doped mobilities.

Silver for EM, heat and electric currents (room temperature): one free-electron Drude pole whose eps_inf absorbs the interband background; at 1.55 um eps -123 - 2.9j (Johnson & Christy -129 - 3.3j: real part 5 %, loss 13 % low); visible / near-IR only, wrong below ~320 nm. ### Dispersion pole models (MaterialSpec.dispersion items)

#### Pole model `drude`

- `omega_p` [rad/s] (default 1.37e+16; >= 0) - Plasma frequency
  Plasma angular frequency of the Drude current dJ/dt + gamma J = eps0 omega_p^2 E (every E component of the polarisation), rad/s not Hz: gold ~1.37e16, aluminium ~2.24e16 (library aluminum: 1.94e16, a 1.55 um fit). em_fdtd_ez / _hz (leap-frog J, O((omega dt)^2)) are stable only where eps_inf * mu_r >= courant_factor^2 + mu_r (omega_p dt)^2 / 4 (square cells; the build checks every cell and names the largest stable courant_factor): eps_inf ~1 at 2.24e16 needs dx <= 5.4 nm at courant_factor 0.99 (<= 0.967 at 10 nm); otherwise the mesh only resolves the skin depth (tens of nm for noble metals in the visible). em_fdfd_ez / _hz use the exact chi(omega) at the solve wavelength.
- `gamma` [rad/s] (default 1.02e+14; >= 0) - Damping rate
  Collision rate of the Drude current; sets the metal loss. Use optical (visible / near-IR) values: gold ~1.0e14 (the DC value ~4e13 gives 2-3x too little near-IR loss), silver ~2.7e13.
- `eps_inf` [1] (default 1; > 0; nullable) - High-frequency permittivity
  Background permittivity of the Drude material, used for a permittivity array only when the material sets no permittivity property owning it (eps_r or a component such as eps_zz wins; only the first Drude pole counts); empty = 1. Gold ~9.8, silver ~3.7.

#### Pole model `lorentz`

- `delta_eps` [1] (default 1; >= 0) - Oscillator strength
  Oscillator strength of d2P/dt2 + gamma dP/dt + omega_0^2 P = eps0 delta_eps omega_0^2 E (every E component of the polarisation): static permittivity = background (eps_r or the component owning the array, as eps_inf) + delta_eps.
- `omega_0` [rad/s] (default 3e+15; >= 0) - Resonance frequency
  Resonance angular frequency (rad/s, not Hz); vacuum wavelength 2 pi C0 / omega_0 (3e15 = 628 nm).
- `gamma` [rad/s] (default 1e+14; >= 0) - Damping rate
  Full width of the Lorentz resonance in omega; smaller = sharper, less lossy.

#### Pole model `nk_fit`

- `n_lorentz` (int; default 2; [0, 6]) - Number of resonances
  Lorentz poles of the fit; a Drude pole is added when Re eps < 0 in the fit range (metals). Each pole adds 1-2 float32 arrays on its bounding box in the FDTD; poles below 1e-6 of |eps| are dropped. 2 suits a visible / near-IR octave.
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Fit from wavelength
  Shortest vacuum wavelength of the fit range, a plain number (no parameters: the fit runs once per material). Cover the study band: frequency_domain wavelengths, the FDFD / em_modes wavelength, or the FDTD source spectra and monitor ranges (validation warns outside). Must lie inside the library table.
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Fit to wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the fit range (> wavelength_start), a plain number; a narrower range fits better with fewer poles.

## Mesh

ModelSpec.meshes sets the cell sizes, one MeshSpec per mesh; each physics runs on one (PhysicsSpec.mesh, "" = the first). check.json reports the resulting grids (cells, dx range, dt, PML cells) before any GPU work.

- Per-physics meshes: every mesh spans the same domain; its padding (PML, mirror ghosts) and auto sizes come from the physics on it only. One mesh is required for all EM physics, physics joined by a coupling whose type does not transfer across meshes, a feature naming another physics, and every physics of a thermal_noise, optomechanics or nonlinear_frequency_domain study (validation errors). Cross-mesh couplings interpolate fields (linear between cell centres, edge-extended into padding) and move densities conservatively (window totals kept); a state-dependent material property reads fields of another mesh interpolated. A mesh no physics uses is a warning and is not built. Fields and feature results live on their physics' own mesh (FieldData / saved fields name it); a derived value is evaluated on the mesh of the first physics (model order) its expression names, the other fields interpolated onto it (validate lists them as info).
- Mesh kind triangles (2D Cartesian models): free triangles following curved boundaries, for the types that declare them (drift_diffusion, electric_currents, electrostatics, em_fdfd_bor, em_fdfd_conical, em_fdfd_ez, em_fdfd_hz, em_modes, heat, magnetic_fields_ac, magnetostatics, membrane, pressure_acoustics, solid_mechanics; some only in one study, validation names the limits). dx = maximum element size, max_ratio = growth rate (null: 1.3), refinements = maximum sizes in / along / at their objects, h_min (null: dx / 100), curvature_factor along circle and ellipse edges; auto: the wavelength rule with points_per_wavelength (null: 5), else the physics-controlled rule; the absorbing ring has pml_layers structured layers.
- Mesh kind tetrahedra (3D Cartesian models): for electric_currents, electrostatics, em_fdfd_3d, heat, magnetostatics_3d, pressure_acoustics, solid_mechanics_3d (em_fdfd_3d: its eigenfrequency study, Nedelec edge elements by the discretization setting). Sizes as triangles; see mesher and sweep_axis. The PML is a shell of pml_cells x dx outside every cpml face meshed like the window. Fields are sampled on a uniform lattice over the window (cut planes, profiles, volumes); derived values of fields reduce degree-4 quadrature points of the window (or selected) elements (not yet: interface selections, max / min over mirror images, fields of physics on other meshes).
- No physics boundary configuration -> no PML. EM CPML cells (pml_cells per cpml face; dx wide on a uniform grid, on a graded one growing by max_ratio from the window edge cell up to the base size) are added outside the domain, so the physical domain keeps its size and the grid grows.
- Several physics may define the boundary configuration when they agree (equal face types, CPML and Bloch settings), else a validation error. E_z and H_z pec / pmc walls are half a cell apart (E_z pec at the outermost cell centre, H_z pec on its inner face); symmetric / antisymmetric mirror planes coincide.
- A uniform mesh has ceil(size / dx) cells per axis, so the meshed window (Domain.physical_extent) can be one cell larger than size_x / size_y.
- nonuniform and auto fall back to a uniform grid when no refinement is finer than the base size, or at the finest target when an enabled feature requires a uniform mesh (laminar_flow.wall, laminar_flow.slip_wall, laminar_flow.inlet_velocity, laminar_flow.pressure, laminar_flow.periodic); the note in check.json mesh says why.
- Refinements apply in nonuniform and auto modes only: each refines the columns and rows spanned by its object plus margin to its dx; rectangle edges inside the domain become cell edges (no staircase), so a gap between two such edges narrower than dx (but >= 0.25 dx) gets cells of its width, which can set the time step; auto mode adds one refinement per material object by its refractive index. MeshSpec.axes adds a per-axis max_ratio, coordinate bands and custom edges or uniform / geometric / tanh segments (replacing that axis, PML padding as usual); outer_dx grows the cells beyond the refined core. The RefinementSpec and MeshAxisSpec fields are listed under spec.
- Time step with EM: dt = courant_factor * dx / (c * sqrt(2)) on a uniform mesh (3D: c * sqrt(3); graded: the limit of the finest cells); the merged courant factor is the smallest declared (default 0.99). check.json study shows dt_estimate and n_steps.
- Limits: 400,000,000 cells and 50,000 cells per axis, PML cells included; a larger mesh fails before any meshing.

### Mesh settings (MeshSpec fields)

- `kind` (default "tensor"; tensor | triangles | tetrahedra) - Mesh kind
  tensor: rectilinear cells (uniform or graded; every physics type); triangles: conforming finite elements (2D Cartesian models only); tetrahedra: finite elements (3D Cartesian models only; see mesher). Physics, features and solvers declare the kinds they run on (validation refuses the others). On triangles / gmsh tetrahedra dx is the maximum element size, max_ratio the element growth rate, refinements the maximum sizes in or along their objects (margin, dx_x / dx_y / dx_z, axes and outer_dx / outer_ratio unused; gmsh tetrahedra also RefinementSpec.where); builtin tetrahedra take the tensor rules (no size_points). h_min, curvature_factor and mesher: triangles / tetrahedra only; pml_layers and mirror_x / mirror_y: triangles only (a tetrahedron PML shell is meshed like the window); face_sizes: tetrahedra only.
- `mode` (default "uniform"; uniform | nonuniform | auto) - Mesh mode
  uniform: one cell size dx; nonuniform: base size dx plus the refinements, graded by max_ratio; auto with an EM physics on this mesh or wavelength_min set: cell size wavelength_min / (points_per_wavelength * n) per material, n = |sqrt(eps * mu_r)| at wavelength_min, largest over the permittivity arrays the mesh's physics use, eps including - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) and the dispersion poles (a metal is meshed by its skin depth: gold |n| ~11 at 1.55 um), plus the refinements; auto without either (physics-controlled): base size = the longest domain side / 50, every domain object the mesh's physics use refined to its smallest bounding-box side / 4, plus the refinements; with laminar_flow a uniform grid at the smallest such side / 16. auto raises for a permittivity, sigma_e, mu_r or pole value depending on x, y, z or a field (use nonuniform). Graded meshes are rectilinear: a refinement refines every column and row its object plus margin spans, across the whole domain (per-axis sizes dx_x / dx_y / dx_z limit that); grading ramps lie outside the refined bands. 3D: z is graded the same way (refinements over their object's z extent plus margin; set prism z0 / z1 faces are exact cell edges; z cells away from refinements take the base size).
- `dx` [m] (default 2e-08; > 0; nullable) - Cell size
  Cell size of a uniform mesh, or the base (coarsest) size of a nonuniform one (required in both); typically lambda / (20 n) for EM, n the largest refractive index. auto: the smallest cell size, every auto size scaled by one factor so the finest equals dx (replacing points_per_wavelength; the material size ratios stay; lattice Boltzmann: its uniform size); null = the auto rule alone. Explicit refinements are not scaled.
- `max_ratio` [1] (> 1; nullable; visible when mode in (nonuniform, auto) or kind in (triangles, tetrahedra)) - Maximum growth ratio
  Largest size ratio of neighbouring cells, or the element growth rate on triangles / tetrahedra; typically 1.1-1.3 (smaller: less numerical reflection, more cells). null = 1.15 (tensor), 1.3 (triangles).
- `wavelength_min` [m] (> 0; nullable; visible when mode in (nonuniform, auto)) - Shortest wavelength
  Shortest vacuum wavelength to resolve in auto mode (see mode). null = the shortest of the physics on this mesh: FDFD and em_modes the shortest solved one, FDTD the shortest significant source wavelength (gaussian lambda / (1 + bandwidth), ricker lambda / 2); a model error when an EM physics gives none. A sweep changing that wavelength re-meshes per value: set it to keep one mesh, to mesh finer, or for a wavelength the physics do not know (e.g. one generated inside the model).
- `points_per_wavelength` [1] (>= 1; nullable; visible when mode in (nonuniform, auto)) - Points per wavelength
  Cells (triangles: elements) per wavelength in each material in auto mode; typically 15-30 on tensor meshes (too few: phase errors growing with distance). null = 20 (tensor), 5 (triangles, quadratic elements). Unused while dx is set.
- `outer_dx` [m] (> 0; nullable; visible when mode in (nonuniform, auto)) - Outer cell size
  Outer grading (null = off): outside the refined core of each axis (its refinements and bands with margins) cells grow from the base size by outer_ratio per cell up to outer_dx, so a domain ~1e3 x the structure costs a few dozen cells per side (quasi-static far fields: steady heat, electrostatics, low-frequency thermal noise). An axis without refinements, or outer_dx <= the base size, is not outer graded; the PML ramp is unaffected. Jacobi-PCG iterations grow with the grading: sparse direct solvers suit it better.
- `outer_ratio` [1] (> 1; nullable; visible when mode in (nonuniform, auto)) - Outer growth ratio
  Cell growth per cell of the outer grading (> 1; null = the axis' max_ratio); 1.2-1.5 is typical for quasi-static fields.
- `h_min` [m] (> 0; nullable; visible when kind in (triangles, tetrahedra)) - Minimum element size
  Triangles / tetrahedra: smallest element size (> 0, <= the maximum size); null = the maximum size (dx, or the auto size) / 100.
- `curvature_factor` [1] (default 0.3; > 0; visible when kind in (triangles, tetrahedra)) - Curvature factor
  Triangles / tetrahedra: element size along circle / ellipse / sphere / cylinder boundaries <= curvature_factor x the local radius of curvature (0.3 = the industry-standard default).
- `mesher` (default "builtin"; builtin | gmsh; visible when kind in (triangles, tetrahedra)) - Mesher
  Triangles: 'builtin' = conforming Delaunay refinement (deterministic); tetrahedra: 'builtin' = the bricks of a rectilinear grid split into 6 tetrahedra each (no slivers at any aspect ratio; periodic sides match), equal cells <= dx in uniform mode, else graded like a nonuniform tensor mesh at base dx (refinements with margin and per-axis sizes, axes, outer grading, face_sizes as bands across their face plane), every flat face of a domain object snapped as an element face, the PML shell in cells of dx; curved objects are a staircase; size_points refused, h_min and a physics' edge sizes unused (a warning). Example, a slender clamped string: refinement {string, dx 0.5 um, dx_y = dx_z = 50 nm} plus face_sizes x_lo / x_hi 50 nm. 'gmsh' = the external gmsh program (OPEN_SOL_GMSH or the PATH; a validation error when not found): tetrahedra conform to boxes, spheres, z cylinders and z-prism rectangles / circles (composite inputs included), other objects are tagged per element.
- `sweep_axis` (default "none"; none | z; visible when kind in (tetrahedra)) - Swept layers
  Tetrahedra only. 'none' = the 3D mesher of mesher. 'z' = swept prism layers: the xy footprint meshed by mesher's triangle mesher (dx, refinement dx over the objects' footprints, h_min, curvature_factor, max_ratio), extruded through z layers graded as builtin tetrahedra along z (refinement dx_z else dx with margins, a z MeshAxisSpec, face_sizes on z_lo / z_hi, outer_dx; every set z face of a domain object a layer plane), each prism split into 3 tetrahedra (about 3 x triangles x layers elements). Conforming: boxes, z cylinders, untapered z prisms and x / y rectangles; spheres, other x / y prisms and tapers are tagged per element (a warning). The x / y PML ring has pml_layers layers. Refused: size_points, x / y axes options, dx_x / dx_y unlike dx, face sizes on x / y faces, where edges / surface.
- `pml_layers` [1] (int; default 8; >= 1; visible when kind in (triangles) or sweep_axis in (z)) - Absorbing layers
  Triangles (and swept tetrahedra, sweep_axis z: the x / y sides): structured element layers across each PML ring side (thickness = the PML cells of the physics x the maximum element size, the tensor CPML stretch profile).
- `mirror_x` (bool; default false; visible when kind in (triangles)) - Mirror-symmetric in x
  Triangles: mesh the half window x <= size_x / 2 (conforming to the geometry and its mirror image) and mirror it about x = size_x / 2, so the mesh and every operator are exactly mirror symmetric (an even drive gives no odd response beyond rounding). Needs equal absorbing rings on x_lo and x_hi; a warning names material objects that are not mirror symmetric (sources and probes are not checked).
- `mirror_y` (bool; default false; visible when kind in (triangles)) - Mirror-symmetric in y
  Triangles: as mirror_x about y = size_y / 2 (equal absorbing rings on y_lo and y_hi); with mirror_x the quarter window is meshed and mirrored twice.

## Solvers

A physics hands its numerical jobs (roles) to solvers: ModelSpec.solvers holds solver nodes (SolverSpec: name, type, settings), PhysicsSpec.solvers {role: node name} assigns them; a role left out is Automatic (the role's default type at its default settings, precision per SolverDefaultsSpec.precision). check.json solvers shows what every role resolves to, summary.json solvers what ran (type, node, backend, precision, settings, counters): Automatic depends on the machine, so that record is the reference for comparing runs.

- Roles: stepper (Time stepping); linear (Linear systems); shifted (Frequency sweeps); eigen (Eigenvalues). A role is used only in the studies listed for it (else all); an assignment in another study is a warning and ignored.
- Validation: an unknown node or role is an error at the physics; a node of the wrong role, operator class, backend, grid kind or precision (solver_misfit) is an error naming the fitting choices; an unused node is a warning; node settings are checked like physics settings.
- Feature precisions: a feature listing "stepper precisions ... only" (e.g. resonance_monitor, the em_fdtd_3d plane wave and mode ports) needs the stepper role of its physics to resolve to one of them (else a validation error at the enabled feature, e.g. with half_storage).
- Solver knobs are never physics settings: e.g. the CG precision / tolerance / max_iterations of heat, electric_currents, electrostatics, magnetostatics, solid_mechanics and solid_mechanics_3d are the settings of a pcg node assigned as their linear solver ({"name": "cg", "type": "pcg", "settings": {"tolerance": 1e-12}} in solvers, {"linear": "cg"} in the physics solvers).
- One node may serve several physics; the build creates one runtime per (physics, role).
- Opt-in: line_block fills the linear role of em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz only (shifted role: heat thermal noise, em_fdfd_bor, em_modes); as the linear solver of any other physics it is a misfit.
- sparse_direct back_end auto: a role's auto_back_end_by_grid (pressure_acoustics on triangles / tetrahedra, membrane on triangles: cudss_mixed) applies on the gpu backend when nvmath-python is installed, for Automatic and for nodes leaving back_end auto; else auto is host SuperLU (scipy_splu).
- sparse_direct back_end / arpack_shift_invert factorization mumps, mumps_mixed, pardiso, pardiso_mixed: the optional multicore host solvers MUMPS (python-mumps) and Intel MKL PARDISO (pydiso, x86-64 only) on both backends, opt-in (only roles whose line under Roles by physics type lists them, else a misfit; never chosen by auto; without the package a validation error). The host SuperLU size rules apply; each factor checks its own memory estimate against 80 % of the available RAM, a refusal raises (no fallback).

### Solver types

#### Solver type `arpack_shift_invert` - Shift-invert eigensolver

Eigenpairs nearest a target: a factorisation of the operator shifted to the target (see factorization) and ARPACK (scipy eigs) in double precision, the ARPACK basis on the host. Used by em_modes (modes near the effective-index guess) and the frequency-domain EM types in an eigenfrequency study (resonances nearest the wavelength setting). solid_mechanics: symmetric shift-invert Lanczos (scipy eigsh) on a real factor of K - sigma M; solid_mechanics_3d on bricks: Lanczos on K^-1 M at 0 without a factor, each K^-1 one PCG solve of its 'linear' solver.

- Roles eigen; operators spd, complex_symmetric, general; backends gpu, cpu; precisions double; grids tensor, triangles, tetrahedra

Params (SolverSpec.settings):
- `tolerance` [1] (default 0; >= 0) - Eigenvalue tolerance
  Relative accuracy ARPACK asks of each eigenvalue (scipy eigs tol); 0 = machine precision (default). solid_mechanics_3d (inexact PCG inner solves) raises it to at least 1e3 x its linear CG tolerance.
- `subspace_size` (int; default 0; >= 0) - Subspace size
  Arnoldi vectors ARPACK keeps (scipy eigs ncv), raised to the eigenpairs wanted + 2; 0 = scipy's default max(2 k + 1, 20) for k wanted eigenpairs. A larger basis converges in fewer operator applications but holds that many complex128 vectors of the system size on the host.
- `factorization` (default "auto"; auto | superlu | cudss | cudss_mixed | mumps | mumps_mixed | pardiso | pardiso_mixed) - Shift-invert factorisation
  LU of the shifted operator (the choices a role offers: its line under Roles by physics type). auto: superlu, except on the gpu backend with nvmath-python for the vibration modes of solid_mechanics on triangles (cudss) and solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra (cudss_mixed), where a cuDSS refusal (zero pivot, missed accuracy, too little GPU memory) switches that solver to superlu for the rest of the run with a warning (up to 2e6 unknowns; the run summary records the resolved value and eigen_auto_fallbacks). superlu: scipy SuperLU on the host (both backends). cudss (GPU backend, nvmath-python with cuDSS): a double-precision device factor (LDL^T where the scaled operator is complex symmetric: em_fdfd_3d, 2D em_fdfd without Bloch phase, solid_mechanics) outside the cupy pool (refused when cuDSS's own estimate exceeds 80 % of the free device memory; no host SuperLU size rule); ARPACK stays on the host, moving one vector per operator application; a probe solve turns on cuDSS refinement when its residual misses 1e-10. cudss_mixed: the equilibrated operator factorised in single precision (~10x faster factorisation on GPUs with slow double arithmetic, half the GPU memory, ~2x cheaper solves); the optics resonance and em_modes solves add one float64 residual step per solve (~3e-8), stop ARPACK at ~1e-6 and re-evaluate each eigenvalue by its float64 Rayleigh quotient (~1e-14; with a Bloch phase full float64 refinement per solve instead); the solid_mechanics pencils refine every solve to 1e-12. mumps / pardiso: the host MUMPS / Intel MKL PARDISO factor (rules: solvers notes) with the cudss equilibration, LDL^T where the scaled operator is (complex) symmetric, else LU; inertia counts of target / band searches from its LDL^T pivots (a counting SuperLU when pivots were perturbed or the pencil is Hermitian). mumps_mixed / pardiso_mixed (only where cudss_mixed is offered): a single-precision host factor, the solves refined and polished as for cudss_mixed; a first factor whose probe misses is refactorised in double for the rest of the run. Ignored by solid_mechanics_3d on brick meshes (no factor).

#### Solver type `banded` - Banded direct solver (1D)

Direct solve of 1D models (domain size_y null: a line of cells): the operator of a window one cell across is banded (tridiagonal for heat, electric_currents, electrostatics), so one host banded Cholesky (scipy.linalg cholesky_banded, double precision) per assembly gives exact solves at a cost linear in the cells; on the GPU backend the operator, rhs and solution move to the host per factorisation / solve. The Automatic linear solver of these types in a 1D model on both backends; refused in 2D / 3D models (a node there is an error).

- Roles linear; operators spd; backends gpu, cpu; precisions double; grids line

Params (SolverSpec.settings): none

#### Solver type `block_eigen` - Block eigensolver

The lowest eigenpairs of a symmetric pencil without a factorisation: preconditioned block iterations (LOBPCG with soft locking) on the physics' own matrix-free products and preconditioner, every vector of the search block in device memory (9 vectors of the system size per block row, nothing else of that size), dense block products on cuBLAS / BLAS; mixed precision (a float32 phase finished in float64) or double. Opt-in where a physics offers it: solid_mechanics_3d on brick (tensor) meshes, eigenfrequency study (the lowest modes; arpack_shift_invert's Lanczos there runs one inner PCG solve per step). Both backends.

- Roles eigen; operators spd; backends gpu, cpu; precisions mixed, double; grids tensor

Params (SolverSpec.settings):
- `tolerance` [1] (default 1e-08; >= 0) - Residual tolerance
  Relative residual ||K x - lambda M x|| / (|lambda| ||M x||) every wanted eigenpair must reach; 0 = the default 1e-08. The eigenvalue error is about the square of it (a symmetric pencil), so 1e-8 gives frequencies to ~1e-15 unless two modes nearly coincide. Below ~1e-12 the float64 rounding floor of stiff 3D operators stops the iteration (a warning).
- `guard_vectors` (int; default 0; >= 0) - Guard vectors
  Extra block rows searched beside the wanted eigenpairs (they speed up the convergence of the highest wanted ones); 0 = max(2, 0.25 x wanted). The solve holds 9 vectors of the system size per block row.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 0; >= 0) - Max iterations
  Block iterations before the solve stops unconverged (a warning); 0 = the physics' default (the 'linear' CG iteration limit of solid_mechanics_3d), else 1000.
- `precision` (default "mixed"; mixed | double) - Solver precision
  mixed: float32 blocks, products and preconditioner until the residual reaches 0.0001 or stalls at the float32 rounding floor, then float64 from there to the tolerance (consumer GPUs run float32 products and the dense block products 32-64x faster than float64). double: float64 throughout. Both end at the same float64 accuracy.
- `preconditioner` (default "multigrid"; multigrid | jacobi) - Preconditioner
  multigrid: one V-cycle of the physics' multigrid per vector and iteration (solid_mechanics_3d: the geometric brick multigrid of its 'linear' solver, built for the eigen solve when that solver runs block Jacobi; a hierarchy that cannot be built falls back to block Jacobi with a warning): iterations nearly independent of the mesh size. jacobi: the 3 x 3 node block Jacobi of the linear solver (no hierarchy memory; iterations grow with the longest mesh axis).

#### Solver type `explicit_kernels` - Explicit time stepping

The fused GPU kernels of an explicit time-stepping engine (em_fdtd_ez / em_fdtd_hz / em_fdtd_3d, elastic_waves, laminar_flow); precision: see the setting. On the CPU backend the same steps run as numpy twins of the kernels, numba-compiled when numba is installed (OPEN_SOL_CPU_KERNELS=numpy keeps numpy); single or double there, several times slower than a GPU: small 2D models and tests.

- Roles stepper; operators spd, complex_symmetric, general; backends gpu, cpu; precisions single, double, half_storage; grids tensor

Params (SolverSpec.settings):
- `precision` (default "single"; single | double | half_storage) - Solver precision
  single: float32 fields and arithmetic (every engine). double (em_fdtd_ez / em_fdtd_hz): float64 fields, coefficients and arithmetic, about 2x the field memory and time, for long or high-Q ring-downs where float32 coefficient rounding (~1e-7 of the mode frequency) drifts the phase; materials, coupling slots, absorbed power, probe traces and DFT spectra stay float32 / complex64; refused with nonlinear_medium and gain_medium. half_storage (em_fdtd_3d, elastic_waves, transient laminar_flow): fp16 storage, float32 arithmetic, about half the field memory and up to ~1.5-2x faster; results carry a ~1e-3 relative noise floor (-60 dB): flux spectra with deep nulls, harmonic inversion / Q values and steady states are refused or unusable (validation says so), decaying tails below ~1e-7 of the peak flush to zero.

#### Solver type `line_block` - Line-block direct solver

Batched block-tridiagonal direct solver for families K + sum s_i M_i + sum t_j N_j of structured 2D systems: unknowns ordered line by line, per shift a block Thomas factorisation (cost lines x b^3, b = unknowns across a line), many shifts per batch (at most 8 operators and 60 % of the free memory), refined against the double-precision operator; both backends. Role shifted: heat thermal noise spectra, em_fdfd_bor (driven systems and shift-invert operators, azimuthal orders as shifts) and em_modes (the mode shift-invert operators, group_index and frequency_domain wavelengths in batches). Role linear (em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz only; Automatic stays sparse_direct): one block factor per wavelength and material state, reused for every source and as the eigenfrequency shift-invert factor; at most one periodic axis (inside the blocks); adjoint solves of the optimization study and rejected solves use the physics' host SuperLU. On the CPU backend each solve is 7-15 x slower than the Automatic host SuperLU: there it only serves comparisons with GPU runs.

- Roles shifted, linear; operators spd, complex_symmetric, general; backends gpu, cpu; precisions mixed, double; grids tensor

Params (SolverSpec.settings):
- `precision` (default "mixed"; mixed | double) - Solver precision
  mixed: block factorisation and sweeps in complex64, refined against the complex128 operator to a relative residual of 1e-09; a shift still above 1e-06 is re-solved by the physics' reference solver (counted as rejected_shifts, or rejected_factor_solves for kept factors: em_fdfd_* linear, em_fdfd_bor, em_modes). double: complex128 throughout (slower on consumer GPUs, rarely rejected; indefinite Helmholtz systems near a resonance may need it).

#### Solver type `pcg` - Iterative linear solver

Preconditioned conjugate gradients for symmetric positive definite systems (the linear role of heat, electric_currents, electrostatics, magnetostatics, solid_mechanics, solid_mechanics_3d), warm-started from the previous solve, on both backends. Automatic is pcg with the defaults below except the preconditioner (see it); on triangle and tetrahedron meshes Automatic is sparse_direct and pcg opt-in (solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra: sparse_direct only). To change a setting add a pcg node and assign it (physics solvers {"linear": "<node name>"}).

- Roles linear; operators spd; backends gpu, cpu; precisions double, single, mixed; grids tensor, triangles, tetrahedra

Params (SolverSpec.settings):
- `precision` (default "double"; double | single | mixed) - Solver precision
  Arithmetic of the CG vectors and operator (the physics stores its fields as float32 either way). single saves solver memory but CG stalls near a relative residual of 1e-06: use tolerance >= 1e-06 with it (validation warns). mixed (heat, electric_currents, electrostatics, magnetostatics with Jacobi; solid_mechanics_3d): CG in float32 (~1.5-2x faster per iteration, +~30 B per cell), the float64 residual replacing its own each time it fell by 0.1, so any tolerance double reaches is reached in about the iterations of double; solid_mechanics_3d runs a float32 matrix-free product, several times cheaper on GPUs with slow float64 arithmetic. Not for 2D solid_mechanics. A node that sets no precision takes solver_defaults.precision, else the physics' Automatic one (solid_mechanics_3d on the gpu backend with a tensor mesh: mixed), else double.
- `tolerance` [1] (default 1e-08; > 0) - Solver tolerance
  CG stopping criterion, a relative residual norm: in a steady solve relative to ||b|| (the sources and boundary drive); in an implicit time step relative to the initial residual of the step (its change from the previous step, never below ~16 machine epsilons of ||b||). 1e-8 suits double; single cannot get below ~1e-06. Outputs that follow the solution linearly (terminal currents and charges, q_joule, reactions, stresses, B and H) carry a relative error of the order of the condition number times the tolerance: use 1e-12 for exact-identity checks; an iron part (mu_dc >> 1) raises the magnetostatics condition number by about its permeability, so use 1e-10 or below for flux-concentration ratios.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 0; >= 0) - Solver iteration limit
  CG iteration limit per solve; 0 = auto: max(5000, 20 x the cells along the longest window axis), twice the ~10 x those cells Jacobi-PCG needs from a cold start (fewer when warm-started from the previous solve); solid_mechanics doubles the auto value (block-Jacobi PCG on the elastic operator needs about twice the iterations, more for poisson_ratio near 0.5). A solve that hits the limit keeps its unconverged (biased) result, and the first one per run is logged as a warning; validation warns when an explicit value is below 10 x the longest window axis (not with a heat out_of_plane_convection on every cell, which converges much faster).
- `preconditioner` (default "jacobi"; jacobi | multigrid) - Preconditioner
  CG preconditioner. jacobi: the inverse diagonal (solid_mechanics: its 2x2 / 3x3 block diagonal), cheap per iteration, but iterations grow with the cells along the longest window axis (~10 per cell), grading, aspect ratio and coefficient contrast (outer grading, 1e3x conductivity ratios: up to ~1e5). multigrid (heat, electric_currents, electrostatics, magnetostatics; precision single or double): smoothed-aggregation algebraic multigrid V(1,1) (strength threshold 0.1, graded cells semi-coarsen), typically 10-40 iterations at any mesh size, each ~4-6 Jacobi iterations, ~150 B per cell (double) on the device; every assembly rebuilds the coarse operators. Best for steady solves on large or strongly graded meshes; for implicit time steps the warm-started Jacobi is often cheaper. Automatic of those four types on the gpu backend is pcg with multigrid (jacobi at mixed precision); a pcg node without this setting uses jacobi. solid_mechanics_3d on a tensor mesh (any precision; not Automatic): geometric multigrid V(2,2) on the brick operator, each iteration ~6-8 block-Jacobi iterations, the hierarchy ~1/6 of the system arrays; a solve that stalls or needs far more iterations than expected (thin solids in void, strong stiffness contrast or grading) switches that solid to block Jacobi with a warning.

#### Solver type `sparse_direct` - Sparse direct solver

Sparse direct factorisation in double precision (back_end). Role linear: the Helmholtz systems of em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz / em_fdfd_nonlinear (one factorisation per wavelength and material state, reused for every source; after a small operator change GMRES on the earlier factor first), every Newton step of drift_diffusion, the eddy-current system of magnetic_fields_ac (host only), the linear role of heat, electric_currents, electrostatics and magnetostatics (their Automatic on the CPU backend: one real host SuperLU per assembly) and the Automatic linear solver of the diffusion and elastic types on triangle meshes and of heat on tetrahedra. Role shifted: one host SuperLU per shift K + s M, the reference of the thermal noise spectra. Iterative solvers are not offered for the indefinite Helmholtz matrix (they stall).

- Roles linear, shifted; operators spd, complex_symmetric, general; backends gpu, cpu; precisions double; grids tensor, triangles, tetrahedra

Params (SolverSpec.settings):
- `back_end` (default "auto"; auto | scipy_splu | cusolver_qr | cudss | cudss_mixed | mumps | mumps_mixed | pardiso | pardiso_mixed) - Back end
  Where the sparse factorisation runs (role linear; the back ends a role offers: its line under Roles by physics type). scipy_splu: host SuperLU (scipy), one factorisation reused for every right-hand side, practical up to ~1e6 unknowns (warning above, refused above 2e6). cusolver_qr: GPU sparse QR (cupy), one factorisation per solve, small models only (~1e5 unknowns on a square grid): its workspace (~64 B * nx * ny * the cells of the narrower axis, doubled by a periodic wrap of the other axis) lies outside the GPU budget: validation warns above 512 MiB and refuses above 2 GiB, the solver refuses more than half the free GPU memory. auto: scipy_splu (cusolver_qr without scipy; always scipy_splu on the cpu backend); on the gpu backend with nvmath-python cudss_mixed for the frequency-response solves of pressure_acoustics (triangles, tetrahedra) and membrane (triangles) and for solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra, cudss for em_fdfd_ez / _hz (tensor, triangles), em_fdfd_bor, em_fdfd_conical and drift_diffusion (tensor; drift_diffusion also triangles), solid_mechanics on triangles and heat / electric_currents / electrostatics / magnetostatics on triangles and tetrahedra (the run summary records the resolved back end); a cuDSS refusal (zero pivot, missed accuracy, too little GPU memory) then switches that solver to scipy_splu for the rest of the run with a warning (up to 2e6 unknowns). The shifted role (thermal noise) and magnetic_fields_ac always factorise on the host. cudss (GPU backend, nvmath-python with cuDSS): a double-precision factor (Cholesky for SPD systems, LDL^T if that fails) kept in GPU memory outside the cupy pool (refused when cuDSS's own estimate exceeds 80 % of the free device memory; no host size rules); a re-assembly with the same sparsity refactorises without replanning; a probe solve checks each factor (cuDSS refinement when its residual misses 1e-10). em_fdfd_nonlinear: opt-in only, one factor per channel (picard Kerr / free-carrier channels refactorise every sweep, no recycled GMRES). cudss_mixed: the equilibrated operator factorised in single precision (~10x faster factorisation on GPUs with slow double arithmetic, half the factor memory), every solve refined in float64 to 1e-12 (~3-4 single solves); refused at the first factor when single precision cannot reach that (very high contrast: use cudss). mumps / mumps_mixed / pardiso / pardiso_mixed: the host MUMPS / Intel MKL PARDISO factor (rules: solvers notes; mumps / pardiso also for magnetic_fields_ac), after the cuDSS equilibration: LDL^T for (complex) symmetric operators (PARDISO: Cholesky for SPD, LDL^T if that fails), else LU; adjoint solves, GMRES on an earlier factor and inertia counts as scipy_splu; a probe solve checks each factor (float64 GMRES refinement when its residual misses 1e-10). mumps_mixed / pardiso_mixed: the equilibrated operator factorised in single precision (float32 / complex64, about half the factor memory), every solve refined by float64 GMRES to 1e-12 as cudss_mixed; a first factor whose probe misses is refactorised in double for the rest of the run. Threads: OMP_NUM_THREADS (MUMPS) / MKL_NUM_THREADS (PARDISO); set them to share the cores with numba or a threaded BLAS. Install: MUMPS: conda install -c conda-forge python-mumps (pip install python-mumps builds against an installed MUMPS); PARDISO: pip install pydiso (Linux / Windows x86-64 wheels, pulls MKL) or conda install -c conda-forge pydiso; x86-64 only.

## Shared help texts

Long texts (param help, feature and type descriptions) occurring more than once in the physics, coupling and study sections below; key = the first owner: <physics>.<param>, <physics>.<feature>, <physics>.<feature>.<param>, <coupling or study type>.<param> or a type name.

#### `elastic_waves.rho`

Mass density (inertia; also read by pressure_acoustics). Unset = 0: elastic_waves treats a cell without density and stiffness as vacuum (a traction-free surface; a face between two such cells does not move). Typical: water 998, silica 2200, silicon 2329, aluminium 2700, gold 19300.

#### `elastic_waves.sound_speed`

Longitudinal (P) wave speed: c11 = c22 = rho sound_speed^2 unless c_ij are set; a fluid sets only this. Set (> 0), the speeds replace the youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio of the cell (library solids carry those). pressure_acoustics: the fluid sound speed c. Typical: air 343, water 1480, silica 5960, aluminium 6420, silicon ~8430 (isotropic average).

#### `elastic_waves.youngs_modulus`

Young's modulus E of an isotropic solid. solid_mechanics: unset = 0 = void (not solved, no stress: air, a liquid, a cladding left out); every solid region needs a support. elastic_waves: c11 = c22 = lambda + 2 mu, c12 = lambda, c66 = mu of cells without a sound_speed (sound_speed / shear_speed win; set c_ij win over both). Typical: silica 7.3e10, silicon 1.65e11 (isotropic average; 1.3e11 along <100>, 1.69e11 along <110>), gold 7.9e10, aluminium 7.0e10. A state field (e.g. heat_T) makes a stationary study iterate.

#### `elastic_waves.poisson_ratio`

Poisson ratio nu of an isotropic solid (unset = 0), used with youngs_modulus. Plane strain stiffens the in-plane response by 1 / (1 - nu^2), sigma_zz = nu (sigma_xx + sigma_yy) - E alpha_zz dT. solid_mechanics: low-order elements lock toward 0.5, too stiff above ~0.45 (validation warns). Typical: silica 0.17, silicon 0.22, gold 0.42, aluminium 0.35.

#### `elastic_waves.photoelastic_p11`

Strain-optic coefficient p11 of an isotropic or cubic material (axes along x, y, z): Delta(1/n^2)_ii = p11 e_ii + p12 (e_jj + e_kk) of the elastic strain. Read only by solid_em_strain_optic, acoustics_em_acousto_optic (into em_fdfd_hz: shear term (p11 - p12) / 2) and optomechanical_coupling (shear: photoelastic_p44). Unset = 0. Typical: silica 0.121, silicon -0.094. With the elastic_waves tensor entries (photoelastic_p16 .. _p66; a crystal entry also sets p11 / p12) it is p_11 of the model-axis row xx; solid_em_strain_optic keeps the isotropic reading, optomechanical_coupling reads a crystal entry's full rotated p (unless the material sets a photoelastic_* itself).

#### `elastic_waves.photoelastic_p12`

Strain-optic coefficient p12 (strain across the field; see photoelastic_p11). Unset = 0. Typical: silica 0.270, silicon 0.017. With the elastic_waves tensor entries: p_12 of row xx and the fallback of the unset p21 / p31 / p32.

#### `elastic_waves.force_source.waveform`

ricker: Ricker wavelet, spectrum peaking at frequency, value 1 at t0 = 4 / frequency (broadband: 3 % of the spectral peak at 2.5 f, 1 % at 2.76 f); gaussian: sin carrier under a gaussian envelope of relative bandwidth, t0 = 4.5 / (pi bandwidth frequency); cw: sin(2 pi f t) ramped in by 1 - exp(-t / (3 T)), T = 1 / f, steady after ~15 periods.

#### `elastic_waves.force_source.frequency`

Centre (gaussian, cw) or peak (ricker) frequency. Mesh: >= 10 (better 20) cells per shortest wavelength = slowest speed (shear in solids) / highest significant frequency (gaussian f (1 + bandwidth), ricker 2.5 f); validation warns.

#### `electric_currents.azimuthal_order`

Azimuthal order m of an axisymmetric (r, z) solve. 0: rotationally symmetric. m >= 1: the order-m part u_m(r, z) cos(m phi) of a load (m = 1: a uniform transverse field, V = -E0 r cos(phi)); the operator gains c_xx m^2 / r_c^2 per cell volume, so u_m vanishes on the axis. Every field, source density, boundary, held and initial value is then a cos(m phi) amplitude (heat: of T - T0), field components the r / z amplitudes, and ring totals carry pi instead of 2 pi: held currents / charges, scalar outputs and field integrals are cos(m phi) moments, a point source P is the order-m part of P at phi = 0, a dissipation density (q_joule) is twice its phi mean (its integral = the total power). Needs geometry 'axisymmetric' on a Cartesian domain; every physics with this setting shares one m; couplings of an order-m physics warn (products such as Joule heating are no single order). solid_mechanics: U_r, U_z ~ cos(m phi), U_phi ~ sin(m phi).

#### `electric_currents.discretization`

Lagrange order on a triangles / tetrahedra mesh (ignored on tensor meshes): quadratic (P2) or linear (P1). Quadratic triangles with an edge on a circle / ellipse are curved (isoparametric), linear ones straight; tetrahedra are always straight.

#### `electric_currents.potential_probe`

Potential (V) of the cell containing the point. time_dependent: one sample per re-solve plus one at the end (V holds in between; electrostatics with a waveform: one per step at its end time); stationary and the frequency-domain background stage: one per fixed-point iteration, all at t = 0.

#### `electrostatics.voltage.waveform`

V(t) = voltage s(t) (the elastic_waves source waveforms): none = constant; ricker = Ricker wavelet peaking at frequency, value 1 at t0 = 4 / frequency; gaussian = sin carrier under a gaussian envelope of relative bandwidth (t0 = 4.5 / (pi bandwidth frequency)); cw = sin(2 pi f t) ramped in by 1 - exp(-t / (3 T)), T = 1 / f, steady after ~15 periods. Exact superposition of one static solve per distinct waveform plus the constant part (redone after every operator change), written at the end time of each step, charges included. time_dependent only (stationary: s(0) ~ 0, validation warns); not with an electrolyte (validation error). A 2D interdigital transducer is two terminals with the same waveform and opposite voltages.

#### `em_eme.pml_cells`

Added outside every cpml face (the domain keeps its size); dx wide on a uniform grid, on a graded one growing by max_ratio per cell from the edge cell to the base size. 10-20 typical; thicker absorbs grazing and long waves better.

#### `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`

Peak CPML conductivity / the vacuum optimum (m + 1) / (150 pi d) S/m (m = pml_order, d = PML cell width); 0.5-2 when tuning. Where a cladding of index n crosses the PML the optimum is ~1/n (silica ~0.7, silicon ~0.3).

#### `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`

Peak shift alpha in the stretch kappa + sigma / (alpha + j omega eps0), largest at the inner edge; 0 = plain CPML. Damps evanescent and low-frequency waves only where alpha ~ omega eps0 (~1.1e4 S/m at 1550 nm, ~0.06 S/m at 1 GHz).

#### `em_eme.eps_xx`

x relative permittivity, the only one E_x sees without an off-diagonal eps_xy (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells); overrides eps_r for E_x. E.g. x-cut lithium niobate at 1.55 um (optic axis x): eps_xx 4.571 = n_e^2, eps_r 4.889 = n_o^2.

#### `em_eme.eps_yy`

y relative permittivity, the only one E_y sees without an off-diagonal eps_xy (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells); overrides eps_r for E_y; optic axis along y: eps_yy = n_e^2.

#### `em_eme.eme_ports.input_mode`

Rank of the incident mode among the input face port modes (mode solver ranking: 1 = largest Re n_eff, PML modes of a cpml face last, so mode k is the k-th mode mode ports would find). It must propagate, else the power fractions are NaN with a run-log warning.

#### `em_eme.eme_length_sweep`

Cheap length scan of the last solve: the sections whose centre lies in [start, stop] get their lengths times each stretch factor and the S-matrix is re-cascaded from the kept interfaces (no mode solve; a taper staircase stays the same taper, longer). Result 'xy' versus the stretched range length [m] (factor order): series transmission_<k> (k = 1 .. n_port_modes), transmission, reflection, as the scalar outputs; extras stretch_factors, wavelength, n_sections_stretched. Keeps every solve's interface S-matrices (4 N^2 complex per section).

#### `em_eme.eme_periodic`

Periodic block (gratings, Bragg mirrors, band edges): the sections whose centre lies in [start, stop] are one period, drawn once and repeated n_periods times: the unit-cell S-matrix (junction from its last to its first section, then its sections) raised to n_periods - 1 by star products is inserted after the drawn period, so port results, scalars and length sweep see the whole device (at least one section must follow the range when n_periods > 1); the field plot shows the first period, the sections after it the field leaving the last. Bloch modes: unit-cell eigenvectors (fields one period on = lam times the fields, lam = exp(-j K period)) from the generalised eigenproblem of its S-matrix. Result 'table' (forward modes: |lam| < 1, or |lam| = 1 with net forward power; least attenuated first): bloch_mode, n_bloch = Re K / k0 (unfolded to the Brillouin zone nearest the length-weighted mean Re n_eff of mode 1 over the cell), n_bloch_imag = Im K / k0 (< 0 decaying; a stop band when the dominant mode decays without loss), multiplier_abs = |lam| per period, phase_per_period_deg = Re K period [deg, in (-180, 180]], dominant_mode (the cell mode carrying most of it). Extras wavelength, period [m], n_periods, first_section / last_section (section table rows). At most one per physics.

#### `em_eme.eme_periodic.n_periods`

The drawn unit cell stands for n_periods copies in a row (cost ~log2(n_periods) star products); the sections after the range follow the last period, so the hi port plane lies (n_periods - 1) periods beyond the window face. 1 = Bloch analysis only.

#### `em_eme.adjoint_objective.quantity`

Power fraction of the excitation (eme_ports, else mode 1 from lo), as the scalar outputs: transmission_mode = into port mode mode_number of the output face (transmission_<k>), reflection_mode = back into that mode of the input face, transmission / reflection = summed over every mode of that face. J = sum of weight * quantity over the enabled adjoint_objective features.

#### `em_eme.design_region.eps_max`

Solid, e.g. silicon 12.08 at 1.55 um. sigma_e, poles and mu_r of design cells stay the material's, not optimised: paint a lossless, non-dispersive material.

#### `em_eme.design_region.filter_radius`

Radius R of the conic filter rho_tilde_a = sum_b w_ab A_b rho_b / sum_b w_ab A_b, w_ab = max(0, R - |c_a - c_b|) (A cell area, c cell centre): smallest feature ~R, no checkerboards; 0 = none. Use >= 2 cells; typical 50-150 nm. Host memory ~ cells x (R / dx)^2.

#### `em_eme.design_region.projection_beta`

beta of rho_bar = (tanh(beta eta) + tanh(beta (rho_tilde - eta))) / (tanh(beta eta) + tanh(beta (1 - eta))); 0 = none. Larger: more binary, stiffer, more local optima; typical 0-8, or 8-32 as the final value of the optimization study continuation_stages.

#### `em_fdfd_3d.bloch_kx`

Bloch wave vector k along this axis, used only when both its faces are periodic: fields repeat with exp(-j k L) per period L (the meshed period; exp(+j omega t)); k and k + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. The resonances at fixed k are the lattice bands at that k (sweep a parameter for a band diagram); the operator becomes complex (no extra unknowns). Typical pi / L at the zone edge.

#### `em_fdfd_3d.eps_r`

n^2 of a lossless dielectric, seen by every E component unless eps_xx / eps_yy / eps_zz override it (stored in the eps_r array, which holds eps_zz). Each E face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells (solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing: anisotropic average on interface faces, in a uint16 face index). May also use z. em_fdtd_3d stores materials as a uint16 index of distinct (eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_zz, sigma_e, mu_r, sigma_m) combinations: continuously varying values (x, y expressions, thermo-optic) are re-quantised to at most 65534 levels per array (max deviation logged, e.g. ~1e-5 in eps over a range of 1) at every material change. Dispersive material: the background eps_inf.

#### `em_fdfd_3d.eps_zz`

The only component E_z sees; overrides eps_r for E_z. Diagonal anisotropy only (crystal axes along x, y, z). Setting any of eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_zz (or dndT_xx / _yy / _zz) on any material allocates the eps_xx and eps_yy arrays (8 B per cell; else E_x, E_y read eps_r) and makes heat_em_thermo_optic write all three.

#### `em_fdfd_3d.eps_xx`

The only component E_x sees; overrides eps_r for E_x, e.g. a uniaxial crystal with its optic axis along x: eps_xx = n_e^2, eps_r = n_o^2. Setting any of eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_zz (or dndT_xx / _yy / _zz) on any material allocates the eps_xx and eps_yy arrays (8 B per cell; else E_x, E_y read eps_r) and makes heat_em_thermo_optic write all three.

#### `em_fdfd_3d.eps_yy`

The only component E_y sees; overrides eps_r for E_y. Setting any of eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_zz (or dndT_xx / _yy / _zz) on any material allocates the eps_xx and eps_yy arrays (8 B per cell; else E_x, E_y read eps_r) and makes heat_em_thermo_optic write all three.

#### `em_fdfd_3d.sigma_m`

Semi-implicit, each H edge takes its lower cell; sigma_m = sigma_e mu0 / eps0 matches the free-space impedance. Not counted in absorbed_power. Setting it on any material allocates its array (4 B per cell).

#### `em_fdfd_3d.resonance_table.min_region_fraction`
