Resonances with region_energy_fraction below this are dropped (counted in the study log; the search widens as for PML modes). 0 keeps all; > 0 needs a domain selection. Typical 0.5: keep cavity modes, drop those of an attached guide.

#### `em_fdfd_bor.geometry`

Always axisymmetric: (r, z) half plane about the x_lo edge (x = r >= 0, y = z). Exists so coupled heat / electric_currents / electrostatics see an axisymmetric partner (no planar-partner warning).

#### `em_fdfd_bor.bc_x_lo`

x_lo is always the axis r = 0. Walls sit on the outer grid edge: pec = tangential E 0, pmc = tangential H 0; cpml adds pml_cells cells outside the face (stretch s = kappa + sigma / (alpha + j omega eps0), pml_* grading; on r_hi the stretched radius enters every metric factor), ending in a pmc edge. A pec / pmc z_lo face is the mirror plane of a structure symmetric about z = 0 (halves the unknowns): pmc keeps modes with E_r, E_phi even (quasi-TE whispering-gallery modes of a disk), pec those with E_z even (quasi-TM). No periodic faces.

#### `em_fdfd_bor.mode_source.power`

Mode power P through the port in the travelling exp(-j m phi) wave (its cos(m phi) standing-wave half carries P / 2 for m != 0); fields scale with sqrt(P).

#### `em_fdfd_conical.bloch_kx`

Used only when both faces of this axis are periodic: Bloch wave F(x + L) = F(x) exp(-j k L) per meshed period L; k and k + 2 pi / L are the same state. Phased operator wrap entries (no extra cost). Point sources repeat in every period image with that phase; a line source along the axis carries exp(-j k s) (s = cell centres from the grid lo corner), so with k_z it launches the conical plane wave (k, k_normal, k_z). Results are those of the Bloch wave at +k.

#### `em_fdfd_conical.mu_r`

Real, 1 for optical materials; H_x (+y face), H_y (+x face), H_z (+x+y corner) take the value of their cell. Solved as mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0).

#### `em_fdfd_conical.point_source.component`

'z' on the E_z point (cell centre); 'x' / 'y' split half on each of the two cell faces along that axis (E_x / E_y points, by dual areas; on a periodic axis the lo face of the first cell is the wrapped last face with the Bloch phase). Every direction is modulated as exp(-j k_z z).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.bc_x_lo`

cpml: pml_cells absorbing cells outside the face. FDFD CPML: complex stretch s = kappa + sigma / (alpha + j omega eps0), FDTD grading of the pml_* settings. periodic: on both faces of the axis; period = the meshed window (uniform mesh: rounded up to whole cells); k = 0 (normal incidence) unless the type has bloch_kx / bloch_ky (em_fdfd_nonlinear: per harmonic_channel). symmetric / antisymmetric: mirror plane on the edge itself, E mirror-even (PMC) / -odd (PEC); a ghost cell outside (edge-cell width and material) holds the image, so draw the structure about the edge (x = 0 for x_lo); the other physics and both polarisations share plane and parity; a source in the outermost cell is mirrored. Results count the unfolded structure: flux lines and derived integrals reaching a mirror face double per face (extra mirror_factor; integrands assumed even), far fields add the image (at most one mirror per axis), Results.field(unfold=True) and the GUI unfold; mode-port powers, source powers and probes stay those of the drawn part. ez / hz walls are half a cell apart (E_z pec, H_z pmc at the outermost cell centre; E_z pmc, H_z pec on its inner face): a cavity is one cell wider or narrower in the other polarisation. The outermost cell of a wall face (ghost cell of a mirror face) takes the em_fdtd_* row: 0 for E_z pec / H_z pmc; the neighbour copied (no flux through the inner face) for E_z pmc / symmetric and H_z pec / antisymmetric; negated for E_z antisymmetric / H_z symmetric. A source in that cell, or an H_z face current on the inner face of a copied row, radiates nothing. A mirror plane through a symmetric guide halves the unknowns.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.wavelength`

Vacuum wavelength lambda0 of a stationary solve (omega = 2 pi C0 / lambda0). The mesh needs >= 10 (better 20) cells per lambda0 / |n| and, in a lossy material or metal, >= 2 (better 4) per skin depth lambda0 / (2 pi |Im n|); validation checks both with the complex eps(omega) at every solved wavelength. A frequency_domain study ignores it (info when not the default) and solves its own list; eigenfrequency (and the optical solve of optomechanics) takes it as the target. A parameter sweep over it repeats a coupled stationary solve (e.g. with heat) per value, cold. Typical 0.4e-6 to 2e-6 m.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.discretization`

Element order on a triangles mesh (tensor meshes ignore it). E_z / H_z on Lagrange elements: quadratic (error ~h^4 in k^2, curved edges isoparametric; + one unknown per edge) or linear (~h^2); materials one value per element (H_z: the in-plane tensor with eps_xy); a cpml face gets mesh pml_layers element layers (pml_* stretch, pec outer side). E_z: pec / antisymmetric faces and pec_domain elements hold E_z = 0, pmc / symmetric are natural; H_z: pmc / symmetric hold H_z = 0, pec / antisymmetric and pec_domain outlines are natural (no staircase). Factorisation: host SuperLU (cusolver_qr unused), cudss / cudss_mixed or mumps / mumps_mixed / pardiso / pardiso_mixed, the analysis reused. Only point_source, field_probe (in-plane components from the element gradient), pec_domain and resonance_table work on triangles; other features, periodic / Bloch faces and the optimization / optomechanics / thermal_noise studies are validation errors.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.bloch_kx`

Bloch wave vector k along this axis, used only when both its faces are periodic: F(x + L) = F(x) exp(-j k L) per meshed period L (k > 0 travels toward +axis); k and k + 2 pi / L are the same state. Phased wrap entries: same unknowns as k = 0; every source repeats per period image with that phase. Line sources and gaussian beams carry exp(-j k.r) (r = cell centres from the grid lo corner), so a line spanning the period launches an oblique plane wave at sin(theta) = k / (n k0) from its normal (k0 = 2 pi / vacuum wavelength); at angle theta an E_z sheet radiates amplitude / cos(theta), an in-plane sheet |E| = amplitude. A plane_wave_tfsf turns oblique with bloch_ky (see that feature), a +x wave repeated per period image with bloch_kx. Mode sources, mode monitors and mode-power objectives on a line spanning a whole Bloch period are refused. Every result (absorbed power, probes, flux, far field, adjoint gradients) is that of the Bloch wave at +k. Band diagrams: an eigenfrequency study swept over k (template fdfd_band_diagram). Typical: k = 2*pi/lambda0*sin(theta) of the vacuum incidence angle.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.eps_zz`

Out-of-plane relative permittivity, the only component E_z sees; overrides eps_r here, so an eps_r override does not change E_z. Anisotropic crystals: eps_r in-plane plus eps_zz, e.g. z-cut lithium niobate eps_r 4.889, eps_zz 4.571 at 1.55 um.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

The source varies as A cos(omega t + phase) = Re(A e^{j phase} e^{j omega t}): 0 = cos carrier, -90 = the sin carrier of the FDTD sources (a cw FDTD steady state is the FDFD solution at phase -90). With a single source it only rotates every phasor, not |E| or the flux.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.line_source`

Sheet current on an axis-aligned line sending amplitude (E_z) to each side in the local medium: a vertical line (x = const) along +x and -x, a horizontal one along +y and -y. For a plane wave span the whole domain (an end on a cpml domain edge continues through the PML; on a periodic axis span the whole period); a shorter line diffracts like a slit. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.gaussian_beam`

Line source with the profile exp(-((s - center) / waist)^2) along the line: a beam of peak E_z = amplitude to each side in the local medium (vertical line: along +x and -x; horizontal: along +y and -y), waist on the line. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.gaussian_beam.waist`

1/e half-width of the field profile along the line (waist on the line); typical 1-5 wavelengths. Keep the line several waists long (validation warns above 1e-2 of the peak at an end inside the domain). On-axis field ~ amplitude (1 + 1/(k waist)^2) for E_z, (1 - 1/(k waist)^2) for H_z types, k = 2 pi n / lambda0 (+-2.5% at waist = lambda0 / n).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.plane_wave_tfsf`

Plane wave along +x on the outline of a total-field box (total field in the box cells, scattered field outside), entering only the right-hand side; phase referred to the centres of the first (lo-x) box column; the incident wave is the discrete plane wave of the FDFD stencil in the background medium (complex eps and mu_r of the outline cell just before the lo-x edge; uniform x cells: (2 / dx) sin(k dx / 2) = n k0; graded x cells: marched on the solved stencil, a grading at the lo-x edge adds a small backward part), so a box in a uniform medium is exactly transparent. The box edges must lie in one uniform medium (else a warning: incident light leaks out), one scattered-field cell inside the domain on every side, except: along a periodic y axis it may cover every y cell (a grating or layer stack may cross it), and at a y mirror face of the wave's parity (ez: symmetric, hz: antisymmetric) it may reach the plane (the other parity, or an x mirror face, is an error). With bloch_ky != 0 the wave is oblique, exp(-j (k_x x + ky y)), phase referred to y = 0, (2 / dx)^2 sin^2(k_x dx / 2) = (n k0)^2 - (2 / dy)^2 sin^2(ky dy / 2) (refused when not positive); it needs uniform y cells. Enclose the scatterers, put a far_field box outside it; flux and mode monitors must not straddle its outline. The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis (an edge exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.mode_number`

Mode rank in descending Re(n_eff) (ranked by Re(k^2) of the transverse eigenvalue, so evanescent modes come after every propagating one): 1 = fundamental; both parities count (in a symmetric slab mode 1 is even, 2 odd); modes localised in the PML of a line continuing through it are not counted. The build fails when the line has fewer modes and warns when the selected one is not guided (Re(n_eff) not above the index of a span-end cell at a cpml or metal end) or carries no forward power. The result table lists the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.direction`

positive: toward +x from a vertical line (x = const), toward +y from a horizontal one; negative: toward -x / -y. Nothing is launched upstream, at every solved wavelength.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.power`

Time-averaged power of the launched mode per unit z length, 1/2 Re of the integral of (E x H*).n over the line; mode amplitude sqrt(power) e^{j phase}. Fields scale with sqrt(power); 1 W/m is usual (peak |E| ~1e4 V/m in a 0.3 um silicon slab).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet`

Zero-thickness conducting sheet (graphene, a TMD monolayer, a metal film much thinner than a cell) on an axis-aligned line: K = sigma_s E_t [A/m] (tangential E only). em_fdfd_ez: E_z of the line cells, diagonal += -j omega mu0 sigma_s / w (w the line-cell width across the line). em_fdfd_hz: E_x (horizontal line) / E_y (vertical) on the hi face of the line cells, face permittivity += -j sigma_s / (omega eps0 w), w the face spacing; not in the last cell before a non-periodic outer face. Vacuum, normal incidence: transmission |1 / (1 + eta0 sigma_s / 2)|^2 (on the grid 1 / |1 + omega mu0 sigma_s w / (2 sin(k w))|^2, k the discrete wavenumber). Its loss 1/2 Re sigma_s |E_t|^2 per sheet area goes into q_abs of the line cells (em_heat_joule heats them). Only the operator sees it, not line-source / TFSF calibrations, port modes or material maps (keep source, port and TFSF lines off it; enclose it in a TFSF box as a scatterer). A span end on a cpml edge continues through the PML; sheets on one line add. Eigenfrequency: sigma_s at the target wavelength (first-order error away from it). The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1). No result.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.model`

'constant': sigma_real + j sigma_imag at every solved wavelength; 'graphene_kubo': the Kubo formula of monolayer graphene per solved wavelength (intraband Drude e^2 tau (mu + 2 kT ln(1 + e^{-mu / kT})) / (pi hbar^2 (1 + j omega tau)) plus the temperature-smeared interband term, sigma_0 = e^2 / (4 hbar) above the 2 |E_F| edge; no spatial dispersion, no magnetic field).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.sigma_real`

Re sigma_s (> 0 absorbs). Default 6.085e-5 S = the universal optical conductivity of graphene (2.3 % absorption in vacuum); a metal film of thickness d << skin depth: sigma_s ~ sigma_bulk d.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.sigma_imag`

Im sigma_s (exp(+j omega t)): < 0 inductive (free carriers, Drude 1 / (1 + j omega tau)), > 0 capacitive; Kubo literature in exp(-i omega t) has the opposite sign.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.fermi_energy`

Chemical potential E_F relative to the Dirac point (|E_F| enters): gated or doped graphene 0.1-0.6 eV, n = (E_F / (hbar v_F))^2 / pi carriers per m^2 (v_F ~ 1e6 m/s). Interband absorption sets in at hbar omega = 2 |E_F| (wavelength 1.24e-6 / (2 |E_F| / eV) m).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.scattering_time`

Carrier relaxation time tau of the intraband (Drude) term: 1e-14 - 1e-12 s (CVD graphene ~1e-13 s; mobility e tau v_F^2 / |E_F|); the interband term is unbroadened.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.effective_index`

Effective-index method (2.5D): at build time slab mode mode_number of the vertical stack layer_indices / layer_thicknesses is solved at wavelength (1D grid of ~wavelength / (100 n_max) cells, claddings deepened until the tails decay) and eps_r = n_eff^2 is written on the selected cells over the material background permittivity (later features win on overlaps; the material's sigma_e and poles stay; a state-dependent permittivity expression overwrites it). Ignores vertical leakage and the vertical mode mismatch at stack boundaries. Validation reports n_eff (info); thermo-optic couplings take n_eff as their reference index n0.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.effective_index.wavelength`

Vacuum wavelength of the slab-mode solve; n_eff is used unchanged at every frequency (FDTD pulses, frequency_domain sweeps): keep the band narrow around it.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.effective_index.slab_polarization`

'te': E parallel to the layers, partner of the in-plane-E top-view types em_fdtd_hz / em_fdfd_hz; 'tm': E mostly normal to the layers, partner of em_fdtd_ez / em_fdfd_ez. Default: the matching one (validation notes a mismatch).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium`

Phase-change medium (e.g. GST-225, the defaults) on the selected cells: a per-cell crystallinity X in [0, 1] (output field crystallinity) sets eps(X) by the mixing rule of the amorphous and crystalline (n - j k)^2, written as Re eps into the permittivity arrays and sigma_e = -Im eps omega eps0 (omega of wavelength) over the material (later features win on overlaps; the material's poles stay; a state-dependent permittivity expression overwrites it). X follows the heat temperature only through heat_em_phase_change (time_dependent study, transient heat): after each heat step theta += k(T) dt at the end-of-step T (JMAK kinetics and melting: see the params; a fast quench stays amorphous); FDTD then recalibrates its sources, FDFD re-solves at its next step. Not modelled: latent heat, liquid optical constants, thermal properties following X (heat uses the material, e.g. gst_225_amorphous), nucleation statistics. Result: timeseries of the mean X over the selection per update (t = heat time). In other studies a static medium at initial_crystallinity. GST crystallises in tens of ns (~1e9 FDTD steps): switch with em_fdfd_* + transient heat in a time_dependent study. GST-225 data: n, k at 1.55 um as used for sputtered films in integrated photonics (e.g. Rios et al., Nat. Photonics 9, 725 (2015); film dependent by ~10 %); crystallisation onset ~150 C and activation energy 2.24 eV from Friedrich et al., J. Appl. Phys. 87, 4130 (2000); melting point 616 C from Yamada et al., J. Appl. Phys. 69, 2849 (1991). The Avrami exponent 2.5 is typical of nucleation-dominated GST (2-4 reported); the cap of 50 ns above 650 K is an illustrative calibration (100 s at the 150 C onset with 2.24 eV, tens of ns in laser / electrical SET pulses): fit both to the device.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.n_amorphous`

Refractive index n of the amorphous phase at wavelength (eps = (n - j k)^2, exp(+j omega t)); default GST-225 at 1.55 um (library material gst_225_amorphous).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.k_amorphous`

Extinction coefficient k of the amorphous phase at wavelength (eps = (n - j k)^2, exp(+j omega t)); default GST-225 at 1.55 um (library material gst_225_amorphous).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.n_crystalline`

Refractive index n of the crystalline phase at wavelength (eps = (n - j k)^2, exp(+j omega t)); default GST-225 at 1.55 um (library material gst_225_crystalline).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.k_crystalline`

Extinction coefficient k of the crystalline phase at wavelength (eps = (n - j k)^2, exp(+j omega t)); default GST-225 at 1.55 um (library material gst_225_crystalline).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.wavelength`

Vacuum wavelength of n and k: the absorption enters as sigma_e = -Im(eps) omega eps0 at this omega, exact there (FDTD pulses see sigma_e / (omega eps0) away from it); validation notes a source / solved wavelength more than 1 % off.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.mixing`

Permittivity of crystallinity X: 'lorentz_lorenz' (eps - 1) / (eps + 2) = (1 - X) (eps_a - 1) / (eps_a + 2) + X (eps_c - 1) / (eps_c + 2) (complex), or 'linear' eps = (1 - X) eps_a + X eps_c.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.initial_crystallinity`

Crystallinity X at t = 0 on every selected cell (theta = (-ln(1 - X))^(1/n)); without an enabled heat_em_phase_change into this physics X stays here (a static medium in any study).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.fast_crystallization_temperature`

T_fast [K]: the rate is capped at 1 / min_crystallization_time from T_fast up to the melting point (the Arrhenius law would otherwise give picosecond crystallisation near melting, so no melt-quench could stay amorphous). Illustrative GST-225 value 650 K.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.min_crystallization_time`

tau_min [s]: JMAK rate k = 1 / tau_min between fast_crystallization_temperature and the melting point; a melt-quench crossing that range in much less than tau_min stays amorphous (with the defaults a 1e11 K/s quench keeps X < 0.01, a 1e8 K/s one recrystallises fully). Illustrative GST-225 value 50 ns (tens of ns in SET pulses).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.activation_energy`

Ea [eV] of the Arrhenius rate k(T) = exp(-Ea / kB (1/T - 1/T_fast)) / tau_min between the onset and T_fast. GST-225 2.24 eV (Friedrich et al. 2000); with the default cap it gives ~100 s at the 423 K onset.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.avrami_exponent`

JMAK exponent n: X = 1 - exp(-theta^n), theta = integral of k(T) dt (the additivity rule, exact for isothermal steps of any length); 2-4 for GST (2.5 default).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.melting_temperature`

T_melt [K]: a cell at T >= T_melt is molten: theta = 0, X = 0 (optically amorphous; the liquid optical constants and the latent heat are not modelled). GST-225 889 K (616 C, Yamada et al. 1991).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.field_probe`

Phasor of one field component in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell) per solved wavelength. Face components (hx / hy, ex / ey) come from neighbouring cells: keep them off a plane_wave_tfsf outline and a mode_source interface face (validation warns). Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength (m, ascending; one point per solved wavelength, a re-solved one keeps its latest): series abs = |phasor| (unit of the component) and phase (rad; field = abs cos(omega t + phase)); y_label the component label; extras frequency (Hz), wavelength (m), component and unit.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.mode_monitor.mode_number`

Mode rank in descending Re(n_eff) (ranked by Re(k^2) of the transverse eigenvalue, so evanescent modes come after every propagating one): 1 = fundamental; both parities count (in a symmetric slab mode 1 is even, 2 odd); modes localised in the PML of a line continuing through it are not counted. The build fails when the line has fewer modes and warns when the selected one is not guided (Re(n_eff) not above the index of a span-end cell at a cpml or metal end) or carries no forward power. Picked at the first solved wavelength (frequency_domain order: its wavelengths list, else wavelength_start to wavelength_stop) and followed by overlap with the previous solve, so it keeps its identity where two modes cross in n_eff.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.far_field`

Near-to-far-field transform of the phasors on a rectangle outline (the out-of-plane field and the in-plane one, from the curl of E_z / Ampere's law of H_z, averaged onto the centres at the em_fdtd_* far_field sample points, so normalised patterns compare directly): power per unit length and angle rho |E|^2 / (2 eta0) in W/(m rad) of the far-field |E| (H_z: |eta0 H_z|; angle integral = power through a closed flux box) versus angle counter-clockwise from +x, one row per solved wavelength (ascending). Assumes vacuum outside the box: enclose every scatterer; with a plane_wave_tfsf keep the box outside it, in the scattered field: x0 / y0 edges at least two cells before those of the TFSF box, x1 / y1 edges in or beyond the first cell past it (samples average the faces on both sides of their cell; validation warns otherwise, and for an edge sampling across a mode_source interface face). The contour runs through the centres of the first box cells and of the cells one beyond x1 / y1 (keep the box one cell off the x_hi / y_hi edges); graded meshes work (actual centres, trapezoid weights). The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis (an edge exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective`

Objective term for the adjoint sensitivity: a flux_monitor or mode_monitor quantity on an axis-aligned line times weight. Output field eps_sensitivity = dJ/d eps_r per unit area [W/m^3] from one extra transposed solve on the forward factorisation, computed when read (snapshot, derived value): d eps over a region R changes J by the integral of eps_sensitivity d eps over R. em_fdfd_hz: the sum of the eps_xx and eps_yy terms (eps_xy fixed), plus eps_xy_sensitivity = dJ/d eps_xy per unit area (0 where the solve drops eps_xy: PEC cells, the outer two rows of a wall or mirror face). Line source calibrations and port / monitor modes are held fixed, so the gradient is exact only off every line source, port and mode monitor line and the cells past their hi faces; sigma_e, poles and mu_r are not differentiated. An optimization study maximises J, summed over every physics, over the design_region densities. Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength: series value (the quantity, W/m) and weighted (weight * value); extras frequency, wavelength, quantity, weight. Keep the line off a TFSF outline and a mode_source interface face. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective.quantity`

W/m: flux = time-averaged Poynting power through the line (as flux_monitor, > 0 toward +x / +y); mode_power_positive / _negative = |a|^2 of mode mode_number toward +normal / -normal (as mode_monitor power_positive / _negative).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective.mode_number`

Mode rank in descending Re(n_eff) (ranked by Re(k^2) of the transverse eigenvalue, so evanescent modes come after every propagating one): 1 = fundamental; both parities count (in a symmetric slab mode 1 is even, 2 odd); modes localised in the PML of a line continuing through it are not counted. The build fails when the line has fewer modes and warns when the selected one is not guided (Re(n_eff) not above the index of a span-end cell at a cpml or metal end) or carries no forward power. Used by the mode_power quantities only; picked at the first solved wavelength and followed by overlap, as mode_monitor.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.design_region`

Density design region on the selected domains (window cells only): each cell has a density rho in [0, 1], filtered and projected to rho_bar, and gets eps = eps_min + rho_bar (eps_max - eps_min) (em_fdfd_ez: eps_r; em_fdfd_hz: eps_xx and eps_yy), overwriting the material permittivity. The optimization study varies rho to maximise the adjoint_objective sum J; other studies solve the initial_density design. Regions of one physics must not share cells; keep them off source, port and objective lines and the cells past their hi faces (inexact gradient there). Output field design_density = rho_bar (0 outside). Result 'xy' versus iteration (0 = initial, one point per accepted L-BFGS-B iteration): series objective (J of the model, W/m) and grayness (mean 4 rho_bar (1 - rho_bar), 0 = binary); extras n_cells, eps_min, eps_max, mean_density, final_grayness and note (non-empty outside an optimization study: iteration 0, objective NaN).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.resonance_table`

Resonances of the last eigenfrequency solve, nearest the target (the wavelength setting) first. Result 'table', one row per resonance: resonance_number (rank by |omega - omega_target|), wavelength = 2 pi C0 / Re(omega) (m), frequency = Re(omega) / (2 pi), frequency_imag = Im(omega) / (2 pi) (Hz; > 0 decays), q_factor = Re(omega) / (2 Im(omega)) (inf when |Im omega| < 1e-12 Re omega; negative = growing, usually a PML artefact), pml_fraction (share of the out-of-plane |field|^2 dA in PML cells: above 0.5 dropped; above ~1e-2 widen the cladding); extras target_wavelength (m), selected_resonance. Accurate only near the target. Q versus a parameter: a derived value with source '<physics>.<this feature>', expression q_factor, operation at, at = 0. An optional domain selection adds region_energy_fraction (share of the same weights in the selected cells; triangles: dofs of the selected elements, outline dofs counting fully) and drops resonances below min_region_fraction like PML modes. One resonance_table with a selection per physics.

#### `em_fdfd_hz.effective_index`

Effective-index method (2.5D): at build time slab mode mode_number of the vertical stack layer_indices / layer_thicknesses is solved at wavelength (1D grid of ~wavelength / (100 n_max) cells, claddings deepened until the tails decay) and eps_xx / eps_yy = n_eff^2 is written on the selected cells over the material background permittivity (later features win on overlaps; the material's sigma_e and poles stay; a state-dependent permittivity expression overwrites it). Ignores vertical leakage and the vertical mode mismatch at stack boundaries. Validation reports n_eff (info); thermo-optic couplings take n_eff as their reference index n0.

#### `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`

d = chi2 / 2 in crystal axes, Voigt il: i = polarisation component (1 x, 2 y, 3 z), l = field pair (1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz, 4 yz, 5 xz, 6 xy); 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V. SHG with one field component: P(2 omega) = eps0 d E^2.

#### `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.orientation`

Crystal x, y, z along model: z_cut x, y, z (c out of plane, E_z channels see d33); x_cut y, z, x (c along x); y_cut z, x, y (c along y); euler: Rz(euler_alpha) Rx(euler_beta) Rz(euler_gamma) (column a = crystal axis a in model coordinates).

#### `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`

harmonic_channel feature name this feature acts on (a polarization both channel: <name>_ez or <name>_hz). Its polarisation picks the em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz form; params of the other form are ignored (warning).

#### `em_fdtd_3d.bloch_kx`

Bloch wave vector k along this axis, used only when both its faces are periodic: fields repeat with exp(-j k L) per period L (the meshed period; exp(+j omega t), so k > 0 travels toward +axis); k and k + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. k != 0 steps a second (imaginary) field set: field and CPML memory, pole states and step time double. Dipoles and mode sources drive the real set only (period images repeat them with the Bloch phase: a dipole plus a resonance monitor per swept k gives slab / metasurface bands); mode ports solve their cross-section mode at the Bloch k of the port plane's periodic axes. DFT monitors (flux, field map, mode monitor, harmonic FDTD) give the +k response at every positive frequency; probes, field plots, expressions and couplings read the real set. Refused with k != 0: the TFSF plane wave (normal incidence only) and absorbed power (track_absorption, q_accum, em_heat_joule). Typical k = k0 sin(theta) (vacuum incidence angle) or pi / L (zone edge).

#### `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`

gaussian: sin carrier of f0 = C0 / wavelength under exp(-((t - t0) / tau)^2), tau = 1 / (pi bandwidth f0), t0 = 4.5 tau, lasting ~2 t0 (550 nm, bandwidth 0.5: ~10 fs); amplitude = envelope peak, the carrier is 0 at t0 (source peak ~0.87 at bandwidth 0.5, ~0.66 at 1). cw: sin(2 pi f0 t) ramped in by 1 - exp(-t / (3 T)), T = 1 / f0, steady after ~15 periods. ricker: spectral peak f0, delayed 4 / f0 (3 % of the peak at 2.5 f0, 1 % at 2.76 f0).

#### `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`

lambda0 = C0 / f0 of the carrier (ricker: spectral peak), in m, not nm: typical 400e-9 to 1600e-9 (validation warns below 1e-9 or above 100 domain diagonals). Mesh: >= 10 (better 20) cells per lambda0 / n at the highest source frequency.

#### `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`

Spectral width / f0: amplitude spectrum exp(-((f - f0) / (bandwidth f0))^2), 1/e at f0 (1 +- bandwidth), power FWHM ~1.18 bandwidth f0; the mesh check and auto mesh resolve f0 (1 + bandwidth). 0.2-1 typical; wider = shorter pulse, finer mesh.

#### `em_fdtd_3d.resonance_monitor.start_time`

Start t_s of the analysed window; empty = the end 2 t0 of the latest gaussian / ricker source pulse (0 with only cw sources). The fit assumes a free ring-down: a start inside a pulse adds spurious poles.

#### `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`

Vacuum wavelength. Keep the range inside the source spectrum (gaussian: lambda0 / (1 +- bandwidth / 2), e.g. 440e-9 to 733e-9 m at 550 nm, bandwidth 0.5), else normalised results get noisy; validation warns where every enabled source is below 1e-2 of its peak (gaussian beyond f0 (1 +- 2.15 bandwidth), ricker outside 0.06-2.76 f0, cw beyond 1 / duration of f0).

#### `em_fdtd_bor.bc_x_lo`

x_lo is always the axis r = 0. Walls on the outer grid edge as in em_fdfd_bor (pec = tangential E 0, pmc = tangential H 0); cpml adds pml_cells cells ending in a pmc edge: on the z faces a convolutional PML (2D FDTD grading), on r_hi a cylindrical PML (the em_fdfd_bor radius stretch, alpha = 0, recursive convolutions) that absorbs as well near the axis and at large m; pml_alpha_max acts on the z faces only. A pec / pmc z_lo face is the mirror plane of a structure symmetric about z = 0 (pmc keeps E_r, E_phi even, pec E_z). No periodic faces.

#### `em_fdtd_bor.resonance_monitor`

Resonance finder (harmonic inversion, as Harminv / matrix pencil): records one component in the cell containing each selected point (1 to 16; a coordinate on a cell edge goes to the upper cell) every step. Reading the result (CPU, ~1 s per point) fits the traces from t_s on jointly (shared poles, amplitudes per point) by damped sinusoids a exp(-gamma (t - t_s)) cos(omega (t - t_s) + phi), so a mode on a nodal line of one point is found through the others. Result 'table', one row per resonance in the band, strongest first: resonance_number, wavelength [m, vacuum C0 / frequency], frequency = omega / (2 pi) [Hz], frequency_imag = gamma / (2 pi) [Hz] (> 0 decays), q_factor = omega / (2 gamma), amplitude a [component unit] and phase phi [rad] at t_s where largest, error = |pole change between two pencil sizes| / omega. Dropped: error > 0.01, amplitude < 0.0001 of the strongest at every point, growth > 2x over the window. Extras: component, unit, dt [s], start_time, end_time [s], sample_interval [steps], n_samples (<= 2000), model_order, wavelength_min, wavelength_max, note ('' or why none was found), points, point_amplitudes / point_phases (per row, one per point). Q far above pi f T_window resolves while the ring-down stays above float32 noise (~1e-7). A mode with a node at every point is missed; a cw source adds an undamped line.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.bloch_kx`

Bloch wave vector k along this axis, used only when both its faces are periodic: fields repeat with exp(-j k L) per meshed period L (k > 0 travels toward +axis); k and k + 2 pi / L are the same state. Any k != 0 steps a second (imaginary) field set: field memory and time per step double. Line sources and gaussian beams carry exp(-j k.r), so a line along the axis launches an oblique plane wave at sin(theta) = k / (n k0) from its normal (k0 = 2 pi / vacuum wavelength): at fixed k the angle changes across a pulse, frequencies below c k / n are evanescent; at angle theta an E_z sheet radiates amplitude / cos(theta), an in-plane sheet |E| = amplitude. Point, plane-wave box and mode sources drive only the real set (each period image repeats them with the Bloch phase: band diagrams from a point source and a resonance monitor per swept k). DFT monitors (flux, field map, far field, mode monitor) give the +k response at every positive frequency; probes, field plots, expressions and couplings read the real set. Absorbed power (track_absorption, q_accum, em_heat_joule) is refused. Typical: k = 2*pi/lambda0*sin(theta) of the vacuum incidence angle.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.plane_wave_tfsf`

Plane wave along +x on the outline of a total-field box: total field inside, only the scattered field outside (H_z: the outline E faces included). Uniform or graded meshes (the 1D incident line runs on the grid's own x widths: graded cells leak nothing). The incident field is computed for vacuum, so the box edges must lie in vacuum (warning otherwise), one scattered-field cell inside the domain on every side, except at a y mirror face of the wave's parity (ez: symmetric, hz: antisymmetric): there it may reach the plane and its image completes it (the other parity, or an x mirror face, is an error). Keep flux and mode monitors (hi face included) entirely inside or outside the box (validation warns). The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis (an edge exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.direction`

positive launches toward +x from a vertical line (x = const), +y from a horizontal one; negative toward -x / -y. The total field starts at the line cells.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.waveform`

gaussian: sin carrier of f0 = C0 / wavelength under exp(-((t - t0) / tau)^2), tau = 1 / (pi bandwidth f0), t0 = 4.5 tau, lasting ~2 t0 (550 nm, bandwidth 0.5: ~10 fs); amplitude = envelope peak, the carrier is 0 at t0 (source peak ~0.87 at bandwidth 0.5, ~0.66 at 1). cw: sin(2 pi f0 t) ramped in by 1 - exp(-t / (3 T)), T = 1 / f0, steady after ~15 periods. No ricker: the complex profile needs the carrier and its cos quadrature partner.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.wavelength`

Vacuum wavelength lambda0 = C0 / f0 of the carrier, the only one the mode is solved at (profile, n_eff, impedance): the launch is exact and one-sided there. Typical 1.31e-6 or 1.55e-6; the mesh needs >= 10 (better 20) cells per lambda0 / n at the highest source frequency.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.bandwidth`

Spectral width / f0 of the gaussian pulse, amplitude spectrum exp(-((f - f0) / (bandwidth * f0))^2) (1/e at f0 (1 +- bandwidth); the mesh check and auto mesh resolve f0 (1 + bandwidth)). The mode is solved at f0 only, so backward leakage and radiation grow toward the band edges as the guide disperses; 0.1-0.3 typical. Above 0.6 the build warns: the cos quadrature partner (not an exact Hilbert partner) biases fraction_* / phase_* toward the lower band edge and adds a DC part.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.power`

Power per unit z length of the launched mode, 1/2 Re integral of (E x H*).n over the line (the 2D port input power): cw = time average after the ramp, gaussian = cycle average at the envelope peak. Fields scale with sqrt(power) (1 W/m: peak |E| ~1e4 V/m in a 0.3 um silicon slab).

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.n2`

dn = n2 I, I = n0 c eps0 |E|^2 / 2 (cycle mean); stepped as instantaneous chi3 = (4/3) n0^2 eps0 c n2 [m^2/V^2], so a cw field also drives its third harmonic. Silicon ~6e-18, Si3N4 ~2.5e-19, silica ~2.6e-20 m^2/W at 1.55 um; negative = self-defocusing. Keep chi3 E^2 << eps (the implicit update assumes a monotonic D(E)).

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.tpa_beta`

dI/dz = -beta I^2 (plane wave), stepped as sigma = (2/3) beta (n0 c eps0)^2 E^2. Silicon ~8e-12 m/W (0.8 cm/GW) at 1.55 um, GaAs ~3e-10. Counts as absorbed power (q_accum, em_heat_joule); with free-carrier values it generates carriers.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.carrier_lifetime`

tau of dN/dt = beta I^2 / (2 hbar omega) - N / tau (implicit Euler, float64). Required (> 0) with fca_cross_section or fcd_coefficient; silicon ~0.5-3 ns. Carriers build up over ~tau: a pulse train shorter than tau sees only part of the steady density.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.fca_cross_section`

Power loss per length alpha = sigma N, stepped as conductivity sigma N n0 eps0 c. Silicon ~1.45e-21 m^2 at 1.55 um (~lambda^2). Counts as absorbed power.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.fcd_coefficient`

dn = -k N, stepped as delta eps = -2 n0 k N. Silicon ~1.35e-27 m^3 at 1.55 um (a linearised Soref-Bennett; the hole term is sublinear, so k depends on the density range).

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.pump_wavelength`

Wavelength of the TPA photons: each absorbed pair (2 hbar omega) creates one carrier pair. Use the source centre wavelength (validation notes a mismatch); unused without free-carrier values.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.d_eff`

P = eps0 chi2 E^2, chi2 = 2 d_eff (not scaled by n0), implicit with the Kerr term: E = Re(E1 exp(j omega t)) drives P(2 omega) = eps0 d_eff E1^2 (the em_fdfd_nonlinear SHG phasor) and DC eps0 d_eff |E1|^2. A scalar per component, no tensor: E_z types P_z = eps0 chi2 E_z^2 (d33, c axis along z), H_z types P_x, P_y likewise (no cross terms). LN d33 ~2.5e-11, GaAs d14 ~1.2e-10 m/V; keep |chi2 E| << eps. Crystal tensors: em_fdfd_nonlinear; this is for pulsed time-domain cross-checks.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.poling`

Sign of chi2 per cell: >= 0 keeps d_eff, < 0 inverts it (Kerr, TPA, carriers unchanged). Periodic poling: sign(sin(2 * pi * x / Lambda)), Lambda = lambda / (2 |n(2 omega) - n(omega)|); H_z faces average two cells, so a domain wall on a cell edge gives 0 there. 1 = unpoled.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.density`

N0 + N1 + N2 + N3 (conserved). Peak small-signal power gain ~ k0 delta_eps omega_a / (gamma n0) per metre, delta_eps = kappa (N2 - N1) / (eps0 omega_a^2) (validation reports it).

#### `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.pump_rate`

W_p of N0 -> N3 per ground-state atom. Steady inversion N2 - N1 = W_p (tau_21 - tau_10) N, N = density / (1 + W_p (tau_32 + tau_21 + tau_10)), built up over ~tau_21 (often millions of steps): short runs use initial_upper_fraction. W_p dt >= 0.1 is a validation error.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor.mode_number`

Mode rank in descending Re(n_eff) (ranked by Re(k^2) of the transverse eigenvalue, so evanescent modes come after every propagating one): 1 = fundamental; both parities count (in a symmetric slab mode 1 is even, 2 odd); modes localised in the PML of a line continuing through it are not counted. The build fails when the line has fewer modes and warns when the selected one is not guided (Re(n_eff) not above the index of a span-end cell at a cpml or metal end) or carries no forward power. Picked at the middle monitor wavelength and followed to the others by overlap, so it keeps its identity where modes cross in n_eff (the build warns where the overlap stays below 0.9 or the mode is no longer guided, e.g. past a cutoff).

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor.n_wavelengths`

Evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency); 1 = the range centre. Each wavelength costs a 1D mode solve at build, two complex spectra per line cell and work per step; 11-41 typical.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.dft_monitor.downsample`

Stride s in cells along x and y: records cells x_start + min(s, box cells) // 2 + k s (likewise y), point samples at those centres (hz in-plane E: still the face mean onto each sampled centre), no block averaging; memory and work per step ~1 / s^2. Result x_centers / y_centers are the sampled centres; extent stays the whole box. Features smaller than s cells alias.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.far_field`

Near-to-far-field transform of the out-of-plane field and the in-plane one on a rectangle outline: power per angle rho |E|^2 / eta0 of the far-field |E| (H_z: |eta0 H_z|; a.u.: dt-weighted spectra without the 1/2, so its angle integral matches a closed flux box) versus angle counter-clockwise from +x, per wavelength. Enclose every scatterer; with a TFSF source keep the box outside the TFSF box, in the scattered field: x0 / y0 edges at least one cell before those of the TFSF box, x1 / y1 edges in the last TFSF cell or beyond (validation warns otherwise). The contour runs through the centres of the first box cells and of the cells one beyond x1 / y1 (keep the box one cell off the x_hi / y_hi edges), the in-plane field averaged onto the centres; graded meshes work. The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis (an edge exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

#### `em_modes.bloch_kx`

Used only when both faces of this axis are periodic: Bloch modes of the periodic cross-section, F(s + L) = F(s) exp(-j k L) per meshed period L along the axis (fields ~ exp(j (omega t - beta z))), e.g. a photonic-crystal fibre supercell or a waveguide array at phase step k L; k and k + 2 pi / L are the same state. Phased operator wrap entries (same cost, operator no longer symmetric); displayed centre fields carry the phase across the wrap. Validation errors with shg_overlap (2 omega modes would need 2 k) and thermal_noise / optomechanics studies (overlaps assume k = 0). Typical: pi / L (first zone edge).

#### `heat.thermorefractive_noise.illumination_physics`

em_fdfd_ez (E along the waveguide) or em_fdfd_hz (E in the cross-section) physics giving the incident field: it solves the cross-section at k_z = 0 as a background physics of the thermal_noise study, at the wavelength of mode_physics. With a mirror face the illumination has the collected mode's parity (validation info).

#### `heat.thermorefractive_noise.mode_physics`

em_modes physics (same model, straight waveguide) whose modes give the weighting; the thermal_noise study solves it first. Its ghost cells outside pec / pmc wall planes weigh 0.

#### `heat.thermorefractive_noise.incident_selection`

collected = the collected mode itself (backscatter / phase noise), te / tm = the fundamental quasi-TE / quasi-TM mode (as collected_selection), number = incident_mode.

#### `heat.thermorefractive_noise.collected_selection`

te / tm = the fundamental quasi-TE (E_x dominant) / quasi-TM mode: the highest-ranked mode with te_fraction > 0.5 / <= 0.5 (run error when none: raise n_modes; a mirror face keeps one family only); te_and_tm = both in one run, one spectrum each (prefix psd_te / psd_tm, extras suffix _te / _tm; twice the factorisations); number = collected_mode.

#### `heat.thermorefractive_noise.collected_direction`

backward: q0 = beta_inc + beta_coll; forward: q0 = |beta_inc - beta_coll| (0 for the same mode); illumination: q0 = beta_coll either way (only the sign of the E_z cross term differs).

#### `heat.thermorefractive_noise.axial_profile`

Envelope g(z) along z. uniform: g = 1 over interaction_length L, S = L S_2D(q0) (exact once L >> 1/q0 and the diffusion length sqrt(D / omega); at q0 = 0 and low f use gaussian). gaussian: g = exp(-z^2 / waist^2) (1/e^2 intensity radius waist), S = integral dq/2pi |g~(q - q0)|^2 S_2D(q) by Gauss-Hermite (exact for any waist).

#### `magnetic_fields_ac.geometry`

planar: A_z of currents along z, totals per m of depth (J/m, Wb/m, H/m). axisymmetric (x = r, y = z; spec notes): currents J_phi circle the axis; solved for psi = r A_phi with coefficients nu / r (2 pi psi = the flux through the circle of radius r), field A reports A_phi, totals are whole rings (J, Wb, H). x_lo is the axis (psi = 0, exact half-cell axis conductance; a face feature on x_lo is a validation error).

#### `magnetic_fields_ac.mu_dc`

Sets mu_dc_xx and mu_dc_yy (component entries override it); unset = 1 (vacuum). NOT the optical mu_r of the wave physics. Typical: air, copper, aluminium 1; ferrite 1e3 - 1e4; electrical steel 4e3; Metglas 1e4 - 1e5; mu-metal 5e4. A large contrast is exact but slows Jacobi-PCG: tighten the tolerance (1e-10). With saturation_polarization: the initial permeability of the B-H curve.

#### `magnetic_fields_ac.magnetic_insulation`

A = 0 on the selected outer faces (the default of every face no feature sets): no normal flux, field lines run along the face. The mirror of an ODD current distribution (J_z changes sign across the plane, e.g. midway between a conductor and its return) or a distant boundary. Axisymmetric: psi = 0, so no net flux crosses an x_hi face (the return flux lies inside it); x_lo (the axis) is a validation error. Anchors the solve.

#### `magnetic_fields_ac.symmetry`

dA/dn = 0 (Neumann) on the selected outer faces: no tangential flux, field lines cross at right angles. The mirror of an EVEN current distribution (J_z equal on both sides) or a face next to an ideal iron yoke. Does not anchor: with symmetry on all four faces add an external_field or fixed_potential. Axisymmetric: refused on x_lo (the axis).

#### `magnetic_fields_ac.external_field`

Uniform applied flux density (B_x, B_y), selection 'all' only, one per physics: the outermost window cells are held at the external potential (planar A = B_x y - B_y x, exact for a uniform field; axisymmetric psi = B_y r^2 / 2, exact on uniform r cells only: graded r cells add a first-order error). Keep objects several object sizes from the edges (the ring holds the undisturbed field). The ring cells leave the solve: B and H read 0 there and outer-face features do nothing. Triangle mesh: A held on the window-edge nodes, no ring (the whole window is free). Anchors the solve. Typical: the Earth field ~5e-5 T, a Helmholtz coil 1e-4 - 1e-2 T.

#### `magnetic_fields_ac.fixed_potential`

Holds the vector potential on the selected cells for the whole run (they leave the solve; B and H read 0 there). One held value excludes all flux (a perfect diamagnet or superconductor); regions held at A_1 and A_2 carry the flux (A_1 - A_2) per m of depth between them (planar). Triangle mesh: held on the element nodes (axisymmetric as psi / r). Anchors the solve.

#### `magnetostatics.nonlinear_tolerance`

Saturation loop stop (materials with saturation_polarization > 0 or a bh_curve; ignored without one). Tensor mesh: converged when a proposal changes ln of the secant reluctivity nu = H / B of every cell by <= this value; keep it above the CG accuracy (one warm-started CG solve per iteration); at single precision a loop that stops improving ends unconverged after 20 iterations (iron B off by up to percents). Triangle mesh (Newton): converged when the step changes A by <= this fraction of max |A| and the largest free residual is <= this fraction of the largest load or internal force.

#### `magnetostatics.nonlinear_max_iterations`

Per solve (tensor: fixed-point proposals, triangles: Newton steps); an unconverged loop keeps its last iterate and logs a warning. Ignored without a saturating material.

#### `magnetostatics.nonlinear_method`

Solver of materials with saturation_polarization > 0 or a bh_curve. 'auto': 'anderson' on a tensor mesh, 'newton' on triangles; 'newton' on tensor and 'anderson' / 'picard' on triangles are validation errors. Tensor mesh, fixed point on ln nu: 'anderson' mixes the last 5 iterates (fixed relaxation), converging also where plain Picard oscillates (currents imposing H on iron past the knee); 'picard' damps with automatic halving. Triangles: 'newton' minimises the convex magnetic energy (exact tangent, energy line search), globally convergent, quadratic near the solution (bh_curve tables: superlinear); one factorisation per step.

#### `magnetostatics.nonlinear_relaxation`

Fraction of each proposed change of ln nu applied (tensor mesh only). 'picard': halves automatically (down to 1/64) while the change grows, recovering up to this value; no damping is needed where the flux is imposed (air gap, applied field), but where the current imposes H on iron past the knee it needs < 2 / (1 + d ln nu / d ln B) (about 0.5 at B ~ 0.7 J_s; 0.2 deep in saturation). 'anderson': the fixed mixing factor (0.5 - 1).

#### `magnetostatics.bh_curve`

Tabulated anhysteretic B-H curve (magnetostatics types only): H, B > 0 except an optional first row [0, 0] (the curve starts at the origin), e.g. [[100, 0.5], [300, 1.0], [1000, 1.4], [5000, 1.7]]. H(B) is linear between rows; beyond the last row B = B_n + mu0 (H - H_n), so end the table well into saturation. Isotropic secant reluctivity nu = |H| / B(|H|) (the mu_dc entries are ignored there), solved like saturation_polarization (settings nonlinear_*; first iterate the first segment's slope); tensor mesh: energy and inductances are secant values; triangle mesh: Newton with the segment slope as tangent, exact energy. Not with saturation_polarization or a remanence in the same material (validation error); ignored by magnetic_fields_ac. A constant table per material (entries may be parameter expressions; no x, y or field dependence).

#### `membrane.squeeze_film_damping.ambient_pressure`

p_a, sets the film compressibility H / p_a; 0 = incompressible (pure damping, needs vents). From squeeze number sigma = 12 mu omega L^2 / (p_a H^2) ~ 1 (L = distance to a vent) damping falls and a gas spring appears. mean_free_path does not follow it: set both.

#### `solid_mechanics.stress_stiffening`

Triangle and tetrahedron meshes; eigenfrequency, frequency_response and optomechanics studies: first solves the static state (eigenfrequency: every load, prescribed displacement, initial_stress, thermal strain and coupled input; frequency_response: initial_stress and thermal strain alone, holds at 0, since the loads are its drive) and adds the lossless geometric stiffness K_sigma = int grad N . sigma grad N dV of its total stress to K in every pencil (strings and membranes stiffen, compression softens toward buckling). A free body, Bloch cell or elastic PML has no static solve: K_sigma of the initial_stress alone (unrelaxed). Off: loads and initial_stress play no part in the pencil. Not with piezoelectric or on a tensor mesh.

#### `solid_mechanics.geometric_nonlinearity`

Triangle and tetrahedron meshes: large deflections and rotations in every static solve (stationary, time_dependent, the static state of eigenfrequency / frequency_response). Total-Lagrangian Saint Venant-Kirchhoff (small strains, large rotations): Green-Lagrange strain E = (H + H^T + H^T H) / 2 (H the displacement gradient), second Piola-Kirchhoff stress S = C E + sigma0 - beta dT; damped Newton on K_T = int (B + B_NL)^T C (B + B_NL) dV + K_sigma(S) over load_steps equal increments (typically 3-6 iterations each). Boundary loads and body forces are dead loads (fixed direction, reference area); the steps scale them, prescribed displacements and coupled body forces; initial stress and thermal strain enter in full every step. Outputs: strain_* Green-Lagrange, stress_* second Piola-Kirchhoff (= Cauchy to first order); support reactions = int (B + B_NL)^T S dV - f at the held dofs (not K u - f). Eigenfrequency linearises about the nonlinear state (K_T, stress stiffening included whatever stress_stiffening says); frequency_response about the state of the initial stress alone (holds at 0). A Bloch cell, elastic PML or free body has no static solve: K + K_sigma of the initial stress. Not with piezoelectric or on a tensor mesh; on triangles not with azimuthal_order >= 1, an elastic PML or generalized plane strain.

#### `solid_mechanics.load_steps`

Geometric nonlinearity: loads and prescribed displacements ramp in this many equal steps, each Newton-converged from the previous (raise it when a large load does not converge; initial stress and thermal strain are not ramped).

#### `solid_mechanics.nonlinear_tolerance`

Geometric nonlinearity: a load step converges when the largest Newton correction is at most this fraction of the largest displacement (quadratic convergence: the remaining error ~ its square).

#### `solid_mechanics.tangent_update`

Geometric nonlinearity: when K_T is refactorised. every_iteration: full Newton (quadratic convergence). when_slow: modified Newton, the factor is kept (one back substitution) while each iteration cuts the largest free residual below 0.25 x the previous, else refactorised, and carried into the next load step when that ended fast; saves factorisations on large 3D meshes at the price of linear convergence near the end (remaining error at most ~1/3 of the nonlinear_tolerance correction). Counters tangent_factorizations / tangent_reuses.

#### `solid_mechanics.pml_reflection`

Round-trip reflection of the elastic PML for the fastest wave at the target frequency (beta = 3 ln(1 / R) c / (2 omega_t w)); slower waves are absorbed more. Too small a value steepens the profile, which the discretisation reflects: 1e-4 to 1e-8 typical.

#### `solid_mechanics.bloch_kx`

Bloch wave vector of this axis (its periodic setting on): phase step exp(-j k L) per period L; k and k + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic, pi / L the zone edge. One eigenfrequency study per k gives a band diagram (template solid_bloch_band_diagram).

#### `solid_mechanics.alpha_zz`

Overrides alpha for this axis (solid types only). 2D plane strain turns alpha_zz dT into out-of-plane stress (and, by Poisson, in-plane strain); plane stress: a free z expansion; generalized plane strain: part of the eps_zz balance; axisymmetric: the hoop expansion. 3D: an ordinary z expansion.

#### `solid_mechanics.rho`

Mass density (consistent mass), read by the solid types only in the eigenfrequency, optomechanics and frequency_response studies, where every solid cell (youngs_modulus or c11 > 0) needs rho > 0. Typical: silica 2200, silicon 2329, gold 19300.

#### `solid_mechanics.piezo_e11`

Piezoelectric stress constant e_11 in model axes: T_J = c_JK S_K - e_kJ E_k, D_k = e_kJ S_J + eps0 eps_dc_kl E_l (row k = 1 x, 2 y, 3 z; Voigt column J = 1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz, 4 yz, 5 xz, 6 xy, engineering shear S_6 = 2 strain_xy). Unset = 0. Read only with setting piezoelectric on, in solid cells (youngs_modulus or c11 > 0): solid_mechanics the in-plane block (k = 1, 2; J = 1, 2, 6; elastic_waves' arrays) and e13 / e23, solid_mechanics_3d (tetrahedra) all 18 (any entry allocates all). A {'model': 'crystal'} entry sets them (3D: 'plane': 'full').

#### `solid_mechanics.eps_dc_xy`

Off-diagonal static permittivity of a rotated material; the eps_dc tensor must stay positive definite (2D: eps_dc_xy^2 < eps_dc_xx eps_dc_yy), else a build error. Unset = 0.

#### `solid_mechanics.c11`

Anisotropic stiffness entry c11 (xx-xx) of the Voigt matrix in model axes (1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz, 4 yz, 5 xz, 6 xy; engineering shear S_6 = 2 strain_xy): T_I = c_IJ S_J - beta_I dT, beta_I = c_IJ alpha_J. Unset (NaN) = the isotropic value of youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio (c11, c22, c33: lambda + 2 mu; c12, c13, c23: lambda; c44, c55, c66: mu; others 0). A cell is solid when c11 > 0; the entries its formulation reads must be positive definite (build error). Usually set by a {'model': 'crystal'} entry (3D: 'plane': 'full'), with piezo_e* and eps_dc*. solid_mechanics reads the ten 2D entries: plane strain the full law with S_zz = S_xz = S_yz = 0 (stress_zz = T_3), plane stress condenses T_3 = 0, generalized plane strain takes a uniform S_3, axisymmetric reads 3 as hoop (orthotropic only: c16 = c26 = c36 = 0, else a build error); a c_ij-only cell needs c11, c12, c22, c66 (plane stress / axisymmetric / generalized: also c13, c23, c33); any entry allocates the eight besides c16 / c26, which only c16 or c26 allocates (as in elastic_waves); guided modes (axial_wavenumber) refuse c_ij. solid_mechanics_3d reads all 21 on tetrahedra only (a tensor mesh refuses them); any entry allocates all 21; a c_ij-only cell needs the nine orthotropic ones.

#### `solid_mechanics.mechanical_loss_factor`

Isotropic structural loss factor eta: every stiffness of the cell becomes c (1 + j eta) (exp(+j omega t)), so Q ~ 1 / eta. Read by the frequency_response study (3D: tetrahedra) and by the eigenfrequency study on triangle / tetrahedron meshes (damped complex modes, Q in the resonance table; not with piezoelectric). The stress_stiffening geometric stiffness stays lossless (dissipation dilution: Q above 1 / eta). Unset = 0; typical 1e-4 (quartz, LN) to 1e-2 (metals; polymers higher).

#### `solid_mechanics.dielectric_loss_tangent`

Dielectric loss tangent tan delta: the static permittivity becomes eps0 eps_dc (1 - j tan delta) (exp(+j omega t)), a conductance omega C tan delta parallel to the electrode capacitance. Read only by the frequency_response study with piezoelectric on (3D: tetrahedra, every window element). Unset = 0; typical 1e-4 to 1e-3 lithium niobate, ~1e-2 PZT.

#### `solid_mechanics.initial_stress_xx`

Initial (residual) stress sigma0_xx, e.g. the deposition stress of a film (tension > 0); unset = 0. The total stress is sigma0 + C eps - beta dT, so a static solve relaxes it (a released structure contracts until it balances the supports); with stress_stiffening it prestresses the modal / frequency_response pencils (a tensioned string rises in frequency). Triangle and tetrahedron meshes only (a tensor mesh refuses it). Constant per element (expressions evaluated at the centroids). 3D: a Voigt row (xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy); 2D: in-plane xx (axisymmetric: rr).

#### `solid_mechanics.initial_stress_zz`

Initial stress sigma0_zz; 2D plane strain: out-of-plane (stress_zz only, no in-plane effect); axisymmetric: hoop; plane stress and generalized plane strain refuse it. Rules: initial_stress_xx.

#### `solid_mechanics.k`

Isotropic thermal conductivity (sets k_xx, k_yy, k_zz); the solid types read it only in the thermoelastic_damping feature. Typical: silicon 130 (library; pure bulk 148), silica 1.38, silicon nitride 10 (library; films 2-15).

#### `solid_mechanics.cp`

Specific heat capacity (heat capacity rho cp); the solid types read it only in the thermoelastic_damping feature, which needs rho > 0 and cp > 0 in every solid cell. Typical: silicon 700, silica 746, silicon nitride 700.

#### `solid_mechanics.temperature_change`

Temperature change for thermal strain without a heat physics (field temperature_rise_ext, added to the coupled temperature_rise of heat_solid_thermal_strain).

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling`

Vacuum optomechanical coupling between one optical mode and every vibration mode of the optomechanics study (2D plane strain, or guided 2.5D modes with scattering backward; rho needed in every solid cell). g_om = d omega_optical / d alpha for the displacement alpha Q, Q = the mode shape with |Q| = 1 at the reference node. Moving boundary: each interior face between cells of different permittivity adds Q_n [eps0 (eps_lo - eps_hi) |E_par|^2 - (1/eps_lo - 1/eps_hi) |D_n|^2 / eps0] x its length (staircase interfaces). Photoelastic: eps0 E* d eps E dA per solid cell, d eps_ii = -eps_ii^2 (p11 S_ii + p12 (S_jj + S_kk)), shear d eps_xy = -eps_xx eps_yy 2 p44 S_xy (pairs E_x, E_y at the cell centres; none for em_fdfd_ez), S the mode strain (S_zz = S_xz = S_yz = 0). A material with a {"model": "crystal"} entry with photoelastic data and no photoelastic_* property uses the crystal's full rotated p: Delta(1/eps)_I = p_IJ S_J (Voigt, engineering shear), d eps_ij = -eps_ii eps_jj Delta(1/eps)_ij (xz / yz rows pair E_x / E_y with E_z: em_modes only); its stiffness stays isotropic. Subpixel smoothing: face jumps and photoelastic eps unsmoothed; fields, D_n and mode energy smoothed. em_fdfd_ez: g_om = -(omega / 2) Re[(I_mb + I_pe) / sum eps0 eps |E_z|^2 dA]; em_fdfd_hz: the same over sum mu0 mu |H_z|^2 dA (E_par on its Yee face, |D_n|^2 the mean of the four nearest normal-E faces, photoelastic over the E_x / E_y faces); em_modes (group_index on): d beta / d alpha = omega (I_mb + I_pe) / (4 P), g_om = -(C0 / n_group) d beta / d alpha (a ring at fixed azimuthal order), dn_eff_dx = d n_eff / d alpha at fixed omega (a bent em_modes: bend-mapped eps, exact for bend_model 'exact'). m_eff = length x Q^T M Q (x 2 per EM mirror face), x_zpf = sqrt(hbar / (2 m_eff Omega)), g0 = g_om x_zpf. Result 'table', one row per vibration mode: mechanical_mode, frequency, effective_mass, zero_point_motion, g_om_moving_boundary, g_om_photoelastic, g_om, dn_eff_dx, g0_moving_boundary, g0_photoelastic, g0, brillouin_gain (Hz, kg, m, rad/s/m, 1/m; g0 columns = g0 / 2 pi in Hz, signed, total = moving boundary + photoelastic); brillouin_gain [1/(W m)] = 2 Q_m |kappa|^2 / (omega m' Omega^2), m' = m_eff / length, kappa = d beta / d alpha (forward; scattering backward: see it), bulk limit g_B / area; em_modes with mechanical_quality_factor or quality_from only, else NaN. Extras optical_physics, optical_mode, optical_frequency, optical_wavelength, n_eff, n_group, length, mirror_factor, scattering, axial_wavenumber (None forward), normalisation, reference_node. Lossy or open optical modes: |E|^2 forms, real part (no quasi-normal-mode correction). An EM mirror face needs a solid roller on it (odd vibration modes do not couple). Field om_integrand (optomechanics study): the moving-boundary g_om density of the shown mode (first coupling) in rad/s/m^3, summing to g_om_moving_boundary. em_fdfd_bor optics (resonance ~ exp(-j m phi) on triangles; solid axisymmetric on triangles or solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra): integrals carry 2 pi r over the window elements (PML ring, PEC and interfaces touching them left out); moving boundary on the curved element edges (isotropic eps_phiphi), q . n [eps0 Delta eps |E_par|^2 - Delta(1/eps) |D_n|^2 / eps0], |E_par|^2 = |E_phi|^2 + |E_t|^2 and |D_n|^2 two-side means, q . n of the solid side; photoelastic with the cylindrical strains (rr, phiphi = u_r / r, zz, rz), isotropic p only; U = sum eps0 eps |E|^2 2 pi r dA. A solid azimuthal_order m >= 1 couples through the ring mean of cos(m phi) (~0); a 3D solid is sampled on 64 angles per (r, z) about the axis (axis_x, axis_y) and phi-averaged. m_eff = Q^T M Q in kg (no length / mirror factors; a pec / pmc z mirror plane counts the drawn half), normalisation point: the nearest solid dof (triangles only), no om_integrand, dn_eff_dx and brillouin_gain NaN; extras optical_azimuthal_order, optical_q_factor, solid_mesh, mechanical_azimuthal_order, prescribed_normal_displacement, prescribed_g_om.

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.optical_physics`

The em_modes (cross-section mode, group_index on), em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz (in-plane resonance near its wavelength) or em_fdfd_bor (BOR resonance on triangles; solid axisymmetric on triangles or solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra) physics; the optomechanics study solves it first.

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.length`

Length L along z turning the per-metre mass into kg: ring circumference 2 pi R or waveguide length (em_modes), device thickness (em_fdfd_ez / _hz). m_eff = L x the 2D modal mass; g_om independent, g0 ~ 1 / sqrt(L). Unused with em_fdfd_bor optics.

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.normalisation`

Where the mode shape is scaled to |u| = 1 for g_om and m_eff: max the peak node, point the solid node nearest (reference_x, reference_y); g0 does not depend on it.

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.mechanical_quality_factor`

Q_m of every vibration mode for the brillouin_gain column (em_modes only); empty: NaN (the modal analysis is undamped). Typical 100-1000 (silicon wires at room temperature).

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.quality_from`

Name of a thermoelastic_damping feature of this solid whose per-mode q_total is Q_m instead of mechanical_quality_factor (set one of the two); '' = unused. Forward scattering, em_modes only.

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.scattering`

forward: the plane-strain (k_z = 0) modes; g0 = the optical frequency shift, brillouin_gain the forward intramodal gain. backward (em_modes only): the study sets the solid's k_z = 2 Re beta before its modal solve (guided 2.5D modes; axial_wavenumber stays empty; supports optional; |Q| and m_eff include u_z) and kappa = omega (I_mb + I_pe) / (4 P) pairs the mode with its counter-propagating twin (E_x, E_y, -E_z) and the conjugated phonon strain (S_zz = k_z u_z in the p11 / p12 terms, S_xz / S_yz with p44 pairing E_x, E_y with E_z; the E_z terms flip sign); g_om = -(C0 / n_group) Re kappa, the g0 / dn_eff_dx columns the forward-backward coupling rate (a ring: between its counter-propagating modes), brillouin_gain the backward gain. All couplings of one solid need the same scattering (backward: same optical physics and mode). Guided modes near 2 v_L n_eff / lambda (tens of GHz) need the solid target_frequency (0 finds the lowest, flexural ones).

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.prescribed_normal_displacement`

em_fdfd_bor optics: a uniform outward motion q . n of every optical permittivity interface bordering the solid, without a mechanical mode; extra prescribed_g_om [rad/s/m] = its moving-boundary d omega / d alpha (q . n = 1 on a sphere: -omega / R). Empty: prescribed_g_om None.

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.axis_x`

solid_mechanics_3d with em_fdfd_bor optics: x of the BOR axis point (axis_x, axis_y, 0), axis parallel to z; optical (r, z) = (x - its x_lo, y) maps to (axis_x + r cos phi, axis_y + r sin phi, z).

#### `solid_mechanics.electrode.connection`

voltage: phi = voltage on every node (0 = ground); the eigenfrequency study holds 0 (short circuit: resonances). floating: one shared unknown potential carrying the charge setting (0 = isolated); eigenfrequency: charge 0 (open circuit: antiresonances). At least one voltage electrode is required (the reference of phi).

#### `solid_mechanics.admittance`

frequency_response study, piezoelectric only. Result 'xy' versus frequency [Hz] of Y = I / V = j omega Q / V of the driven electrode (Q from the discrete Gauss law of D, dielectric loss included): series abs, re, im, phase, bvd_abs (|Y|, Re Y, Im Y in S/m per m of depth, S with the 2D thickness setting or in 3D; phase deg; bvd_abs = |Y| of the fit, NaN without one). Extras (derived values: operation last): the Butterworth-Van Dyke fit Y = j omega C0 (1 - j tan_delta_0) + 1 / (R1 + j omega L1 + 1 / (j omega C1)) over the fit band (least squares on the relative complex residual, started at f_s = the max-|Y| sample, f_p = the min-|Y| sample above it): f_s, f_p, k_eff2, Q_s, C0, C1, L1, R1, tan_delta_0, f_peak, f_dip, fit_error, fit_points (f_s = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L1 C1)), f_p = f_s sqrt(1 + C1 / C0) the lossless antiresonance, k_eff2 = (f_p^2 - f_s^2) / f_p^2 = C1 / (C0 + C1), Q_s = 2 pi f_s L1 / R1, f_peak / f_dip the sampled max / min of |Y|, fit_error the rms relative residual), kappa_e = load_impedance / L1 [rad/s] (the coupling rate into a resistive load in series with the motional branch; internal R1 / L1 = 2 pi f_s / Q_s), omega_C0_Z = 2 pi f_s C0 load_impedance (kappa_e valid while it is << 1; both NaN per m of depth, kappa_e_warning), load_impedance, bvd_units, electrode. Under 6 band points or no peak with a dip above it: fit values NaN, fit_warning says why. One resonance per band, resolved with a step well below f_s / Q_s.

#### `solid_mechanics_3d.bloch_kx`

Bloch wave vector of this axis (its periodic setting on): phase step exp(-j k L) per period L; k and k + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic, pi / L the zone edge. One eigenfrequency study per k gives a band diagram (template solid_bloch_band_diagram_3d).

#### `solid_mechanics_3d.electrode.connection`

voltage: phi = voltage on every node (0 = ground); the eigenfrequency study holds 0 (short circuit: resonances). floating: one shared unknown potential carrying the charge setting (0 = isolated); eigenfrequency: charge 0 (open circuit: antiresonances). At least one voltage electrode is required (the reference of phi). resistive_load: one shared potential V tied to ground through load_resistance R, j omega Q = -V / R (exp(+j omega t)); eigenfrequency (target_frequency > 0): damped complex modes, energy_decay_rate = 2 Im omega = kappa_e of a line of impedance R (pencil frozen at the target, each mode Newton-refined: exact at the target, second order elsewhere); frequency_response: it loads the driven response; static studies refuse it.

#### `eigenfrequency.max_iterations`

Background fixed point before the study solve, background physics only (unused without them): Gauss-Seidel iterations over the physics of a coupling loop (model order, each coupling applied once its sources are solved); sinks (feeding no coupling back) are solved once afterwards; no loop = a single pass. Typically 10-50. Warns when the tolerance is not reached; stops early with a warning when the change has not decreased for 3 iterations (from iteration 4); non-finite fields fail the run.

#### `eigenfrequency.tolerance`

Background fixed point before the study solve, background physics only (unused without them): Converged when every primary field of the loop physics changes by at most this fraction of its range max|f| (heat T as its rise T - T0). The remaining error is about change * g / (1 - g) for loop gain g (at g = 0.9, 1e-4 means ~1e-3); with anderson_depth about the change. Typically 1e-4.

#### `eigenfrequency.relaxation`

Relaxation w of the loop-back couplings (those writing a physics solved earlier in the iteration, e.g. heat_em_thermo_optic in an FDFD + heat loop): each injects previous + w (new - previous); 1 = plain Picard. For loop gain g (ratio of successive relative changes, negative when alternating) w ~ 1/(1 - g): w > 1 speeds a slow monotone loop, w < 1 damps an oscillating one (a thermo-optic shift past a resonance); nothing cures a physical runaway (monotone g > 1). The change compared with the tolerance is divided by w. With anderson_depth > 0: the Anderson mixing parameter (change divided by w only when w < 1).

#### `eigenfrequency.anderson_depth`

Background fixed point before the study solve, background physics only (unused without them): Anderson acceleration of the loop-back couplings (Walker-Ni, depth m, mixing parameter = relaxation): before each sweep every loop-back value becomes the least-squares combination of the last m iterates and changes (host float64, ~3 m + 3 copies per value); 0 = plain relaxation. A monotone loop of gain g needs ~ln(tolerance)/ln(g) Picard iterations (~120 at g = 0.9, 1e-6), far fewer accelerated. It can converge to fixed points Picard cannot reach (an unstable bistable branch, an unphysical one past a runaway), so it is opt-in. Typically 3-5.

#### `eigenfrequency.warm_start`

Parameter sweeps only: start each value from the previous value's solution when the mesh is unchanged (heat T and Q, potential V and its source, magnetic potentials; couplings reading only these applied first). drift_diffusion ramps contact / gate voltages and generation from the previous converged state (an I-V sweep: about one continuation step per value). A geometrically nonlinear solid (solid_mechanics on triangles, solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra) starts Newton from the previous displacement, extrapolated linearly in the swept parameter (at most one step ahead), ramping load_steps from that state; a failed start falls back to the cold ramp. Results differ from a cold start within the tolerance; off, every value starts cold (T0, V = 0, u = 0) and is reproducible alone.

#### `eigenfrequency.parity_sectors`

Run the study once per symmetric / antisymmetric combination of the model's k mirror faces (bc_<face> symmetric / antisymmetric or a membrane symmetry / antisymmetry feature; 2^k runs, each solving the drawn sources plus their images) and merge them; needs a mirror face. stationary / frequency_domain / time_dependent / frequency_response give the response of the drawn sources alone on the unfolded domain: per snapshot one combined snapshot (stationary: 'combined') with the mean of the unfolded sector fields of every linear signed stored field (|E|, intensities, losses, phases left out), then the sector snapshots '<label> [<sector>]'. Derived values: quadratic integrals / means (power, flux, absorbed power, intensity over regions symmetric about every mirror plane) as quadratic totals, mean / 2^k; linear ones the sector mean; feature-sourced ones from the combined feature results; anything else (max / min, mode volumes, phases, scalar outputs) NaN with a warning. Combined feature results (Results.sector_result(physics, feature, combined=True)): far_field (mean complex amplitude), flux_spectrum reaching every mirror plane (quadratic totals), membrane field_probe phasors, port / mode_projection guide modes (renumbered to the unfolded guide: a free mirror wall gives modes 2k - 1, a held one 2k). A membrane port mode on a guide ending on a mirror face is driven at twice its amplitude in its parity's sector only. Assumes a linear model (couplings see each sector's own field; validation warns). mode_analysis / eigenfrequency: every sector's modes or resonances labelled with their parity ('mode k [x_lo symmetric]: ...'); derived values NaN. Summary parity_sectors: labels, derived, results, combined_results, snapshot_sectors; the live state is the last sector. Sweeps: each value runs its sectors (cold starts); sweep derived = the combined values, sweep results the last sector's, sweep sector_derived per sector.

## Physics type `drift_diffusion` - Semiconductor (drift-diffusion, 2D)

Stationary drift-diffusion per unit z length (or axisymmetric, setting geometry), finite volumes on the physical window: Poisson -div(eps0 eps_dc grad psi) = q (p - n + N_D - N_A) and continuity div J_n = q (R - G), div J_p = q (G - R) with Scharfetter-Gummel face currents (D = mu V_T, Boltzmann statistics), solved fully coupled by Newton with sparse direct solves. psi (output V) is referred to the intrinsic level, equilibrium Fermi level at 0 V: neutral n-type silicon at 1e22 1/m^3 has V = V_T asinh(N_D / 2 n_i) = +0.36 V, an ohmic contact adds its voltage. Cells with n_intrinsic > 0 are semiconductor, the others insulators (Poisson only, e.g. oxide or air). Outer faces are insulating (zero normal D and current). At least one ohmic contact. Recombination: SRH (mid-gap trap) + radiative + Auger features; generation: generation features + the coupled slot. Each solve continues from the last solution, ramping voltages (max_bias_step) and generation, the first from equilibrium; a failed step is halved, a solve that cannot converge raises. Outputs: J = Jn + Jp (face currents averaged to the centres), phi_n = V - V_T ln(N / n_i), phi_p = V + V_T ln(P / n_i), space_charge q (P - N + N_D - N_A), recombination R (0 in contacts and insulators); all edge-extended into an EM PML ring. Contact currents are exact face sums; the electron currents into all contacts sum to q times the integral of G - R. Optics: semiconductor_em_plasma_dispersion (carriers -> EM index contribution) and em_semiconductor_generation (absorption -> G), iterated by a stationary study. LIMITS: homojunctions only, constant mobilities (an expression may make them field- or state-dependent), no Fermi-Dirac statistics or incomplete ionisation, no transient (time_dependent re-solves the steady state when an input changed). Needs about 1-3 cells per Debye length sqrt(eps V_T / (q N)) near junctions (13 nm at 1e23 1/m^3). Triangle meshes: box method on the P1 nodes (edge-averaged elements, curved outlines faceted); a node takes the volume-weighted mean of its semiconductor elements (a junction on element edges has mixed doping at its nodes); a contact holds every node of its semiconductor elements, a gate every node of its elements; V, N, P, phi_n / phi_p are nodal (linear across an insulator element next to the semiconductor), E and J per element; non-Delaunay edges (negative coefficient, e.g. obtuse triangles at an interface) give one run warning. Linear solver: host SuperLU or cuDSS (cusolver_qr: tensor only); Automatic = cuDSS on the GPU backend with nvmath-python (a Jacobian cuDSS refuses switches the run to host SuperLU, with a warning), else host SuperLU; cudss_mixed falls back to double when float64 refinement misses 1e-12; MUMPS / PARDISO (opt-in) keep the host SuperLU size limits and raise on a refusal.

- Default instance name `semiconductor`; studies stationary, time_dependent (default {"type": "stationary"})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields V; dispersion poles not used
- Features: doping, ohmic_contact, gate, auger_recombination, generation

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (default "planar"; planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  planar: 2D drift-diffusion per unit z length (contact currents A/m, gate charges C/m). axisymmetric (x = r, y = z; spec notes): (r, z) drift-diffusion, every conductance, face and cell volume weighted by 2 pi r: densities and rates keep their units, contact currents and gate charges (table results, scalar outputs) are whole-ring A and C. x_lo is the axis (no radial current or D flux).
- `temperature` [K] (default 300; > 0) - Temperature
  Lattice temperature: thermal voltage V_T = k_B T / q (25.85 mV at 300 K) of D = mu V_T and the Boltzmann statistics. n_intrinsic is NOT rescaled (make it depend on heat_T yourself). 300 K is the temperature of the library semiconductor data, not heat T0 (293.15 K): with a heat physics use one parameter for both if they should agree.
- `tolerance` [1] (default 1e-08; > 0) - Newton tolerance
  Newton stops when the largest potential update <= tolerance * V_T and the largest carrier update |dn| / (n + n_i) (holes alike) <= tolerance. 1e-8 suits float64.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; >= 1) - Newton iteration limit
  Newton iterations per continuation step (and the equilibrium start); a step that does not converge is halved, down to 1/64, then the run fails.
- `max_bias_step` [V] (default 0.1; > 0) - Largest bias step
  Largest change of any contact or gate voltage per continuation step; about 4 V_T keeps Newton safe for forward-biased junctions.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_dc` [1] (>= 1; nullable; writes eps_dc_xx, eps_dc_yy) - Static relative permittivity
  Sets eps_dc_xx and eps_dc_yy (component entries override it); unset = 1. Silicon 11.7, silica 3.9.
- `eps_dc_xx`, `eps_dc_yy` [1] (>= 1; nullable) - Static relative permittivity along x / Static relative permittivity along y
  Overrides eps_dc for this axis.
- `n_intrinsic` [1/m^3] (>= 0; nullable) - Intrinsic carrier density
  n_i: cells with n_i > 0 are semiconductor, the rest insulators (Poisson only). Silicon 1.0e16 at 300 K (1e10 cm^-3), GaAs 2.1e12, germanium 2.0e19. One band structure (no heterojunction offsets).
- `mobility_n` [m^2/(V s)] (>= 0; nullable) - Electron mobility
