  No built-in doping or field dependence (give an expression). Lightly doped silicon 0.135 (1350 cm^2/Vs), at 1e24 1/m^3 ~0.03.
- `mobility_p` [m^2/(V s)] (>= 0; nullable) - Hole mobility
  As mobility_n. Lightly doped silicon 0.048 (480 cm^2/Vs).
- `lifetime` [s] (> 0; nullable; writes lifetime_n, lifetime_p) - Carrier lifetime
  SRH lifetime (mid-gap trap) of both carriers: sets lifetime_n and lifetime_p; unset = 1e-6 s. Silicon 1e-9 (heavily doped) .. 1e-3 (float zone).
- `lifetime_n`, `lifetime_p` [s] (> 0; nullable) - Electron lifetime / Hole lifetime
  Overrides lifetime for this carrier.
- `radiative_recombination` [m^3/s] (>= 0; nullable) - Radiative recombination coefficient
  B of R_rad = B (n p - n_i^2); unset = 0. Silicon 1.1e-20, GaAs 7.2e-16.

### Fields

Output fields (primary V; [state] = also a state field):
- `V` - Electric potential (V) [state]
- `N` - Electron density (1/m^3) [state]
- `P` - Hole density (1/m^3) [state]
- `E_x` - Electric field x (V/m) [state]
- `E_y` - Electric field y (V/m) [state]
- `J_x` - Current density x (A/m^2) [state]
- `J_y` - Current density y (A/m^2) [state]
- `Jn_x` - Electron current density x (A/m^2) [state]
- `Jn_y` - Electron current density y (A/m^2) [state]
- `Jp_x` - Hole current density x (A/m^2) [state]
- `Jp_y` - Hole current density y (A/m^2) [state]
- `phi_n` - Electron quasi-Fermi potential (V) [state]
- `phi_p` - Hole quasi-Fermi potential (V) [state]
- `net_doping` - Net doping (1/m^3) [state]
- `space_charge` - Space charge density (C/m^3) [state]
- `recombination` - Net recombination rate (1/(m^3 s)) [state]
- `generation` - Coupled generation rate (1/(m^3 s)) [state]
- `generation_ext` - Applied generation rate (1/(m^3 s)) [state]

Scalar outputs: current_<contact> (A/m) per enabled ohmic_contact: its total current of the last solve, as its table result; charge_<gate> (C/m) per enabled gate: its free charge, as its table result; geometry 'axisymmetric': whole-ring A and C. Example derived value {"name": "I_anode", "expression": "semiconductor_current_anode"}; a sweep of a contact voltage gives the I-V curve (with reuse_build each point continues from the previous state).

### Source slots

- `generation` (1/(m^3 s)): Pair generation G (field generation) written by em_semiconductor_generation (absorbed power / photon energy), added to generation_ext; free semiconductor cells only.

### Feature `drift_diffusion.doping` - Doping

Adds N_D - N_A to the net doping of the selected cells (features add; fully ionised; ignored in insulators). A step between features is an abrupt junction on cell edges (triangles: the nodes there take the mean of both sides).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result none

Params:
- `donors` [1/m^3] (default 0; >= 0; may use x, y) - Donor density
  Ionised donors N_D (1e22 = 1e16 cm^-3), e.g. a Gaussian implant profile in x, y. A uniform value follows reuse_build (then starts cold from equilibrium).
- `acceptors` [1/m^3] (default 0; >= 0; may use x, y) - Acceptor density
  Ionised acceptors N_A; follows reuse_build as donors.

### Feature `drift_diffusion.ohmic_contact` - Ohmic contact

Holds every selected semiconductor cell (other selected cells stay insulators) at charge-neutral equilibrium with its own doping, shifted by the voltage: n p = n_i^2, n - p = N_D - N_A, V = voltage + V_T asinh((N_D - N_A) / 2 n_i), at the cell centres (the drop starts at the outermost held centres). A later contact or gate takes shared cells (validation warns). Result 'table', one row [feature, voltage, current, electron_current, hole_current] (units '', V, A/m x 3; A when axisymmetric) and the same extras: the current out of the contact into the device (positive = conventional current leaving the contact), summed over the face currents between its held cells and their neighbours (triangle meshes: through the contact outline).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result kind `table`

Params:
- `voltage` [V] (default 0) - Voltage
  Applied voltage (Fermi level at -voltage in energy); follows reuse_build.

### Feature `drift_diffusion.gate` - Gate

Holds every selected cell at V = voltage - work_function_difference (an ideal conductor: the value sits on its faces). The cells must be insulating (n_intrinsic 0; run error otherwise): put the gate on an oxide. No current flows into a gate. Result 'table', one row [feature, voltage, charge] (units '', V, C/m; C when axisymmetric) and the extras voltage and charge: the free charge on the gate, its outward D flux.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result kind `table`

Params:
- `voltage` [V] (default 0) - Voltage
  Applied gate voltage; follows reuse_build.
- `work_function_difference` [V] (default 0) - Work-function difference
  phi_ms: gate work function minus the intrinsic-level work function of the semiconductor (electron affinity + E_g / 2 q). 0 = mid-gap gate; n+ polysilicon on silicon ~ -0.56, p+ ~ +0.56. Referred to the intrinsic level, not the Fermi level: the flat-band voltage (= the textbook work-function difference) is phi_ms + V_bulk, V_bulk = V_T asinh(net doping / 2 n_i) (p-type silicon at N_A = 1e23 1/m^3: -0.42 V).

### Feature `drift_diffusion.auger_recombination` - Auger recombination

Sets the Auger coefficients of the selected semiconductor cells (a later feature takes shared cells; unselected cells have none): R_Auger = (C_n N + C_p P) (N P - n_i^2) adds to the recombination. Constants per feature, no x, y (float32 subnormal, so no material property); triangles: a node takes the semiconductor-volume mean.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result none

Params:
- `electron_coefficient` [m^6/s] (default 2.8e-43; >= 0) - Electron Auger coefficient
  C_n (eeh process); silicon 2.8e-43 (2.8e-31 cm^6/s), GaAs ~1e-42.
- `hole_coefficient` [m^6/s] (default 9.9e-44; >= 0) - Hole Auger coefficient
  C_p (ehh process); silicon 9.9e-44 (9.9e-32 cm^6/s).

### Feature `drift_diffusion.generation` - Generation

Adds the rate to generation_ext on the selected cells (features and the coupled slot add); acts on free semiconductor cells only.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result none

Params:
- `rate` [1/(m^3 s)] (default 1e+27; >= 0; may use x, y) - Generation rate
  Electron-hole pairs, e.g. G0 * exp(-alpha * (y0 - y)) for light entering from the top. 1 W/m^2 absorbed at 1.55 um is 7.8e18 pairs / (m^2 s).

## Physics type `elastic_waves` - Elastic and Acoustic Waves, time domain (2D, in-plane)

2D velocity-stress FDTD (Virieux staggered grid; plane strain, or axisymmetric (r, z) by setting geometry): vx / vy [m/s] on the +x / +y cell faces at half steps, sxx / syy [Pa] at the cell centres, sxy on the +x +y corners; tension positive, pressure = -(sxx + syy) / 2. Fluids (shear_speed unset), isotropic solids (sound_speed / shear_speed, or youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio as in solid_mechanics and the library solids), orthotropic (c11, c12, c22, c66) and monoclinic (+ c16, c26) solids share one grid: a face takes the width-weighted mean density of its two cells, a corner the harmonic mean of its four shear moduli (0 at fluid-solid and vacuum corners), so interfaces need no special treatment and vacuum cells (no density, no stiffness) are traction-free surfaces. dt = courant x the stability limit of the build materials; alone the physics sets dt_sync, with another time-stepping physics the shorter step wins. Tensor mesh, uniform or nonuniform (auto mode meshes by the optical index). elastic_strain_xx / _yy = the stiffness inverted on the centre stresses (fluids: half the volumetric strain each; thermoelastic stress counts as minus the thermal strain); with piezo_e* or c16 / c26 arrays the accumulated total strain instead (thermoelastic heating then shows as expansion). Couplings: acoustics_em_acousto_optic (photoelastic index of an em_fdfd_* physics, re-solved on the frozen strain every k acoustic steps; the tensor entries also drive the eps_xy of em_fdfd_hz), em_acoustics_photoacoustic (absorbed light power into heating_power), electrostatics_acoustics_piezo (stress -e^T E; two-way by default: the bound charge of the accumulated strain re-solves the electrostatics every step, so the waves are stiffened and dt uses c^D); the state fields can drive a state-dependent material property or a field_transfer. Stepper precision single, or half_storage (fields stored as fp16 in units scaled from the peak source stress and the largest impedance: 10 B per cell less, ~1e-3 relative noise floor), which refuses the resonance finder, piezoelectric and monoclinic materials and every coupling into this physics. cpu backend: numpy twins (numba for the velocity / stress updates when installed), single precision only, several times slower: small models and tests.

- Default instance name `acoustics`; studies time_dependent (default {"type": "time_dependent", "settings": {"duration": 2e-05}})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor; refinement indicator fields pressure; dispersion poles not used
- Features: force_source, volume_source, traction_line_source, heat_pulse_source, rigid_domain, initial_velocity, field_probe, resonance_monitor

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (default "planar"; planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  planar: plane strain per unit z length. axisymmetric (x = r, y = z; spec notes): (r, z) waves without torsion (v_phi = 0); the hoop stress s_tt (field and probe component stt) is stepped with c_tt = c11, c_rt = c_zt = c12 (exact for isotropic solids and fluids, approximate for c_ij crystals: validation warns); an x-face density is the ring-volume mean of its two cells. The stiffness must be positive definite in 3D (isotropic: shear_speed < 0.866 sound_speed). Point sources are per unit ring length (the axis cell is a ring of radius dx / 2), traction sheets per area (a vertical line is a cylinder, a horizontal one a disc or annulus); pressure = -(s_rr + s_zz + s_tt) / 3; the stable step is a few % shorter (see courant); an absorbing x_hi stretches only the radial derivatives. x_lo is the axis (bc_x_lo rigid and no other physics padding the grid at x_lo, else validation errors).
- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (default "absorbing"; absorbing | rigid | periodic) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  absorbing: CPML in the outermost pml_cells cells, backed by a rigid wall; these lie inside the domain unless another physics (an EM CPML) pads the grid there: keep sources, probes and objects out (validation warns). rigid: slip wall (normal velocity and shear stress 0; also a mirror symmetry plane), also where another physics pads the grid (the padding stays idle). periodic: wraps to the opposite face (set both; an error where another physics pads the grid). A traction-free surface is a material boundary: cells without density and stiffness are vacuum. geometry axisymmetric: x_lo must be rigid (the axis: v_r = 0, s_rz = 0); a rigid x_hi is a slip wall on r = r_max, an absorbing one a radial CPML.
- `pml_cells` [cells] (int; default 20; >= 2) - Absorbing layer thickness
  CPML cells per absorbing layer (polynomial grading of order 2, kappa 1); typically 10-30, about one wavelength at the lowest frequency of interest.
- `pml_reflection` [1] (default 0.0001; (0, 0.5]) - Absorbing layer reflection
  Target normal-incidence reflection R: peak damping d0 = 3 c ln(1 / R) / (2 L), c the largest longitudinal speed, L the layer thickness. 1e-3..1e-6 typical; thin layers with very small R reflect from their own grading.
- `courant` [1] (default 0.9; (0, 1]) - Time step factor
  dt = courant / (c_bound sqrt(1 / dx_min^2 + 1 / dy_min^2)) from the build materials, c_bound^2 = the largest stability stiffness S of a cell times the largest 1 / rho of its faces (face density = mean of its two cells: a solid next to vacuum has rho / 2). S = the largest eigenvalue of [[c11 wx + c66 wy, |c12 + c66| sqrt(wx wy)], [same, c66 wx + c22 wy]], wx = (1 / dx_min^2) / (1 / dx_min^2 + 1 / dy_min^2), wy = 1 - wx, at least max(c11, c22): c11 for isotropic solids and fluids, more for crystals (silicon [100]: 194 GPa on square cells vs c11 = 166 GPa); courant 1 is the exact limit of a uniform material. c16 / c26 enter by absolute value (diagonals + 2 |c16| s, + 2 |c26| s, off-diagonal + |c16| wx + |c26| wy, s = sqrt(wx wy)), a bound: dt ~2 % short of exact for YZ lithium niobate, ~8 % with c16 / c26 of 10 % of c11. Two-way piezo (back_action bound_charge): S of the stiffened c^D = c^E + e^T (eps0 eps_dc)^-1 e (a bound). geometry axisymmetric: 1 / dx_min^2 times F >= 1 (~1.047 on uniform cells), a bound: keep courant <= 0.95. Runtime material rewrites (state-dependent speeds) are not stability-checked: keep their speeds below the build values.
- `heating_envelope` (default "instantaneous"; instantaneous | gaussian) - Coupled heating envelope
  Time dependence of the coupled 'heating_power' slot: instantaneous = the delivered array is the heating rate (held until the next transfer); gaussian = the array (e.g. a cw absorbed power map) x exp(-((t - heating_pulse_delay) / heating_pulse_width)^2), a pulse of energy density array x sqrt(pi) width.
- `heating_pulse_width` [s] (default 1e-08; > 0; visible when heating_envelope in (gaussian)) - Heating pulse width
  1/e half-width w; the pressure rise resolves only if c w spans a few cells.
- `heating_pulse_delay` [s] (>= 0; nullable; visible when heating_envelope in (gaussian)) - Heating pulse delay
  Envelope centre time; empty = 3 x heating_pulse_width.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `rho` [kg/m^3] (>= 0; nullable) - Density. Help: shared `elastic_waves.rho`
- `sound_speed` [m/s] (>= 0; nullable) - Sound speed (longitudinal). Help: shared `elastic_waves.sound_speed`
- `shear_speed` [m/s] (>= 0; nullable) - Shear speed
  Transverse (S) wave speed: c66 = rho shear_speed^2, c12 = rho (sound_speed^2 - 2 shear_speed^2) unless c_ij are set; unset = 0 = a fluid. Must be below sound_speed. Typical: silica 3760, aluminium 3040, silicon ~5840.
- `c11` [Pa] (>= 0; nullable) - Stiffness c11
  In-plane plane-strain stiffnesses c11, c12, c22, c66 (Voigt x = 1, y = 2, xy = 6); set, they override the values from sound_speed / shear_speed and rho (or youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio). Isotropic: c11 = c22 = lambda + 2 mu, c12 = lambda, c66 = mu; silicon along [100] / [010]: c11 = c22 = 165.7e9, c12 = 63.9e9, c66 = 79.6e9. The effective set with c16 / c26 must be positive definite (c11, c22, c66 > 0, c12^2 < c11 c22, det [[c11, c12, c16], [c12, c22, c26], [c16, c26, c66]] > 0; a fluid: c66 = c16 = c26 = 0, c12 = c11 = c22), else validation errors.
- `c12` [Pa] (nullable) - Stiffness c12
  Plane-strain stiffness; overrides the value from the speeds or E / nu. See c11.
- `c22`, `c66` [Pa] (>= 0; nullable) - Stiffness c22 / Stiffness c66
  Plane-strain stiffness; overrides the value from the speeds or E / nu. See c11.
- `c16` [Pa] (nullable) - Stiffness c16
  In-plane monoclinic stiffnesses c16 / c26 (Voigt: T_xx = c11 S_xx + c12 S_yy + c16 g, T_yy = c12 S_xx + c22 S_yy + c26 g, T_xy = c16 S_xx + c26 S_yy + c66 g, g = 2 S_xy); default 0 (none from the speeds or E / nu). Non-zero when the model axes are not crystal symmetry axes in the plane, e.g. YZ lithium niobate c26 = c14 (a {'model': 'crystal'} entry sets both). Energy-conserving corner / centre 4-point means; corners without shear stiffness (fluids, vacuum, slip walls) carry none. The set must stay positive definite (see c11); dt takes |c16|, |c26| as bounds (see courant). Either one allocates 8 float32 grids (both arrays, strain accumulator, rate buffers); elastic_strain_xx / _yy then show the accumulated total strain. Planar geometry and single-precision stepper only. CPML can be unstable in some strongly anisotropic media (Becache, Fauqueux and Joly 2003): check long runs for growth near the layers.
- `c26` [Pa] (nullable) - Stiffness c26
  Monoclinic stiffness; see c16.
- `youngs_modulus` [Pa] (>= 0; nullable) - Young's modulus. Help: shared `elastic_waves.youngs_modulus`
- `poisson_ratio` [1] ((-1, 0.499]; nullable) - Poisson ratio. Help: shared `elastic_waves.poisson_ratio`
- `acoustic_damping` [1/s] (>= 0; nullable) - Acoustic damping rate
  Mass-proportional damping g of the particle velocity (rho dv/dt = div s - rho g v, semi-implicit): a wave with omega >> g decays as exp(-g t / 2). Default 0.
- `gruneisen` [1] (nullable) - Grueneisen parameter
  Thermoelastic G = beta c^2 / cp (beta the volumetric expansion): a heating rate q [W/m^3] adds -G q to d(sxx)/dt and d(syy)/dt, so an instantly absorbed energy density H raises the pressure by G H. Read by heat_pulse_source and the 'heating_power' slot; default 0. Typical: water 0.11 at 20 C, soft tissue ~0.2.
- `photoelastic_p11` [1] (nullable) - Photoelastic coefficient p11. Help: shared `elastic_waves.photoelastic_p11`
- `photoelastic_p12` [1] (nullable) - Photoelastic coefficient p12. Help: shared `elastic_waves.photoelastic_p12`
- `photoelastic_p16` [1] (nullable) - Photoelastic coefficient p16
  In-plane photoelastic tensor photoelastic_p16 .. _p66 in model axes, read only by acoustics_em_acousto_optic: Delta(1/n^2)_I = p_I1 S_xx + p_I2 S_yy + p_I6 g, index-ellipsoid row I = 1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz (the diagonal permittivity slots) or 6 xy (the eps_xy slot of em_fdfd_hz: Delta eps_xy = -n0_xx^2 n0_yy^2 Delta(1/n^2)_xy), g = 2 S_xy at the cell centre (4-corner mean); photoelastic_p11 / _p12 are row 1. Unset = the isotropic value (here 0). Usually set by a {'model': 'crystal'} entry (only when the cut is not isotropic in these rows); YZ lithium niobate (model x = crystal Z, y = -Y): p11 = p33, p12 = p31, p16 = 0, p21 = p13, p22 = p11, p26 = p14, p31 = p13, p32 = p12, p36 = -p14, p61 = 0, p62 = p41, p66 = p44. Any one set allocates all ten arrays.
- `photoelastic_p21` [1] (nullable) - Photoelastic coefficient p21
  Photoelastic tensor entry (see photoelastic_p16); unset = photoelastic_p12.
- `photoelastic_p22` [1] (nullable) - Photoelastic coefficient p22
  Photoelastic tensor entry (see photoelastic_p16); unset = photoelastic_p11.
- `photoelastic_p26` [1] (nullable) - Photoelastic coefficient p26
  Photoelastic tensor entry (see photoelastic_p16); unset = 0.
- `photoelastic_p31`, `photoelastic_p32` [1] (nullable) - Photoelastic coefficient p31 / Photoelastic coefficient p32
  Photoelastic tensor entry (see photoelastic_p16); unset = photoelastic_p12.
- `photoelastic_p36`, `photoelastic_p61`, `photoelastic_p62` [1] (nullable) - Photoelastic coefficient p36 / Photoelastic coefficient p61 / Photoelastic coefficient p62
  Photoelastic tensor entry (see photoelastic_p16); unset = 0.
- `photoelastic_p66` [1] (nullable) - Photoelastic coefficient p66
  Photoelastic tensor entry (see photoelastic_p16); unset = (photoelastic_p11 - photoelastic_p12) / 2.
- `piezo_e11` [C/m^2] (nullable) - Piezoelectric e11
  Piezoelectric stress constants e_kJ (piezo_e11 .. _e26) of the in-plane block in model axes (reduced Voigt: D_k = e_kJ S_J + eps0 eps_dc E, T_J = c_JK S_K - e_kJ E_k, k = 1 x / 2 y, J = 1 xx, 2 yy, 6 xy, S_6 = 2 S_xy); default 0. Read through electrostatics_acoustics_piezo: the stress -e^T E of the electric_field_x / _y slots and, two-way (default), the bound charge -div(e S) of the accumulated strain back into the electrostatics plus the stiffened dt. Usually set by a {'model': 'crystal'} entry of the material's dispersion list (also sets c_ij, rho and the clamped eps_dc_xx / _yy / _xy); YZ lithium niobate (euler_deg 0, 90, 90; model x = crystal Z, y = -Y): piezo_e11 = e33 = 1.3, piezo_e12 = e31 = 0.2, piezo_e22 = -e22 = -2.5, piezo_e26 = e15 = 3.7. Any one set allocates all six arrays and the strain accumulator (9 float32 grids; elastic_strain_xx / _yy then show the accumulated total strain). Planar geometry only.
- `piezo_e12`, `piezo_e16`, `piezo_e21`, `piezo_e22`, `piezo_e26` [C/m^2] (nullable) - Piezoelectric e12 / Piezoelectric e16 / Piezoelectric e21 / Piezoelectric e22 / Piezoelectric e26
  Piezoelectric stress constant; see piezo_e11.

### Fields

Output fields (primary pressure; [state] = also a state field):
- `pressure` - Pressure (Pa) [state]
- `sxx` - Normal stress xx (Pa) [state]
- `syy` - Normal stress yy (Pa) [state]
- `sxy` - Shear stress xy (Pa) [state]
- `stt` - Hoop stress (axisymmetric) (Pa)
- `vx` - Particle velocity x (m/s) [state]
- `vy` - Particle velocity y (m/s) [state]
- `v_abs` - Particle speed |v| (m/s)
- `elastic_strain_xx` - Elastic strain xx (1)
- `elastic_strain_yy` - Elastic strain yy (1)

### Source slots

- `heating_power` (W/m^3): Heating rate q (em_acoustics_photoacoustic contributions summed, or one field_transfer), kept by reference; adds -gruneisen q x the heating_envelope to d(sxx)/dt and d(syy)/dt every step.
- `electric_field_x` (V/m): Electric field x at the cell centres (electrostatics_acoustics_piezo): each transfer adds -e^T (E - E_last) to the stresses (sxy at the corners from the 4-cell mean, none where a corner has no shear stiffness), so T = c S - e^T E; the first transfer counts as already present (no stress: the initial state is its equilibrium). Ignored without piezo_e* arrays.
- `electric_field_y` (V/m): Electric field y at the cell centres (electrostatics_acoustics_piezo): each transfer adds -e^T (E - E_last) to the stresses (sxy at the corners from the 4-cell mean, none where a corner has no shear stiffness), so T = c S - e^T E; the first transfer counts as already present (no stress: the initial state is its equilibrium). Ignored without piezo_e* arrays.

### Feature `elastic_waves.force_source` - Point force

force * waveform(t) along angle in the cell containing the point, half on each of its two x faces (x component) and y faces (y component) as force density over each face dual cell, at the start of each step. A point in the outermost cell of a non-periodic face loses the half on its outer face.

- Category source; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `waveform` (default "ricker"; ricker | gaussian | cw) - Waveform. Help: shared `elastic_waves.force_source.waveform`
- `frequency` [Hz] (default 1e+06; > 0) - Frequency. Help: shared `elastic_waves.force_source.frequency`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Spectral width / frequency: the amplitude spectrum is 1/e at f (1 +- bandwidth).
- `force` [N/m] (default 1) - Line force
  Peak force per unit z length (geometry axisymmetric: per unit length of the ring through the point, total 2 pi r_c force).
- `angle` [deg] (default 0) - Force direction
  Counter-clockwise from +x (90 = +y).

### Feature `elastic_waves.volume_source` - Point volume source

Monopole line source in the cell containing the point: volume_rate * waveform(t) acts as an isotropic strain rate on the cell (sampled half a step after the velocity forces). In a fluid it radiates |p| = rho omega Q / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)|, mesh-independent; in a solid mainly compression waves.

- Category source; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `waveform` (default "ricker"; ricker | gaussian | cw) - Waveform. Help: shared `elastic_waves.force_source.waveform`
- `frequency` [Hz] (default 1e+06; > 0) - Frequency. Help: shared `elastic_waves.force_source.frequency`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Spectral width / frequency: the amplitude spectrum is 1/e at f (1 +- bandwidth).
- `volume_rate` [m^2/s] (default 0.001) - Volume injection rate
  Peak volume per second and unit z length: d(sxx)/dt -= (c11 + c12) / 2 q, d(syy)/dt -= (c12 + c22) / 2 q, q = rate / cell area. geometry axisymmetric: per unit length of the ring through the point (total 2 pi r_c rate), a 3D strain rate q / 3 per axis (a fluid again gets p += K q dt).

### Feature `elastic_waves.traction_line_source` - Line source (traction sheet)

traction * waveform(t) at the centres of the cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) under an axis-aligned line, continuing through any padding where an end touches the domain edge: the normal component split over the two faces around each line cell, the tangential one on the faces along the line. A sheet across the whole domain (periodic or absorbing ends) launches plane waves to each side; a shorter one diffracts.

- Category source; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `waveform` (default "ricker"; ricker | gaussian | cw) - Waveform. Help: shared `elastic_waves.force_source.waveform`
- `frequency` [Hz] (default 1e+06; > 0) - Frequency. Help: shared `elastic_waves.force_source.frequency`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Spectral width / frequency: the amplitude spectrum is 1/e at f (1 +- bandwidth).
- `traction` [Pa] (default 1000) - Traction
  Peak force per area; a domain-spanning sheet sends a plane wave of stress traction / 2 and velocity traction / (2 rho c) to each side (fluid: pressure traction / 2 for a normal traction).
- `direction` (default "x"; x | y) - Force direction
  Normal to the line launches P waves, along it S waves (vertical line: x = P, y = S).

### Feature `elastic_waves.heat_pulse_source` - Heating pulse (photoacoustic)

Thermoelastic source: the heating rate q (see power_density) adds -gruneisen q to d(sxx)/dt and d(syy)/dt of the selected cells (at the half step); cells without gruneisen ignore it. Heating from another time-stepped physics goes into the 'heating_power' slot instead (field_transfer, optionally with heating_envelope gaussian).

- Category source; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params:
- `power_density` [W/m^3] (default 1e+12; may use x, y) - Peak heating power density
  Peak q0: q = q0 exp(-((t - delay) / pulse_width)^2), absorbed energy density H = q0 sqrt(pi) pulse_width; a short pulse (c pulse_width << heated size) raises the pressure by gruneisen H. E.g. Beer-Lambert exp(-mu_a (y1 - y)).
- `pulse_width` [s] (default 1e-08; > 0) - Pulse width
  1/e half-width; keep c pulse_width >= ~5 cells (validation warns below 2), else the front is under-resolved and rings.
- `delay` [s] (>= 0; nullable) - Pulse delay
  Envelope maximum; empty = 3 x pulse_width.

### Feature `elastic_waves.rigid_domain` - Rigid domain

Zero velocity on every face of the selected cells (staircased): a fluid slides along it, a solid sticks to it.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params: none

### Feature `elastic_waves.initial_velocity` - Initial velocity

v_x / v_y are written into the staggered velocity fields on the +x / +y faces of the selected cells before the first step (the leap-frog start v^(-1/2), stresses 0); a later feature wins shared faces. Faces the scheme pins (rigid walls, rigid_domain, the axis) drop it at the first step.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; stepper precisions single only (see solvers); result none

Params:
- `v_x` [m/s] (default 0; may use x, y) - Initial velocity x
  Evaluated at the +x face centre of each selected cell (the staggered vx position: exact for a discrete mode). Axisymmetric: v_r.
- `v_y` [m/s] (default 0; may use x, y) - Initial velocity y
  Evaluated at the +y face centre of each selected cell. Axisymmetric: v_z.

### Feature `elastic_waves.field_probe` - Field probe

Time series in the cell containing the point (a coordinate on a cell edge goes to the upper cell), sampled after every step.

- Category probe; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result kind `timeseries`

Params:
- `component` (default "pressure"; pressure | vx | vy | sxx | syy | sxy | stt) - Recorded quantity
  pressure = -(sxx + syy) / 2 (axisymmetric: -(s_rr + s_zz + s_tt) / 3) and the stresses [Pa] at the cell centre (sxy on its +x +y corner) at t; stt (hoop stress) axisymmetric only, else a validation error; vx / vy [m/s] on the +x / +y face at t - dt / 2.

### Feature `elastic_waves.resonance_monitor` - Resonance finder

Resonance finder (harmonic inversion, as Harminv / matrix pencil): records one component in the cell containing each selected point (1 to 16; a coordinate on a cell edge goes to the upper cell) every step. Reading the result (CPU, ~1 s per point) fits the traces from t_s on jointly (shared poles, amplitudes per point) by damped sinusoids a exp(-gamma (t - t_s)) cos(omega (t - t_s) + phi), so a mode on a nodal line of one point is found through the others. Result 'table', one row per resonance in the band, strongest first: resonance_number, frequency = omega / (2 pi) [Hz], frequency_imag = gamma / (2 pi) [Hz] (> 0 decays), q_factor = omega / (2 gamma), amplitude a [component unit] and phase phi [rad] at t_s where largest, error = |pole change between two pencil sizes| / omega. Dropped: error > 0.01, amplitude < 0.0001 of the strongest at every point, growth > 2x over the window. Extras: component, unit, dt [s], start_time, end_time [s], sample_interval [steps], n_samples (<= 2000), model_order, frequency_min, frequency_max, note ('' or why none was found), points, point_amplitudes / point_phases (per row, one per point). Q far above pi f T_window resolves while the ring-down stays above float32 noise (~1e-7). A mode with a node at every point is missed; a cw source adds an undamped line. Velocities carry their own time stamps (t - dt / 2): no sample delay. dt = the acoustic step.

- Category monitor; selection point entities, object kinds point, 1 to 16; stepper precisions single, double only (see solvers); result kind `table`

Params:
- `component` (default "pressure"; pressure | vx | vy | sxx | syy | sxy | stt) - Recorded quantity
  pressure = -(sxx + syy) / 2 (axisymmetric: -(s_rr + s_zz + s_tt) / 3) and the stresses [Pa] at the cell centre (sxy on its +x +y corner) at t; stt (hoop stress) axisymmetric only, else a validation error; vx / vy [m/s] on the +x / +y face at t - dt / 2. Pressure misses the S modes of a solid; stresses and velocities see both.
- `frequency_min` [Hz] (default 500000; > 0) - Lowest frequency
  Keep the band inside the source spectrum; narrower = faster, better conditioned fit.
- `frequency_max` [Hz] (default 2e+06; > 0) - Highest frequency
  > frequency_min, below the Nyquist frequency 1 / (2 dt).
- `start_time` [s] (>= 0; nullable) - Analysis start
  Start t_s of the analysed window; empty = the end of the latest pulsed source (ricker / gaussian waveform: 2 t0; heat_pulse_source and a gaussian heating_envelope: delay + 4.5 width) (0 with only cw sources). The fit assumes a free ring-down: a start inside a pulse adds spurious poles.

## Physics type `electric_currents` - Electric Currents

Quasi-static -div(sigma_dc grad V) = s, s the current_source features plus the coupled slot, finite volumes on the physical window, outputs edge-extended into an EM PML ring. Unreferenced outer faces are insulated (zero normal current); a later boundary feature on a face wins (validation warning). Needs an anchor: a voltage or terminal touching every conducting region (a pure Neumann problem is singular). 2D units per m of depth: currents A/m, conductances S/m, resistances Ohm m (axisymmetric and 3D: whole totals). E_x / E_y and J_x / J_y are face fluxes averaged to the cell centres (E = 0 in non-conducting cells, E and J = 0 in held cells; J_x / J_y include the xy cross flux, E stays -grad V); q_joule [W/m^3] = each face dissipation split between its two cells by half-cell resistance, so its window integral equals the sum over voltage / terminal features of V * current plus V times the current_source and inward current_density (currents_heat_joule hands it to heat). A stationary study iterates it with the couplings and state-dependent properties (sigma_dc of heat_T); time_dependent re-solves only when sigma_dc, a boundary condition, a held potential or a source changed (sigma_dc(T) is rewritten right after each heat step: leave every at 1 so the currents re-solve before the Joule power goes to heat). Triangle meshes (planar or axisymmetric): elements of the discretization order, V nodal; a voltage on objects holds their outline edges, a terminal every node of its elements, object current_density / surface_charge is an outline edge source (both sides), a probe reads the point's node; held currents / charges are reactions (exact Gauss balance); E, J / D and q_joule are element means (q_joule integrates to V * I); electrolytes linear only (none in terminal elements; a selected voltage object carries ions); no waveforms or azimuthal_order. 3D models (size_z set) need a tetrahedra mesh (a 3D tensor mesh is a validation error): elements of the discretization order, diagonal sigma_dc_xx / _yy / _zz (sigma_dc_zz set by the isotropic sigma_dc; sigma_dc_xy is a validation error); a voltage on objects holds their interface faces, a terminal every node of its elements, object current_density is a sheet source on the interface faces (both sides); held currents are reactions in A (exact Gauss balance; the integral of q_joule equals the sum of V * I); E, J_x / J_y and q_joule are element means, plus 3D-only output fields E_z, J_z, sigma_dc_zz (not in expressions), sampled on the uniform mesh lattice. Not in 3D (validation errors): electrolytes, voltage waveforms, Stern layers, axisymmetric / azimuthal_order, mirror faces of the model.

- Default instance name `currents`; studies stationary, time_dependent (default {"type": "stationary"})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; refinement indicator fields V; dispersion poles not used
- Features: voltage, terminal, current_density, current_source, potential_probe

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (default "planar"; planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  planar: 2D currents per unit z length (terminal currents A/m). axisymmetric (x = r, y = z; spec notes): (r, z) currents, every conductance, face and cell volume (and object-perimeter current_density) weighted by 2 pi r (pi r for azimuthal_order m != 0):densities keep their units, the current of a voltage / terminal (table result, scalar output) is that of the whole ring in A (the 'integral' of q_joule: total power in W); sigma_dc_xy is a validation error. x_lo is the axis (any feature there does nothing; validation warns).
- `azimuthal_order` (int; default 0; >= 0; visible when geometry in (axisymmetric)) - Azimuthal order. Help: shared `electric_currents.azimuthal_order`
- `discretization` (default "quadratic"; quadratic | linear) - Discretization. Help: shared `electric_currents.discretization`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `sigma_dc` [S/m] (>= 0; nullable; writes sigma_dc_xx, sigma_dc_yy, sigma_dc_zz) - Static conductivity
  Sets sigma_dc_xx, _yy and _zz (component entries override it; zz read only on 3D tetrahedra); unset = 0 = insulator: no current, the cell keeps its potential, so every conducting region needs a voltage or terminal. NOT the optical sigma_e (water: sigma_e 4.22 S/m at 1.55 um, sigma_dc 5.5e-6 S/m). Gold 4.1e7, silver 6.3e7, aluminium 3.8e7, water 5.5e-6; e.g. gold 4.1e7 / (1 + 0.0034 * (heat_T - 293.15)) (a stationary study iterates).
- `sigma_dc_xx`, `sigma_dc_yy` [S/m] (>= 0; nullable) - Static conductivity along x / Static conductivity along y
  Overrides sigma_dc for this axis.
- `sigma_dc_zz` [S/m] (>= 0; nullable) - Static conductivity along z
  Overrides sigma_dc for this axis (3D tetrahedra only; 2D ignores it).
- `sigma_dc_xy` [S/m] (nullable) - Static conductivity, cross term
  Off-diagonal sigma_dc (cross conduction of a rotated anisotropic material); keep sigma_dc_xy^2 < sigma_dc_xx sigma_dc_yy (validation error for plain numbers; on strongly graded cells clearly below: the discrete operator is positive below it times 4 r / (1 + r)^2 per axis, r = neighbour width ratio). Cross flux flows only inside 2x2 cell blocks whose xx and yy are all > 0, never through outer faces. E stays -grad V; J include -sigma_dc_xy (dV/dy, dV/dx); q_joule includes the cross power (its integral equals V * I).

### Fields

Output fields (primary V; [state] = also a state field):
- `V` - Electric potential (V) [state]
- `E_x` - Electric field x (V/m) [state]
- `E_y` - Electric field y (V/m) [state]
- `J_x` - Current density x (A/m^2) [state]
- `J_y` - Current density y (A/m^2) [state]
- `q_joule` - Joule heating density (W/m^3) [state]
- `current_source` - Coupled current source (A/m^3) [state]
- `current_source_ext` - Applied current source (A/m^3) [state]
- `sigma_dc_xx` - DC conductivity xx (S/m) [state]
- `sigma_dc_yy` - DC conductivity yy (S/m) [state]
- `E_z` - Electric field z (V/m)
- `J_z` - Current density z (A/m^2)
- `sigma_dc_zz` - DC conductivity zz (S/m)

Scalar outputs: current_<feature> (A/m; axisymmetric and 3D: A) per enabled voltage / terminal: its table result current of the last solve. Example derived value {"name": "I_anode", "expression": "currents_current_anode"}; a voltage sweep gives the I-V curve. A name equal to an output field (a terminal named source) gets none. Under an EM mirror face of the model: the unfolded structure's value, x 2 per mirror plane the voltage face or terminal touches (a face on the opposite side does not touch).

### Source slots

- `current_source` (A/m^3): Field current_source, added to current_source_ext of the features; each transfer replaces it.

### Feature `electric_currents.voltage` - Voltage

Fixed potential (Dirichlet): outer faces at the face (half-cell conductance 2 sigma_dc / dx); on object perimeters the boundary cells inside the object are held, the value on their faces toward the free cells (the window edge is no perimeter: select the outer face). Anchors the solve. Result 'table', one row [feature, voltage, current] (units '', V, A/m; axisymmetric and 3D A) and the extras voltage and current: positive = current (electrostatics: free charge, the outward D flux) leaving the held faces / cells into the domain (a source injected inside a terminal is subtracted). A cell held by two features counts for each (the later voltage holds it; validation warns on possible overlaps); an outer face replaced by a later feature counts only for that one. E and J / D read 0 inside held cells (ideal conductor): the surface current / charge is this result.

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, at least 1, outer faces and object perimeters; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result kind `table`

Params:
- `voltage` [V] (default 1) - Voltage
  Held on the selected outer faces or in the boundary cells inside the selected objects. Follows reuse_build.

### Feature `electric_currents.terminal` - Terminal

Holds every selected cell at the voltage (current flows in or out freely), the value on their faces toward the free cells (half-cell conductance 2 sigma_dc / dx of the free neighbour, whatever the held cells' own); anchors the solve. A metal with its own sigma_dc is equipotential anyway: a terminal feeds current in and reads it out (its cells need no sigma_dc). Result 'table', one row [feature, voltage, current] (units '', V, A/m; axisymmetric and 3D A) and the extras voltage and current: positive = current (electrostatics: free charge, the outward D flux) leaving the held faces / cells into the domain (a source injected inside a terminal is subtracted). A cell held by two features counts for each (the later voltage holds it; validation warns on possible overlaps); an outer face replaced by a later feature counts only for that one. E and J / D read 0 inside held cells (ideal conductor): the surface current / charge is this result.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result kind `table`

Params:
- `voltage` [V] (default 1) - Voltage
  Held in every selected cell (times the waveform when one is set). Follows reuse_build.

### Feature `electric_currents.current_density` - Current density

Prescribed normal current density. Outer faces: a Neumann condition; object perimeters: current_density * perimeter length / cell area into the boundary cells inside the object (true perimeter length to ~2 %; conformal_boundaries: per cut-cell chord of the drawn outline). Does not anchor the solve: the current must leave through a voltage or terminal.

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, at least 1, outer faces and object perimeters; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result none

Params:
- `current_density` [A/m^2] (default 10000) - Inward current density
  > 0 injects current into the domain or the object, < 0 extracts it.

### Feature `electric_currents.current_source` - Current source

Adds density to current_source_ext on the selected cells (sources add; the coupled slot is separate); the current leaves through the voltage / terminal features.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result none

Params:
- `density` [A/m^3] (default 1e+12; may use x, y) - Injected current per volume
  Volumetric current injection; 2D: density * area is the current per m of depth (axisymmetric: density * ring volume, A). Must be finite on the selected cells; non-conducting cells ignore it.

### Feature `electric_currents.potential_probe` - Potential probe

Help: shared `electric_currents.potential_probe`

- Category probe; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result kind `timeseries`

Params: none

## Physics type `electrostatics` - Electrostatics

Quasi-static -div(eps0 eps_dc grad V) = rho_free + rho_ion, rho_free the charge_density features plus the coupled slot, rho_ion the electrolyte features, finite volumes on the physical window, outputs edge-extended into an EM PML ring. Unreferenced outer faces are insulated (zero normal D); a later boundary feature on a face wins (validation warning). Needs an anchor: one voltage, terminal or electrolyte anywhere (every cell is a dielectric) (a pure Neumann problem is singular). 2D units per m of depth: charges C/m, capacitances F/m (charge / voltage of a terminal with the others at 0 V) (axisymmetric and 3D: whole totals). E_x / E_y and D_x / D_y are face fluxes averaged to the cell centres (E = D / (eps0 eps_dc) without eps_dc_xy, both 0 in held cells; D_x / D_y include the xy cross flux, E stays -grad V). A stationary study iterates it with the couplings and state-dependent properties (eps_dc of heat_T); time_dependent re-solves only when eps_dc, a boundary condition, a held potential or a source changed (a state-dependent eps_dc re-solves at the cadence of the physics it reads; a voltage or terminal waveform writes its superposition every step instead). Triangle meshes (planar or axisymmetric): elements of the discretization order, V nodal; a voltage on objects holds their outline edges, a terminal every node of its elements, object current_density / surface_charge is an outline edge source (both sides), a probe reads the point's node; held currents / charges are reactions (exact Gauss balance); E, J / D and q_joule are element means (q_joule integrates to V * I); electrolytes linear only (none in terminal elements; a selected voltage object carries ions); no waveforms or azimuthal_order. 3D models (size_z set) need a tetrahedra mesh (a 3D tensor mesh is a validation error): elements of the discretization order, diagonal eps_dc_xx / _yy / _zz (eps_dc_zz set by the isotropic eps_dc; eps_dc_xy is a validation error); a voltage on objects holds their interface faces, a terminal every node of its elements, object surface_charge is a sheet source on the interface faces (both sides); held charges are reactions in C (exact Gauss balance); E, D_x / D_y are element means, plus 3D-only output fields E_z, D_z, eps_dc_zz (not in expressions), sampled on the uniform mesh lattice. Not in 3D (validation errors): electrolytes, voltage waveforms, Stern layers, axisymmetric / azimuthal_order, mirror faces of the model.

- Default instance name `electrostatics`; studies stationary, time_dependent (default {"type": "stationary"})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; refinement indicator fields V; dispersion poles not used
- Features: voltage, terminal, surface_charge, charge_density, potential_probe, electrolyte

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (default "planar"; planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  planar: 2D electrostatics per unit z length (terminal charges C/m). axisymmetric (x = r, y = z; spec notes): (r, z) electrostatics, every conductance, face and cell volume (and object-perimeter surface_charge) weighted by 2 pi r (pi r for azimuthal_order m != 0):densities keep their units, the charge of a voltage / terminal (table result, scalar output) is that of the whole ring in C; eps_dc_xy is a validation error. x_lo is the axis (any feature there does nothing; validation warns).
- `azimuthal_order` (int; default 0; >= 0; visible when geometry in (axisymmetric)) - Azimuthal order. Help: shared `electric_currents.azimuthal_order`
- `discretization` (default "quadratic"; quadratic | linear) - Discretization. Help: shared `electric_currents.discretization`
- `nonlinear_tolerance` [1] (default 1e-06; > 0) - Electrolyte iteration tolerance
  Damped Newton of nonlinear electrolytes: converged when a step changes V by at most this times kB T / (e max |z_i|) (the smallest over the nonlinear electrolytes; 25.7 mV for 1:1 at 298.15 K). Keep it above the CG accuracy in V (pcg tolerance times the condition number). Ignored without a nonlinear electrolyte.
- `nonlinear_max_iterations` (int; default 100; >= 1) - Electrolyte iteration limit
  Per solve of a nonlinear electrolyte; an unconverged loop keeps its damped V and logs a warning. Steps are capped at 4 kB T / (e max |z_i|), so a surface or electrode potential of P such units needs at least P / 4 iterations.
- `nonlinear_relaxation` [1] (default 1; [0.015625, 1]) - Electrolyte iteration damping
  Fraction of each Newton update applied; halves automatically (to 1/64) while the update grows, recovers once it shrinks. 1 suits the convex Boltzmann charge; lower it only when the loop oscillates.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_dc` [1] (>= 1; nullable; writes eps_dc_xx, eps_dc_yy, eps_dc_zz) - Static relative permittivity
  Sets eps_dc_xx, _yy and _zz (component entries override it; zz read only on 3D tetrahedra); unset = 1 (vacuum): every cell takes part, one voltage / terminal anchors everything. NOT the optical eps_r = n^2: lithium niobate eps_dc 43 (eps_a) / 28 (eps_c) vs eps_r 4.9 / 4.6; silicon 11.7 vs 12.08; silica 3.9 vs 2.085; water 80.1 vs 1.73.
- `eps_dc_xx`, `eps_dc_yy` [1] (>= 1; nullable) - Static relative permittivity along x / Static relative permittivity along y
  Overrides eps_dc for this axis.
- `eps_dc_zz` [1] (>= 1; nullable) - Static relative permittivity along z
  Overrides eps_dc for this axis (3D tetrahedra electrostatics, solid_mechanics_3d with piezoelectric on; 2D ignores it).
- `eps_dc_xy` [1] (nullable) - Static relative permittivity, cross term
  Off-diagonal eps_dc (cross polarisation of a rotated anisotropic material); keep eps_dc_xy^2 < eps_dc_xx eps_dc_yy (validation error for plain numbers; on strongly graded cells clearly below: the discrete operator is positive below it times 4 r / (1 + r)^2 per axis, r = neighbour width ratio). Cross flux flows only inside 2x2 cell blocks whose xx and yy are all > 0, never through outer faces. E stays -grad V; D include -eps0 eps_dc_xy (dV/dy, dV/dx).
- `r` [m/V] (nullable; writes r_xx, r_yy, r_zz) - Electro-optic coefficient
  Isotropic Pockels coefficient: sets r_xx, r_yy and r_zz (component entries override it), read only by electrostatics_em_pockels: dn_ii = -1/2 n0_ii^3 r_ii E_k, E_k the applied component chosen by its field_component; unset = 0. x-cut lithium niobate, field along the optic axis: r33 = 31e-12 on the optic-axis component, r13 = 10e-12 on the others (library lithium_niobate_x_cut); 0 for silicon and silica. A crystal entry sets pockels_r11 .. _r62 instead.
- `r_xx` [m/V] (nullable) - Electro-optic coefficient along x
  Overrides r for n_xx (light polarised along x).
- `r_yy` [m/V] (nullable) - Electro-optic coefficient along y
  Overrides r for n_yy (light polarised along y).
- `r_zz` [m/V] (nullable) - Electro-optic coefficient along z
  Overrides r for n_zz (light polarised along z).
- `pockels_r11`, `pockels_r12`, `pockels_r21`, `pockels_r22`, `pockels_r31`, `pockels_r32`, `pockels_r61`, `pockels_r62` [m/V] (nullable) - Electro-optic tensor r11 / Electro-optic tensor r12 / Electro-optic tensor r21 / Electro-optic tensor r22 / Electro-optic tensor r31 / Electro-optic tensor r32 / Electro-optic tensor r61 / Electro-optic tensor r62
  In-plane Pockels tensor entry r_Ik (pockels_r<I><k>) of a crystal in model axes: Delta(1/n^2)_I = r_I1 E_x + r_I2 E_y, row I = 1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz or 6 xy (eps_xy of em_fdfd_hz: Delta eps_xy = -n0_xx^2 n0_yy^2 Delta(1/n^2)_xy; other EM types drop it, validation warns). Read only by electrostatics_em_pockels, which adds -1/2 n0_ii^3 (r_i1 E_x + r_i2 E_y) whatever its field_component, on top of r_ii E_k: set these or r / r_ii, not both. Usually from a {'model': 'crystal'} entry: the clamped r^S in model axes (a piezoelectric strain from elastic_waves adds its index change via acoustics_em_acousto_optic, no double counting); YZ lithium niobate (model x = crystal Z, y = -Y): r11 = r33, r12 = 0, r21 = r13, r22 = -r22, r31 = r13, r32 = r22, r61 = 0, r62 = r51. Unset = 0; setting one allocates all eight arrays.

### Fields

Output fields (primary V; [state] = also a state field):
- `V` - Electric potential (V) [state]
- `E_x` - Electric field x (V/m) [state]
- `E_y` - Electric field y (V/m) [state]
- `D_x` - Electric displacement x (C/m^2) [state]
- `D_y` - Electric displacement y (C/m^2) [state]
- `rho_free` - Coupled charge density (C/m^3) [state]
- `rho_free_ext` - Applied charge density (C/m^3) [state]
- `rho_ion` - Ionic space charge (C/m^3) [state]
- `c_ion_1` - Ion concentration, species 1 (mol/L)
- `c_ion_2` - Ion concentration, species 2 (mol/L)
- `c_ion_3` - Ion concentration, species 3 (mol/L)
- `c_ion_4` - Ion concentration, species 4 (mol/L)
- `eps_dc_xx` - DC relative permittivity xx (1) [state]
- `eps_dc_yy` - DC relative permittivity yy (1) [state]
- `E_z` - Electric field z (V/m)
- `D_z` - Electric displacement z (C/m^2)
- `eps_dc_zz` - DC relative permittivity zz (1)

Scalar outputs: charge_<feature> (C/m; axisymmetric and 3D: C) per enabled voltage / terminal: its table result charge of the last solve. Example {"name": "C_top", "expression": "electrostatics_charge_top / V_top"} = the capacitance (F/m) with every other electrode at 0 V. Per enabled electrolyte: ionic_strength_<feature> (mol/L, 1/2 sum z_i^2 c_i) and debye_length_<feature> (m; bulk, linearised, at the mean eps_dc of its cells), constants of the build. Under an EM mirror face of the model: the unfolded structure's value, x 2 per mirror plane the voltage face or terminal touches.

### Source slots

- `charge_density` (C/m^3): Field rho_free, added to rho_free_ext of the features; each transfer replaces it.

### Feature `electrostatics.voltage` - Voltage

Fixed potential (Dirichlet): outer faces at the face (half-cell conductance 2 eps0 eps_dc / dx); on object perimeters the boundary cells inside the object are held, the value on their faces toward the free cells (the window edge is no perimeter: select the outer face). Anchors the solve. Result 'table', one row [feature, voltage, charge] (units '', V, C/m; axisymmetric and 3D C) and the extras voltage and charge: positive = current (electrostatics: free charge, the outward D flux) leaving the held faces / cells into the domain (a source injected inside a terminal is subtracted). A cell held by two features counts for each (the later voltage holds it; validation warns on possible overlaps); an outer face replaced by a later feature counts only for that one. E and J / D read 0 inside held cells (ideal conductor): the surface current / charge is this result.

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, at least 1, outer faces and object perimeters; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result kind `table`

Params:
- `voltage` [V] (default 1) - Voltage
  Held on the selected outer faces or in the boundary cells inside the selected objects. Follows reuse_build.
- `waveform` (default "none"; none | ricker | gaussian | cw) - Voltage waveform. Help: shared `electrostatics.voltage.waveform`
- `frequency` [Hz] (default 1e+08; > 0; visible when waveform in (ricker, gaussian, cw)) - Frequency
  Centre (gaussian, cw) or peak (ricker) frequency of the waveform.
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Spectral width / frequency of the gaussian (amplitude spectrum 1/e at f (1 +- bandwidth)).
- `stern_thickness` [m] (default 0; >= 0) - Stern layer thickness
  Thickness d_S of a compact (Stern / Helmholtz) layer between the electrode and the first cells; 0 = none (V on the face). > 0: a Robin face h = C_S = eps0 stern_permittivity / d_S [F/m^2], external = voltage, so V drops by sigma / C_S across it (sigma = D.n into the domain = electrode charge per area; Gouy-Chapman-Stern: voltage = psi_d + sigma / C_S). The layer is not drawn and holds no ions (the electrolyte begins at the face). Outer faces only (validation error with objects); the charge is the D flux through it. Typical 0.2 to 0.5 nm.
- `stern_permittivity` [1] (default 10; >= 1) - Stern layer permittivity
  eps_S (oriented water: 6 to 30); only with stern_thickness > 0.

### Feature `electrostatics.terminal` - Terminal

Holds every selected cell at the voltage (charge flows in or out freely), the value on their faces toward the free cells (half-cell conductance 2 eps0 eps_dc / dx of the free neighbour, whatever the held cells' own); anchors the solve. Electrostatics has no conductors of its own: a terminal is the conductor (its cells need no eps_dc) and its free charge is read out. Result 'table', one row [feature, voltage, charge] (units '', V, C/m; axisymmetric and 3D C) and the extras voltage and charge: positive = current (electrostatics: free charge, the outward D flux) leaving the held faces / cells into the domain (a source injected inside a terminal is subtracted). A cell held by two features counts for each (the later voltage holds it; validation warns on possible overlaps); an outer face replaced by a later feature counts only for that one. E and J / D read 0 inside held cells (ideal conductor): the surface current / charge is this result.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result kind `table`

Params:
- `voltage` [V] (default 1) - Voltage
  Held in every selected cell (times the waveform when one is set). Follows reuse_build.
- `waveform` (default "none"; none | ricker | gaussian | cw) - Voltage waveform. Help: shared `electrostatics.voltage.waveform`
- `frequency` [Hz] (default 1e+08; > 0; visible when waveform in (ricker, gaussian, cw)) - Frequency
  Centre (gaussian, cw) or peak (ricker) frequency of the waveform.
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Spectral width / frequency of the gaussian (amplitude spectrum 1/e at f (1 +- bandwidth)).

### Feature `electrostatics.surface_charge` - Surface charge

Prescribed surface charge. Outer faces: a Neumann condition D.n = surface_charge into the domain (nothing beyond the face); object perimeters: surface_charge * perimeter length / cell area in the boundary cells inside the object (true perimeter length to ~2 %; conformal_boundaries: per cut-cell chord of the drawn outline). Does not anchor the solve.

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, at least 1, outer faces and object perimeters; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result none

Params:
- `surface_charge` [C/m^2] (default 1e-06) - Surface charge
  > 0 raises V.

### Feature `electrostatics.charge_density` - Charge density

Adds density to rho_free_ext on the selected cells (sources add; the coupled slot, field rho_free, is separate).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result none

Params:
- `density` [C/m^3] (default 0.001; may use x, y) - Charge density
  rho in div(eps0 eps_dc grad V) = -rho; positive raises V. 2D: density * area is the charge per m of depth (axisymmetric: density * ring volume, C). Must be finite on the selected cells.

### Feature `electrostatics.potential_probe` - Potential probe

Help: shared `electric_currents.potential_probe`

- Category probe; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result kind `timeseries`

Params: none

### Feature `electrostatics.electrolyte` - Electrolyte

Mobile ions screening the field: on the selected cells -div(eps0 eps_dc grad V) = rho_free + rho_ion (rho_ion: see model). k = sum_i z_i^2 e^2 n_i / (kB T) [F/m^3], n_i = 1000 N_A c_i; V decays over the Debye length lambda_D = sqrt(eps0 eps_dc / k) (water, eps_dc 80, 298.15 K: 0.307 nm / sqrt(I [mol/L]), 9.7 nm at 1 mM NaCl). nonlinear: damped Newton, one warm-started CG solve per iteration (the first is the linear solution), steps capped at 4 kB T / (e max |z_i|) (iterations: summary solvers nonlinear_iterations); point ions without size: counter-ion concentrations above a few mol/L (|V - V_bulk| beyond ~0.2 V / |z| at 1 mM) are unphysical, the Boltzmann exponent is clipped at 80. Both models anchor the solve (no voltage or terminal needed). Held cells (terminals, voltage perimeters) have no ions; overlapping electrolytes add. Fields rho_ion [C/m^3] and c_ion_1 .. c_ion_4 [mol/L] = the local concentration of species k at the solved V (linear: c_k (1 - z_k e (V - V_bulk) / (kB T)), negative beyond kB T / (|z_k| e)), 0 outside electrolytes and on held cells; at most 4 species (more: validation warning); output only (not in expressions). Resolve lambda_D: cells of lambda_D / 3 or finer at charged surfaces and electrodes, finer for nonlinear at high potentials (1:1 layer lambda_D / cosh(e (V - V_bulk) / (2 kB T))). Triangle meshes: model linear only, per element (from the element mean V).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result none

Params:
- `concentrations` [mol/L] (float_list; default [0.001, 0.001]; >= 0) - Ion concentrations
  Bulk concentration c_i per species (1 mM = 1e-3), in the order of valences; the bulk must be neutral, sum z_i c_i = 0 (validation error). Uniform over the selection.
- `valences` [1] (float_list; default [1, -1]) - Ion valences
  Charge number z_i per concentration, none 0: Na+ / K+ 1, Cl- -1, Ca2+ 2, SO4 2- -2 (CaCl2: 2, -1 with concentrations c, 2 c).
- `temperature` [K] (default 298.15; > 0) - Temperature
  T of the Boltzmann factor kB T (screening coefficient ~ 1 / T).
- `bulk_potential` [V] (default 0) - Bulk potential
  V_bulk, where every species has its bulk concentration (e.g. a reference electrode); V relaxes to it away from charges and electrodes.
- `model` (default "linear"; linear | nonlinear) - Electrolyte model
  linear (Debye-Hueckel, one solve): rho_ion = -k (V - V_bulk), valid for |V - V_bulk| << kB T / (|z| e) = 25.7 mV / |z| at 298 K (beyond, it overestimates the screening charge); nonlinear (Poisson-Boltzmann, damped Newton, physics settings nonlinear_*): rho_ion = sum_i z_i e n_i exp(-z_i e (V - V_bulk) / (kB T)), for potentials of several kB T / e.

## Physics type `em_eme` - Electromagnetic Waves, eigenmode expansion (2D)

Bidirectional eigenmode expansion (EME) of a 2D in-plane device cut into sections along propagation_axis, for long devices (tapers, MMIs, couplers, gratings) where em_fdfd_* would be large. Each section line is solved once for n_modes slab modes (em_fdfd_ez / _hz line stencil, transverse bc_* faces, PML modes kept as radiation; repeated material rows reuse their modes), normalised to the unconjugated <e, h> = 1 (orthogonal also when lossy); interfaces are mode-matched by these overlaps (R = (I + P P^T)^-1 (I - P P^T), T = P^T (I + R)) and S-matrices cascaded by Redheffer star products (stable with evanescent modes). Exact for a complete basis (n_modes 0), else converging in n_modes. Outputs of the excitation (eme_ports), from the reconstructed phasor at cell centres (sum of a_n e^{-j k_n s} + b_n e^{-j k_n (L - s)} per section): <pol>_re / _im / _abs / _phase of the out-of-plane field (the other polarisation reads 0), e_abs (primary), e_intensity, h_abs (in-plane component along the axis from line differences, face mean), absorbed_power = 1/2 omega eps0 (-Im eps) times the 3-point Gauss cell mean of |E|^2 along the axis (integrates to 1 - T - R of a lossy guide between lossless ports), and the materials. em_heat_joule reads absorbed_power (last solve); heat_em_thermo_optic / Pockels write eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy. Studies: stationary (a solve whenever materials changed), frequency_domain (one solve per wavelength) and optimization (design_region + adjoint_objective, ez or hz). Bloch k is not supported; cannot share the model with another EM type.

- Default instance name `eme`; studies stationary, frequency_domain, optimization (default {"type": "stationary"})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor; refinement indicator fields e_abs; dispersion poles used
- Features: eme_ports, eme_section_table, eme_length_sweep, eme_periodic, eme_bend, pec_domain, adjoint_objective, design_region

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `polarization` (default "ez"; ez | hz) - Polarisation
  ez: E_z, H_x, H_y, reads eps_r (= eps_zz); hz: H_z, E_x, E_y, reads eps_xx / eps_yy. Lines and interfaces as em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz.
- `propagation_axis` (default "x"; x | y) - Propagation axis
  Axis along which the device is cut: each cell layer normal to it is a slice, consecutive equal slices form a section (a taper is a staircase at the mesh resolution: refine there); its lo / hi faces are the ports.
- `wavelength` [m] (default 1.55e-06; > 0) - Wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength of a stationary solve; a frequency_domain study solves its own wavelengths instead. Materials enter at omega (sigma_e and poles complex). Line modes need >= 10 cells per lambda0 / |n| along the line (validated at the build value only). A sweep with reuse_build follows it without rebuilding (not on an auto mesh sized by it). Typical 1.31e-6 or 1.55e-6 m.
- `n_modes` (int; default 20; >= 0) - Modes per section
  Modes per section line (descending Re(k_t^2), evanescent last, PML modes kept). 0 = every active line cell, a complete basis: mode matching exact for the discretised line (reciprocal S; lossless: power conserved), O(m^3) per section for m line cells. A truncated basis leaves a projection error, reported as the section table reciprocity_defect (run-log warning above 1e-3): raise n_modes until the port results converge. 10-40 typical, more with cpml line faces.
- `section_tolerance` [1] (default 0; >= 0) - Section tolerance
  Slices whose material rows (permittivity, sigma_e, mu_r, sigma_m, pole regions, PEC) differ from the section's first slice by at most this fraction of each row's max |value| join it (solved on that slice); 0 = identical slices only. > 0 merges smoothly varying (e.g. heated) regions into a material staircase.
- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (default "cpml"; cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  The faces along propagation_axis are the ports: the end cell layers continue to infinity and their bc is not read (pec / pmc avoid the unused cpml padding; periodic and mirrors are refused). The transverse faces bound every section line as in em_fdfd_*: cpml: pml_cells absorbing cells outside the face. The mode solves keep the PML modes as radiation (unlike em_modes and mode ports), so radiating structures converge more slowly in n_modes. periodic: on both faces of the axis; period = the meshed window (uniform mesh: rounded up to whole cells); k = 0 (normal incidence) unless the type has bloch_kx / bloch_ky (em_fdfd_nonlinear: per harmonic_channel). pec, pmc and mirrors pin the outermost cell as the em_fdfd_* walls do.
- `pml_cells` [cells] (int; default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` [1] (default 1; > 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` [1] (default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real CPML stretch (1 = none); larger damps evanescent and grazing waves; 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1; writes eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic: sets eps_zz (ez) and eps_xx, eps_yy (hz) unless the material sets those. The mode solves use eps - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) + every Drude / Lorentz pole chi(omega). Dispersive material: the background eps_inf.
- `eps_zz` [1] (default 1; >= 1; writes eps_r) - Relative permittivity, z (along the guide)
  The only component E_z sees (polarization ez); overrides eps_r for E_z.
- `eps_xx` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, x. Help: shared `em_eme.eps_xx`
- `eps_yy` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, y. Help: shared `em_eme.eps_yy`
- `sigma_e` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss on every E component. The mode solves use eps - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) + every Drude / Lorentz pole chi(omega).
- `mu_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability, 1 for practically every optical material.
- `sigma_m` [Ohm/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss: mu_r gains -j sigma_m / (omega mu0) (artificial absorbers only).

### Fields

Output fields (primary e_abs; [state] = also a state field):
- `ez_re` - Re E_z (V/m) [state]
- `ez_im` - Im E_z (V/m) [state]
- `ez_abs` - |E_z| (V/m)
- `ez_phase` - arg E_z (rad)
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2) [state]
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity (1) [state]
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m) [state]
- `absorbed_power` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)
- `eps_sensitivity` - Objective sensitivity dJ/d eps_r (1/m^2)
- `design_density` - Design density (1)
- `hz_re` - Re H_z (A/m) [state]
- `hz_im` - Im H_z (A/m) [state]
- `hz_abs` - |H_z| (A/m)
- `hz_phase` - arg H_z (rad)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity xx (1) [state]
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity yy (1) [state]
- `eps_xy` - Relative permittivity xy (off-diagonal) (1)

Scalar outputs: Power fractions (unit 1) of the excitation (eme_ports, else mode 1 from lo), last solve: transmission_<k> into port mode k of the output face (k = 1 .. n_port_modes, modes found only), transmission and reflection summed over every mode of the output / input face (|S|^2 p_out / p_in; lossless: transmission + reflection = 1, kept PML modes included). NaN plus a run-log warning when missing (evanescent input mode, too few modes). Example derived value {"name": "T1", "expression": "eme_transmission_1"}.

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_eme.eme_ports` - Ports

Ports and excitation. Result 'table', one row per reported port mode of each face (input face first = reflection, then output face = transmission): output_face, mode_number, n_eff, n_eff_imag (Im < 0 lossy), s_abs2 = |S|^2 of the bilinear-normalised amplitudes, phase_deg = arg S (reference planes = the window faces along propagation_axis; each mode real > 0 at its peak cell), power_fraction = |S|^2 p_out / p_in (p = flux per unit amplitude; = |S|^2 for lossless propagating modes). Port mode k = the k-th mode of the first / last section (input_mode ranking). Extras: wavelength, input_face, input_mode, input_power, transmission and reflection (summed over every mode of the face), s_matrix_real / s_matrix_imag = port S-matrix [[S11, S12], [S21, S22]] over the reported modes (lo first; S21 = lo -> hi), s_matrix_modes {'lo': n, 'hi': n}. Without this feature: mode 1 at 1 W/m from lo. At most one per physics.

- Category source; selection none (a selection is ignored with a warning); result kind `table`

Params:
- `input_face` (default "lo"; lo | hi) - Input face
  Port face of the incident mode: lo = x_lo / y_lo of propagation_axis (incident toward +axis), hi the opposite.
- `input_mode` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Input mode. Help: shared `em_eme.eme_ports.input_mode`
- `input_power` [W/m] (default 1; > 0) - Input power
  Incident mode power per unit length in z; scales only the reconstructed fields, not the S-matrix or power fractions.
- `n_port_modes` (int; default 4; >= 1) - Reported port modes
  Port modes per face in the result table and S-matrix extras; also the number of transmission_<k> scalar outputs.

### Feature `em_eme.eme_section_table` - Section table

Sections of the last solve. Result 'table', one row per section from lo to hi: section (1-based), start and length [m] along propagation_axis, n_slices (cell layers), n_modes (modes found), n_eff_1 / n_eff_2 (Re n_eff of its first two modes), power_defect and reciprocity_defect of the interface to the next section (NaN for the last): power = max over propagating incident modes of |1 - power reflected and transmitted into propagating modes| (lossless lines without cpml only), reciprocity = max |S12 - S21^T| / max |S21| (0 for a complete basis; the n_modes convergence measure). Extra wavelength.

- Category monitor; selection none (a selection is ignored with a warning); result kind `table`

Params: none

- `stop` [m] (default 1e-06) - Range stop
