### Feature `em_fdfd_ez.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

Time-averaged Poynting flux through an axis-aligned line per solved wavelength: S_x = -1/2 Re(E_z H_y*) (vertical line), S_y = 1/2 Re(E_z H_x*) (horizontal), E_z of the line cells, H from the curl of E_z on their hi face; > 0 toward +x / +y. Keep its measuring face (hi face of the line cells) off a mode_source interface face (the line one cell upstream of a positive source, or the line of a negative one) and entirely inside or outside a plane_wave_tfsf box: the field jumps there between total and scattered field (validation warns). Result 'flux_spectrum' in W/m (power per unit z length over the line cells, absolute: a line source of amplitude A spanning a period L in vacuum sends A^2 L / (2 eta0) to each side), one entry per solved wavelength, sorted. The discrete flux is conserved exactly through lossless cells; transmission = device power / power of a reference run with the same source. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

- Category monitor; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params: none

### Feature `em_fdfd_ez.mode_monitor` - Mode monitor

Port monitor splitting the field on an axis-aligned line into the forward (positive: toward +x / +y) and backward (negative) amplitudes a of one guided mode at every solved wavelength: E_z in the line cells and H_y (vertical line) / H_x (horizontal) from the curl of E_z on their hi face are projected on the mode solved there, so each direction is measured separately, unlike a flux_monitor. The 1D line eigenmodes use the FDFD discretisation (Yee widths, PML stretch, complex eps and mu of the line cells with poles, sigma_e, sigma_m), re-solved at every solved wavelength and after any material change (thermo-optic coupling, state-dependent permittivity). Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side, on a locally uniform mesh (validation warns when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line and when its face lies inside a CPML layer, i.e. the line is in the outermost window cell). Span ends: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML (open); an end on a pec domain edge takes E_z = 0, one on a pmc or symmetric edge dE_z/dn = 0 and one on an antisymmetric edge E_z odd about the plane; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E_z = 0 in the next cell), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns above 1% of the mode peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. Keep its measuring face (hi face of the line cells) off a mode_source interface face (the line one cell upstream of a positive source, or the line of a negative one) and entirely inside or outside a plane_wave_tfsf box: the field jumps there between total and scattered field (validation warns). The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength (m, ascending): power_positive / power_negative = |a|^2 in W/m (modes normalised to 1 W/m); with exactly one enabled mode_source in the physics also fraction_positive / fraction_negative = |a / (sqrt(P) e^{j phase})|^2 (source power P and phase; |S|^2: transmission downstream of the source, reflection upstream) and phase_positive / phase_negative (rad), the phase of that S-parameter relative to the source's own line, not de-embedded (each mode profile phased with its largest sample real positive, the lowest-coordinate one of mirror-equal peaks); extras frequency, wavelength, n_eff, n_eff_imag (per wavelength), mode_number and normalized (True with the fractions).

- Category monitor; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Mode number. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_monitor.mode_number`

## Physics type `em_fdfd_hz` - Electromagnetic Waves, frequency domain (2D, magnetic field out of plane)

2D finite-difference frequency-domain (FDFD) solver for the H_z polarisation: H_z out of plane in A/m, E_x and E_y in plane in V/m, x to the right and y up, on the em_fdtd_hz Yee grid (H_z at cell centres, E_x on the +y and E_y on the +x cell faces; face materials: see eps_r). e_abs / e_intensity / h_abs = |E|, |E|^2, |H| at the cell centres (in-plane face phasors averaged there first): peak amplitudes, where em_fdtd_* give instantaneous values. One sparse direct solve of the discrete Helmholtz equation per vacuum wavelength, exp(+j omega t): fields are complex phasors F (real field Re(F e^{j omega t})), every source a phasor (phase setting) with the calibrated, mesh-independent amplitude of the matching FDTD source. absorbed_power (state q_abs) = 1/2 omega eps0 (-Im eps) |E|^2 in W/m^3 (magnetic loss not counted), what em_heat_joule hands to heat. Solver roles (see solvers): linear = sparse_direct (scipy_splu: host SuperLU, ~1e6 unknowns nx * ny incl. PML; cusolver_qr ~1e5; cudss: cuDSS LDL^T, ~20 x SuperLU at 1e5 - 5e5 unknowns (cudss_mixed solves slower); mumps / mumps_mixed / pardiso / pardiso_mixed: the same factor on host cores; a Bloch phase, eps_xy or gyration_z makes it a general LU) or line_block (elongated grids), one factorisation per wavelength and material state, reused for every source; eigen = arpack_shift_invert (factor: SuperLU, cudss / cudss_mixed, mumps / mumps_mixed / pardiso / pardiso_mixed or the line_block one when that is the linear solver; a rejected solve redoes it on SuperLU). Studies: stationary at the wavelength setting (with heat, em_heat_joule and heat_em_thermo_optic iterate to a fixed point; plain Picard oscillates once the self-heating shift exceeds about one linewidth: set the study relaxation < 1); frequency_domain a wavelength list (with em_heat_joule each wavelength's fixed point, continued from the previous), one snapshot each; eigenfrequency the source-free resonances nearest the wavelength setting, one snapshot each plus resonance_table; optomechanics likewise when a solid_mechanics optomechanical_coupling names it (else a stationary background; no coupling or material may read it); optimization maximises the adjoint_objective sum over the design_region densities (L-BFGS-B); time_dependent (beside a time-stepped physics such as elastic_waves, never em_fdtd_*) re-solves on the frozen state every k steps (k = its every) when an input changed; monitors keep the last solve. Periodic faces take bloch_kx / bloch_ky. On a triangles mesh: Lagrange finite elements (see discretization; materials and state fields per element, the same output names on a display raster). With an em_fdfd_ez physics in the same model (e.g. one per polarisation) it needs another instance name (e.g. em_hz) and equal bc_* / pml_* settings (one shared boundary configuration).

- Default instance name `em`; studies stationary, frequency_domain, eigenfrequency, optimization, time_dependent, optomechanics (default {"type": "stationary"})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields hz_re; dispersion poles used
- Features: point_source, line_source, gaussian_beam, plane_wave_tfsf, mode_source, pec_domain, conducting_sheet, effective_index, phase_change_medium, field_probe, flux_monitor, mode_monitor, far_field, adjoint_objective, design_region, resonance_table

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (default "cpml"; cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.bc_x_lo`
- `pml_cells` [cells] (int; default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` [1] (default 1; > 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` [1] (default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real CPML stretch (1 = none); larger damps evanescent and grazing waves; 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `wavelength` [m] (default 1.55e-06; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.wavelength`
- `discretization` (default "quadratic"; quadratic | linear) - Discretization. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.discretization`
- `bloch_kx` [rad/m] (default 0; visible when bc_x_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector x. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.bloch_kx`
- `bloch_ky` [rad/m] (default 0; visible when bc_y_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector y. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.bloch_kx`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1; writes eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic in-plane value: sets eps_xx and eps_yy unless the material sets those (a component wins). n^2 of a lossless dielectric (glass ~2.1-2.25, silicon ~12.1 at 1.55 um). E_x / E_y sit on cell faces: each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells (complex values; solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages the real permittivity of interface faces anisotropically). Solved as the complex eps(omega) = this value - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) + chi(omega) of every Drude / Lorentz pole (exp(+j omega t): loss has Im < 0). With poles it is the background eps_inf (an explicit permittivity wins over the Drude eps_inf). A state-dependent value (e.g. of T) is rewritten at every coupling update of a stationary study (once, after the background solve, in a frequency_domain study). Tabulated eps1 + j eps2 (eps2 <= 0) at one omega: eps1 >= 1: this value eps1, sigma_e = -eps2 omega eps0; a metal (eps1 < 1, below the >= 1 bound shared with em_fdtd_*): no permittivity, a Drude pole with eps_inf 1, a = 1 - eps1, omega_p = omega sqrt((a^2 + eps2^2) / a), gamma = -omega eps2 / a, exact at that omega only (gold -115 - 11j at 1.55 um: omega_p 1.31e16, gamma 1.15e14 rad/s).
- `eps_xx` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, x. Help: shared `em_eme.eps_xx`
- `eps_yy` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, y. Help: shared `em_eme.eps_yy`
- `sigma_e` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss on E_x and E_y (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells): eps gains -j sigma_e / (omega eps0). Weak absorber of index n, extinction kappa at omega: sigma_e = 2 n kappa omega eps0; model metals with a Drude pole, not their DC conductivity.
- `mu_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permeability
  H_z sees mu_zz = mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0) of its cell; also sets the local impedance of line sources. 1 for practically every optical material.
- `sigma_m` [Ohm/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss on H_z: mu_r gains -j sigma_m / (omega mu0); sigma_m / (mu0 mu_r) = sigma_e / (eps0 eps_r) is an impedance-matched absorber (no reflection at normal incidence).
- `eps_xy` [1] (default 0; no fields) - Relative permittivity, xy (off-diagonal)
  eps_xy = eps_yx (real) of a crystal whose in-plane axes are turned against x / y: optic axis in the plane at angle theta from x gives eps_xx = n_o^2 + (n_e^2 - n_o^2) cos^2 theta, eps_yy = n_o^2 + (n_e^2 - n_o^2) sin^2 theta, eps_xy = (n_e^2 - n_o^2) sin theta cos theta; eps_xx eps_yy > eps_xy^2 is required. Solved through eta = eps^-1 per cell: an E_x (E_y) face takes the mean of eps_xx - eps_xy^2 / eps_yy (eps_yy - eps_xy^2 / eps_xx) of its two cells and couples to the other component through eta_xy of the four faces around it (at normal incidence on a layer only eps_yy - eps_xy^2 / eps_xx matters). 9 points per operator row (dearer direct solve), allocated only when a material sets it; 0 in PEC cells and the outer two cell rows of a wall or mirror face. Mode ports, line-source / beam calibrations and the TFSF background ignore it (the build warns for such a line on eps_xy cells). The adjoint holds eps_xy fixed; output eps_xy_sensitivity = dJ / d eps_xy. Acousto-optic and Pockels couplings add to it (slot eps_xy_update); em_fdtd_hz and em_modes have no eps_xy.
- `gyration_z` [1] (default 0; no fields) - Gyration, z (magneto-optic)
  Gyration g (real) of a magneto-optic material magnetised along z: in-plane eps = [[eps_xx, eps_xy + j g], [eps_xy - j g, eps_yy]] (exp(+j omega t); Hermitian, a real g absorbs nothing); g flips sign with the magnetisation. A uniform medium keeps one index, eps_eff = eps - g^2 / eps, but interfaces and guides become non-reciprocal: a slab guide without mirror symmetry across it has beta_forward != beta_backward, and S_21(g) = S_12(-g). Faraday rotation per length |theta_F| = pi |g| / (lambda n): Ce:YIG at 1550 nm (library ce_yig, n ~ 2.2, theta_F ~ -4500 deg/cm) |g| ~ 0.009, Bi:YIG ~ 0.01-0.02. det = eps_xx eps_yy - eps_xy^2 - g^2 must stay > 0; direct solves take a general LU (the adjoint: the transposed solve, g held fixed). 0 in PEC cells and the outer two cell rows of a wall face; mode ports, line-source / beam calibrations and the TFSF background ignore it (the build warns). Validation errors: mirror faces and parity sectors (the image reverses the magnetisation), triangles meshes, every other EM type (em_modes takes gyration_x / gyration_y).

### Fields

Output fields (primary hz_re; [state] = also a state field):
- `hz_re` - Re H_z (A/m) [state]
- `hz_im` - Im H_z (A/m) [state]
- `hz_abs` - |H_z| (A/m)
- `hz_phase` - arg H_z (rad)
- `ex_re` - Re E_x (phasor, cell centres) (V/m)
- `ex_im` - Im E_x (phasor, cell centres) (V/m)
- `ey_re` - Re E_y (phasor, cell centres) (V/m)
- `ey_im` - Im E_y (phasor, cell centres) (V/m)
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity xx (1) [state]
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity yy (1) [state]
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m) [state]
- `absorbed_power` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)
- `eps_sensitivity` - Objective sensitivity dJ/d eps_r (W/m^3)
- `design_density` - Design density (1)
- `crystallinity` - Crystallinity (1)
- `eps_xy` - Relative permittivity xy (off-diagonal) (1)
- `eps_xy_sensitivity` - Objective sensitivity dJ/d eps_xy (W/m^3)
State fields that are no output field:
- `q_abs` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)

### Source slots

- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xy_update` (1): Delta eps_xy over the whole grid (PML ring included), added to the material eps_xy at each transfer (sum slot: acousto-optic and Pockels add -n0_xx^2 n0_yy^2 Delta(1/n^2)_xy).

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.point_source` - Point source

Current-calibrated, mesh-independent point excitation phasor (see excitation) in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell).

- Category source; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result none

Params:
- `excitation` (default "magnetic_current"; magnetic_current | electric_dipole) - Excitation
  magnetic_current: z-directed magnetic line current at the cell centre (isotropic). electric_dipole: in-plane current element along orientation on the four E faces of the cell.
- `magnetic_current` [V] (default 1; visible when excitation in (magnetic_current)) - Magnetic line current
  Peak z-directed magnetic line current K_m (dual of a filament current); mesh-independent field: in a homogeneous medium of eps_r and wavenumber k, |H_z| = omega eps0 eps_r K_m / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| (1 V at 1 um in vacuum: ~1.3e3 A/m at r = 1 um). A fixed K_m radiates power ~ n^2 of its cell, so it drifts when eps there changes; a filament current or dipole radiates n-independent power. Sign: the current is minus the textbook impressed current, so phases (and powers from probe fields) are pi off textbook formulas; moduli and fluxes agree.
- `dipole_moment` [A] (default 0.001; visible when excitation in (electric_dipole)) - Dipole strength
  Peak in-plane dipole strength M = integral of J over the cross-section (A m of current moment per m of z), along orientation; mesh-independent field: in a homogeneous medium of wavenumber k, |H_z| = k M / 4 |H1^(2)(k r)| |sin(phi - orientation)|, phi counter-clockwise from +x (1 mA at 1 um in vacuum: ~5e2 A/m at r = 1 um broadside). Sign: the current is minus the textbook impressed current, so phases (and powers from probe fields) are pi off textbook formulas; moduli and fluxes agree.
- `orientation` [deg] (default 0; visible when excitation in (electric_dipole)) - Dipole orientation
  Dipole current direction counter-clockwise from +x: 0 drives only the E_x faces, 90 only E_y. Radiates most broadside, nothing along it.
- `phase` [deg] (default 0) - Phase. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.line_source` - Line source

Electric sheet current on the hi face of the line cells (+x face of a vertical line, +y face of a horizontal one) sending amplitude (tangential E) to each side in the local medium: a vertical line (x = const) drives E_y along +x and -x, a horizontal one E_x along +y and -y. For a plane wave span the whole domain (an end on a cpml domain edge continues through the PML; on a periodic axis span the whole period); a shorter line diffracts like a slit. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

- Category source; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `amplitude` [V/m] (default 1) - Amplitude
  Tangential E (E_x for a horizontal line, E_y for a vertical one) radiated to each side of the line in the local medium (a plane wave of this amplitude when the line spans a periodic axis); calibrated with the complex face permittivity (sigma_e, dispersion) and mu of the line cells at the solved wavelength: exact in any homogeneous medium. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so across several media (core / cladding) the current steps at the interfaces and diffracts (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. Its medium is the face mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, so on an interface sqrt(mean eps) is not the mean index (Si / air: ~14% off). A recalibration (e.g. thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2).
- `phase` [deg] (default 0) - Phase. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.gaussian_beam` - Gaussian beam

Line source with the profile exp(-((s - center) / waist)^2) along the line: a beam of peak tangential E = amplitude to each side in the local medium (vertical line: E_y, along +x and -x; horizontal: E_x, along +y and -y), waist on the line, sheet on the hi face of the line cells. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

- Category source; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `amplitude` [V/m] (default 1) - Amplitude
  Peak tangential E (E_x for a horizontal line, E_y for a vertical one) at the beam centre on the waist line, radiated to each side in the local medium; calibrated with the complex face permittivity (sigma_e, dispersion) and mu of the line cells at the solved wavelength: exact in any homogeneous medium. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so across several media (core / cladding) the current steps at the interfaces and diffracts (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. Its medium is the face mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, so on an interface sqrt(mean eps) is not the mean index (Si / air: ~14% off). A recalibration (e.g. thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2).
- `phase` [deg] (default 0) - Phase. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`
- `waist` [m] (default 1e-06; > 0) - Waist radius. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.gaussian_beam.waist`
- `center` [m] (nullable) - Beam centre
  Beam axis along the line (x for a horizontal line, y for a vertical one); empty = midpoint. Off the line only the tail launches (validation warns).

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.plane_wave_tfsf` - Plane wave box (+x)

Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.plane_wave_tfsf`

- Category source; selection domain entities, object kinds rectangle, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `amplitude` [V/m] (default 1) - Amplitude
  Peak incident in-plane |E| (E_y at normal incidence) of the wave of the uniform medium on the box outline: H_z = n |E| / (eta0 mu_r), n = sqrt(eps_yy mu_r), also for an oblique Bloch ky wave.
- `phase` [deg] (default 0) - Phase. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.mode_source` - Mode source

Port source launching one guided mode of the cross-section under an axis-aligned line in one direction. One-sided total-field / scattered-field line: total field from the line cells downstream, only the scattered field (what comes back) upstream; the interface is the lo face of the line cells for positive, their hi face for negative. The launch is exact and one-sided at every solved wavelength of a straight guide. Mode monitors normalise by it when it is the only enabled mode source of the physics. The 1D line eigenmodes use the FDFD discretisation (Yee widths, PML stretch, complex eps and mu of the line cells with poles, sigma_e, sigma_m), re-solved at every solved wavelength and after any material change (thermo-optic coupling, state-dependent permittivity). Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side, on a locally uniform mesh (validation warns when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line and when its face lies inside a CPML layer, i.e. the line is in the outermost window cell). Span ends: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML (open); an end on a pec or antisymmetric domain edge takes tangential E = 0 on the inner face of the outermost cell (dH_z/dn = 0), one on a pmc edge H_z = 0 and one on a symmetric edge H_z odd; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E along the propagation direction = 0 on the face beyond the end, so dH_z/dn = 0), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns above 1% of the mode peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The in-plane E faces use the permittivity of the operator (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells), so a guide edge on a face line takes the core / cladding mean. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). Result 'table' of the latest port solve (frequency_domain: its last wavelength), one row per mode for the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes: mode_number, n_eff, n_eff_imag (< 0 = loss, exp(+j omega t)), loss_db_per_cm, n_group, edge_field (largest |field| at the line ends / peak; above 1e-2 at a metal end the line cuts the mode), selected (the launched mode); extras wavelength (m), power (W/m), direction, mode_number and phase (deg).

- Category source; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `table`

Params:
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Mode number. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.mode_number`
- `direction` (default "positive"; positive | negative) - Direction. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.direction`
- `power` [W/m] (default 1; > 0) - Mode power. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.power`
- `phase` [deg] (default 0) - Phase. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor: tangential E = 0 on the four faces of each cell whose centre lies in the selected domains (H_z inside is 0), staircased. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (Dey-Mittra) only faces wholly inside the drawn metal are PEC; cut cells use their free face lengths and free area (>= 0.02 of the cell), keeping the operator reciprocal; mode ports, sources and eps_xy couplings keep the cell mask.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result none

Params: none

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

Time-averaged Poynting flux through an axis-aligned line per solved wavelength: S_x = 1/2 Re(E_y H_z*) (vertical line), S_y = -1/2 Re(E_x H_z*) (horizontal), H_z of the line cells, E on their hi face from Ampere's law (curl of H_z plus a source current on that face); > 0 toward +x / +y. Keep it off the line cells of a line source or gaussian beam: their sheet sits on that face, where the flux jumps, and the monitor reads the line-cell side (minus the power sent toward -x / -y). Keep its measuring face (hi face of the line cells) off a mode_source interface face (the line one cell upstream of a positive source, or the line of a negative one) and entirely inside or outside a plane_wave_tfsf box: the field jumps there between total and scattered field (validation warns). Result 'flux_spectrum' in W/m (power per unit z length over the line cells, absolute: a line source of amplitude A spanning a period L in vacuum sends A^2 L / (2 eta0) to each side), one entry per solved wavelength, sorted. The discrete flux is conserved exactly through lossless cells; transmission = device power / power of a reference run with the same source. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

- Category monitor; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params: none

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.mode_monitor` - Mode monitor

Port monitor splitting the field on an axis-aligned line into the forward (positive: toward +x / +y) and backward (negative) amplitudes a of one guided mode at every solved wavelength: H_z in the line cells and E_y (vertical line) / E_x (horizontal) from Ampere's law on their hi face are projected on the mode solved there, so each direction is measured separately, unlike a flux_monitor. The 1D line eigenmodes use the FDFD discretisation (Yee widths, PML stretch, complex eps and mu of the line cells with poles, sigma_e, sigma_m), re-solved at every solved wavelength and after any material change (thermo-optic coupling, state-dependent permittivity). Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side, on a locally uniform mesh (validation warns when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line and when its face lies inside a CPML layer, i.e. the line is in the outermost window cell). Span ends: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML (open); an end on a pec or antisymmetric domain edge takes tangential E = 0 on the inner face of the outermost cell (dH_z/dn = 0), one on a pmc edge H_z = 0 and one on a symmetric edge H_z odd; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E along the propagation direction = 0 on the face beyond the end, so dH_z/dn = 0), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns above 1% of the mode peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The in-plane E faces use the permittivity of the operator (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells), so a guide edge on a face line takes the core / cladding mean. Keep its measuring face (hi face of the line cells) off a mode_source interface face (the line one cell upstream of a positive source, or the line of a negative one) and entirely inside or outside a plane_wave_tfsf box: the field jumps there between total and scattered field (validation warns). The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength (m, ascending): power_positive / power_negative = |a|^2 in W/m (modes normalised to 1 W/m); with exactly one enabled mode_source in the physics also fraction_positive / fraction_negative = |a / (sqrt(P) e^{j phase})|^2 (source power P and phase; |S|^2: transmission downstream of the source, reflection upstream) and phase_positive / phase_negative (rad), the phase of that S-parameter relative to the source's own line, not de-embedded (each mode profile phased with its largest sample real positive, the lowest-coordinate one of mirror-equal peaks); extras frequency, wavelength, n_eff, n_eff_imag (per wavelength), mode_number and normalized (True with the fractions).

- Category monitor; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Mode number. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_monitor.mode_number`
