## Physics type `em_fdfd_nonlinear` - Nonlinear optics, frequency domain (2D, harmonic channels)

2D frequency-domain chi2 / chi3 mixing between harmonic channels: every harmonic_channel feature is one em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz solve at its own frequency on the shared mesh and materials (phase matching from the material dispersion). chi2_medium / chi3_medium add the nonlinear polarisation as a phasor source of the target channels (exp(+j omega t), P = eps0 2^(1-n) sum chi : E..E); surface_chi2 (selection interface) and sheet_nonlinearity (2D material on a line) add surface polarisations. coupling_mode: undepleted (one pass in rank order) or pump_depleted (self-consistent; picard may not converge for high-gain parametric or bistable cavities: newton). Sources and monitors are the em_fdfd_ez / _hz features with a channel param; fields and powers are absolute and per unit z length (2D SHG efficiency P_2w / P_w^2 in m/W). Each channel factorises its own operator (host SuperLU, MUMPS or PARDISO memory adds up per channel). Studies: nonlinear_frequency_domain (one snapshot per channel), optimization (design_region on the shared permittivity, adjoint_objective on the channels; pump_depleted needs newton with a chi3 medium). Output fields of the shown channel: phasors of both polarisations (the other reads 0), nonlinear_polarization_abs |P_NL|, poling, carrier_density (0 without carriers), eps_sensitivity (adjoint of the adjoint_objective features), design_density. Couplings: permittivity writers (thermo-optic) act on every channel; em_heat_joule reads the absorbed power of every channel (linear q_abs plus the exact TPA and free-carrier absorption, the same for picard and newton) into a background heat physics (solution feedback rounds). Bloch phase and mirror parity per channel: see harmonic_channel. Instance usually 'nl'.

- Default instance name `nl`; studies nonlinear_frequency_domain, optimization (default {"type": "nonlinear_frequency_domain"})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor; refinement indicator fields e_abs; dispersion poles used
- Features: harmonic_channel, chi2_medium, chi3_medium, surface_chi2, sheet_nonlinearity, pec_domain, conducting_sheet, design_region, point_source, line_source, gaussian_beam, plane_wave_tfsf, mode_source, field_probe, flux_monitor, mode_monitor, far_field, adjoint_objective

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (default "cpml"; cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.bc_x_lo`
- `pml_cells` [cells] (int; default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` [1] (default 1; > 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` [1] (default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real CPML stretch (1 = none); larger damps evanescent and grazing waves; 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `coupling_mode` (default "undepleted"; undepleted | pump_depleted) - Coupling mode
  undepleted: each channel solved once in rank order (inputs 0, a combination 1 + the highest rank it names), fed only by lower-rank channels (no back-action, SPM / XPM or free carriers; small conversion). pump_depleted: every mixing term and the chi3 free carriers, self-consistent by iteration_method to tolerance.
- `iteration_method` (default "picard"; picard | newton; visible when coupling_mode in (pump_depleted)) - Iteration method
  picard: block Gauss-Seidel sweeps in rank order with relaxation and Anderson acceleration, the SPM / XPM / carrier diagonal lagged in the channel operator (reassembled, GMRES on the recycled factor each sweep); cheap, converges while conversion per pass is moderate. newton: Newton-Krylov with the exact Wirtinger Jacobian, GMRES (restart 20, <= 60 products per step) preconditioned by the channels' factors, Eisenstat-Walker forcing, backtracking; one back-substitution per nonlinear channel per product; quadratic near the solution (high conversion, parametric gain near threshold, cavities, strong Kerr). Kerr and carriers stay in the rhs (q_abs then holds only linear losses). cusolver_qr refactorises every solve, which newton multiplies.
- `tolerance` [1] (default 1e-08; > 0; visible when coupling_mode in (pump_depleted)) - Iteration tolerance
  Stop at max_k ||G_k - x_k|| / ||G_k|| <= tolerance, G = channel fields solved from the stored fields x (picard: one sweep; newton: one solve per channel from the iterate): the fixed-point update, not the operator residual. Picard GMRES reaches 1e-10: stay above ~1e-9.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; >= 1; visible when coupling_mode in (pump_depleted)) - Iteration limit
  Sweeps (picard) or Newton steps per continuation step; not converged: warning, last iterate kept (snapshot labels say so, summary nonlinear_solve converged false).
- `relaxation` [1] (default 1; (0, 1]; visible when coupling_mode in (pump_depleted)) - Relaxation
  picard only: x + beta f (1 = plain sweeps); 0.3-0.7 for an oscillating iteration (high conversion, cavities).
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 5; >= 0; visible when coupling_mode in (pump_depleted)) - Anderson depth
  picard only: history m (0 = relaxed Picard); 2 m stacked copies of every channel field on the GPU.
- `continuation_steps` (int; default 1; >= 1; visible when coupling_mode in (pump_depleted)) - Continuation steps
  Ramp every source amplitude through k / steps, each step warm-started from the previous (1 = none). Helps near bistability; on a Kerr S-curve the branch reached depends on the ramp.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1; writes eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic: eps_zz (E_z channels) and eps_xx, eps_yy (H_z channels) unless the material sets a component. Each channel uses the complex value at its own frequency: this - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) + every Drude / Lorentz pole chi(omega), so the dispersion sets the phase mismatch (non-dispersive materials are phase matched by construction). For a dispersive material the background eps_inf.
- `eps_zz` [1] (default 1; >= 1; writes eps_r) - Relative permittivity, z (along the guide)
  The component E_z channels see; overrides eps_r for E_z. z-cut LN: eps_r = n_o^2, eps_zz = n_e^2.
- `eps_xx` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, x. Help: shared `em_eme.eps_xx`
- `eps_yy` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, y. Help: shared `em_eme.eps_yy`
- `sigma_e` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Electric conductivity
  On every E component; enters each channel at its own omega (see eps_r).
- `mu_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permeability
  Real, 1 for optical materials; mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0) per channel.
- `sigma_m` [Ohm/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Magnetic conductivity
  mu_r gains -j sigma_m / (omega mu0) (artificial absorbers only).

### Fields

Output fields (primary e_abs; [state] = also a state field):
- `ez_re` - Re E_z (V/m) [state]
- `ez_im` - Im E_z (V/m) [state]
- `ez_abs` - |E_z| (V/m)
- `ez_phase` - arg E_z (rad)
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity (1) [state]
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m) [state]
- `absorbed_power` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)
- `eps_sensitivity` - Objective sensitivity dJ/d eps_r (W/m^3)
- `design_density` - Design density (1)
- `hz_re` - Re H_z (A/m) [state]
- `hz_im` - Im H_z (A/m) [state]
- `hz_abs` - |H_z| (A/m)
- `hz_phase` - arg H_z (rad)
- `ex_re` - Re E_x (phasor, cell centres) (V/m)
- `ex_im` - Im E_x (phasor, cell centres) (V/m)
- `ey_re` - Re E_y (phasor, cell centres) (V/m)
- `ey_im` - Im E_y (phasor, cell centres) (V/m)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity xx (1) [state]
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity yy (1) [state]
- `eps_xy` - Relative permittivity xy (off-diagonal) (1)
- `nonlinear_polarization_abs` - |P_NL| (shown channel) (C/m^2)
- `poling` - Poling sign (chi2 media) (1)
- `carrier_density` - Free-carrier density (chi3 media) (1/m^3)
State fields that are no output field:
- `q_abs` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)

Scalar outputs: power_exchange_<channel> (W/m): time-averaged power the applied mixing terms (and free carriers) deliver to that channel, W_k = (omega_k / 2) sum_cells A Im(conj(E_k) . P_k); > 0 = gains (generated channel), < 0 = loses (depleted pump, pump_depleted only), 0 on inputs undepleted. power_exchange_imbalance (1): |sum_k W_k| / sum_k |W_k| over the whole mixing table, ~1e-12 for real Kleinman-symmetric tensors whatever the fields: an implementation check, not convergence (larger for general / non-Kleinman d, per-process or Miller factors, Im chi3 and carriers, where the sum is the nonlinear loss). nonlinear_absorption (W/m): -W of the applied SPM / XPM terms of chi3 media and sigma3 sheets (TPA; 0 undepleted). free_carrier_absorption (W/m): -W of the carrier polarisation over every channel (> 0 absorbs). peak_carrier_density (1/m^3): the largest steady-state N. iterations (1): sweeps or Newton steps of the last solve (1 undepleted, summed over continuation steps); residual (1): the last iterate's largest relative channel change (0 undepleted).

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.harmonic_channel` - Harmonic channel

One frequency (and polarisation); the feature name (an identifier) is the channel name. Every channel is its own em_fdfd_ez / _hz solve on the shared mesh, materials evaluated at its frequency (phase matching comes from the dispersion). Only chi2 / chi3 processes landing on a declared channel are computed (no automatic closure; validation info lists near misses). At least one input channel; sources and monitors name their channel. Mirror faces: inputs have that E parity, a generated channel s^(sum of its coefficients) (2 p, p - s even; 3 p, p + s - i odd), so an even channel solves an antisymmetric face as symmetric (unfolded fields follow); an input reached by frequency only must have the parity of the process (validation error). The image half holds the mirrored crystal.

- Category domain_condition; selection none (a selection is ignored with a warning); result none

Params:
- `definition` (default "wavelength"; wavelength | combination) - Defined by
  wavelength: an input channel (rank 0). combination: a generated channel at an integer combination of other channels (rank 1 + the highest rank it names), so mixing products land on it exactly.
- `wavelength` [m] (default 1.55e-06; > 0; visible when definition in (wavelength)) - Wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength of an input channel; sweep it for spectra (e.g. SHG versus pump wavelength). Typical 0.8e-6 to 2e-6 m.
- `combination` (str; default "2 p"; visible when definition in (combination)) - Combination
  Integer combination of other channel names, e.g. '2 p' (SHG of p), 'p + s' (SFG), 'p - s' (DFG), '2 p - s' (FWM idler); '*' optional. Parsed, not evaluated; frequency > 0, no cycles. A polarization both channel is named without _ez / _hz.
- `polarization` (default "ez"; ez | hz | both) - Polarisation
  ez: E_z (an em_fdfd_ez solve); hz: E_x, E_y (em_fdfd_hz); both: two channels <name>_ez, <name>_hz (two factorisations: memory doubles). Chi2 tensors couple the polarisations (d31 E_z^2 -> P_x, GaAs d14 E_x E_y -> P_z), so a generated channel may need the other polarisation than its pump.
- `bloch_kx` [rad/m] (default 0; visible when definition in (wavelength)) - Bloch wave vector x
  Input channels, only with periodic bc_x_lo / _hi (validation warns otherwise): Bloch wave F(x + L) = F(x) exp(-j kx L) per meshed period L, as em_fdfd_* bloch_kx (oblique incidence: k0 sin(theta)). A generated channel carries the combination of its inputs' k (2 p: 2 k_p); an input reached by frequency only must match k modulo 2 pi / L (validation error). k != 0 on any channel: no surface_chi2 / sheet_nonlinearity (error), no port line spanning that period.
- `bloch_ky` [rad/m] (default 0; visible when definition in (wavelength)) - Bloch wave vector y
  Input channels, only with periodic bc_y_lo / _hi (validation warns otherwise): Bloch wave F(y + L) = F(y) exp(-j ky L) per meshed period L, as em_fdfd_* bloch_ky (oblique incidence: k0 sin(theta)). A generated channel carries the combination of its inputs' k (2 p: 2 k_p); an input reached by frequency only must match k modulo 2 pi / L (validation error). k != 0 on any channel: no surface_chi2 / sheet_nonlinearity (error), no port line spanning that period.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium` - Second-order nonlinear medium

Bulk chi2 of the selected domains: the crystal-class tensor rotated into model axes, times the poling sign per cell. Response (exp(+j omega t) phasors): P(w3) = eps0 2^(1-n) sum over ordered source tuples chi2 : E E, so SHG P(2w) = eps0 d E^2, SFG P(w1 + w2) = 2 eps0 d E1 E2, DFG P(w1 - w2) = eps0 chi2 E1 conj(E2). Products at the cell centres (hz E_x / E_y by face means, P returned by the area-weighted adjoint: discrete power exchange exact). Overlapping media add. 2D: fields and powers per unit z length, so P_2w / P_w^2 is in m/W (multiply by an effective height for a 3D guide).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params:
- `crystal_class` (default "3m"; 3m | -43m | 6mm | mm2 | 32 | general) - Crystal class
  Point group fixing the non-zero d_il (Kleinman symmetry, except general): 3m (LiNbO3, LiTaO3, BBO: d22, d31 = d15 = d24, d33, d16 = d21 = -d22; LN |d33| ~ 2.5e-11, |d31| ~ 4.6e-12, |d22| ~ 2.1e-12 m/V at 1.06 um), -43m (GaAs, GaP, InP, ZnS: d14 = d25 = d36; GaAs ~ 1.2e-10 m/V at 1.55 um), 6mm (AlN, GaN, ZnO: d15 = d24, d31 = d32, d33), mm2 (KTP: d15, d24, d31, d32, d33), 32 (quartz: d11, d12 = d26 = -d11, d14, d25 = -d14), general (all 18; power exchange exact only for Kleinman-symmetric values). Signs follow the crystal axes of orientation.
- `d11` [m/V] (default 0; visible when crystal_class in (32, general)) - d11. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`
- `d12`, `d13` [m/V] (default 0; visible when crystal_class in (general)) - d12 / d13. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`
- `d14` [m/V] (default 0; visible when crystal_class in (-43m, 32, general)) - d14. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`
- `d15` [m/V] (default 0; visible when crystal_class in (6mm, mm2, general)) - d15. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`
- `d16`, `d21` [m/V] (default 0; visible when crystal_class in (general)) - d16 / d21. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`
- `d22` [m/V] (default 0; visible when crystal_class in (3m, general)) - d22. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`
- `d23` [m/V] (default 0; visible when crystal_class in (general)) - d23. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`
- `d24` [m/V] (default 0; visible when crystal_class in (mm2, general)) - d24. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`
- `d25`, `d26` [m/V] (default 0; visible when crystal_class in (general)) - d25 / d26. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`
- `d31` [m/V] (default 0; visible when crystal_class in (3m, 6mm, mm2, general)) - d31. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`
- `d32` [m/V] (default 0; visible when crystal_class in (mm2, general)) - d32. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`
- `d33` [m/V] (default 0; visible when crystal_class in (3m, 6mm, mm2, general)) - d33. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`
- `d34`, `d35`, `d36` [m/V] (default 0; visible when crystal_class in (general)) - d34 / d35 / d36. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.d11`
- `orientation` (default "z_cut"; z_cut | x_cut | y_cut | euler) - Orientation. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.orientation`
- `euler_alpha`, `euler_beta`, `euler_gamma` [deg] (default 0; visible when orientation in (euler)) - Euler alpha / Euler beta / Euler gamma
  z-x-z Euler angle of the rotation crystal -> model axes Rz(alpha) Rx(beta) Rz(gamma).
- `poling` [1] (default 1; may use x, y) - Poling
  Domain sign per cell: >= 0 keeps the tensor, < 0 inverts it. Periodic poling (QPM): sign(sin(2 * pi * x / Lambda)), Lambda = 2 pi / |k(2 omega) - 2 k(omega)| = lambda / (2 |n(2 omega) - n(omega)|) of the guided modes; chirped gratings likewise. 1 = unpoled.
- `miller_scaling` (bool; default false) - Miller's rule
  Miller's rule on every process: chi(n)(w; w1..wn) ~ chi1(w) chi1(w1)..chi1(wn), chi1 = Re eps_r - 1 averaged over the medium at each channel frequency (once at build; run log lists the factors), normalised so the given coefficients hold for SHG of reference_wavelength, d(2 w_r; w_r, w_r). Off: one frequency-independent tensor. Validation uses unscaled values; scaled tensors are not fully permutation symmetric (power_exchange_imbalance no longer ~0).
- `reference_wavelength` [m] (> 0; nullable; visible when miller_scaling in (true)) - Reference wavelength
  Pump wavelength of the SHG process the d coefficients are given for (Miller's rule reference); empty = the first input channel.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi3_medium` - Third-order nonlinear medium

Bulk chi3 of the selected domains (tensor rotated into model axes, n2 / beta scaled by n0^2 per cell). Response (exp(+j omega t) phasors): THG P(3w) = (1/4) eps0 chi3 E^3, SPM P(w) = (3/4) eps0 chi3 |E|^2 E, XPM P(w1) = (6/4) eps0 chi3 |E2|^2 E1, degenerate FWM P(2 wp - ws) = (3/4) eps0 chi3 Ep^2 conj(Es). Undepleted keeps only THG / FWM-type terms feeding higher-rank channels; SPM / XPM (a channel on itself) need pump_depleted. Products at the cell centres as chi2_medium; overlapping media add; 2D (per unit z length).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params:
- `tensor` (default "isotropic"; isotropic | cubic) - Tensor
  isotropic: chi_xxyy = chi_xyxy = chi_xyyx = chi_xxxx / 3 (glasses, amorphous films); cubic: chi_iijj = chi_ijij = chi_ijji = anisotropy chi_xxxx / 3 in crystal axes (m3m: Si, Ge, GaAs), rotated by orientation.
- `anisotropy` [1] (default 1; >= 0; visible when tensor in (cubic)) - Anisotropy
  rho = 3 chi_xxyy / chi_xxxx of the cubic tensor (1 = isotropic; silicon ~1.27 at 1.55 um).
- `orientation` (default "z_cut"; z_cut | x_cut | y_cut | euler; visible when tensor in (cubic)) - Orientation. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.orientation`
- `euler_alpha`, `euler_beta`, `euler_gamma` [deg] (default 0; visible when orientation in (euler)) - Euler alpha / Euler beta / Euler gamma
  z-x-z Euler angle of the rotation crystal -> model axes Rz(alpha) Rx(beta) Rz(gamma).
- `strength` (default "n2_beta"; n2_beta | chi3) - Strength given by
  n2_beta: chi_xxxx = (4 eps0 c n0^2 / 3) (n2 - j c tpa_beta / (2 omega_ref)) (as em_fdtd_* nonlinear_medium); chi3: chi_xxxx = chi3_real + j chi3_imag. One chi3 serves every process (real materials differ: thg_scale, fwm_scale, miller_scaling).
- `n2` [m^2/W] (default 0; visible when strength in (n2_beta)) - Kerr index n2
  dn = n2 I, I = n0 c eps0 |E|^2 / 2 (linearly polarised plane wave). Silicon ~4.5e-18 to 6e-18, Si3N4 ~2.5e-19, silica ~2.6e-20 m^2/W at 1.55 um.
- `tpa_beta` [m/W] (default 0; >= 0; visible when strength in (n2_beta)) - Two-photon absorption
  dI/dz = -beta I^2 (Im chi3 < 0); silicon ~8e-12 m/W at 1.55 um. Its power: scalar nonlinear_absorption (pump_depleted).
- `background_index` [1] (> 0; nullable; visible when strength in (n2_beta) or free_carriers in (true)) - Background index
  n0 of the n2 / beta conversion and the free-carrier permittivity; empty = Re sqrt(eps_r(omega_ref)) per cell (poles included, once at build).
- `reference_wavelength` [m] (> 0; nullable; visible when strength in (n2_beta) or any of miller_scaling, free_carriers in (true)) - Reference wavelength
  Wavelength of n2 / tpa_beta (omega_ref of the TPA term and n0), the Miller's-rule reference (SPM) and the free-carrier coefficients; empty = the first input channel.
- `chi3_real` [m^2/V^2] (default 0; visible when strength in (chi3)) - chi3 real part
  Re chi_xxxx (silicon ~2.5e-19 at 1.55 um).
- `chi3_imag` [m^2/V^2] (default 0; <= 0; visible when strength in (chi3)) - chi3 imaginary part
  Im chi_xxxx (< 0 = loss).
- `thg_scale` [1] (default 1) - Third-harmonic factor
  Factor on chi3 for THG (3 w) and TFG (w1 + w2 + w3) of this medium (real THG chi3 differs from the Kerr one); 1 = Kerr chi3, 0 drops them. != 1 breaks full permutation symmetry (power_exchange_imbalance no longer ~0).
- `fwm_scale` [1] (default 1) - Four-wave mixing factor
  Factor on chi3 for FWM (w1 + w2 - w3 onto a channel, not SPM / XPM) of this medium; 1 = Kerr chi3, 0 drops them.
- `miller_scaling` (bool; default false) - Miller's rule
  Miller's rule on every process: chi(n)(w; w1..wn) ~ chi1(w) chi1(w1)..chi1(wn), chi1 = Re eps_r - 1 averaged over the medium at each channel frequency (once at build; run log lists the factors), normalised so the given coefficients hold for SPM at reference_wavelength (the n2 / tpa_beta process). Off: one frequency-independent tensor. Validation uses unscaled values; scaled tensors are not fully permutation symmetric (power_exchange_imbalance no longer ~0).
- `free_carriers` (bool; default false) - Free carriers
  Steady-state carriers from TPA (pump_depleted only; undepleted ignores them with a warning): N = carrier_lifetime G per cell, G = TPA power density of the SPM / XPM terms / (2 hbar omega) (no diffusion: N follows the local I^2); every channel sees dn = -fcd_coefficient N and alpha = fca_cross_section N, both x (lambda / reference_wavelength)^2, as delta eps = 2 n0 dn - j n0 c alpha / omega. Linear in N. Field carrier_density, scalars free_carrier_absorption, peak_carrier_density.
- `carrier_lifetime` [s] (default 1e-09; >= 0; visible when free_carriers in (true)) - Carrier lifetime
  Effective lifetime: silicon wires ~0.5-3 ns, ~10-100 ps with sweep-out by a reverse-biased junction; 0 = no carriers.
- `fcd_coefficient` [m^3] (default 1.35e-27; >= 0; visible when free_carriers in (true)) - Carrier index coefficient
  dn = -fcd_coefficient N at reference_wavelength; silicon at 1.55 um ~1.35e-27 (equal electron and hole densities, linear Soref-Bennett fit).
- `fca_cross_section` [m^2] (default 1.45e-21; >= 0; visible when free_carriers in (true)) - Carrier absorption cross-section
  alpha = fca_cross_section N at reference_wavelength; silicon at 1.55 um ~1.45e-21 (equal electron and hole densities).

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.surface_chi2` - Surface second-order nonlinearity

Surface chi2 sheet on the interface of the selected domains: P_s [C/m] = eps0 2^(1-n) sum chi_s : E E with the isotropic-surface (C_inf_v) tensor in the local frame of the outward normal n, tangent t = z x n and z; SHG of one channel P_s,n = (1/2) eps0 (chi_s_nnn E_n^2 + chi_s_ntt (E_t^2 + E_z^2)), P_s,t = eps0 chi_s_tnt E_n E_t, P_s,z = eps0 chi_s_tnt E_n E_z. Sites: cell faces between a selected and an unselected cell (tangential E on the face, E_z the mean of its two cells, E_n at the selvedge cell), P_s returned by the exact adjoint (discrete power exchange exact). Its terms join the chi2 media in the mixing table (hz channels carry E_n / E_t, ez channels E_z). Normal-incidence SHG of a flat interface vanishes by symmetry: curvature, corners or oblique fields are needed. 2D: powers per unit z length.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params:
- `chi_s_nnn` [m^2/V] (default 0) - chi_s nnn
  chi_perp,perp,perp: normal polarisation from the normal field. Noble metals ~1e-19 to 1e-18 m^2/V (literature spreads by an order of magnitude and depends on the selvedge convention).
- `chi_s_ntt` [m^2/V] (default 0) - chi_s ntt
  = chi_s_nzz (chi_perp,par,par): normal polarisation from the tangential fields, a dipole layer that jumps the tangential E (no radiation at normal incidence on a flat interface).
- `chi_s_tnt` [m^2/V] (default 0) - chi_s tnt
  = chi_s_ttn = chi_s_znz = chi_s_zzn (chi_par,perp,par): tangential polarisation from E_n times a tangential field. chi_s_ntt = chi_s_tnt makes the tensor fully permutation symmetric (power_exchange_imbalance ~0).
- `selvedge` (default "inside"; inside | outside) - Normal field side
  Cell row whose normal E is sampled and whose normal-E faces carry P_s,n / w (a one-cell dipole layer): inside = the selected cell, outside = its unselected neighbour. E_n jumps by eps_out / eps_in, so this is the field convention of chi_s_nnn; tangential E and E_z are sampled on the interface. The tangential jump sits half a cell off the interface (first order in the mesh).
- `interface` (default "staircase"; staircase | smoothed) - Interface shape
  staircase: sites = faces between selected and unselected cells, normals +-x / +-y, face lengths: exact for axis-aligned sides, a curve up to 4 / pi too long with axis normals. smoothed: same faces with the normal of the drawn shape where it crosses the line between the two cells (point tests at build) and length face x |n . face normal|: true curve length and normal (sites stay on faces: first order; corners rounded over ~a cell).
- `interface_with` (names: geometry names; default []) - Only facing
  Domain objects: only interface faces whose unselected cell lies in one of them carry the sheet (e.g. the metal / air side of a ridge on a substrate); empty = every unselected neighbour.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.sheet_nonlinearity` - Nonlinear sheet

Nonlinear 2D-material sheet on an axis-aligned line: P_s [C/m] = eps0 2^(1-n) sum chi_s : E E (D3h or general) or K [A/m] (sigma3, entered as P_s = K / (j omega) of the target channel) from the tangential fields at the conducting_sheet sites (E_z at line-cell centres, tangential E on their hi faces), returned to the same sites (exact for the discrete equations). Terms join the mixing table (sigma3 as up to two media: THG / TFG under the feature name, SPM / XPM / FWM as '<name>:kerr'). Add conducting_sheet on the same line for the linear response. pump_depleted: sheet SPM / XPM stay in the rhs; their absorption (Re sigma3 > 0) is in nonlinear_absorption and absorbed_power (line cells, heated by em_heat_joule). The adjoint differentiates the sheet terms. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1); a span end on a cpml edge continues through the PML.

- Category boundary_condition; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `sheet_model` (default "D3h"; D3h | chi2_general | sigma3) - Nonlinearity
  D3h: TMD monolayer chi_s(2) (MoS2, WS2, ...): chi_aaa = chi_s, chi_abb = chi_bab = chi_bba = -chi_s, armchair axis a at armchair_angle in the sheet plane (t, z); chi2_general: the six chi_s_<ijk> of (t, z); sigma3: in-plane isotropic third-order conductivity of graphene, K = 2^(1-n) sum sigma3 : E E E [A/m] (THG K = sigma3 E^3 / 4, SPM K = (3/4) sigma3 |E|^2 E), separate THG / TFG and SPM / XPM / FWM values (orders of magnitude apart in graphene; no Cheng-Vermeulen-Sipe model).
- `chi_s` [m^2/V] (default 0; visible when sheet_model in (D3h)) - chi_s
  chi_aaa; MoS2 / WS2 monolayers ~1e-20 to 1e-19 m^2/V at near-infrared SHG (bulk d x 0.65 nm; literature spans an order of magnitude).
- `armchair_angle` [deg] (default 0; visible when sheet_model in (D3h)) - Armchair angle
  Armchair axis a from t toward z in the sheet frame: t along the line (+x horizontal, +y vertical), z out of plane; the normal field does not enter; 0 = along the line (E_z alone drives P_t = -(1/2) eps0 chi_s E_z^2), 90 = out of plane (E_t alone drives P_z = -(1/2) eps0 chi_s E_t^2); 120 degree period.
- `chi_s_ttt`, `chi_s_tzz`, `chi_s_ttz`, `chi_s_ztt`, `chi_s_zzz`, `chi_s_zzt` [m^2/V] (default 0; visible when sheet_model in (chi2_general)) - chi_s ttt / chi_s tzz / chi_s ttz / chi_s ztt / chi_s zzz / chi_s zzt
  General 2D chi_s(2) in the sheet frame: t along the line (+x horizontal, +y vertical), z out of plane; the normal field does not enter (ttz = tzt, zzt = ztz).
- `sigma3_real` [S m^2/V^2] (default 0; visible when sheet_model in (sigma3)) - sigma3 (Kerr) real part
  SPM / XPM / FWM (sigma_tttt = sigma_zzzz, sigma_ttzz = sigma_tztz = sigma_tzzt = sigma / 3); Re > 0 absorbs. Graphene: strongly Fermi- and photon-energy dependent (literature ~1e-24 to 1e-20).
- `sigma3_imag` [S m^2/V^2] (default 0; visible when sheet_model in (sigma3)) - sigma3 (Kerr) imaginary part
  SPM / XPM / FWM (exp(+j omega t): opposite sign to exp(-i omega t) literature).
- `thg_sigma3_real`, `thg_sigma3_imag` [S m^2/V^2] (default 0; visible when sheet_model in (sigma3)) - sigma3 (THG) real part / sigma3 (THG) imaginary part
  THG / TFG, same tensor form as sigma3_real.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

In every channel. E_z channels: Perfect electric conductor: E_z = 0 in every cell whose centre lies in the selected domains, staircased; with solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries the H links from free cells put E_z = 0 at the drawn wall (exact wall distance t d, t >= 0.02). H_z channels: Perfect electric conductor: tangential E = 0 on the four faces of each cell whose centre lies in the selected domains (H_z inside is 0), staircased. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (Dey-Mittra) only faces wholly inside the drawn metal are PEC; cut cells use their free face lengths and free area (>= 0.02 of the cell), keeping the operator reciprocal; mode ports, sources and eps_xy couplings keep the cell mask.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params: none

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.conducting_sheet` - Conducting sheet

In every channel, sigma_s at each channel frequency (linear; sheet_nonlinearity on the same line adds the nonlinear response). Zero-thickness conducting sheet (graphene, a TMD monolayer, a metal film much thinner than a cell) on an axis-aligned line: K = sigma_s E_t [A/m] (tangential E only). em_fdfd_ez: E_z of the line cells, diagonal += -j omega mu0 sigma_s / w (w the line-cell width across the line). em_fdfd_hz: E_x (horizontal line) / E_y (vertical) on the hi face of the line cells, face permittivity += -j sigma_s / (omega eps0 w), w the face spacing; not in the last cell before a non-periodic outer face. Vacuum, normal incidence: transmission |1 / (1 + eta0 sigma_s / 2)|^2 (on the grid 1 / |1 + omega mu0 sigma_s w / (2 sin(k w))|^2, k the discrete wavenumber). Its loss 1/2 Re sigma_s |E_t|^2 per sheet area goes into q_abs of the line cells (em_heat_joule heats them). Only the operator sees it, not line-source / TFSF calibrations, port modes or material maps (keep source, port and TFSF lines off it; enclose it in a TFSF box as a scatterer). A span end on a cpml edge continues through the PML; sheets on one line add. Eigenfrequency: sigma_s at the target wavelength (first-order error away from it). The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1). No result.

- Category boundary_condition; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `model` (default "constant"; constant | graphene_kubo) - Conductivity model. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.model`
- `sigma_real` [S] (default 6.08534e-05; visible when model in (constant)) - Conductivity (real part). Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.sigma_real`
- `sigma_imag` [S] (default 0; visible when model in (constant)) - Conductivity (imaginary part). Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.sigma_imag`
- `fermi_energy` [eV] (default 0.2; visible when model in (graphene_kubo)) - Fermi energy. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.fermi_energy`
- `scattering_time` [s] (default 1e-13; > 0; visible when model in (graphene_kubo)) - Scattering time. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.scattering_time`
- `temperature` [K] (default 300; > 0; visible when model in (graphene_kubo)) - Temperature
  Electron temperature of the Fermi functions (intraband weight, interband edge smeared over ~4 kT).

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.design_region` - Design region

Density design region on the selected domains (window cells only): each cell has a density rho in [0, 1], filtered and projected to rho_bar, and gets eps = eps_min + rho_bar (eps_max - eps_min) (em_fdfd_ez: eps_r; em_fdfd_hz: eps_xx and eps_yy), overwriting the material permittivity. The optimization study varies rho to maximise the adjoint_objective sum J; other studies solve the initial_density design. Regions of one physics must not share cells; keep them off source, port and objective lines and the cells past their hi faces (inexact gradient there). Output field design_density = rho_bar (0 outside). Result 'xy' versus iteration (0 = initial, one point per accepted L-BFGS-B iteration): series objective (J of the model, W/m) and grayness (mean 4 rho_bar (1 - rho_bar), 0 = binary); extras n_cells, eps_min, eps_max, mean_density, final_grayness and note (non-empty outside an optimization study: iteration 0, objective NaN). Here one region writes eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy (every channel at its own frequency); chi2 / chi3 media and poling stay as drawn. Optimization: undepleted (cascade adjoint) or pump_depleted (fixed-point adjoint; iteration_method newton with a chi3 medium).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `eps_min` [1] (default 2.085; >= 1) - Permittivity at density 0
  Void or cladding, e.g. silica 2.085 at 1.55 um.
- `eps_max` [1] (default 12.08; >= 1) - Permittivity at density 1. Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.eps_max`
- `initial_density` [1] (default 0.5; [0, 1]) - Initial density
  rho of every design cell before the first iteration (the fixed design outside an optimization study); 0.5 leaves the optimiser free both ways.
- `filter_radius` [m] (default 1e-07; >= 0) - Filter radius. Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.filter_radius`
- `projection_beta` [1] (default 0; >= 0) - Projection sharpness. Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.projection_beta`
- `projection_eta` [1] (default 0.5; [0, 1]) - Projection threshold
  eta of the projection: filtered densities above it move toward 1; 0.5 neutral, lower dilates.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source` - Point source

em_fdfd_ez / _hz point_source on one harmonic channel (param channel) at its frequency. E_z channels: z-directed filament current phasor I e^{j phase} in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell), radiating a mesh-independent cylindrical wave. H_z channels: Current-calibrated, mesh-independent point excitation phasor (see excitation) in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell). Amplitudes are absolute: the nonlinear response scales as P ~ E^n.

- Category source; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `current` [A] (default 0.001) - Electric line current
  E_z channels only: Peak z-directed filament current I; mesh-independent field |E_z| = omega mu0 I / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| in a homogeneous non-magnetic medium of wavenumber k (1 mA at wavelength 1 um: ~2e5 V/m at r = 1 um). Sign: the current is minus the textbook impressed current, so phases (and powers from probe fields) are pi off textbook formulas; moduli and fluxes agree.
- `phase` [deg] (default 0) - Phase. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`
- `excitation` (default "magnetic_current"; magnetic_current | electric_dipole) - Excitation
  H_z channels only: magnetic_current: z-directed magnetic line current at the cell centre (isotropic). electric_dipole: in-plane current element along orientation on the four E faces of the cell.
- `magnetic_current` [V] (default 1; visible when excitation in (magnetic_current)) - Magnetic line current
  H_z channels only: Peak z-directed magnetic line current K_m (dual of a filament current); mesh-independent field: in a homogeneous medium of eps_r and wavenumber k, |H_z| = omega eps0 eps_r K_m / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| (1 V at 1 um in vacuum: ~1.3e3 A/m at r = 1 um). A fixed K_m radiates power ~ n^2 of its cell, so it drifts when eps there changes; a filament current or dipole radiates n-independent power. Sign: the current is minus the textbook impressed current, so phases (and powers from probe fields) are pi off textbook formulas; moduli and fluxes agree.
- `dipole_moment` [A] (default 0.001; visible when excitation in (electric_dipole)) - Dipole strength
  H_z channels only: Peak in-plane dipole strength M = integral of J over the cross-section (A m of current moment per m of z), along orientation; mesh-independent field: in a homogeneous medium of wavenumber k, |H_z| = k M / 4 |H1^(2)(k r)| |sin(phi - orientation)|, phi counter-clockwise from +x (1 mA at 1 um in vacuum: ~5e2 A/m at r = 1 um broadside). Sign: the current is minus the textbook impressed current, so phases (and powers from probe fields) are pi off textbook formulas; moduli and fluxes agree.
- `orientation` [deg] (default 0; visible when excitation in (electric_dipole)) - Dipole orientation
  H_z channels only: Dipole current direction counter-clockwise from +x: 0 drives only the E_x faces, 90 only E_y. Radiates most broadside, nothing along it.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.line_source` - Line source

em_fdfd_ez / _hz line_source on one harmonic channel (param channel) at its frequency. E_z channels: Sheet current on an axis-aligned line sending amplitude (E_z) to each side in the local medium: a vertical line (x = const) along +x and -x, a horizontal one along +y and -y. H_z channels: Electric sheet current on the hi face of the line cells (+x face of a vertical line, +y face of a horizontal one) sending amplitude (tangential E) to each side in the local medium: a vertical line (x = const) drives E_y along +x and -x, a horizontal one E_x along +y and -y. For a plane wave span the whole domain (an end on a cpml domain edge continues through the PML; on a periodic axis span the whole period); a shorter line diffracts like a slit. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). Amplitudes are absolute: the nonlinear response scales as P ~ E^n.

- Category source; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `amplitude` [V/m] (default 1) - Amplitude
  E_z channels: E_z radiated to each side of the line in the local medium (a plane wave of this amplitude when the line spans a periodic axis); calibrated with the complex eps_r (sigma_e, dispersion) and mu of the line cells at the solved wavelength: H_z channels: Tangential E (E_x for a horizontal line, E_y for a vertical one) radiated to each side of the line in the local medium (a plane wave of this amplitude when the line spans a periodic axis); calibrated with the complex face permittivity (sigma_e, dispersion) and mu of the line cells at the solved wavelength: exact in any homogeneous medium. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so across several media (core / cladding) the current steps at the interfaces and diffracts (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. H_z channels only: Its medium is the face mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, so on an interface sqrt(mean eps) is not the mean index (Si / air: ~14% off). A recalibration (e.g. thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2).
- `phase` [deg] (default 0) - Phase. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.gaussian_beam` - Gaussian beam

em_fdfd_ez / _hz gaussian_beam on one harmonic channel (param channel) at its frequency. Line source with the profile exp(-((s - center) / waist)^2) along the line: E_z channels: a beam of peak E_z = amplitude to each side in the local medium (vertical line: along +x and -x; horizontal: along +y and -y), waist on the line. H_z channels: a beam of peak tangential E = amplitude to each side in the local medium (vertical line: E_y, along +x and -x; horizontal: E_x, along +y and -y), waist on the line, sheet on the hi face of the line cells. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). Amplitudes are absolute: the nonlinear response scales as P ~ E^n.

- Category source; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `amplitude` [V/m] (default 1) - Amplitude
  E_z channels: Peak E_z at the beam centre on the waist line, radiated to each side in the local medium; calibrated with the complex eps_r (sigma_e, dispersion) and mu of the line cells at the solved wavelength: H_z channels: Peak tangential E (E_x for a horizontal line, E_y for a vertical one) at the beam centre on the waist line, radiated to each side in the local medium; calibrated with the complex face permittivity (sigma_e, dispersion) and mu of the line cells at the solved wavelength: exact in any homogeneous medium. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so across several media (core / cladding) the current steps at the interfaces and diffracts (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. H_z channels only: Its medium is the face mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, so on an interface sqrt(mean eps) is not the mean index (Si / air: ~14% off). A recalibration (e.g. thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2).
- `phase` [deg] (default 0) - Phase. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`
- `waist` [m] (default 1e-06; > 0) - Waist radius. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.gaussian_beam.waist`
- `center` [m] (nullable) - Beam centre
  Beam axis along the line (x for a horizontal line, y for a vertical one); empty = midpoint. Off the line only the tail launches (validation warns).

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.plane_wave_tfsf` - Plane wave box (+x)

em_fdfd_ez / _hz plane_wave_tfsf on one harmonic channel (param channel) at its frequency. Plane wave along +x on the outline of a total-field box (total field in the box cells, scattered field outside), entering only the right-hand side; phase referred to the centres of the first (lo-x) box column; the incident wave is the discrete plane wave of the FDFD stencil in the background medium (complex eps and mu_r of the outline cell just before the lo-x edge; uniform x cells: (2 / dx) sin(k dx / 2) = n k0; graded x cells: marched on the solved stencil, a grading at the lo-x edge adds a small backward part), so a box in a uniform medium is exactly transparent. The box edges must lie in one uniform medium (else a warning: incident light leaks out), one scattered-field cell inside the domain on every side, except: along a periodic y axis it may cover every y cell (a grating or layer stack may cross it), and at a y mirror face of the wave's parity (ez: symmetric, hz: antisymmetric) it may reach the plane (the other parity, or an x mirror face, is an error). With bloch_ky != 0 the wave is oblique, exp(-j (k_x x + ky y)), phase referred to y = 0, (2 / dx)^2 sin^2(k_x dx / 2) = (n k0)^2 - (2 / dy)^2 sin^2(ky dy / 2) (refused when not positive); it needs uniform y cells. Enclose the scatterers, put a far_field box outside it; flux and mode monitors must not straddle its outline. The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis (an edge exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). Amplitudes are absolute: the nonlinear response scales as P ~ E^n.

- Category source; selection domain entities, object kinds rectangle, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `amplitude` [V/m] (default 1) - Amplitude
  E_z channels: Peak incident E_z (wave of the uniform medium on the box outline). H_z channels: Peak incident in-plane |E| (E_y at normal incidence) of the wave of the uniform medium on the box outline: H_z = n |E| / (eta0 mu_r), n = sqrt(eps_yy mu_r), also for an oblique Bloch ky wave.
- `phase` [deg] (default 0) - Phase. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.mode_source` - Mode source

em_fdfd_ez / _hz mode_source on one harmonic channel (param channel) at its frequency. Port source launching one guided mode of the cross-section under an axis-aligned line in one direction. One-sided total-field / scattered-field line: total field from the line cells downstream, only the scattered field (what comes back) upstream; the interface is the lo face of the line cells for positive, their hi face for negative. The launch is exact and one-sided at every solved wavelength of a straight guide. Mode monitors normalise by it when it is the only enabled mode source of the physics. The 1D line eigenmodes use the FDFD discretisation (Yee widths, PML stretch, complex eps and mu of the line cells with poles, sigma_e, sigma_m), re-solved at every solved wavelength and after any material change (thermo-optic coupling, state-dependent permittivity). Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side, on a locally uniform mesh (validation warns when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line and when its face lies inside a CPML layer, i.e. the line is in the outermost window cell). Span ends: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML (open); E_z channels: an end on a pec domain edge takes E_z = 0, one on a pmc or symmetric edge dE_z/dn = 0 and one on an antisymmetric edge E_z odd about the plane; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E_z = 0 in the next cell), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns above 1% of the mode peak at a metal end); H_z channels: an end on a pec or antisymmetric domain edge takes tangential E = 0 on the inner face of the outermost cell (dH_z/dn = 0), one on a pmc edge H_z = 0 and one on a symmetric edge H_z odd; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E along the propagation direction = 0 on the face beyond the end, so dH_z/dn = 0), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns above 1% of the mode peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. H_z channels only: The in-plane E faces use the permittivity of the operator (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells), so a guide edge on a face line takes the core / cladding mean. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). Result 'table' of the latest port solve (frequency_domain: its last wavelength), one row per mode for the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes: mode_number, n_eff, n_eff_imag (< 0 = loss, exp(+j omega t)), loss_db_per_cm, n_group, edge_field (largest |field| at the line ends / peak; above 1e-2 at a metal end the line cuts the mode), selected (the launched mode); extras wavelength (m), power (W/m), direction, mode_number and phase (deg). Amplitudes are absolute: the nonlinear response scales as P ~ E^n.

- Category source; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `table`

Params:
- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Mode number. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.mode_number`
- `direction` (default "positive"; positive | negative) - Direction. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.direction`
- `power` [W/m] (default 1; > 0) - Mode power. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.power`
- `phase` [deg] (default 0) - Phase. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.field_probe` - Field probe

em_fdfd_ez / _hz field_probe on one harmonic channel (param channel) at its frequency. Phasor of one field component in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell) per solved wavelength. Face components (hx / hy, ex / ey) come from neighbouring cells: keep them off a plane_wave_tfsf outline and a mode_source interface face (validation warns). Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength (m, ascending; one point per solved wavelength, a re-solved one keeps its latest): series abs = |phasor| (unit of the component) and phase (rad; field = abs cos(omega t + phase)); y_label the component label; extras frequency (Hz), wavelength (m), component and unit.

- Category probe; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `component` (ez | hx | hy | hz | ex | ey; nullable) - Field component
  Empty (default) = the channel's out-of-plane field (ez or hz). E_z channels: ez (V/m) at the centre of the cell containing the point; hx / hy (A/m) on its +y / +x face (the FDTD probe positions), from the discrete curl of E_z. H_z channels: hz (A/m) at the centre of the cell containing the point; ex / ey (V/m) from Ampere's law (curl of H_z plus any line source / beam / dipole current on the face), averaged over the two faces of the cell carrying it (collocated, unlike the raw face samples of the FDTD probe).

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

em_fdfd_ez / _hz flux_monitor on one harmonic channel (param channel) at its frequency. Time-averaged Poynting flux through an axis-aligned line per solved wavelength: E_z channels: S_x = -1/2 Re(E_z H_y*) (vertical line), S_y = 1/2 Re(E_z H_x*) (horizontal), E_z of the line cells, H from the curl of E_z on their hi face; H_z channels: S_x = 1/2 Re(E_y H_z*) (vertical line), S_y = -1/2 Re(E_x H_z*) (horizontal), H_z of the line cells, E on their hi face from Ampere's law (curl of H_z plus a source current on that face); > 0 toward +x / +y. H_z channels only: Keep it off the line cells of a line source or gaussian beam: their sheet sits on that face, where the flux jumps, and the monitor reads the line-cell side (minus the power sent toward -x / -y). Keep its measuring face (hi face of the line cells) off a mode_source interface face (the line one cell upstream of a positive source, or the line of a negative one) and entirely inside or outside a plane_wave_tfsf box: the field jumps there between total and scattered field (validation warns). Result 'flux_spectrum' in W/m (power per unit z length over the line cells, absolute: a line source of amplitude A spanning a period L in vacuum sends A^2 L / (2 eta0) to each side), one entry per solved wavelength, sorted. The discrete flux is conserved exactly through lossless cells; transmission = device power / power of a reference run with the same source. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

- Category monitor; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params:
- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`

H_z channels: H_z in the line cells and E_y (vertical line) / E_x (horizontal) from Ampere's law on their hi face are projected on the mode solved there, so each direction is measured separately, unlike a flux_monitor. The 1D line eigenmodes use the FDFD discretisation (Yee widths, PML stretch, complex eps and mu of the line cells with poles, sigma_e, sigma_m), re-solved at every solved wavelength and after any material change (thermo-optic coupling, state-dependent permittivity). H_z channels only: The in-plane E faces use the permittivity of the operator (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells), so a guide edge on a face line takes the core / cladding mean. Keep its measuring face (hi face of the line cells) off a mode_source interface face (the line one cell upstream of a positive source, or the line of a negative one) and entirely inside or outside a plane_wave_tfsf box: the field jumps there between total and scattered field (validation warns). The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).
