### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.far_field` - Far-field pattern

em_fdfd_ez / _hz far_field on one harmonic channel (param channel) at its frequency. Near-to-far-field transform of the phasors on a rectangle outline (the out-of-plane field and the in-plane one, from the curl of E_z / Ampere's law of H_z, averaged onto the centres at the em_fdtd_* far_field sample points, so normalised patterns compare directly): power per unit length and angle rho |E|^2 / (2 eta0) in W/(m rad) of the far-field |E| (H_z: |eta0 H_z|; angle integral = power through a closed flux box) versus angle counter-clockwise from +x, one row per solved wavelength (ascending). Assumes vacuum outside the box: enclose every scatterer; with a plane_wave_tfsf keep the box outside it, in the scattered field: x0 / y0 edges at least two cells before those of the TFSF box, x1 / y1 edges in or beyond the first cell past it (samples average the faces on both sides of their cell; validation warns otherwise, and for an edge sampling across a mode_source interface face). The contour runs through the centres of the first box cells and of the cells one beyond x1 / y1 (keep the box one cell off the x_hi / y_hi edges); graded meshes work (actual centres, trapezoid weights). The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis (an edge exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

- Category monitor; selection domain entities, object kinds rectangle, exactly 1; result kind `far_field`

Params:
- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `n_angles` (int; default 360; >= 1) - Number of angles
  Far-field angles evenly spaced over 360 degrees counter-clockwise from +x.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.adjoint_objective` - Optimization objective

em_fdfd_ez / _hz adjoint_objective on one harmonic channel (param channel) at its frequency. Objective term for the adjoint sensitivity: a flux_monitor or mode_monitor quantity on an axis-aligned line times weight. Output field eps_sensitivity = dJ/d eps_r per unit area [W/m^3] from one extra transposed solve on the forward factorisation, computed when read (snapshot, derived value): d eps over a region R changes J by the integral of eps_sensitivity d eps over R. em_fdfd_hz: the sum of the eps_xx and eps_yy terms (eps_xy fixed), plus eps_xy_sensitivity = dJ/d eps_xy per unit area (0 where the solve drops eps_xy: PEC cells, the outer two rows of a wall or mirror face). Line source calibrations and port / monitor modes are held fixed, so the gradient is exact only off every line source, port and mode monitor line and the cells past their hi faces; sigma_e, poles and mu_r are not differentiated. An optimization study maximises J, summed over every physics, over the design_region densities. Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength: series value (the quantity, W/m) and weighted (weight * value); extras frequency, wavelength, quantity, weight. Keep the line off a TFSF outline and a mode_source interface face. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). Here eps_sensitivity is dJ/d eps of J summed over every channel's objectives through the coupled channels (undepleted: one transposed solve per channel in reverse order; pump_depleted: the transposed fixed point (I - T) nu = T(c) by real GMRES to the physics tolerance, then one gradient sweep, as accurate as that tolerance); nonlinear sources, back-action, SPM / XPM, sheet sites and free carriers (newton) back-propagated exactly; an isotropic change adds the eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy terms. Not differentiated: pump_depleted picard with a chi3 medium (use newton) and an em_fdfd_hz eps_xy (error with a weighted objective; validation error in an optimization study). Held fixed: chi2 / chi3 / sheet tensors, poling, sheet sites, chi3 n0^2 / Miller factors (free carriers: where generation > 0).

- Category monitor; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel. Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `quantity` (default "flux"; flux | mode_power_positive | mode_power_negative) - Quantity. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective.quantity`
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; >= 1; visible when quantity in (mode_power_positive, mode_power_negative)) - Mode number. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective.mode_number`
- `weight` [1] (default 1) - Weight
  Factor in J = sum of weight * quantity over the enabled objectives of the physics: 1 maximises the quantity, -1 minimises it, 0 only records it.

## Physics type `em_fdfd_sphere` - Electromagnetic Waves, frequency domain (spherically symmetric, multipole orders)

Spherically symmetric finite-difference frequency-domain solver: on a spherical domain (DomainSpec coordinates spherical, radius_min 0 for a full sphere or > 0 for a shell region): a 2D (r, theta) window over the whole theta = 0 .. pi (size_y pi, angle_min 0; the drawing is the meridional half disc) or a 1D radial line (size_y null), the structure eps(r), mu(r) is a stack of concentric shells, and Maxwell's equations separate into multipole terms (vector spherical harmonics of order l and family er / hr), each a 1D radial equation for y = r H_t (er) or r E_t (hr) solved on the radial cell edges (second order, complex symmetric tridiagonal operator, host SuperLU or the opt-in cuDSS / MUMPS / PARDISO back ends of the 'linear' role). Fields vary as exp(+j omega t). Every multipole term (order l >= 1, family er or hr, all its 2 l + 1 degenerate m) is one radial solve; the shown fields are sphere-RMS radial profiles: |E_r|, |E_t| (tangential), |H_r|, |H_t| = the square root of the mean over the sphere of radius r of the component squared, summed over every solved term and source class (different terms are orthogonal on the sphere, so this is the exact sphere mean of the total field); e_intensity = |E_r|^2 + |E_t|^2 and absorbed_power are sphere means, so their integral over the whole shells (the spherical metric volumes, 4 pi r^2 dr per radial cell) is the 3D integral (field energy, absorbed power in W). On an (r, theta) window the profiles are drawn along every theta (the fields of a spherically symmetric structure averaged over the sphere do not depend on the angle), so the angle cells only serve the picture: a few tens are plenty (mesh mode nonuniform with a mesh axis 'y' of segments, e.g. 90 cells). The outer end 'radiation' is the exact outgoing spherical wave of each term (no PML). True 3D results of layered spheres at the cost of one radial line: Mie scattering (plane_wave: extinction, scattering and absorption cross sections of coated / graded / plasmonic spheres), emitters near or inside spheres (dipole_source: emitted power and Purcell factor), resonances (eigenfrequency: complex omega and Q of whispering-gallery modes, Mie and cavity resonances per order and family; shift-invert of the 'eigen' role about the target with the radiation term frozen there, then each resonance refined with the exact radiation condition at its own complex frequency by Rayleigh-functional iteration, so Q carries no PML or target error; materials stay at the target, as in the other EM eigen-solves). Studies: stationary (one driven solve at the wavelength setting; with heat through heat_em_thermo_optic / em_heat_joule: the heat physics should share the spherical domain, it gets the sphere-mean absorbed power), frequency_domain (one driven solve per wavelength), eigenfrequency. Features: plane_wave, dipole_source, field_probe, pec_domain, resonance_table. Materials: isotropic eps_r, sigma_e, mu_r, sigma_m and dispersion poles (no anisotropy), constant on every shell (a material varying along theta is a run error: draw circles about the origin). Cannot share a model with other EM types. heat_em_thermo_optic writes eps_r (slot eps_r_update). The instance is usually named 'em'.

- Default instance name `em`; studies frequency_domain, stationary, eigenfrequency (default {"type": "frequency_domain"})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor; refinement indicator fields e_intensity; dispersion poles used
- Features: plane_wave, dipole_source, field_probe, pec_domain, resonance_table

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (default "axisymmetric"; choice axisymmetric only) - Geometry
  Always axisymmetric: on a spherical domain (coordinates spherical: the (r, theta) half disc over the whole 0 .. pi, or a 1D radial line) the drawing rotates about its vertical axis and every radial cell is a whole spherical shell. The setting exists so that the spherical-domain rule and coupled physics with a geometry setting (heat, electric_currents, electrostatics) see a consistent spherical partner.
- `bc_x_lo` (default "centre"; centre | pec | pmc) - Inner end
  Inner end of the radial line: 'centre' when radius_min = 0 (the sphere centre, fields regular: y = r x field = 0; required there and only there), else 'pec' (tangential E = 0 on the sphere r = radius_min) or 'pmc' (tangential H = 0).
- `bc_x_hi` (default "radiation"; radiation | pec | pmc) - Outer end
  Outer end r = R of the radial line: 'radiation' (default) continues the last cell's medium to infinity with the exact outgoing spherical wave of each multipole term (Riccati-Hankel xi_l(k r), a Dirichlet-to-Neumann condition: no PML, no reflection at any l, so the domain may end just outside the structure; the last cell must not be pec_domain; a plane wave needs it and a lossless last cell); 'pec' / 'pmc' close a spherical metal / magnetic cavity at R.
- `wavelength` [m] (default 1.55e-06; > 0) - Wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength lambda0 of the solve in a stationary study (omega = 2 pi C0 / lambda0); an eigenfrequency study searches the resonances nearest it (the target; materials are evaluated there); a frequency_domain study solves its own wavelengths. The radial mesh needs >= 10 (better 20) cells per lambda0 / |n| in every material and >= 2 per skin depth (validation warns).
- `multipole_order` (int; default 1; [1, 100000]) - Multipole order
  Multipole (angular) order l >= 1 of the fields (each l carries 2 l + 1 degenerate m, all solved at once): l = 1 dipole, 2 quadrupole, ...; whispering-gallery modes of a sphere of radius a have l ~ 2 pi a n / lambda. For a plane wave (Mie series) or a dipole source list every order 1..L in multipole_orders instead (L above k a + 4 (k a)^(1/3) + 2 for a sphere of radius a, k the exterior wave number; a dipole at a distance d from a surface needs l up to a few a / d).
- `multipole_orders` [1] (float_list; [1, 100000]; nullable) - Multipole order list
  Distinct integer orders l >= 1 solved in one run; a non-empty list replaces multipole_order. Driven studies sum the terms of every listed order (plane-wave cross sections, dipole powers and the shown sphere-RMS fields: list 1..L); an eigenfrequency study searches n_resonances resonances per order and family, order by order (er before hr), resonance labels 'resonance k: l = <l> <family>, lambda = ...' and resonance_table columns multipole_order, family (a curve of lambda versus multipole_order gives the free spectral range of whispering-gallery modes). null or [] = multipole_order alone.
- `multipole_family` (default "both"; both | er | hr) - Multipole family
  Multipole families solved: 'er' = electric multipoles (radial E, no radial H; Mie a_l; the radial function y = r H_t solves -(y' / eps)' + l (l + 1) y / (eps r^2) = k0^2 mu y), 'hr' = magnetic multipoles (radial H, no radial E; Mie b_l; y = r E_t solves -(y' / mu)' + l (l + 1) y / (mu r^2) = k0^2 eps y), 'both' (default) = every term of both families (a plane wave and tangential dipoles excite both; a radial dipole only er). One radial solve per family and listed order.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic relative permittivity of the shell (>= 1; n^2 of a lossless dielectric); may depend on r (x) and physics fields. Cell values; the tangential fields see the dual-cell mean, the radial ones the mean of 1 / eps (normal D_r continuous). The solve uses this value - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) plus every Drude / Lorentz pole chi(omega) (exp(+j omega t): loss has Im < 0). The last radial cell is the exterior medium of a 'radiation' end.
- `sigma_e` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss in S/m, default 0: eps gains -j sigma_e / (omega eps0). Model metals with a Drude pole (a plasmonic nanosphere) or pec_domain.
- `mu_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability (>= 1), 1 for optical materials; the solve uses mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0).
- `sigma_m` [Ohm/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss in Ohm/m, default 0 (artificial absorbers only).

### Fields

Output fields (primary e_intensity; [state] = also a state field):
- `er` - |E_r| (rms over the sphere) (V/m)
- `et` - |E_t| tangential (rms over the sphere) (V/m)
- `hr` - |H_r| (rms over the sphere) (A/m)
- `ht` - |H_t| tangential (rms over the sphere) (A/m)
- `e_abs` - |E| (rms over the sphere) (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (mean over the sphere) (V^2/m^2) [state]
- `h_abs` - |H| (rms over the sphere) (A/m)
- `absorbed_power` - Absorbed power density (mean over the sphere) (W/m^3)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity (1) [state]
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m) [state]
State fields that are no output field:
- `q_abs` - Absorbed power density (mean over the sphere) (W/m^3)

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdfd_sphere.plane_wave` - Plane wave

Incident plane wave of amplitude E0 (x-polarised, along +z) in the exterior medium (the last radial cell, continued to infinity; needs bc_x_hi 'radiation' and a lossless last cell): per listed order and family its regular multipole wave (both m = +-1) enters through the outgoing condition, and the outgoing coefficient gives the Mie coefficient (a_l: er, b_l: hr; the complex conjugate of Bohren and Huffman's, since fields go as exp(+j omega t)). Result 'xy' versus wavelength: sigma_ext, sigma_sca, sigma_abs [m^2] = sums over the solved terms of 2 pi / k^2 (2 l + 1) Re(a) and |a|^2 (k the exterior wave number), sigma_abs their difference; extras frequency, wavelength, multipole_orders, a_real / a_imag and b_real / b_imag (n_wavelengths x n_orders, NaN for a family not solved). List every order 1..L (see multipole_order). At most one per physics, not together with a dipole_source (validation error).

- Category source; selection none (a selection is ignored with a warning); result kind `xy`

Params:
- `amplitude` [V/m] (default 1; > 0) - Amplitude
  Electric field amplitude E0 [V/m] of the incident plane wave (x-polarised, travelling along +z in the exterior medium); fields scale linearly with it, the cross sections do not depend on it.

### Feature `em_fdfd_sphere.dipole_source` - Dipole source

Point current element at the radius of the point object (x = r, y = 0; on the polar axis in 3D), radial or tangential (see orientation); every listed order and family it couples to is solved and summed (dipoles of one orientation interfere coherently; radial and tangential ones excite orthogonal m and are solved apart). Result 'xy' versus wavelength: power [W] = -1/2 Re(E . (I d)*) at the element (radiated plus absorbed; keep its cell lossless), power_homogeneous [W] = eta k^2 (I d)^2 / (12 pi) in the medium of its cell, purcell = their ratio (the decay-rate enhancement of an emitter there); extras frequency, wavelength, radius, orientation, multipole_orders, power_orders (n_wavelengths x n_orders). Not together with a plane_wave.

- Category source; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `orientation` (default "radial"; radial | tangential) - Orientation
  'radial' excites the electric multipoles (er) only, every l with m = 0; 'tangential' both families with m = +-1 (the dipole is on the polar axis, parallel to the plane-wave polarisation).
- `current_moment` [A m] (default 1e-12; > 0) - Current moment
  Current moment I d [A m] of the point current element (= j omega times its dipole moment p); in an unbounded medium it radiates eta k^2 (I d)^2 / (12 pi) (eta = eta0 sqrt(mu / eps), k = n k0); powers scale with its square.
- `phase` [deg] (default 0) - Phase
  Phasor phase of the current moment in degrees; it matters only between several dipoles of one orientation (they interfere).

### Feature `em_fdfd_sphere.field_probe` - Field probe

Sphere-RMS amplitude of one field component in the radial cell containing the point at every driven solve. Result 'xy' versus wavelength: series abs (unit of the component) and phase (rad; NaN unless one term and source class was solved); extras frequency, wavelength, component, unit.

- Category probe; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `component` (default "et"; er | et | hr | ht) - Field component
  Component recorded: its sphere-RMS amplitude in the radial cell containing the point (a point object at x = r, y = 0), per driven solve; the phase only when the solve had exactly one term and source class (one order, one family), else NaN.

### Feature `em_fdfd_sphere.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor shells: every radial cell whose centre lies in the selected domains (circles about the origin select shells) holds tangential E = 0 on its outline (er: its cells leave the operator, hr: y = 0 on its nodes); not on the last cell of a 'radiation' end.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params: none

### Feature `em_fdfd_sphere.resonance_table` - Resonance table

Resonances of the last eigenfrequency study solve, term by term (orders in list order, er before hr), nearest the target (the wavelength setting) first within each term. Result 'table', one row per resonance: resonance_number, wavelength = 2 pi C0 / Re(omega) in m, frequency / frequency_imag = Re / Im(omega) / (2 pi) in Hz (> 0 decays), q_factor = Re(omega) / (2 Im(omega)) (radiation through the exact outgoing condition and material loss; inf when lossless and closed), pml_fraction (always 0: no PML), multipole_order, family; extras target_wavelength (m), selected_resonance, multipole_orders and families.

- Category monitor; selection none (a selection is ignored with a warning); result kind `table`

Params: none

## Physics type `em_fdtd_3d` - Electromagnetic Waves, time domain (3D)

3D finite-difference time-domain (Yee): E_x, E_y, E_z on the +x / +y / +z cell faces, H_x, H_y, H_z on the (+y +z) / (+x +z) / (+x +y) edges, H half a step earlier. Materials eps_r or diagonal eps_xx / eps_yy / eps_zz, sigma_e, mu_r, sigma_m, Drude / Lorentz poles (on their material bounding box), stored as a uint16 material index (see eps_r). Periodic faces take an optional Bloch k (a second, imaginary field set). Outputs the raw components, e_abs, e_intensity, h_abs (cell centres), eps_r (the eps_zz array) and absorbed_power, shown as z cut planes. Couplings: heat_em_thermo_optic (index slots of the allocated permittivity arrays), em_heat_joule into 3D heat. Memory ~26 B per cell plus 12 B of material arrays (+8 B with eps_xx / eps_yy, +4 B with sigma_m, +8 B tracking absorption). A stepper solver with precision half_storage stores fp16 fields (14 B per cell; gpu and time_dependent only; no poles, plane wave, mode ports or resonance finder; ~1e-3 relative noise floor). One 3D Courant step per runner tick (every must be 1). cpu backend: numpy twins of every kernel (numba for the Yee updates, CPML and ohmic loss when installed), far slower: small models and tests. A frequency_domain study runs one pulse for the phasors at every study wavelength: all enabled sources share one gaussian or ricker waveform (study wavelengths outside its band warn), no coupling reads this physics.

- Default instance name `em`; studies time_dependent, frequency_domain (default {"type": "time_dependent", "settings": {"duration": 5e-14}})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor; refinement indicator fields ez; dispersion poles used
- Features: dipole_source, field_probe, resonance_monitor, flux_plane, flux_box, dft_plane, pec_domain, plane_wave_source, mode_source, mode_monitor, far_field

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi`, `bc_z_lo`, `bc_z_hi` (default "cpml"; cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge / Lower z face / Upper z face
  cpml absorbs outgoing waves in pml_cells extra cells outside the domain (z faces too); pec = tangential E 0 at the centres of the outermost cell layer (it becomes conductor); pmc = tangential H 0 on the outer face of the outermost cell (pec and pmc walls lie half a cell apart: a cavity differs by one cell in width); periodic on both faces of an axis, Bloch phase bloch_k<axis>. Mirror planes on the domain edge itself (any face): symmetric = E mirror-even (PMC plane: tangential H and normal E 0), antisymmetric = E mirror-odd (PEC plane); a ghost cell outside (edge-cell material; on a graded z axis its width follows the PML grading: keep z cells uniform near a z mirror) holds the image, so draw the structure about the edge; the other physics of the model have their faces on the same plane. Each mirror halves memory and time. Results count the unfolded structure: flux planes / boxes reaching a mirror face are doubled per such face (extra mirror_factor), mode ports solve the whole mirrored mode (full-structure powers), the far field adds the box-current images (at most one mirror per axis); a dipole half a cell from the plane is mirrored with it.
- `pml_cells` [cells] (int; default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` [1] (default 1; > 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` [1] (default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real CPML stretch (1 = none); larger damps evanescent and grazing waves; 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `bloch_kx` [rad/m] (default 0; visible when bc_x_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector x. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.bloch_kx`
- `bloch_ky` [rad/m] (default 0; visible when bc_y_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector y. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.bloch_kx`
- `bloch_kz` [rad/m] (default 0; visible when bc_z_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector z. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.bloch_kx`
- `courant_factor` [1] (default 0.99; (0, 1]) - Time step factor
  Fraction of the 3D CFL limit: dt = factor / (C0 sqrt(1/dx^2 + 1/dy^2 + 1/dz^2)) of the finest cells. Dispersive poles need eps_r mu_r >= factor^2 + mu_r (omega_p dt)^2 / 4 per Drude pole (about delta_eps (omega_0 dt)^2 / 4 per Lorentz pole); the build checks every material and names the largest stable factor.
- `track_absorption` (bool; default false) - Track absorption
  Accumulate J.E losses also without an em_heat_joule coupling: output absorbed_power [W/m^3], state q_accum [J/m^3] (face sigma_e split between the two cells by half-cell conductance, pole work time-centred and split to the dispersive cells). Costs a pass over the conducting-cell and pole boxes per step plus 8 B per cell.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1; writes eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity. Help: shared `em_fdfd_3d.eps_r`
- `eps_zz` [1] (default 1; >= 1; writes eps_r) - Relative permittivity, z. Help: shared `em_fdfd_3d.eps_zz`
- `eps_xx` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, x. Help: shared `em_fdfd_3d.eps_xx`
- `eps_yy` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, y. Help: shared `em_fdfd_3d.eps_yy`
- `sigma_e` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss J = sigma_e E (isotropic, face mean like eps_r); model metals with a Drude pole. Counted in absorbed_power / em_heat_joule.
- `mu_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability; each H edge takes its lower cell (i, j, k).
- `sigma_m` [Ohm/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Magnetic conductivity. Help: shared `em_fdfd_3d.sigma_m`

### Fields

Output fields (primary ez; [state] = also a state field):
- `ex` - E_x (+x face) (V/m) [state]
- `ey` - E_y (+y face) (V/m) [state]
- `ez` - E_z (+z face) (V/m) [state]
- `hx` - H_x (+y +z edge) (A/m) [state]
- `hy` - H_y (+x +z edge) (A/m) [state]
- `hz` - H_z (+x +y edge) (A/m) [state]
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity (eps_zz) (1) [state]
- `absorbed_power` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)
- `e_abs_harmonic` - |E| (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `e_intensity_harmonic` - |E|^2 (phasor) (V^2/m^2) [frequency_domain study only]
- `absorbed_power_harmonic` - Absorbed power density (time average) (W/m^3) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ex_re` - Re E_x (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ex_im` - Im E_x (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ex_abs` - |E_x| (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ex_phase` - arg E_x (phasor, centre) (rad) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ey_re` - Re E_y (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ey_im` - Im E_y (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ey_abs` - |E_y| (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ey_phase` - arg E_y (phasor, centre) (rad) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_re` - Re E_z (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_im` - Im E_z (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_abs` - |E_z| (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_phase` - arg E_z (phasor, centre) (rad) [frequency_domain study only]
State fields that are no output field:
- `q_accum` - Absorbed energy density (J/m^3)

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source` - Dipole source

Electric point dipole (current element) on the E face nearest the point (point z param = height, mid-height when unset); calibrated to the live face coefficient, so the moment holds in any medium. Refused in the outermost cell layer of a pec face parallel to it (tangential E pinned there); normal to a pec face it may sit next to it (e.g. a monopole on a ground plane).

- Category source; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `dipole_axis` (default "z"; x | y | z) - Dipole direction
  Drives the one E face of this direction nearest the point (containing cell on the other two axes); radiates most broadside, nothing along its axis.
- `waveform` (default "gaussian"; gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` [m] (default 5.5e-07; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `current_moment` [A m] (default 1e-12) - Current moment
  Peak current moment I l, injected as J = I l / V on the volume V of its E face (dual length along the dipole x the two cell widths across), so the radiated field is mesh-independent: a cw dipole in vacuum radiates eta0 k^2 (I l)^2 / (12 pi) W (1e-12 A m at 1 um: ~4e-10 W). Sign: the current is minus the textbook impressed current, so phases (and powers from probe fields) are pi off textbook formulas; moduli and fluxes agree.

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.field_probe` - Field probe

Time series of one raw field component in the cell containing the point (t in s, V/m or A/m), sampled after every step.

- Category probe; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result kind `timeseries`

Params:
- `component` (default "ez"; ex | ey | ez | hx | hy | hz) - Field component
  Raw Yee sample of the containing cell (E on its + faces, H on its + edges, as the field list); H samples are dt/2 older than the recorded time.

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.resonance_monitor` - Resonance finder

Resonance finder (harmonic inversion, as Harminv / matrix pencil): records one component in the cell containing each selected point (1 to 16; a coordinate on a cell edge goes to the upper cell) every step. Reading the result (CPU, ~1 s per point) fits the traces from t_s on jointly (shared poles, amplitudes per point) by damped sinusoids a exp(-gamma (t - t_s)) cos(omega (t - t_s) + phi), so a mode on a nodal line of one point is found through the others. Result 'table', one row per resonance in the band, strongest first: resonance_number, wavelength [m, vacuum C0 / frequency], frequency = omega / (2 pi) [Hz], frequency_imag = gamma / (2 pi) [Hz] (> 0 decays), q_factor = omega / (2 gamma), amplitude a [component unit] and phase phi [rad] at t_s where largest, error = |pole change between two pencil sizes| / omega. Dropped: error > 0.01, amplitude < 0.0001 of the strongest at every point, growth > 2x over the window. Extras: component, unit, dt [s], start_time, end_time [s], sample_interval [steps], n_samples (<= 2000), model_order, wavelength_min, wavelength_max, note ('' or why none was found), points, point_amplitudes / point_phases (per row, one per point). Q far above pi f T_window resolves while the ring-down stays above float32 noise (~1e-7). A mode with a node at every point is missed; a cw source adds an undamped line. 3D: the raw Yee sample of the field_probe (point z param = height, mid-height when unset); the reference time accounts for the dt/2 older H samples.

- Category monitor; selection point entities, object kinds point, 1 to 16; stepper precisions single, double only (see solvers); result kind `table`

Params:
- `component` (default "ez"; ex | ey | ez | hx | hy | hz) - Field component
  Raw Yee sample of the containing cell (E on its + faces, H on its + edges, as the field list); H samples are dt/2 older than the recorded time.
- `wavelength_min` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength. Keep the band inside the source spectrum; narrower = faster, better conditioned fit.
- `wavelength_max` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_min.
- `start_time` [s] (>= 0; nullable) - Analysis start. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.resonance_monitor.start_time`

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane` - Flux plane

Spectral power through a plane spanning the whole physical window. Result 'flux_spectrum': power a.u. (dt-weighted spectra, Re(E x H*) without the 1/2, E averaged across the plane and over two steps as the 2D flux monitor), power_per_cw [W] = power / (2 |S|^2) when every source shares one waveform (cw time-averaged power at unit source amplitude). half_storage stepper: fp16 field noise (~1e-3 of the peak field, ~-60 dB in power), so integrated powers keep ~1e-3 and deep spectral nulls are not resolved.

- Category monitor; selection none (a selection is ignored with a warning); result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params:
- `normal` (default "z"; x | y | z) - Plane normal
  Power > 0 flows toward +normal.
- `position` [m] (default 0) - Plane position
  Coordinate along the normal; snaps to the nearest cell edge of the physical window, which needs a cell on both sides (an edge on a non-PML outer face is refused).
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 100; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths
  Evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency); 1 = the range centre. 50-200 for a smooth spectrum; the work per time step grows with it.

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.flux_box` - Flux box

Net outward spectral power through the six faces of a box object, each snapped to the nearest cell edge (trapezoid weights along face edges, corners shared); every face needs a cell on both sides. Result 'flux_spectrum': power a.u. (dt-weighted spectra, Re(E x H*) without the 1/2, E averaged across the plane and over two steps as the 2D flux monitor), power_per_cw [W] = power / (2 |S|^2) when every source shares one waveform (cw time-averaged power at unit source amplitude). half_storage stepper: fp16 field noise (~1e-3 of the peak field, ~-60 dB in power), so integrated powers keep ~1e-3 and deep spectral nulls are not resolved. Enclose a source to get its radiated power.

- Category monitor; selection domain entities, object kinds box, exactly 1; result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params:
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 100; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths
  Evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency); 1 = the range centre. 50-200 for a smooth spectrum; the work per time step grows with it.

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.dft_plane` - Field map layer

Running DFT of E_x, E_y, E_z averaged to the cell centres of one window layer. Result 'dft_fields': x / y centres and the extra 'z' [m]; quantity 'abs(E_x)^2 + abs(E_y)^2 + abs(E_z)^2'; intensity (a.u.) with freq_index; intensity_per_cw_factor as the 2D DFT monitor.

- Category monitor; selection none (a selection is ignored with a warning); result kind `dft_fields`

Params:
- `position` [m] (default 0) - Layer height
  Height z of the recorded layer (always normal to z): the containing cell, an edge goes to the upper cell.
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 5; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths
  Evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency); 1 = the range centre. Each wavelength stores three complex64 window layers (24 B per window xy cell).

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor cells: every E face between two selected cells is pinned to 0 (the surface lies at the centres of the outermost conductor cells; normal E on it free). Select objects: 'all' is refused. solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (Dey-Mittra): every H face between four cell centres cut by the drawn surface takes the free lengths of its four E edges over its free area, floored so the time step stays stable; faces touching a pec wall layer, the window edge or a pec_domain without the option stay staircased; sources, ports, poles and the stability check keep the cell mask.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params: none

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.plane_wave_source` - Plane wave

Total-field / scattered-field plane wave along one axis on a box object: total field inside (incident + scattered), scattered only outside, fed by a 1D incident line in the background medium (read from the cell before the upstream face) on the grid's own cell widths, so graded meshes leak nothing. Every box face needs one scattered-field cell inside the domain, except: on a periodic axis the box spans the whole period (its extent ignored); with both transverse axes periodic a downstream face on the domain edge opens the box into the CPML (one-sided source: everything downstream is total field); a transverse face may reach a mirror face about which the incident wave is even (symmetric when the plane is normal to the third axis, antisymmetric when normal to the polarization; the other parity is an error): the box opens there and its image completes it. Keep the box faces in one uniform lossless medium (the build warns otherwise).

- Category source; selection domain entities, object kinds box, exactly 1; stepper precisions single only (see solvers); result none

Params:
- `direction` (default "+z"; +x | -x | +y | -y | +z | -z) - Direction
  Along one axis (normal incidence on the box faces); not along a periodic axis.
- `polarization` (default "x"; x | y | z) - Electric field direction
  Axis of the incident E (linear), perpendicular to the propagation axis; H = k x E / eta along the third axis.
- `waveform` (default "gaussian"; gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` [m] (default 5.5e-07; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `amplitude` [V/m] (default 1) - Amplitude
  Peak incident E of the envelope in the background medium (exact at the centre wavelength, where the 1D incident line is calibrated); cw intensity amplitude^2 / (2 eta), eta = eta0 sqrt(mu_r / eps_r) of the background.

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.mode_source` - Mode source

Guided cross-section mode (full-vector solve with scipy at build, on the whole grid layer containing position, PML included, at the FDTD numerical frequency) injected as a one-sided total-field / scattered-field plane: total field from that layer downstream. Solved once before the first step; later material changes keep it. pec / pmc domain faces are approximate for modes reaching them. Result 'table' at the source wavelength: mode_number, n_eff, n_eff_imag, loss_db_per_cm, te_fraction, effective_area [m^2], pml_fraction, selected; extras wavelength, power, direction, mode_number.

- Category source; selection none (a selection is ignored with a warning); stepper precisions single only (see solvers); result kind `table`

Params:
- `normal` (default "z"; x | y | z) - Propagation axis
  Normal of the port plane (the waveguide axis); the plane spans the whole grid cross-section (PML included) and must cut a straight guide.
- `position` [m] (default 0) - Plane position
  Plane coordinate along the normal: a source takes the containing cell (its first total-field layer), a monitor the nearest cell edge.
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Mode number
  Mode rank in descending Re(beta^2) of the cross-section solve: 1 = fundamental; near-degenerate pairs of symmetric guides (square cores, fibres) come back as arbitrary mixtures: make the cross-section asymmetric to select one. The result table lists the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes.
- `direction` (default "positive"; positive | negative) - Direction
  positive launches toward +normal, negative toward -normal; one-sided at the source wavelength.
- `waveform` (default "gaussian"; gaussian | cw) - Waveform
  gaussian (sin carrier, gaussian envelope) or cw; the complex profile is driven by the carrier and its cos quadrature, so no ricker.
- `wavelength` [m] (default 1.55e-06; > 0) - Wavelength
  Vacuum carrier wavelength C0 / f0, the only one at which the mode (profile, n_eff) is solved: the launch is exact and one-sided there.
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.3; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Spectral width / f0; away from f0 the dispersing guide makes the launch leak backward and into radiation; above 0.6 the build warns (quadrature partner, DC part).
- `power` [W] (default 1; > 0) - Mode power
  Mode power as a flux plane on the guide reads it at the source wavelength (discrete Yee flux; cw: time average after the ramp, gaussian: at the envelope peak).

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.mode_monitor` - Mode monitor

Mode decomposition on a plane across the physical window: running DFTs of the tangential E (averaged across the plane) and H, projected on the cross-section mode solved per wavelength at build. Result 'xy' versus wavelength: power_positive / power_negative (a.u., flux-plane convention), power_per_cw_* [W] when every source shares one waveform, fraction_* = mode power / source power with exactly one mode source (downstream transmission, upstream reflection; NaN where its spectrum is below 1e-6 of the peak); extras n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag, mode_number, normalized.

- Category monitor; selection none (a selection is ignored with a warning); stepper precisions single only (see solvers); result kind `xy`

Params:
- `normal` (default "z"; x | y | z) - Propagation axis
  Normal of the port plane (the waveguide axis); the plane spans the whole grid cross-section (PML included) and must cut a straight guide.
- `position` [m] (default 0) - Plane position
  Plane coordinate along the normal: a source takes the containing cell (its first total-field layer), a monitor the nearest cell edge.
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Mode number
  Mode rank in descending Re(beta^2) of the cross-section solve: 1 = fundamental; near-degenerate pairs of symmetric guides (square cores, fibres) come back as arbitrary mixtures: make the cross-section asymmetric to select one. Picked at the middle wavelength and followed to the others by overlap (the build warns where the overlap stays below 0.9).
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 5; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths
  Evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency); 1 = the range centre. Each wavelength costs a cross-section mode solve at build (host scipy) and four complex128 window planes; 3-11 typical.

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.far_field` - Far-field pattern

Near-to-far-field transform of the tangential E and H on the six faces of a closed box object (each snapped to the nearest cell edge; the box must enclose every source and scatterer, vacuum outside; periodic axes are refused). Result 'far_field' in one cut plane: angles [rad] from its first axis, power (n_f, n_angles) = radiated power per steradian of the dt-weighted spectra (a.u., no 1/2), power_per_cw [W/sr] when every source shares one waveform (its sphere integral = flux box power_per_cw / cos(omega dt / 2), ~0.3 % at 25 cells per wavelength), quantity 'abs(E)^2', extras cut_plane, angle_axes. Mirror faces: the pattern of the unfolded structure (box-current images added, a box face on a mirror plane dropped, so box plus images must enclose the unfolded sources; at most one mirror per axis).

- Category monitor; selection domain entities, object kinds box, exactly 1; result kind `far_field`

Params:
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 5; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths
  Evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency); 1 = the range centre. Each wavelength stores four complex128 spectra on the six box faces (64 B per face cell).
- `cut_plane` (default "xz"; xz | yz | xy) - Cut plane
  Angles run counter-clockwise from its first axis (+x for xz and xy, +y for yz) toward its second (+z, +z, +y).
- `n_angles` (int; default 360; >= 1) - Number of angles
  Evenly spaced over 360 degrees in the cut plane.

## Physics type `em_fdtd_bor` - Electromagnetic Waves, time domain (axisymmetric, azimuthal order m)

Body-of-revolution (BOR) FDTD: the (r, z) half plane of a structure rotationally symmetric about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z), one azimuthal order m stepped in time on the em_fdfd_bor finite-integration operator (same Yee layout, ring metric and axis rules). Fields are the real time-domain amplitudes of the standing wave of order m: E_r, E_z, H_phi ~ cos(m phi), E_phi, H_r, H_z ~ sin(m phi) (m = 0: the TM and TE fields themselves). DFT phasors / source spectrum = the em_fdfd_bor travelling-wave phasors (E_phi, H_r, H_z times j) at omega_tilde = (2 / dt) sin(omega dt / 2), exactly: an em_fdfd_bor resonance omega rings at (2 / dt) asin(omega dt / 2). Leap-frog at the exact time-step limit of the order (courant_factor); CPML faces, pec / pmc walls; real eps components (em_fdfd_bor vocabulary), mu_r, sigma_e, sigma_m and Drude / Lorentz poles (velocity form on all three components; DFT phasors then solve em_fdfd_bor at omega_tilde with the pole at omega_tilde and damping gamma cos(omega dt / 2)). An azimuthal_orders list: the driven order sum of off-axis point sources (see that setting). Outputs at cell centres: components instantaneous (H half a step earlier); derived values weight by the ring volume 2 pi r dr dz. GPU or CPU backend (operators built on the host, sparse products per step). Cannot share a model with another EM type. heat_em_thermo_optic writes the three permittivity arrays. A frequency_domain study runs one pulse for the phasors at every study wavelength: all enabled sources share one gaussian or ricker waveform (study wavelengths outside its band warn), no coupling reads this physics. Its phasor fields are <component>_re / <component>_abs and e_abs_harmonic (em_fdfd_bor convention). Instance usually 'em'.

- Default instance name `em`; studies time_dependent, frequency_domain (default {"type": "time_dependent", "settings": {"duration": 2e-13}})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor; refinement indicator fields e_intensity; dispersion poles used
- Features: point_source, field_probe, resonance_monitor, pec_domain, flux_monitor, far_field, mode_source, mode_monitor

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (default "axisymmetric"; choice axisymmetric only) - Geometry. Help: shared `em_fdfd_bor.geometry`
- `bc_x_lo` (default "axis"; choice axis only) - Left edge. Help: shared `em_fdtd_bor.bc_x_lo`
- `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (default "cpml"; cpml | pec | pmc) - Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge. Help: shared `em_fdtd_bor.bc_x_lo`
- `pml_cells` [cells] (int; default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` [1] (default 1; > 0; visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` [1] (default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real CPML stretch (1 = none); larger damps evanescent and grazing waves; 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0; visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `azimuthal_order` (int; default 0; [0, 10000]) - Azimuthal order
  m of the fields (+m and -m are degenerate). m = 0: on-axis dipoles, radial modes (TE and TM decouple); m = 1: on-axis focused / plane waves; larger m: whispering-gallery modes, m ~ 2 pi R n_eff / lambda. dt ~ dr / (C0 (|m| + 1)) (the m / r terms near the axis), so large m costs steps (em_fdfd_bor eigenfrequency is cheaper for whispering-gallery resonances). Off-axis point source: azimuthal_orders.
- `azimuthal_orders` [1] (float_list; [0, 10000]; nullable) - Azimuthal order list
  Distinct integer orders m >= 0 of a driven order sum (as em_fdfd_bor); a non-empty list replaces azimuthal_order, null or [] = azimuthal_order alone. Every point_source becomes a 3D point current at phi = 0 (see point_source) expanded in exp(-j m phi); each m > 0 stands for +m and -m (a cos(m phi) standing wave), one stepper per order and source kind (r / z currents, phi currents; m = 0 one), all in lockstep at courant_factor x the limit of the largest order, summed. Fields, field_probe / resonance_monitor traces and frequency_domain phasors are the phi = 0 half plane of the 3D field (physical phasors, without the single-order j on E_phi, H_r, H_z; their ring-weighted integrals are not 3D integrals); flux_monitor and far_field add the orders exactly and report each. List every order 0..M: powers and far field converge once M exceeds k rho_s by a few (rho_s = source radius, k = n omega / c). Cost: up to 2 M + 1 steppers at the time step of order M. Sources must exist at the build (no later scripted source of a new kind); mode_source / mode_monitor need a single order.
- `courant_factor` [1] (default 0.99; (0, 1]) - Time step factor
  Fraction of the exact leap-frog limit 2 / omega_max of this grid and order (vacuum operator, host eigen-solve at the build), not the 2D CFL rule; stable for eps >= 1, mu_r >= 1 (the build refuses a field point below 1). Poles need eps_inf - P >= courant_factor^2 at every field point, P = (omega_p dt)^2 / 4 per Drude and delta_eps (omega_0 dt)^2 / (4 - (omega_0 dt)^2) per Lorentz pole (else the build stops: refine the mesh or lower this).

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1; writes eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic, all three components; n^2 of a lossless dielectric (silicon ~12.1, silica ~2.1 at 1.55 um); field-dependent values rewrite the coefficients at each change; a component property wins over it. Diagonal cylindrical components (rotationally invariant): eps_xx = eps_rr (E_r), eps_yy = axial eps_zz (E_z; drawing y = z), eps_zz = eps_phiphi (E_phi; writes the eps_r array). z-cut uniaxial crystal (optic axis on the rotation axis): eps_r = n_o^2, eps_yy = n_e^2; radially anisotropic shell: eps_xx. E_phi sees the cell value, E_r / E_z (cell edges) the ring-volume / length weighted mean of their non-PEC cells (no subpixel smoothing). Real values only; below 1 at a field point stops the build. Drude / Lorentz poles are stepped on all three components (2D FDTD velocity form; an E_r / E_z point sees the pole times the share of its cells carrying it), this value or the first Drude eps_inf the background; pole time-step bound: courant_factor.
- `eps_zz` [1] (default 1; >= 1; writes eps_r) - Relative permittivity, phi (azimuthal)
  eps_phiphi, the only component E_phi sees (stored in the eps_r array, overriding eps_r for E_phi only); the axial component is eps_yy.
- `eps_xx` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, r (radial)
  eps_rr, the only component E_r sees.
- `eps_yy` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, z (axial, drawing y)
  Axial eps_zz (drawing y), the only component E_z sees.
- `sigma_e` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Electric conductivity
  J = sigma_e E on every component (semi-implicit; E_r / E_z take the mean of their cells as eps); weak absorber of index n, extinction kappa: sigma_e = 2 n kappa omega eps0.
- `mu_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permeability
  Real, 1 for optical materials; H_r, H_phi, H_z take the mean of the cells around their points.
- `sigma_m` [Ohm/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Magnetic conductivity
  Loss on H (semi-implicit; artificial absorbers only).

### Fields

Output fields (primary e_intensity; [state] = also a state field):
- `er` - E_r (cos m phi wave) (V/m)
- `ephi` - E_phi (sin m phi wave) (V/m)
- `ez` - E_z (cos m phi wave) (V/m)
- `hr` - H_r (sin m phi wave) (A/m)
- `hphi` - H_phi (cos m phi wave) (A/m)
- `hz` - H_z (sin m phi wave) (A/m)
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2) [state]

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.point_source` - Point source

Current element in the cell containing the point (x = r, y = z): a ring in 3D with the azimuthal dependence of the order, driven by the waveform; see component and current.

- Category source; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `waveform` (default "gaussian"; gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` [m] (default 5.5e-07; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `component` (default "z"; r | phi | z) - Direction
  Normalised as the em_fdfd_bor point source ('phi': J_phi = I / (w h); 'z' / 'r': current I through the cell's ring cross-section; axis cell 'z': on-axis dipole of moment I h). For m != 0, I is the amplitude of the standing-wave current, cos(m phi) (z, r) / sin(m phi) (phi); a 'phi' current is the em_fdfd_bor one at phase +90 deg (same power). In a driven order sum (azimuthal_orders) a 3D point current at phi = 0 of moment I d as in em_fdfd_bor (free space: radiates eta0 k^2 (I d)^2 / (12 pi)).
- `current` [A] (default 0.001) - Current
  Peak current I times the waveform; fields are linear in it. Sign: the current is minus the textbook impressed current, so phases (and powers from probe fields) are pi off textbook formulas; moduli and fluxes agree.

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.field_probe` - Field probe

Time series of one component on its Yee point of the containing cell, sampled after every step (t in s, V/m or A/m); a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell.

- Category probe; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result kind `timeseries`

Params:
- `component` (default "ez"; er | ephi | ez | hr | hphi | hz) - Field component
  Raw sample every step on its Yee point of the containing cell: E_phi at the centre, E_r / H_z on the +r edge, E_z / H_r on the +z edge, H_phi on the +r +z corner; H half a step before the recorded time.

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.resonance_monitor` - Resonance finder

Help: shared `em_fdtd_bor.resonance_monitor`

- Category monitor; selection point entities, object kinds point, 1 to 16; stepper precisions single, double only (see solvers); result kind `table`

Params:
- `component` (default "ez"; er | ephi | ez | hr | hphi | hz) - Field component
  Recorded field: Raw sample every step on its Yee point of the containing cell: E_phi at the centre, E_r / H_z on the +r edge, E_z / H_r on the +z edge, H_phi on the +r +z corner; H half a step before the recorded time.
- `wavelength_min` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength. Keep the band inside the source spectrum; narrower = faster, better conditioned fit.
- `wavelength_max` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_min.
- `start_time` [s] (>= 0; nullable) - Analysis start. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.resonance_monitor.start_time`

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Rings in 3D: E_phi = 0 in cells whose centre lies in the domains, E_r / E_z = 0 on edges between two such cells (staircased; fixed at the build).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params: none

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

Spectral power through an axis-aligned line with the em_fdfd_bor flux_monitor pairing (E of the line cells, H on their hi face; exactly conserved through lossless cells): horizontal (z = const) along +z through the swept annulus, vertical (r = const) along +r through the cylinder, ring-weighted for the travelling exp(-j m phi) wave. Result 'flux_spectrum' in monitor order: power = pi sum Re(E H*) of the dt-weighted DFT spectra ('a.u.'); power_per_cw = power / |S(omega)|^2 = the power [W] of the cw source of the same current (em_fdfd_bor at omega_tilde). per_cw values need one waveform shared by every source feature (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives not counted); S = its dt-weighted spectrum over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 < 1e-6 of its source-wavelength value (cw: or |f - f0| >= 1 / (steps x dt)). They match em_fdfd_* at equal amplitudes, exactly at the source wavelength only. Driven order sum: totals of the 3D field (orders add exactly), extras power_orders / power_orders_per_cw (n_wavelengths x n_orders, each m with -m) and azimuthal_orders. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell); its hi face must be inside the grid.

- Category monitor; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params:
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 100; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths
  Evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency); 1 = the range centre. 50-200 for a smooth spectrum; the work per time step grows with it.

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.far_field` - Far-field pattern

Near-to-far-field transform of the DFT phasors on a rectangle as the em_fdfd_bor far_field (same surfaces and z_lo mirror images; vacuum outside the box). Result 'far_field' in monitor order: power r^2 |E|^2 / (2 eta0) [W/sr] of the cw source of the same current when every source shares one waveform (NaN outside its spectrum), else of the raw dt-weighted spectra ('a.u.'), versus meridional angle counter-clockwise from +r; extras power_theta / power_phi, angle_axes, azimuthal_order. Driven order sum: the pattern of the summed 3D field in the plane through the sources (cos >= 0 at phi = 0, the others at phi = pi); extras power_azimuthal_mean (phi average), power_orders (n_wavelengths x n_orders x n_angles, each m with -m), azimuthal_orders instead of azimuthal_order. Needs one cell beyond x1 / y1 and below y0 inside the domain; the box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis (an edge exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

- Category monitor; selection domain entities, object kinds rectangle, exactly 1; result kind `far_field`

Params:
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 21; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths
  Evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency); 1 = the range centre. Each wavelength accumulates complex128 spectra of the E / H rows and columns around the box faces (little memory); 1-41 typical.
- `n_angles` (int; default 360; >= 1) - Number of angles
  Far-field angles evenly spaced over 360 degrees counter-clockwise from +x.

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.mode_source` - Mode source

Launches one guided mode of a guide along the axis (fibre, pillar, metal pipe, coax) from a horizontal line in one direction: a one-sided TFSF interface between the line row and the row upstream, Re and Im of the carrier-frequency profile driven by the waveform and its quadrature (one-frequency mode, as industry transient ports). Exact and one-sided at the carrier; elsewhere in a pulse band the power differs somewhat and a little leaks backward (more with n_eff change over the band, near cutoff): for spectra divide by the forward power of a mode_monitor between source and device. Port line as the em_fdfd_bor ports (horizontal, from the axis or annular, metal ends); the line row and its neighbour rows must lie outside the z cpml. Modes ~ exp(-j beta z): full-vector solutions of the stepped BOR operator at omega_tilde = (2 / dt) sin(omega dt / 2) (stepped poles and conductivities), solved once on the build materials (later material changes not followed); exact for a guide invariant along z over a cell on each side of the line. Ranked by descending Re n_eff (mode 1 highest), 1 W each in the travelling exp(-j m phi) wave. Not in a driven order sum. Result 'table' of the carrier solve, one row per mode found (up to max(mode_number + 2, 4)): mode_number, n_eff, n_eff_imag, loss_db_per_cm, n_group, edge_field, selected; extras wavelength (carrier) [m], power [W], direction, mode_number, phase [deg].

- Category source; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `table`

Params:
- `waveform` (default "gaussian"; gaussian | cw) - Waveform
  gaussian: sin carrier of f0 = C0 / wavelength under exp(-((t - t0) / tau)^2), tau = 1 / (pi bandwidth f0), t0 = 4.5 tau, lasting ~2 t0 (550 nm, bandwidth 0.5: ~10 fs); amplitude = envelope peak, the carrier is 0 at t0 (source peak ~0.87 at bandwidth 0.5, ~0.66 at 1). cw: sin(2 pi f0 t) ramped in by 1 - exp(-t / (3 T)), T = 1 / f0, steady after ~15 periods. ricker: spectral peak f0, delayed 4 / f0 (3 % of the peak at 2.5 f0, 1 % at 2.76 f0). mode_source: gaussian or cw only (the launch drives the imaginary part of the profile with the quadrature partner of the waveform; keep a gaussian bandwidth <= 0.6).
- `wavelength` [m] (default 5.5e-07; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `power` [W] (default 1; >= 0) - Power. Help: shared `em_fdfd_bor.mode_source.power`
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; [1, 50]) - Mode number
  1 = highest Re n_eff at this order (HE11 of a fibre at m = 1, TE11 of a metal pipe); the result table lists the modes found.
- `direction` (default "positive"; positive | negative) - Direction
  'positive': toward +z (total field on the line row and above, only what comes back below); 'negative': toward -z (total field on the row and below).
- `phase` [deg] (default 0) - Phase
  Mode amplitude sqrt(P) e^{j phase} on the line row (each mode phased with its largest field sample real and positive).

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.mode_monitor` - Mode monitor

Splits the field on a horizontal line into the upward (positive) and downward (negative) amplitudes of one guided mode per monitor wavelength (DFT spectra of the line row and the row above, discrete reciprocity: other modes drop out); modes solved per wavelength (mode_number at the centre one, followed outward by overlap). Port line as the em_fdfd_bor ports (horizontal, from the axis or annular, metal ends); the line row and its neighbour rows must lie outside the z cpml. Modes ~ exp(-j beta z): full-vector solutions of the stepped BOR operator at omega_tilde = (2 / dt) sin(omega dt / 2) (stepped poles and conductivities), solved once on the build materials (later material changes not followed); exact for a guide invariant along z over a cell on each side of the line. Ranked by descending Re n_eff (mode 1 highest), 1 W each in the travelling exp(-j m phi) wave. Not in a driven order sum. Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength: power_positive / power_negative = |a|^2 of the dt-weighted DFT spectra (a.u.); with one shared source waveform power_per_cw_* = |a / S(omega)|^2 [W]; with exactly one enabled mode_source fraction_positive / fraction_negative = |a / (S sqrt(P) e^{j phase})|^2 (transmission / reflection into this mode) and phase_positive / phase_negative (rad, not de-embedded); per_cw rules as flux_monitor. Extras frequency, wavelength, n_eff, n_eff_imag, mode_number, normalized. Keep the line and the row above off the rows of a mode_source.

- Category monitor; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 100; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths
  Evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency); 1 = the range centre. 50-200 for a smooth spectrum; the work per time step grows with it.
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; [1, 50]) - Mode number
  Guided mode measured (ranked as mode_source); later wavelengths follow it by overlap.

## Physics type `em_fdtd_ez` - Electromagnetic Waves, time domain (2D, electric field out of plane)

2D finite-difference time-domain solver for the E_z polarisation: E_z out of plane in V/m, H_x and H_y in plane in A/m, x to the right and y up; Yee grid: E_z at cell centres, H_x / H_y on the +y / +x cell faces half a time step earlier. gaussian and cw sources use a sin carrier (ricker is a real wavelet), DFT-based monitors accumulate exp(-i omega t) at the actual sample times, every wavelength is a vacuum wavelength; CPML cells are added outside the domain. e_abs / e_intensity / h_abs = |E|, |E|^2, |H| at the cell centres: instantaneous values, where em_fdfd_* give phasor moduli. One Courant step per runner tick, so every must be 1. A frequency_domain study runs one pulse for the phasors at every study wavelength: all enabled sources share one gaussian or ricker waveform (study wavelengths outside its band warn), no coupling reads this physics. Stepper (role stepper, explicit_kernels): precision single (float32, default) or double (float64 fields, coefficients, CPML and pole arrays: ~2x field memory and time, for long or high-Q ring-downs where float32 coefficient rounding, ~1e-7 of a mode frequency, accumulates into phase drift); materials, absorbed power, probe traces and field-map spectra stay float32; nonlinear_medium / gain_medium need single.

- Default instance name `em`; studies time_dependent, frequency_domain (default {"type": "time_dependent", "settings": {"duration": 2e-13}})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor; refinement indicator fields ez; dispersion poles used
- Features: point_source, line_source, gaussian_beam, plane_wave_tfsf, mode_source, pec_domain, effective_index, nonlinear_medium, gain_medium, phase_change_medium, field_probe, resonance_monitor, flux_monitor, mode_monitor, dft_monitor, far_field

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (default "cpml"; cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  cpml: pml_cells absorbing cells outside the face. pec / pmc are perfect electric / magnetic walls up to one cell inside the domain edge. periodic: on both faces of the axis; period = the meshed window (uniform mesh: rounded up to whole cells); k = 0 (normal incidence) unless the type has bloch_kx / bloch_ky (em_fdfd_nonlinear: per harmonic_channel). symmetric / antisymmetric: mirror plane on the edge itself, E mirror-even (PMC) / -odd (PEC); a ghost cell outside (edge-cell width and material) holds the image, so draw the structure about the edge (x = 0 for x_lo); the other physics and both polarisations share plane and parity; a source in the outermost cell is mirrored. Results count the unfolded structure: flux lines and derived integrals reaching a mirror face double per face (extra mirror_factor; integrands assumed even), far fields add the image (at most one mirror per axis), Results.field(unfold=True) and the GUI unfold; mode-port powers, source powers and probes stay those of the drawn part. ez / hz walls are half a cell apart (E_z pec, H_z pmc at the outermost cell centre; E_z pmc, H_z pec on its inner face): a cavity is one cell wider or narrower in the other polarisation. E_z: symmetric = E_z even, antisymmetric = E_z odd about the plane. Walls are re-applied after source injection: a source value in the outermost cell of a pec or pmc face radiates nothing; a source next to a mirror plane sees its exact image.
- `pml_cells` [cells] (int; default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` [1] (default 1; > 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` [1] (default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real CPML stretch (1 = none); larger damps evanescent and grazing waves; 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `courant_factor` [1] (default 0.99; (0, 1]) - Time step factor
  Time step as a fraction of the 2D CFL limit: dt = factor / (C0 sqrt(1/dx^2 + 1/dy^2)) (graded mesh: the finest cells). Stable only where eps_r * mu_r >= (C0 dt)^2 (1/dx^2 + 1/dy^2) + mu_r P, P = (omega_p dt)^2 / 4 per Drude pole and delta_eps (omega_0 dt)^2 / (4 - (omega_0 dt)^2) per Lorentz pole: an eps_inf ~1 metal needs a lower factor at coarse cells. The build checks every cell and names the worst one and the largest stable factor; runtime eps_r rewrites (thermo-optic) are not checked.
- `track_absorption` (bool; default false) - Track absorption
  Accumulate J.E losses (output absorbed_power in W/m^3, state q_accum in J/m^3) also without em_heat_joule; ~one extra GPU pass per step over the bounding boxes of the conducting and dispersive cells. q_accum (and jz_total, with a Drude pole) exists only while accumulating. Switched on automatically when a material expression, derived value, field_transfer, em_heat_joule or em_semiconductor_generation reads q_accum, or a derived value reads absorbed_power (else absorbed_power is 0). absorbed_power shows the current accumulation window, else the last completed one; em_heat_joule resets q_accum at each transfer, else the window spans the whole run.
- `bloch_kx` [rad/m] (default 0; visible when bc_x_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector x. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.bloch_kx`
- `bloch_ky` [rad/m] (default 0; visible when bc_y_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector y. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.bloch_kx`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity
  n^2 of a lossless dielectric (glass ~2.1-2.25, silicon ~12.1 at 1.55 um). E_z sees eps_zz instead when set. With poles it is the background eps_inf (an explicit eps_r or eps_zz wins over the Drude eps_inf). A state-dependent eps_r (e.g. of T) is rewritten once per step of the physics it reads, not every EM step.
- `eps_zz` [1] (default 1; >= 1; writes eps_r) - Relative permittivity, z (out of plane). Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.eps_zz`
- `sigma_e` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss J = sigma_e E_z. Weak absorber of index n, extinction kappa at omega: sigma_e = 2 n kappa omega eps0; model metals with a Drude pole, not their DC conductivity.
- `mu_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permeability
  Enters the Courant check (eps_r * mu_r) and the local impedance of line sources; 1 for practically every optical material.
- `sigma_m` [Ohm/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss on H_x, H_y; sigma_m / (mu0 mu_r) = sigma_e / (eps0 eps_r) is an impedance-matched absorber (no reflection at normal incidence).

### Fields

Output fields (primary ez; [state] = also a state field):
- `ez` - E_z (V/m) [state]
- `hx` - H_x (+y face) (A/m) [state]
- `hy` - H_y (+x face) (A/m) [state]
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity (1) [state]
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m) [state]
- `absorbed_power` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)
- `carrier_density` - Free-carrier density (1/m^3)
- `population_inversion` - Population inversion N2 - N1 (1/m^3)
- `crystallinity` - Crystallinity (1)
- `ez_re` - Re E_z (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_im` - Im E_z (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_abs` - |E_z| (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_phase` - arg E_z (phasor) (rad) [frequency_domain study only]
- `e_abs_harmonic` - |E| (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `e_intensity_harmonic` - |E|^2 (phasor) (V^2/m^2) [frequency_domain study only]
- `absorbed_power_harmonic` - Absorbed power density (time average) (W/m^3) [frequency_domain study only]
State fields that are no output field:
- `jz_total` - Dispersive current density J_z (A/m^2)
- `q_accum` - Absorbed energy density (J/m^3)

### Source slots

- `ez_source` (V/m per EM step): Raw increment added to E_z every EM step (after the sources) until the next transfer, not a calibrated source: a constant b acts like a current density ~ -eps0 eps_r b / dt, so it scales with 1/dt (mesh, courant_factor); not in the DFT decimation bound.
- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.point_source` - Point source

z-directed filament current I in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell), radiating a mesh-independent cylindrical wave.

- Category source; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `waveform` (default "gaussian"; gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` [m] (default 5.5e-07; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `current` [A] (default 0.001) - Electric line current
  Peak z-directed filament current I; mesh-independent field, for cw |E_z| = omega mu0 I / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| in a homogeneous non-magnetic medium of wavenumber k (1 mA at wavelength 1 um: ~2e5 V/m at r = 1 um). Sign: the current is minus the textbook impressed current, so phases (and powers from probe fields) are pi off textbook formulas; moduli and fluxes agree.

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.line_source` - Line source

Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.line_source`

- Category source; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `waveform` (default "gaussian"; gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` [m] (default 5.5e-07; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `amplitude` [V/m] (default 1) - Amplitude
  E_z radiated to each side of the line in the local medium (a cw plane wave of this amplitude when the line spans a periodic axis); calibrated with |eta| of the line cells at the centre frequency (sigma_e, dispersion included), so other frequencies of a pulse in a dispersive medium deviate. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so across several media (core / cladding) the current steps at the interfaces and diffracts (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. A recalibration (e.g. thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2).
