### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source` - Mode source

Port source launching one guided mode of the cross-section under an axis-aligned line in one direction: the mode drives E_z in the line cells and H_y (vertical line) / H_x (horizontal line) on their upstream face (lo face of the line cells for positive, hi face for negative). One-sided total-field / scattered-field line: total field from the line cells downstream, only reflections upstream. Exact at the source wavelength; toward the band edges of a gaussian pulse some power leaks upstream or into radiation (the mode disperses), so keep the bandwidth modest in dispersive guides. Mode monitors normalise by it when it is the only enabled mode source of the physics. Its interface face holds scattered field, so a flux or mode monitor on the line of a negative source mixes both (validation warns). The 1D line eigenmodes are FDTD-consistent (Yee dispersion, PML stretch, complex line-cell eps / mu), solved at build and re-solved during the run (following the mode by overlap) whenever the line materials drift by > 1e-3 relative (thermo-optic, Pockels, state-dependent eps); a mode monitor then decomposes its whole-run spectra with the latest modes (run log note), valid only for light passing after the medium settled. Put the line across a straight guide, same cross-section a few cells either side, locally uniform mesh (validation refuses a line whose face is on the outer grid wall and warns when a wall pins the line cell or its face, when its face lies in a CPML layer, or when the normal cell widths change by > 1% around it). Span ends: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML (open); an end on a pec domain edge takes E_z = 0, one on a pmc or symmetric edge dE_z/dn = 0 and one on an antisymmetric edge E_z odd about the plane; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E_z = 0 in the next cell), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns above 1% of the mode peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). Result 'table' at the source wavelength, one row per mode for the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes: mode_number, n_eff, n_eff_imag (< 0 = loss, exp(+j omega t)), loss_db_per_cm, n_group, edge_field (largest |field| at the line ends / peak; above 1e-2 at a metal end the line cuts the mode), selected (the launched mode); extras wavelength, power, direction, mode_number, tracked_mode_number (rank of the launched mode in the latest solve, changed by a re-solve during the run; selected follows it).

- Category source; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `table`

Params:
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Mode number. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.mode_number`
- `direction` (default "positive"; positive | negative) - Direction. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.direction`
- `waveform` (default "gaussian"; gaussian | cw) - Waveform. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` [m] (default 5.5e-07; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.3; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.bandwidth`
- `power` [W/m] (default 1; > 0) - Mode power. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.power`

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor: E_z = 0 (no dispersive current) in every cell whose centre lies in the selected domains, staircased; with solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries the H links from free cells put E_z = 0 at the drawn wall (exact wall distance, floored per cell so the time step stays stable).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params: none

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium` - Nonlinear medium

chi2 (d_eff, poling), Kerr, two-photon absorption (TPA) and TPA free carriers on the selected cells (later features win on overlaps), on top of the linear material. Each step corrects E_z at the cell centres, n0^2 = eps_r of the cell after the linear update, solving D = eps0 (eps + chi2 E + chi3 E^2 + delta eps(N)) E with the TPA + FCA conductivity implicitly (one kernel on the selection box; n0 read live, so thermo-optic changes carry over). Carrier density N (output field carrier_density, 1/m^3) follows dN/dt = TPA power / (2 hbar omega) - N / tau. Breaks superposition: time_dependent study only, Bloch k = 0 only (validation errors). Resolve the generated harmonics (>= 10 cells per wavelength / 2 with d_eff, / 3 for strong Kerr) or they alias; DFT monitors sample often enough for up to three times the source band. Single-precision stepper only (a double stepper is a validation error).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; stepper precisions single only (see solvers); result none

Params:
- `n2` [m^2/W] (default 0) - Kerr index n2. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.n2`
- `tpa_beta` [m/W] (default 0; >= 0) - Two-photon absorption. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.tpa_beta`
- `carrier_lifetime` [s] (default 0; >= 0) - Carrier lifetime. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.carrier_lifetime`
- `fca_cross_section` [m^2] (default 0; >= 0) - Free-carrier absorption cross-section. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.fca_cross_section`
- `fcd_coefficient` [m^3] (default 0; >= 0) - Free-carrier index change. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.fcd_coefficient`
- `pump_wavelength` [m] (default 1.55e-06; > 0) - Pump wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.pump_wavelength`
- `d_eff` [m/V] (default 0) - Second-order coefficient d. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.d_eff`
- `poling` [1] (default 1; may use x, y) - Poling. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.poling`

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium` - Gain medium

Four-level two-electron gain medium (Chang and Taflove, Opt. Express 12, 3827, 2004) on the selected cells, acting on E_z at the cell centres: a Lorentz polarisation d2P/dt2 + gamma dP/dt + omega_a^2 P = kappa (N1 - N2) E, kappa = 6 pi eps0 c^3 / (omega_a^2 tau_21), coupled to the rate equations of populations N0..N3 (pump W_p N0 -> N3, decays N3 -> N2 -> N1 -> N0, stimulated transitions (E . dP/dt) / (hbar omega_a)); N2 > N1 amplifies, N1 > N2 absorbs. Overlapping regions are two species. Output field population_inversion = N2 - N1 (1/m^3). Not in absorbed power; not in the build Courant check (keep |delta eps| (omega_a dt)^2 / 4 << 1). Time_dependent study, Bloch k = 0 and single-precision stepper only (as nonlinear_medium).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; stepper precisions single only (see solvers); result none

Params:
- `wavelength` [m] (default 1.55e-06; > 0) - Transition wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength lambda_a of the lasing transition 2 -> 1 (omega_a = 2 pi c / lambda_a).
- `linewidth` [rad/s] (default 1e+14; >= 0) - Gain linewidth
  Full width gamma of the Lorentzian line (angular, not Hz; FWHM in wavelength ~ lambda_a^2 gamma / (2 pi c)); peak gain ~ 1 / gamma.
- `density` [1/m^3] (default 1e+24; > 0) - Active ion density. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.density`
- `pump_rate` [1/s] (default 0; >= 0) - Pump rate. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.pump_rate`
- `tau_32` [s] (default 1e-13; > 0) - Lifetime level 3 -> 2
  Non-radiative lifetime 3 -> 2; >= 10 time steps (explicit rate step; validation error).
- `tau_21` [s] (default 1e-09; > 0) - Lifetime level 2 -> 1
  Upper lasing level lifetime, also the radiative lifetime in kappa: longer = weaker coupling per atom but larger steady inversion; >= 10 time steps.
- `tau_10` [s] (default 1e-13; > 0) - Lifetime level 1 -> 0
  Lower lasing level lifetime into the ground state; >= 10 time steps.
- `initial_upper_fraction` [1] (default 0; [0, 1]) - Initial upper-level fraction
  Share of density in level 2 at t = 0 (rest in level 0): initial inversion fraction x density, for runs much shorter than tau_21.

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

Spectral Poynting flux through an axis-aligned line: the Yee discrete flux through the hi face of the line cells, > 0 toward +x (vertical line) / +y (horizontal). power in a.u. per unit z length, not normalised by the source spectrum: compare runs by ratios (transmission = device run / reference run with the same source); power_per_cw = power / (2 |S(omega)|^2) is the cw power in W/m. per_cw values need one waveform shared by every source feature (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives not counted); S = its dt-weighted spectrum over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 < 1e-6 of its source-wavelength value (cw: or |f - f0| >= 1 / (steps x dt)). They match em_fdfd_* at equal amplitudes, exactly at the source wavelength only. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

- Category monitor; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params:
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 100; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths
  Evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency); 1 = the range centre. 50-200 for a smooth spectrum; the work per time step grows with it.

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor` - Mode monitor

Port monitor splitting the field on an axis-aligned line into the forward (positive: toward +x / +y) and backward (negative) amplitudes a of one guided mode per monitor wavelength: running DFTs of E_z in the line cells and of H_y (vertical line) / H_x (horizontal line) on their hi face are projected on the mode solved at that wavelength, so each direction is measured separately, unlike a flux_monitor. The 1D line eigenmodes are FDTD-consistent (Yee dispersion, PML stretch, complex line-cell eps / mu), solved at build and re-solved during the run (following the mode by overlap) whenever the line materials drift by > 1e-3 relative (thermo-optic, Pockels, state-dependent eps); a mode monitor then decomposes its whole-run spectra with the latest modes (run log note), valid only for light passing after the medium settled. Put the line across a straight guide, same cross-section a few cells either side, locally uniform mesh (validation refuses a line whose face is on the outer grid wall and warns when a wall pins the line cell or its face, when its face lies in a CPML layer, or when the normal cell widths change by > 1% around it). Span ends: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML (open); an end on a pec domain edge takes E_z = 0, one on a pmc or symmetric edge dE_z/dn = 0 and one on an antisymmetric edge E_z odd about the plane; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E_z = 0 in the next cell), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns above 1% of the mode peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). Result 'xy' versus wavelength: power_positive / power_negative = 2 |a|^2 in a.u. (flux_monitor convention, comparable with its power); power_per_cw_positive / _negative = |a|^2 / |S|^2 in W/m (cw mode power, as em_fdfd_* power_*); with exactly one enabled mode_source in the physics also fraction_positive / _negative = mode power / source power (transmission into this mode downstream of the source, reflection upstream; NaN as for per_cw) and phase_positive / _negative (rad) = the phase of that S-parameter relative to the amplitude the source launches on its own line, not de-embedded (each profile phased with its largest sample real and positive, the lowest-coordinate one of mirror-equal peaks); extras frequency, wavelength, n_eff, n_eff_imag (per wavelength), mode_number, tracked_mode_number (rank of the followed mode at the middle wavelength in the latest solve), normalized (fractions present). Run until the pulse has passed every monitor; the fractions inherit the source leakage, most accurate near its wavelength. per_cw values need one waveform shared by every source feature (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives not counted); S = its dt-weighted spectrum over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 < 1e-6 of its source-wavelength value (cw: or |f - f0| >= 1 / (steps x dt)). They match em_fdfd_* at equal amplitudes, exactly at the source wavelength only.

- Category monitor; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Mode number. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor.mode_number`
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 21; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor.n_wavelengths`

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.dft_monitor` - Field map monitor

Running DFT of E_z over a rectangle (exp(-i omega t) at the actual sample times): |E_z(omega)|^2 per wavelength (one per freq_index) in a.u., not normalised by the source spectrum; intensity x intensity_per_cw_factor[freq_index] (1 / |S(omega)|^2) is the cw |E_z|^2 in (V/m)^2. per_cw values need one waveform shared by every source feature (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives not counted); S = its dt-weighted spectrum over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 < 1e-6 of its source-wavelength value (cw: or |f - f0| >= 1 / (steps x dt)). They match em_fdfd_* at equal amplitudes, exactly at the source wavelength only. The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis (an edge exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

- Category monitor; selection domain entities, object kinds rectangle, exactly 1; result kind `dft_fields`

Params:

- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 5; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths
  Evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency); 1 = the range centre. GPU memory 2 * n_wavelengths * box cells * 4 B / downsample^2 (1000 x 1000 cells at 10 wavelengths: 80 MB; validation warns above 1 GiB), and each wavelength adds work per step; 1-21 typical.
- `downsample` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Record every n-th cell. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.dft_monitor.downsample`

## Physics type `em_fdtd_hz` - Electromagnetic Waves, time domain (2D, magnetic field out of plane)

2D finite-difference time-domain solver for the H_z polarisation: H_z out of plane in A/m, E_x and E_y in plane in V/m, x to the right and y up; Yee grid: H_z at cell centres half a time step before the recorded time, E_x on the +y and E_y on the +x cell faces (face materials: see eps_r). Curved interfaces are staircased and plasmon resonances shift on coarse meshes: use cells of a few nm for plasmonics. gaussian and cw sources use a sin carrier (ricker is a real wavelet), DFT-based monitors accumulate exp(-i omega t) at the actual sample times, every wavelength is a vacuum wavelength; CPML cells are added outside the domain. e_abs / e_intensity / h_abs = |E|, |E|^2, |H| at the cell centres: instantaneous values, where em_fdfd_* give phasor moduli. One Courant step per runner tick, so every must be 1. With an em_fdtd_ez physics in the same model (e.g. one per polarisation) it needs another instance name (e.g. em_hz) and equal bc_* / pml_* settings (one shared boundary configuration). A frequency_domain study runs one pulse for the phasors at every study wavelength: all enabled sources share one gaussian or ricker waveform (study wavelengths outside its band warn), no coupling reads this physics. Stepper (role stepper, explicit_kernels): precision single (float32, default) or double (float64 fields, coefficients, CPML and pole arrays: ~2x field memory and time, for long or high-Q ring-downs where float32 coefficient rounding, ~1e-7 of a mode frequency, accumulates into phase drift); materials, absorbed power, probe traces and field-map spectra stay float32; nonlinear_medium / gain_medium need single.

- Default instance name `em`; studies time_dependent, frequency_domain (default {"type": "time_dependent", "settings": {"duration": 2e-13}})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor; refinement indicator fields hz; dispersion poles used
- Features: point_source, line_source, gaussian_beam, plane_wave_tfsf, mode_source, pec_domain, effective_index, nonlinear_medium, gain_medium, phase_change_medium, field_probe, resonance_monitor, flux_monitor, mode_monitor, dft_monitor, far_field

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (default "cpml"; cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  cpml: pml_cells absorbing cells outside the face. pec / pmc are perfect electric / magnetic walls up to one cell inside the domain edge. periodic: on both faces of the axis; period = the meshed window (uniform mesh: rounded up to whole cells); k = 0 (normal incidence) unless the type has bloch_kx / bloch_ky (em_fdfd_nonlinear: per harmonic_channel). symmetric / antisymmetric: mirror plane on the edge itself, E mirror-even (PMC) / -odd (PEC); a ghost cell outside (edge-cell width and material) holds the image, so draw the structure about the edge (x = 0 for x_lo); the other physics and both polarisations share plane and parity; a source in the outermost cell is mirrored. Results count the unfolded structure: flux lines and derived integrals reaching a mirror face double per face (extra mirror_factor; integrands assumed even), far fields add the image (at most one mirror per axis), Results.field(unfold=True) and the GUI unfold; mode-port powers, source powers and probes stay those of the drawn part. ez / hz walls are half a cell apart (E_z pec, H_z pmc at the outermost cell centre; E_z pmc, H_z pec on its inner face): a cavity is one cell wider or narrower in the other polarisation. H_z: symmetric = H_z odd, antisymmetric = H_z even (tangential E = 0 on the plane, as pec). Walls are re-applied after source injection, so a source value on a pinned row or face radiates nothing (validation warns; cases: the point_source, line_source and gaussian_beam texts).
- `pml_cells` [cells] (int; default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` [1] (default 1; > 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` [1] (default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real CPML stretch (1 = none); larger damps evanescent and grazing waves; 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `courant_factor` [1] (default 0.99; (0, 1]) - Time step factor
  Time step as a fraction of the 2D CFL limit: dt = factor / (C0 sqrt(1/dx^2 + 1/dy^2)) (graded mesh: the finest cells). Stable only where min(eps_xx, eps_yy) * mu_r >= (C0 dt)^2 (1/dx^2 + 1/dy^2) + mu_r P, P = (omega_p dt)^2 / 4 per Drude pole and delta_eps (omega_0 dt)^2 / (4 - (omega_0 dt)^2) per Lorentz pole: an eps_inf ~1 metal needs a lower factor at coarse cells. The build checks every cell and names the worst one and the largest stable factor; runtime eps_xx / eps_yy rewrites (thermo-optic) are not checked.
- `track_absorption` (bool; default false) - Track absorption
  Accumulate J.E losses J_x E_x + J_y E_y + sigma_e |E|^2 on the cell faces (output absorbed_power in W/m^3, state q_accum in J/m^3) also without em_heat_joule; ~one extra full-grid GPU pass per step. A face's conductivity loss goes to each of its two cells by that cell's sigma_e, a pole current's loss to the dispersive cells (half / half between two different dispersive cells). q_accum exists only while accumulating. Switched on automatically when a material expression, derived value, field_transfer, em_heat_joule or em_semiconductor_generation reads q_accum, or a derived value reads absorbed_power (else absorbed_power is 0). absorbed_power shows the current accumulation window, else the last completed one; em_heat_joule resets q_accum at each transfer, else the window spans the whole run.
- `bloch_kx` [rad/m] (default 0; visible when bc_x_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector x. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.bloch_kx`
- `bloch_ky` [rad/m] (default 0; visible when bc_y_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector y. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.bloch_kx`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1; writes eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic in-plane value: sets eps_xx and eps_yy unless the material sets those (a component wins). n^2 of a lossless dielectric (glass ~2.1-2.25, silicon ~12.1 at 1.55 um). E_x / E_y sit on cell faces: each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells (solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages interface faces anisotropically). With poles it is the background eps_inf (an explicit permittivity wins over the Drude eps_inf). A state-dependent eps_r (e.g. of T) is rewritten once per step of the physics it reads, not every EM step.
- `eps_xx` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, x. Help: shared `em_eme.eps_xx`
- `eps_yy` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, y. Help: shared `em_eme.eps_yy`
- `sigma_e` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss J = sigma_e E on E_x and E_y (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells). Weak absorber of index n, extinction kappa at omega: sigma_e = 2 n kappa omega eps0; model metals with a Drude pole, not their DC conductivity.
- `mu_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permeability
  H_z sees mu_zz = mu_r. Enters the Courant check (min(eps_xx, eps_yy) * mu_r) and the local impedance of line sources; 1 for practically every optical material.
- `sigma_m` [Ohm/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss on H_z; sigma_m / (mu0 mu_r) = sigma_e / (eps0 eps_r) is an impedance-matched absorber (no reflection at normal incidence).

### Fields

Output fields (primary hz; [state] = also a state field):
- `hz` - H_z (A/m) [state]
- `ex` - E_x (V/m)
- `ey` - E_y (V/m)
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity xx (1) [state]
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity yy (1) [state]
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m) [state]
- `absorbed_power` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)
- `carrier_density` - Free-carrier density (1/m^3)
- `population_inversion` - Population inversion N2 - N1 (1/m^3)
- `crystallinity` - Crystallinity (1)
- `hz_re` - Re H_z (phasor) (A/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `hz_im` - Im H_z (phasor) (A/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `hz_abs` - |H_z| (phasor) (A/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `hz_phase` - arg H_z (phasor) (rad) [frequency_domain study only]
- `e_abs_harmonic` - |E| (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `e_intensity_harmonic` - |E|^2 (phasor) (V^2/m^2) [frequency_domain study only]
- `absorbed_power_harmonic` - Absorbed power density (time average) (W/m^3) [frequency_domain study only]
State fields that are no output field:
- `q_accum` - Absorbed energy density (J/m^3)

### Source slots

- `hz_source` (A/m per EM step): Raw increment added to H_z every EM step (after the magnetic sources) until the next transfer, not a calibrated source: a constant b acts like a magnetic current density ~ -mu0 mu_r b / dt, so it scales with 1/dt (mesh, courant_factor); not in the DFT decimation bound.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.point_source` - Point source

Current-calibrated, mesh-independent point excitation (see excitation) in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell). Walls overwrite some values every step (warning): a magnetic_current in the outermost cell of a pec, pmc, symmetric or antisymmetric face radiates nothing, nor does the face-parallel current of an electric_dipole in one of the two outermost cells of a pec or antisymmetric face.

- Category source; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `excitation` (default "magnetic_current"; magnetic_current | electric_dipole) - Excitation
  magnetic_current: z-directed magnetic line current added to H_z at the cell centre (isotropic). electric_dipole: in-plane current element along orientation on the four E faces of the cell.
- `waveform` (default "gaussian"; gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` [m] (default 5.5e-07; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `magnetic_current` [V] (default 1; visible when excitation in (magnetic_current)) - Magnetic line current
  Peak z-directed magnetic line current K_m (dual of a filament current); mesh-independent field: for cw in a homogeneous medium of eps_r and wavenumber k, |H_z| = omega eps0 eps_r K_m / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| (1 V at 1 um in vacuum: ~1.3e3 A/m at r = 1 um). A fixed K_m radiates power ~ n^2 of its cell, so it drifts when eps there changes; a filament current or dipole radiates n-independent power. Sign: the current is minus the textbook impressed current, so phases (and powers from probe fields) are pi off textbook formulas; moduli and fluxes agree.
- `dipole_moment` [A] (default 0.001; visible when excitation in (electric_dipole)) - Dipole strength
  Peak in-plane dipole strength M = integral of J over the cross-section (A m of current moment per m of z), along orientation; mesh-independent field: for cw in a homogeneous medium of wavenumber k, |H_z| = k M / 4 |H1^(2)(k r)| |sin(phi - orientation)|, phi counter-clockwise from +x (1 mA at 1 um in vacuum: ~5e2 A/m at r = 1 um broadside). Sign: the current is minus the textbook impressed current, so phases (and powers from probe fields) are pi off textbook formulas; moduli and fluxes agree.
- `orientation` [deg] (default 0; visible when excitation in (electric_dipole)) - Dipole orientation
  Dipole current direction counter-clockwise from +x: 0 drives only the E_x faces, 90 only E_y. Radiates most broadside, nothing along it.

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.line_source` - Line source

Electric sheet current on the hi face of the line cells (+x face of a vertical line, +y face of a horizontal one) sending amplitude (tangential E) to each side in the local medium: a vertical line (x = const) drives E_y along +x and -x, a horizontal one E_x along +y and -y. For a plane wave span the whole domain (an end on a cpml domain edge continues through the PML; on a periodic axis span the whole period); a shorter line diffracts like a slit. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). The line must not lie in the last cell row / column before a non-periodic hi face without PML (the sheet would be the outer grid wall), nor, next to a pec or antisymmetric face, put the sheet on the inner face of the outermost cell (line in the outermost lo cell or the last-but-one hi cell), which the wall pins to 0 every step (warning: it radiates nothing).

- Category source; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `waveform` (default "gaussian"; gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` [m] (default 5.5e-07; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `amplitude` [V/m] (default 1) - Amplitude
  Tangential E (E_x for a horizontal line, E_y for a vertical one) radiated to each side of the line in the local medium (a cw plane wave of this amplitude when the line spans a periodic axis); calibrated with |eta| of the line faces at the centre frequency (sigma_e, dispersion included), so other frequencies of a pulse in a dispersive medium deviate. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so across several media (core / cladding) the current steps at the interfaces and diffracts (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. Its medium is the face mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, so on an interface sqrt(mean eps) is not the mean index (Si / air: ~14% off). A recalibration (e.g. thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2).

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.gaussian_beam` - Gaussian beam

Line source with the profile exp(-((s - center) / waist)^2) along the line: a beam of peak tangential E = amplitude to each side in the local medium (vertical line: E_y, along +x and -x; horizontal: E_x, along +y and -y), waist on the line, sheet on the hi face of the line cells. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). The line must not lie in the last cell row / column before a non-periodic hi face without PML (the sheet would be the outer grid wall), nor, next to a pec or antisymmetric face, put the sheet on the inner face of the outermost cell (line in the outermost lo cell or the last-but-one hi cell), which the wall pins to 0 every step (warning: it radiates nothing).

- Category source; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `waveform` (default "gaussian"; gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` [m] (default 5.5e-07; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.5; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `amplitude` [V/m] (default 1) - Amplitude
  Peak tangential E (E_x for a horizontal line, E_y for a vertical one) at the beam centre on the waist line, radiated to each side in the local medium; calibrated with |eta| of the line faces at the centre frequency (sigma_e, dispersion included), so other frequencies of a pulse in a dispersive medium deviate. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so across several media (core / cladding) the current steps at the interfaces and diffracts (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. Its medium is the face mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, so on an interface sqrt(mean eps) is not the mean index (Si / air: ~14% off). A recalibration (e.g. thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2).
- `waist` [m] (default 1e-06; > 0) - Waist radius. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.gaussian_beam.waist`
- `center` [m] (nullable) - Beam centre
  Beam axis along the line (x for a horizontal line, y for a vertical one); empty = midpoint. Off the line only the tail launches (validation warns).

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.plane_wave_tfsf` - Plane wave box (+x)

Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.plane_wave_tfsf`

- Category source; selection domain entities, object kinds rectangle, exactly 1; result none

Params:
- `waveform` (default "gaussian"; gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` [m] (default 5.5e-07; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`

  Peak incident E_y (computed for vacuum, H_z = E_y / eta0).

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.mode_source` - Mode source

Port source launching one guided mode of the cross-section under an axis-aligned line in one direction: the mode drives H_z in the line cells and E_y (vertical line) / E_x (horizontal line) on their upstream face (lo face of the line cells for positive, hi face for negative). One-sided total-field / scattered-field line: total field from the line cells downstream, only reflections upstream. Exact at the source wavelength; toward the band edges of a gaussian pulse some power leaks upstream or into radiation (the mode disperses), so keep the bandwidth modest in dispersive guides. Mode monitors normalise by it when it is the only enabled mode source of the physics. Its interface face holds scattered field, so a flux or mode monitor on the line of a negative source mixes both (validation warns). The 1D line eigenmodes are FDTD-consistent (Yee dispersion, PML stretch, complex line-cell eps / mu), solved at build and re-solved during the run (following the mode by overlap) whenever the line materials drift by > 1e-3 relative (thermo-optic, Pockels, state-dependent eps); a mode monitor then decomposes its whole-run spectra with the latest modes (run log note), valid only for light passing after the medium settled. Put the line across a straight guide, same cross-section a few cells either side, locally uniform mesh (validation refuses a line whose face is on the outer grid wall and warns when a wall pins the line cell or its face, when its face lies in a CPML layer, or when the normal cell widths change by > 1% around it). Span ends: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML (open); an end on a pec or antisymmetric domain edge takes tangential E = 0 on the inner face of the outermost cell (dH_z/dn = 0), one on a pmc edge H_z = 0 and one on a symmetric edge H_z odd; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E along the propagation direction = 0 on the face beyond the end, so dH_z/dn = 0), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns above 1% of the mode peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The in-plane E faces use the permittivity the engine uses (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells), so a guide edge on a face line takes the core / cladding mean. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). Result 'table' at the source wavelength, one row per mode for the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes: mode_number, n_eff, n_eff_imag (< 0 = loss, exp(+j omega t)), loss_db_per_cm, n_group, edge_field (largest |field| at the line ends / peak; above 1e-2 at a metal end the line cuts the mode), selected (the launched mode); extras wavelength, power, direction, mode_number, tracked_mode_number (rank of the launched mode in the latest solve, changed by a re-solve during the run; selected follows it).

- Category source; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `table`

Params:
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Mode number. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.mode_number`
- `direction` (default "positive"; positive | negative) - Direction. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.direction`
- `waveform` (default "gaussian"; gaussian | cw) - Waveform. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` [m] (default 5.5e-07; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` [1] (default 0.3; > 0; visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.bandwidth`
- `power` [W/m] (default 1; > 0) - Mode power. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.power`

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor: tangential E = 0 (no dispersive current) on the four faces of each cell whose centre lies in the selected domains, staircased. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (Dey-Mittra) only faces wholly inside the drawn metal are PEC; cut cells update H_z from their free face lengths and free area (enlarged where needed so the time step stays stable).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params: none

Help: shared `em_fdfd_hz.effective_index`

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params:
- `layer_indices` [1] (float_list; default [1.444, 3.476, 1.444]; > 0) - Layer refractive indices

- `layer_thicknesses` [m] (float_list; default [2.2e-07]; > 0) - Film thicknesses
  Film thicknesses, bottom to top: exactly len(layer_indices) - 2 entries.
- `wavelength` [m] (default 1.55e-06; > 0) - Wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.effective_index.wavelength`

  Guided slab mode by descending n_eff, 1 = fundamental; an error when the stack guides fewer.

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.nonlinear_medium` - Nonlinear medium

chi2 (d_eff, poling), Kerr, two-photon absorption (TPA) and TPA free carriers on the selected cells (later features win on overlaps), on top of the linear material. Each step corrects E_x / E_y each on its own faces (face mean of the cell values, n0^2 = the face permittivity); |E|^2, chi2 and the TPA carriers are per component (E_x^2 on E_x faces, ...): exact for a field along one in-plane axis (slab modes, plane waves), approximate for mixed polarisation (cross-component terms dropped) after the linear update, solving D = eps0 (eps + chi2 E + chi3 E^2 + delta eps(N)) E with the TPA + FCA conductivity implicitly (one kernel on the selection box; n0 read live, so thermo-optic changes carry over). Carrier density N (output field carrier_density, 1/m^3) follows dN/dt = TPA power / (2 hbar omega) - N / tau. Breaks superposition: time_dependent study only, Bloch k = 0 only (validation errors). Resolve the generated harmonics (>= 10 cells per wavelength / 2 with d_eff, / 3 for strong Kerr) or they alias; DFT monitors sample often enough for up to three times the source band. Single-precision stepper only (a double stepper is a validation error).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; stepper precisions single only (see solvers); result none

Params:
- `n2` [m^2/W] (default 0) - Kerr index n2. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.n2`
- `tpa_beta` [m/W] (default 0; >= 0) - Two-photon absorption. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.tpa_beta`
- `carrier_lifetime` [s] (default 0; >= 0) - Carrier lifetime. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.carrier_lifetime`
- `fca_cross_section` [m^2] (default 0; >= 0) - Free-carrier absorption cross-section. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.fca_cross_section`
- `fcd_coefficient` [m^3] (default 0; >= 0) - Free-carrier index change. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.fcd_coefficient`
- `pump_wavelength` [m] (default 1.55e-06; > 0) - Pump wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.pump_wavelength`
- `d_eff` [m/V] (default 0) - Second-order coefficient d. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.d_eff`
- `poling` [1] (default 1; may use x, y) - Poling. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.poling`

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.gain_medium` - Gain medium

Four-level two-electron gain medium (Chang and Taflove, Opt. Express 12, 3827, 2004) on the selected cells, acting on the E_x and E_y faces separately (weight = face mean of the selected cells; each face set has its own populations): a Lorentz polarisation d2P/dt2 + gamma dP/dt + omega_a^2 P = kappa (N1 - N2) E, kappa = 6 pi eps0 c^3 / (omega_a^2 tau_21), coupled to the rate equations of populations N0..N3 (pump W_p N0 -> N3, decays N3 -> N2 -> N1 -> N0, stimulated transitions (E . dP/dt) / (hbar omega_a)); N2 > N1 amplifies, N1 > N2 absorbs. Overlapping regions are two species. Output field population_inversion = N2 - N1 (1/m^3). Not in absorbed power; not in the build Courant check (keep |delta eps| (omega_a dt)^2 / 4 << 1). Time_dependent study, Bloch k = 0 and single-precision stepper only (as nonlinear_medium).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; stepper precisions single only (see solvers); result none

Params:
- `wavelength` [m] (default 1.55e-06; > 0) - Transition wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength lambda_a of the lasing transition 2 -> 1 (omega_a = 2 pi c / lambda_a).
- `linewidth` [rad/s] (default 1e+14; >= 0) - Gain linewidth
  Full width gamma of the Lorentzian line (angular, not Hz; FWHM in wavelength ~ lambda_a^2 gamma / (2 pi c)); peak gain ~ 1 / gamma.
- `density` [1/m^3] (default 1e+24; > 0) - Active ion density. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.density`
- `pump_rate` [1/s] (default 0; >= 0) - Pump rate. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.pump_rate`
- `tau_32` [s] (default 1e-13; > 0) - Lifetime level 3 -> 2
  Non-radiative lifetime 3 -> 2; >= 10 time steps (explicit rate step; validation error).
- `tau_21` [s] (default 1e-09; > 0) - Lifetime level 2 -> 1
  Upper lasing level lifetime, also the radiative lifetime in kappa: longer = weaker coupling per atom but larger steady inversion; >= 10 time steps.
- `tau_10` [s] (default 1e-13; > 0) - Lifetime level 1 -> 0
  Lower lasing level lifetime into the ground state; >= 10 time steps.
- `initial_upper_fraction` [1] (default 0; [0, 1]) - Initial upper-level fraction
  Share of density in level 2 at t = 0 (rest in level 0): initial inversion fraction x density, for runs much shorter than tau_21.

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.phase_change_medium` - Phase-change medium

Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium`

Params:

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.field_probe` - Field probe

Time series of one field component in the cell containing the point, sampled after every time step (t in s, values in A/m or V/m); a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell.

- Category probe; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result kind `timeseries`

Params:
- `component` (default "hz"; hz | ex | ey) - Field component
  hz (A/m) at the centre of the cell containing the point, half a time step before the recorded time; ex / ey (V/m) on its +y / +x face (raw staggered samples, not averaged).

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.resonance_monitor` - Resonance finder

Help: shared `em_fdtd_bor.resonance_monitor`

- Category monitor; selection point entities, object kinds point, 1 to 16; stepper precisions single, double only (see solvers); result kind `table`

Params:
- `component` (default "hz"; hz | ex | ey) - Field component
  Recorded field: hz [A/m] at the centre of the cell containing the point (sampled half a step earlier, accounted for in the reference time), or ex / ey [V/m] on its +y / +x face.
- `wavelength_min` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength. Keep the band inside the source spectrum; narrower = faster, better conditioned fit.
- `wavelength_max` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_min.
- `start_time` [s] (>= 0; nullable) - Analysis start. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.resonance_monitor.start_time`

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

Spectral Poynting flux through an axis-aligned line: S_x = Re(E_y H_z*) (vertical line), S_y = -Re(E_x H_z*) (horizontal), > 0 toward +x / +y; E on the hi face of the line cells, H_z at their centres (time-centred, not interpolated in space). power in a.u. per unit z length, not normalised by the source spectrum: compare runs by ratios (transmission = device run / reference run with the same source); power_per_cw = power / (2 |S(omega)|^2) is the cw power in W/m. per_cw values need one waveform shared by every source feature (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives not counted); S = its dt-weighted spectrum over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 < 1e-6 of its source-wavelength value (cw: or |f - f0| >= 1 / (steps x dt)). They match em_fdfd_* at equal amplitudes, exactly at the source wavelength only. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

- Category monitor; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params:
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 100; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths
  Evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency); 1 = the range centre. 50-200 for a smooth spectrum; the work per time step grows with it.

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.mode_monitor` - Mode monitor

Port monitor splitting the field on an axis-aligned line into the forward (positive: toward +x / +y) and backward (negative) amplitudes a of one guided mode per monitor wavelength: running DFTs of H_z in the line cells and of E_y (vertical line) / E_x (horizontal line) on their hi face are projected on the mode solved at that wavelength, so each direction is measured separately, unlike a flux_monitor. The 1D line eigenmodes are FDTD-consistent (Yee dispersion, PML stretch, complex line-cell eps / mu), solved at build and re-solved during the run (following the mode by overlap) whenever the line materials drift by > 1e-3 relative (thermo-optic, Pockels, state-dependent eps); a mode monitor then decomposes its whole-run spectra with the latest modes (run log note), valid only for light passing after the medium settled. Put the line across a straight guide, same cross-section a few cells either side, locally uniform mesh (validation refuses a line whose face is on the outer grid wall and warns when a wall pins the line cell or its face, when its face lies in a CPML layer, or when the normal cell widths change by > 1% around it). Span ends: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML (open); an end on a pec or antisymmetric domain edge takes tangential E = 0 on the inner face of the outermost cell (dH_z/dn = 0), one on a pmc edge H_z = 0 and one on a symmetric edge H_z odd; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E along the propagation direction = 0 on the face beyond the end, so dH_z/dn = 0), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns above 1% of the mode peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The in-plane E faces use the permittivity the engine uses (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells), so a guide edge on a face line takes the core / cladding mean. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) (an end exactly on a cell edge adds a cell). Result 'xy' versus wavelength: power_positive / power_negative = 2 |a|^2 in a.u. (flux_monitor convention, comparable with its power); power_per_cw_positive / _negative = |a|^2 / |S|^2 in W/m (cw mode power, as em_fdfd_* power_*); with exactly one enabled mode_source in the physics also fraction_positive / _negative = mode power / source power (transmission into this mode downstream of the source, reflection upstream; NaN as for per_cw) and phase_positive / _negative (rad) = the phase of that S-parameter relative to the amplitude the source launches on its own line, not de-embedded (each profile phased with its largest sample real and positive, the lowest-coordinate one of mirror-equal peaks); extras frequency, wavelength, n_eff, n_eff_imag (per wavelength), mode_number, tracked_mode_number (rank of the followed mode at the middle wavelength in the latest solve), normalized (fractions present). Run until the pulse has passed every monitor; the fractions inherit the source leakage, most accurate near its wavelength. per_cw values need one waveform shared by every source feature (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives not counted); S = its dt-weighted spectrum over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 < 1e-6 of its source-wavelength value (cw: or |f - f0| >= 1 / (steps x dt)). They match em_fdfd_* at equal amplitudes, exactly at the source wavelength only.

- Category monitor; selection line entities, object kinds line, exactly 1; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Mode number. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor.mode_number`
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 21; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor.n_wavelengths`

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.dft_monitor` - Field map monitor

Running DFT of H_z, E_x and E_y over a rectangle (exp(-i omega t) at the actual sample times, H_z half a step earlier; E_x / E_y averaged onto the cell centres): intensity = |E_x(omega)|^2 + |E_y(omega)|^2 and hz_intensity = |H_z(omega)|^2 per wavelength (one per freq_index) in a.u., not normalised by the source spectrum; intensity x intensity_per_cw_factor[freq_index] (1 / |S(omega)|^2) is the cw |E|^2 in (V/m)^2. per_cw values need one waveform shared by every source feature (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives not counted); S = its dt-weighted spectrum over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 < 1e-6 of its source-wavelength value (cw: or |f - f0| >= 1 / (steps x dt)). They match em_fdfd_* at equal amplitudes, exactly at the source wavelength only. The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis (an edge exactly on a cell edge adds a cell).

- Category monitor; selection domain entities, object kinds rectangle, exactly 1; result kind `dft_fields`

Params:
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 8e-07; > 0) - Longest wavelength
  > wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 5; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths
  Evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency); 1 = the range centre. GPU memory 6 * n_wavelengths * box cells * 4 B / downsample^2 (H_z, E_x, E_y; 1000 x 1000 cells at 10 wavelengths: 240 MB; validation warns above 1 GiB), and each wavelength adds work per step; 1-21 typical.
- `downsample` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Record every n-th cell. Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.dft_monitor.downsample`

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.far_field` - Far-field pattern

Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.far_field`

- Category monitor; selection domain entities, object kinds rectangle, exactly 1; result kind `far_field`

Params:
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 4e-07; > 0) - Shortest wavelength. Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
