## Physics type `em_modes` - Electromagnetic Waves, cross-section modes

Full-vector finite-difference eigenmodes of a waveguide cross-section: xy is the cross-section (x right, y up), the guide runs along z; fields ~ exp(j (omega t - beta z)), n_eff = beta / k0, so lossy / leaky modes have Im n_eff < 0. Projected 3D Yee cell (transverse-H formulation, Fallahkhair, Li and Murphy, JLT 2008): E_z at cell centres, E_x, H_y on +x faces, E_y, H_x on +y faces, H_z at the +x+y corner; eps_zz (array eps_r) the cell value, eps_xx / eps_yy on faces the width-weighted mean of the two cells, mu the cell value (solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing at interfaces: E_x / E_y faces 1 / (n^2 <1/eps> + (1 - n^2) / <eps>), n the in-plane normal component, E_z cells the area mean <eps>); all complex at the solve wavelength. A h = beta^2 B h for h = eta0 (H_x, H_y), shift-invert Arnoldi around (k0 n_eff_guess)^2 on the host (scipy; 2 unknowns per cell incl. PML; validation warns near and refuses beyond the factor size limit). Role 'eigen' arpack_shift_invert (tolerance, subspace_size, factorization: superlu; cudss = GPU LU without size limit, guarded by free device memory; mumps / mumps_mixed / pardiso / pardiso_mixed = host MUMPS / PARDISO under the size limit; _mixed factorizations only on triangles: this operator is not complex symmetric). Role 'shifted': Automatic = that SuperLU factor; line_block factors the shift-invert operators on its backend (grid rows or columns, a periodic axis inside the blocks, two periodic axes an error; mixed or double, refined against complex128), batching the omega and group_index omega (1 +- 1e-3) operators and frequency_domain wavelengths, up to 8 per batch within 60 % of free memory; a rejected solve is redone on SuperLU (run-log warning); shg_overlap / bend_overlap stay SuperLU. Modes are dropped (> half their |H|^2 in PML) and ranked as n_modes. Each carries 1 W, P = 1/2 Re int (E x H*).z dA, phased so its dominant transverse E is real positive at its peak (the lowest-index cell of mirror-equal peaks). Degenerate pairs (HE11 of a round fibre, TE11 / TM11 of a metal pipe) come back as arbitrary, not necessarily orthogonal, combinations. Outputs (the displayed mode = mode_number setting, at cell centres, face / corner components averaged): components = real parts, sz = 1/2 Re(E_x H_y* - E_y H_x*) (power flow along z; its window integral equals 1 W only to discretisation order and misses any PML share); state fields e_intensity and sz. No absorbed power: not an em_heat_joule source. Studies: mode_analysis (one solve at the wavelength setting after any background heat / current solve, one snapshot per mode), frequency_domain (one solve per wavelength). heat_em_thermo_optic rewrites eps_zz, eps_xx, eps_yy. xy is a cross-section, so em_modes cannot share a model with em_fdtd_* / em_fdfd_* (validation error), except em_fdfd_ez / _hz as the k_z = 0 illumination in a thermal_noise study. Triangles mesh: finite elements of the discretization setting (Lee-Sun-Cendes mixed form, complex symmetric with PML / loss), one material value per element, a structured PML ring, the same outputs on a display raster (state fields per element) and the same table / dispersion results; refusals under discretization. Instance usually 'modes'.

- Default instance name `modes`; studies mode_analysis, frequency_domain, thermal_noise, optomechanics (default {"type": "mode_analysis"})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields e_intensity; dispersion poles used
- Features: mode_table, mode_dispersion, shg_overlap, bend_overlap, pec_domain

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (default "cpml"; cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  cpml: pml_cells absorbing cells outside the face. Mode-solve CPML: stretch s = kappa + sigma / (alpha + j omega eps0), pml_* grading; a mode tail reaching it gains a small artificial loss (Im n_eff, see pml_fraction); modes with > half their |H|^2 in PML cells are dropped. periodic: on both faces of the axis; period = the meshed window (uniform mesh: rounded up to whole cells); k = 0 (normal incidence) unless the type has bloch_kx / bloch_ky (em_fdfd_nonlinear: per harmonic_channel). Walls and mirrors sit on the inner face of the outermost cell (a ghost: each component centred along that axis takes -1 (pec, antisymmetric) or +1 (pmc, symmetric) times its inner neighbour; components on the plane free (pec) or 0 (pmc)): half a cell off the em_fdtd_ez pec / em_fdtd_hz pmc walls, so a guide between two pec walls of an n-cell domain is n - 2 cells wide. Mirrors add their ghost outside the domain (plane = domain edge): symmetric = E even (PMC plane), antisymmetric = E odd (PEC plane). A mirror through a symmetric guide halves the unknowns and keeps one parity: on x_lo, antisymmetric keeps E_x even (quasi-TE, e.g. TE0 of a strip), symmetric E_y even (quasi-TM).
- `pml_cells` [cells] (int; default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` [1] (default 1; > 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` [1] (default 15; >= 1; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real CPML stretch (1 = none); larger damps evanescent and grazing waves; 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0; visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping. Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `wavelength` [m] (default 1.55e-06; > 0) - Wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength of a mode_analysis solve (k0 = 2 pi / lambda0); materials enter at that omega (sigma_e and poles as complex eps). frequency_domain solves its own wavelengths instead (validation info when this is not the default; n_eff versus wavelength: mode_dispersion). Mesh: >= 10 (better 20) cells per lambda0 / |n| and, in metals, >= 2 (better 4) per skin depth lambda0 / (2 pi |Im n|) (validation checks both); a 220 nm silicon core needs ~20 nm cells (or refinement) for n_eff to ~1e-2. Typical 1.31e-6 or 1.55e-6 m.
- `n_modes` (int; default 4; [1, 100]) - Number of modes
  Modes kept per solve: the eigen-solve finds the 2 n_modes + 10 beta^2 nearest the target (k0 n_eff_guess)^2 (n_modes + 4 on a lossless cross-section without bend or n_eff_guess, back to 2 n_modes + 10 when PML modes leave too few), drops PML modes (> half their |H|^2 in PML), ranks by descending Re(beta^2), ties by descending Im (= descending Re n_eff for low-loss guided modes; evanescent modes last) and keeps up to n_modes (fewer near cutoff or when most candidates are PML modes). 2-10 typical.
- `n_eff_guess` [1] (> 0; nullable) - Effective index guess
  Shift-invert target sigma = (k0 n_eff_guess)^2: the modes with n_eff^2 nearest it. Empty: the largest Re sqrt(eps mu) over non-PEC cells and all three components at the solve wavelength (before any bend map): the most strongly guided modes. Lower it for higher-order modes; set it near the expected value for a surface plasmon or a mode far below the core index.
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Displayed mode
  Rank (see n_modes) of the mode shown after the study: Results.field and the GUI view, state fields e_intensity / sz, selected = True in mode_table. frequency_domain shows that rank at every wavelength (no tracking; mode_dispersion follows by overlap). > n_modes is a validation error; when fewer modes are found the last one is shown (run-log warning).
- `group_index` (bool; default false) - Compute group index
  Group index n_g = C0 d(Re beta) / d(omega) of every mode by a central difference in omega (relative step 1e-3), materials re-evaluated (pole chi and sigma_e: material dispersion included; plain eps_r has none). Tensor meshes: two more eigen-solves per wavelength, modes followed by overlap (~3x the time); triangles: first-order perturbation of the pencil, two more assemblies. Off: n_group NaN.
- `bend_radius` [m] (default 0) - Bend radius
  Signed radius R of a guide bent in the xz plane (0 = straight), around the y axis (rings in the chip plane, y vertical). R > 0: centre of curvature at x_ref - R (outer side +x); R < 0: at x_ref + |R| (outer side -x); x_ref = bend_reference_x; radius r = |R| s, s = 1 + (x - x_ref) / R. n_eff refers to the radius at x_ref: angular propagation constant (ring azimuthal order) nu = beta R = k0 n_eff R. Bend radiation toward the outer side shows as Im n_eff < 0 / loss_db_per_cm: keep a cpml face and cladding there (validation warns otherwise) and set pml_kappa_max 1 (the default 15 reflects grazing radiation). s > 0 over the whole grid incl. PML and a non-periodic x axis are required (validation errors). Typical 5e-6 to 1e-4 m.
- `bend_reference_x` [m] (nullable) - Bend reference x
  x (physical frame) where s = 1: the radius n_eff refers to, usually the guide centre. Empty: size_x / 2. Unused when bend_radius = 0.
- `bend_model` (default "exact"; exact | conformal) - Bend model
  Unused when bend_radius = 0. 'exact': the bend written as a straight guide in (x, y, R phi): eps diag(s, s, 1/s), mu diag(s, s, 1/s), so the true bend mode to discretisation order while the centre of curvature lies outside the grid; E_x, E_y, H_x, H_y are the physical E_r, E_y, H_r, H_y, E_z, H_z = s x the physical E_phi, H_phi; power and overlaps use the straight formulas. 'conformal': the approximate bend-loss map, every eps component times s^2, mu untouched: error second order in w / R (w = mode width; e.g. -5e-4 relative in n_eff for a 50 um metal-rimmed ring at 1.55 um).
- `discretization` (default "quadratic"; quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Element order on a triangles mesh (tensor meshes use the Yee cross-section). quadratic (industry standard): second-order Nedelec for E_x, E_y, P2 Lagrange for E_z (Lee-Sun-Cendes mixed form, no spurious modes), curved edges isoparametric, so circles and ellipses follow the mesh; linear: Whitney / P1 on straight elements, cheaper, error ~h^2 instead of ~h^4 in beta^2. ~7 (quadratic) or 2 (linear) unknowns per element; shift-invert by the eigen solver (host SuperLU; factorization cudss: GPU LDL^T of the complex symmetric pencil; mumps / mumps_mixed / pardiso / pardiso_mixed: host MUMPS / PARDISO LDL^T; _mixed: complex64 with one float64 refinement per solve, ARPACK to 1e-6, beta^2 from float64 Rayleigh quotients, error ~ the square of the vector error). Materials one value per element (at its centroid). pec / antisymmetric faces fix tangential E on the window edge, pmc / symmetric are natural (mirror plane = window edge, no ghost); a cpml face gets mesh pml_layers structured element layers, pml_cells x the maximum element size thick, pml_* stretch, pec outer side (pml_kappa_max 1 suits leaky modes, the default 15 evanescent tails); pec_domain removes its elements (E = 0 on their outline). On triangles periodic faces, bend_radius, shg_overlap, bend_overlap, a line_block shifted solver and thermal_noise / optomechanics studies are validation errors; no subpixel smoothing or conformal boundaries.
- `bloch_kx` [rad/m] (default 0; visible when bc_x_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector x. Help: shared `em_modes.bloch_kx`
- `bloch_ky` [rad/m] (default 0; visible when bc_y_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector y. Help: shared `em_modes.bloch_kx`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1; writes eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic: eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_zz unless the material sets a component (it wins). n^2 of a lossless dielectric: silica ~2.085, silicon ~12.1 at 1.55 um. E_z sees the cell value, E_x / E_y on the +x / +y cell faces the width-weighted mean of the two cells sharing that face (solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages interface faces anisotropically). Solved with the complex value at the solve wavelength: this - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) + chi(omega) of every Drude / Lorentz pole (exp(+j omega t): loss Im < 0, giving Im n_eff < 0). For a dispersive material it is the background eps_inf (an explicit permittivity wins over the Drude eps_inf). A state-dependent value (e.g. of T) is rewritten once after the background solve, before the mode solve.
- `eps_zz` [1] (default 1; >= 1; writes eps_r) - Relative permittivity, z (along the guide)
  Component along the guide, the one E_z sees at the cell centres; overrides eps_r for E_z. Uniaxial, optic axis along the guide: eps_zz = n_e^2, eps_r = n_o^2.
- `eps_xx` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, x
  The one E_x sees on the +x cell faces (face mean as eps_r); overrides eps_r for E_x. E.g. x-cut lithium niobate at 1.55 um: eps_xx 4.571 = n_e^2, eps_r 4.889 = n_o^2.
- `eps_yy` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permittivity, y
  The one E_y sees on the +y cell faces (face mean as eps_r); overrides eps_r for E_y. Optic axis along y: eps_yy = n_e^2.
- `sigma_e` [S/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Electric conductivity
  All three E components gain -j sigma_e / (omega eps0): Im n_eff < 0, loss_db_per_cm > 0. Weak absorber of index n, extinction kappa: sigma_e = 2 n kappa omega eps0; metals: a Drude pole, not their DC conductivity.
- `mu_r` [1] (default 1; >= 1) - Relative permeability. Help: shared `em_fdfd_conical.mu_r`
- `sigma_m` [Ohm/m] (default 0; >= 0) - Magnetic conductivity
  mu_r gains -j sigma_m / (omega mu0) on H_x, H_y, H_z (artificial absorbers only).
- `gyration_x` [1] (default 0; no fields) - Gyration, x (magneto-optic)
  Gyration g_x of a material magnetised along x (across the guide): eps_ij += j e_ijk g_k (exp(+j omega t)), so eps_yz = -eps_zy = j g_x, eps_zx = -eps_xz = j g_y; Hermitian for real g, sign flips with the magnetisation. Not in the mode solve: each mode gets the first-order non-reciprocal shift delta_beta = beta_forward - beta_backward = -(omega eps0 / P) integral [g_x Im(conj(E_y) E_z) + g_y Im(conj(E_z) E_x)] dA (Mizumoto / Shintaku; P = 1 W, mode toward +z): scalar output delta_beta_<k>, mode_table column delta_beta; error ~g^2 relative (the ~g^2 n_eff change is not computed). E_y couples to E_z, so g_x shifts quasi-TM modes (E along y), and only where the guide is not mirror symmetric across y (magneto-optic cladding on one side, or opposite magnetisations: push-pull). L_pi = pi / |delta_beta|. Ce:YIG at 1550 nm (library ce_yig, n ~ 2.2): |g| ~ 0.009 (g = theta_F lambda n / pi, theta_F ~ -4500 deg/cm); the sign is the material's. Never subpixel-smoothed (cell-centre staircase): put magneto-optic interfaces on cell edges. The same guide drawn in plane for em_fdfd_hz: (x, y, z) here = (z, y, -x) there, so gyration_x = -gyration_z. Allocated only when a material sets it. Validation errors: a y_lo / y_hi mirror face (its image reverses the magnetisation), a bend, a triangles mesh, any other EM type (em_fdfd_hz takes gyration_z).
- `gyration_y` [1] (default 0; no fields) - Gyration, y (magneto-optic)
  Gyration g_y of a material magnetised along y: as gyration_x with x and y swapped: E_x couples to E_z, so it shifts quasi-TE modes (E along x) where the guide is not mirror symmetric across x; an x_lo / x_hi mirror face is a validation error.

### Fields

Output fields (primary e_intensity; [state] = also a state field):
- `ex` - Re E_x (V/m)
- `ey` - Re E_y (V/m)
- `ez` - Re E_z (V/m)
- `hx` - Re H_x (A/m)
- `hy` - Re H_y (A/m)
- `hz` - Re H_z (A/m)
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2) [state]
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `sz` - S_z (power flow along z) (W/m^2) [state]
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity zz (1) [state]
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity xx (1) [state]
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity yy (1) [state]
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m) [state]

Scalar outputs: n_eff_<k>, k = 1 .. n_modes (unit 1): Re n_eff of mode k of the last solve, ranked as mode_table (frequency_domain: the last wavelength); a mode not found gives NaN plus a run-log warning. Example derived value {"name": "n_eff_te0", "expression": "modes_n_eff_1"} (operation mean of a constant = the value); per sweep value in a parameter sweep. delta_beta_<k> (1/m): beta_forward - beta_backward of mode k from gyration_x / gyration_y (0 without them; NaN for an evanescent mode); L_pi = pi / |delta_beta_<k>|.

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array (PML ring included); index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_modes.mode_table` - Mode table

Modes of the last solve (frequency_domain: the last wavelength). Result 'table', one row per mode, ranked as n_modes: mode_number, n_eff (Re beta / k0), n_eff_imag (< 0 = loss; exp(+j omega t), exp(-j beta z)), loss_db_per_cm = -20 log10(e) Im(beta) / 100 (> 0 for lossy or leaky modes), n_group (C0 d(Re beta) / d(omega); NaN unless group_index or when the mode was not followed to the shifted frequencies, run-log warning), te_fraction = int |E_x|^2 dA / int (|E_x|^2 + |E_y|^2) dA (1 = E along x, e.g. quasi-TE of a strip on a substrate parallel to xz), effective_area = (int |E|^2 dA)^2 / int |E|^4 dA [m^2] (all three components at the cell centres, nonlinear-optics definition; whole mode incl. mirror images, as the 1 W normalisation), pml_fraction (share of the |H|^2 in PML cells: kept modes < 0.5; above ~1e-2 the PML shapes the mode: widen the cladding), delta_beta (beta_forward - beta_backward [1/m] of gyration_x / gyration_y materials; 0 without them), selected (the mode_number setting); extras wavelength [m], selected_mode. n_eff in a sweep: scalar output <physics>_n_eff_<k>; any other column: derived value source '<physics>.<this feature>', expression = column name, operation at, at = mode_number - 1 (row index).

- Category monitor; selection none (a selection is ignored with a warning); mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result kind `table`

Params: none

### Feature `em_modes.mode_dispersion` - Mode dispersion

Scalars of one mode versus vacuum wavelength. Result 'xy' (x = wavelength [m], ascending; one point per solved wavelength, a mode_analysis study gives one; a re-solved wavelength keeps its latest), series = the mode_table scalar columns (n_eff, n_eff_imag, loss_db_per_cm, n_group, te_fraction, effective_area, pml_fraction, delta_beta) and overlap (|overlap| with the mode followed at the previous solve, 1 at the first; well below 1 = the mode changed character or crossed another); extras frequency [Hz], wavelength [m], mode_number. The first solve finding mode_number modes picks that rank; later solves follow the largest overlap, keeping identity where modes swap order (solve order: the frequency_domain wavelengths list, else wavelength_start to wavelength_stop). NaN rows while the mode is not found.

- Category monitor; selection none (a selection is ignored with a warning); mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Mode number
  Rank (as mode_table) of the followed mode at the first solve that finds that many modes; later solves follow it by overlap.

### Feature `em_modes.shg_overlap` - Second-harmonic overlap

Coupled-mode second-harmonic generation of a 3D waveguide from its cross-section modes. Result 'xy' versus pump vacuum wavelength [m] (one point per solve): after every em_modes solve at omega it solves the 2 omega modes (same materials, walls, bend and eigen solver: ~2x the time) and pairs rank pump_mode (omega) with rank harmonic_mode (2 omega), no tracking. Series: n_eff_pump, n_eff_harmonic, delta_beta = Re beta(2 omega) - 2 Re beta(omega) [1/m], coherence_length = pi / |delta_beta| and poling_period = 2 pi / |delta_beta| [m] (NaN at delta_beta = 0), overlap = |kappa| [V^2/W^1.5], kappa = int conj(e_2w) . (d : e_w e_w) dA over the selected domains (1 W modes, cell-centre fields), efficiency = (omega eps0 / 2)^2 |kappa|^2 [%/(W cm^2)] (P_2w = efficiency P_w^2 L^2 phase matched, times sinc^2(delta_beta L / 2) otherwise; a plane-wave mode of area A gives 8 pi^2 d^2 / (eps0 c n_w^2 n_2w lambda^2 A)), efficiency_qpm = (2 / pi)^2 efficiency (first-order QPM, 50 % duty). Convention: exp(j (omega t - beta z)), P(2 omega)_i = eps0 sum_jk d_ijk E_j E_k, d = chi2 / 2 as Voigt d_il in MODEL axes (x, y cross-section, z along the guide): rotate crystal values yourself, e.g. x-cut lithium niobate, c axis along x, TE modes: d11 = d33(LN) ~ 2.5e-11 m/V, d12 = d13 = d31(LN) ~ -4.6e-12 m/V. The mesh must resolve the 2 omega modes (>= 10 cells per lambda / (2 n)); mirror faces and Bloch k != 0 are validation errors (the integrand has no single parity); loss enters only through Re beta. Bend: kappa is the physical overlap per arc length at bend_reference_x (where delta_beta and L are measured): exact integrates s dA with E_phi = E_z / s, conformal s^2 dA with the fields taken as physical (exact for E along y). ring_crystal local: d in the local frame (x radial, y vertical, z along the guide), turning with the guide: right for terms invariant under rotations about y (d33, d31, d15 of a z-cut crystal, c axis along y). ring_crystal fixed (bend only; x- or y-cut ring): d given at the reference cross-section (phi = 0), crystal fixed while the guide turns about y: local d(phi) = Q(phi) Q Q : d, Q rows (cos phi, 0, sin phi), (0, 1, 0), (-sin phi, 0, cos phi), phi = z / R (signed R, z the arc at x_ref); kappa(phi) = sum_m=-3..3 kappa_m exp(j m phi) (exact from 8 azimuths), order m phase matched when delta_beta R + m = 0. Extra series: azimuthal_mismatch = delta_beta R [1] (nu_2w - 2 nu_w), ring_order m* = round(-delta_beta R) (NaN when |m*| > 3), ring_mismatch = delta_beta + m* / R [1/m], ring_overlap = |kappa_m*|, ring_efficiency = (omega eps0 / 2)^2 |kappa_m*|^2 [%/(W cm^2)] (0 when |m*| > 3; P_2w = ring_efficiency P_w^2 L^2 sinc^2(ring_mismatch L / 2) over an arc L), ring_overlap_minus3 .. ring_overlap_plus3 = |kappa_m| [V^2/W^1.5]; overlap / efficiency stay those at phi = 0. E.g. x-cut LN, TE: kappa(phi) ~ cos^3 phi: orders +-1 (3/8) and +-3 (1/8) of kappa(0).

- Category monitor; selection domain entities, at least 1; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `pump_mode` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Pump mode
  Rank (as mode_table) of the pump mode of each em_modes solve; must not exceed n_modes.
- `harmonic_mode` (int; default 1; >= 1) - Second-harmonic mode
  Rank of the 2 omega mode among the n_harmonic_modes; must not exceed n_harmonic_modes.
- `n_harmonic_modes` (int; default 4; [1, 100]) - Modes at the second harmonic
  Modes kept by the 2 omega solve (as n_modes).
- `harmonic_n_eff_guess` [1] (> 0; nullable) - Second-harmonic index guess
  n_eff_guess of the 2 omega solve; empty = the largest index of the cross-section at 2 omega.
- `ring_crystal` (default "local"; local | fixed) - Crystal around the ring
  'local': d_il in the guide's local frame everywhere. 'fixed' (bent guides only, validation error otherwise): d_il at the reference cross-section, crystal fixed while the guide turns, so phase matching picks an azimuthal order m = -3..3 (ring_* series; see the feature).
- `d11`, `d12`, `d13`, `d14`, `d15`, `d16`, `d21`, `d22`, `d23`, `d24`, `d25`, `d26`, `d31`, `d32`, `d33`, `d34`, `d35`, `d36` [m/V] (default 0) - d11 / d12 / d13 / d14 / d15 / d16 / d21 / d22 / d23 / d24 / d25 / d26 / d31 / d32 / d33 / d34 / d35 / d36
  Voigt d_il in model axes: i = polarisation component, l = field pair (1, 2, 3 = x, y, z; 4 yz, 5 xz, 6 xy); 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.

### Feature `em_modes.bend_overlap` - Straight-to-bend overlap

Straight-to-bend junction of a bent guide (bend_radius != 0, validation error otherwise). Result 'table' of the last solve (frequency_domain: the last wavelength): after every em_modes solve it solves the same cross-section straight (same materials, walls, eigen solver; n_straight_modes near straight_n_eff_guess) and pairs each bent mode with the straight mode of largest power coupling overlap = |c_bs c_sb| / |c_bb c_ss|, c_ab = 1/2 int (E_a x H_b*).z dA (bent transverse fields = the physical E_r, E_y, H_r, H_y in both bend models). Columns: mode_number (bent rank), n_eff, n_eff_imag (bent, referred to bend_reference_x), straight_mode, n_eff_straight, overlap (1 = perfect), junction_loss_db = -10 log10(overlap) (one junction, ~1 / R^2 for large R; a ring coupler or S-bend has two per transition), overlap_same_rank (straight mode of the same rank, NaN when fewer found); extras wavelength [m], n_straight_found. The junction is centred: the outward shift of the bent mode (compensable by a lateral offset) counts as loss.

- Category monitor; selection none (a selection is ignored with a warning); result kind `table`

Params:
- `n_straight_modes` (int; default 4; [1, 100]) - Straight modes
  Modes kept by the straight solve (as n_modes).
- `straight_n_eff_guess` [1] (> 0; nullable) - Straight index guess
  n_eff_guess of the straight solve; empty = the largest index of the cross-section.

### Feature `em_modes.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

E_z = 0 in cells whose centre lies in the domains, E_x / E_y = 0 on faces between two such cells (eps^-1 = 0), staircased. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (Dey-Mittra on the projected Yee cell) the drawn outline instead: E_z = 0 at the bisected wall distance along each centre link into the metal, H_z takes the free lengths of its E_x / E_y edges over the free dual-cell area (free fractions >= 0.02); links and dual cells crossing a pec / pmc / mirror wall plane stay staircased. Triangles: elements whose centroid lies in the domains leave the unknowns, tangential E and E_z = 0 on their outline (curved outlines isoparametric with quadratic).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result none

Params: none

## Physics type `heat` - Heat Transfer in Solids

Anisotropic heat conduction, finite volumes on the rise T - T0, 2D per unit z length or 3D (7-point stencil with k_zz; boundary features on outer faces only, no k_xy, no out_of_plane_convection): steady state or implicit-Euler transient (time_mode), on the physical window (T edge-extended into an EM PML ring). Unreferenced outer faces are insulated (a later boundary feature on a face wins). A steady solve needs an anchor: a temperature, h > 0 convection, radiation, a fixed-temperature domain or out-of-plane convection. With EM in a time-dependent study set every to a few hundred EM steps (validation warns below 100). Triangle meshes (planar or axisymmetric): elements of the discretization order on the conducting window elements; object perimeters are outline edges (heat_flux heats both sides), a point is its mesh node, T nodal; no azimuthal_order, noise features or thermal_noise study. Tetrahedra (3D): the same with interface faces; fields sampled on the uniform mesh lattice (no field derived values yet); host SuperLU warns above ~1e5 P2 unknowns.

- Default instance name `heat`; studies stationary, time_dependent, thermal_noise (default {"type": "stationary"})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; refinement indicator fields T; dispersion poles not used
- Features: temperature, heat_flux, convection, radiation, symmetry, heat_source, point_heat_source, fixed_temperature_domain, out_of_plane_convection, initial_temperature, temperature_probe, thermorefractive_noise, particle_noise

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `time_mode` (default "stationary"; stationary | transient) - Time dependence
  stationary: a steady solve at every heat step (no heat capacity); transient: implicit Euler with rho*cp in steps <= time_step, in a time_dependent study only (every other study solves the steady state).
- `T0` [K] (default 293.15; > 0) - Reference temperature
  Initial temperature of every cell and reference of the thermo-optic change n = n0 + dndT (T - T0). Cells that neither conduct, lose heat nor (transient, rho and cp set) store heat keep T0 (or their initial temperature) and ignore heat sources.
- `time_step` [s] (default 0.001; > 0; visible when time_mode in (transient)) - Time step
  Largest implicit-Euler step (heat dt_limit). Heat alone steps by time_step (every must be 1); with EM each heat step is every * dt_EM <= time_step. Stable for any step but first order: keep it well below the diffusion time rho*cp*L^2/k of interest. T is at the end of the step just taken, so heat time labels and probe times run up to (every - 1) * dt_EM ahead of the snapshot time.
- `geometry` (default "planar"; planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  planar: 2D conduction per unit z length (W/m). axisymmetric (x = r, y = z; spec notes): (r, z) conduction, every conductance, face and cell volume (and object-perimeter heat_flux / convection) weighted by 2 pi r (pi r for azimuthal_order m != 0): densities keep their units, point_heat_source P is the ring's total power in W and the 'integral' of Q the body's total power in W; k_xy is a validation error. x_lo is the axis (any feature there does nothing; validation warns).
- `azimuthal_order` (int; default 0; >= 0; visible when geometry in (axisymmetric)) - Azimuthal order. Help: shared `electric_currents.azimuthal_order`
- `discretization` (default "quadratic"; quadratic | linear) - Discretization. Help: shared `electric_currents.discretization`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `k` [W/(m K)] (>= 0; nullable; writes k_xx, k_yy, k_zz) - Thermal conductivity
  Sets k_xx, k_yy and k_zz (component entries override it; k_zz acts only in 3D); unset (no library value) = 0: no conduction. E.g. k_300*(300/T)**1.3 (a stationary study iterates). Silica 1.38, silicon 130, aluminium 237, gold 317, silver 429, water 0.6.
- `k_xx`, `k_yy` [W/(m K)] (>= 0; nullable) - Thermal conductivity along x / Thermal conductivity along y
  Overrides k for this axis.
- `k_zz` [W/(m K)] (>= 0; nullable) - Thermal conductivity along z
  Overrides k for this axis (3D only; 2D has no z conduction).
- `k_xy` [W/(m K)] (nullable) - Thermal conductivity, cross term
  Off-diagonal k (cross conduction of a rotated anisotropic crystal); 2D Cartesian planar only. Keep k_xy^2 < k_xx k_yy (validation error for plain numbers; on strongly graded cells clearly below: the discrete operator is positive below it times 4 r / (1 + r)^2 per axis, r = neighbour width ratio, 0.99 at r = 1.2). Cross heat flows only inside 2x2 cell blocks that all conduct, never through outer faces; heat_flux_abs includes it.
- `rho` [kg/m^3] (>= 0; nullable) - Density
  Transient heat only (capacity rho*cp). Unset = 0: no capacity, so those cells are quasi-static (conducting ones follow their neighbours, others keep their temperature and ignore heat sources; validation warns). Silica 2200, silicon 2329, water 998.
- `cp` [J/(kg K)] (>= 0; nullable) - Specific heat capacity
  Transient heat only; unset = 0 (see rho). Silica 746, silicon 700, water 4182.
- `dndT` [1/K] (nullable; writes dndT_xx, dndT_yy, dndT_zz) - Thermo-optic coefficient
  dn/dT: sets dndT_xx, dndT_yy and dndT_zz (component entries override it), read by heat_em_thermo_optic (n = n0 + dndT (T - T0)). Use the measured dn/dT of the free material (it contains the density change of expansion; alpha adds only the growth of the structure). Dispersive materials: shifts only the background permittivity. Silica 1e-5, silicon 1.8e-4, water -9e-5.
- `dndT_xx` [1/K] (nullable) - Thermo-optic coefficient along x
  Overrides dndT for n_xx (eps_xx of em_fdtd_hz, em_fdfd_hz, em_modes).
- `dndT_yy` [1/K] (nullable) - Thermo-optic coefficient along y
  Overrides dndT for n_yy (eps_yy of em_fdtd_hz, em_fdfd_hz, em_modes).
- `dndT_zz` [1/K] (nullable) - Thermo-optic coefficient along z
  Overrides dndT for n_zz, the out-of-plane index E_z sees (eps_zz of em_fdtd_ez, em_fdfd_ez, em_modes). Without dndT and dndT_zz it is 0: E_z types see no change even with dndT_xx / dndT_yy set. z-cut lithium niobate (dn_e/dT) 3.3e-5.
- `alpha` [1/K] (nullable; writes alpha_xx, alpha_yy) - Thermal expansion coefficient
  Linear expansion: sets alpha_xx and alpha_yy (and alpha_zz with a solid_mechanics / solid_mechanics_3d physics: thermal strain via heat_solid_thermal_strain). heat_em_thermo_optic scales eps by (1 + alpha_xx dT)(1 + alpha_yy dT), the in-plane growth on the fixed grid, first order per cell (dropped when solid_em_strain_optic maps the solid strain). A film clamped to a substrate grows with the substrate: override the free-crystal library value (LN on Si 2.6e-6, not 1.5e-5). Leave 0 for liquids. Silica 5.5e-7, silicon 2.6e-6, gold 1.4e-5.
- `alpha_xx`, `alpha_yy` [1/K] (nullable) - Thermal expansion along x / Thermal expansion along y
  Overrides alpha for this axis.

### Fields

Output fields (primary T; [state] = also a state field):
- `T` - Temperature (K) [state]
- `T_rise` - Temperature rise (K)
- `Q` - Coupled heat source (W/m^3) [state]
- `Q_ext` - Applied heat source (W/m^3) [state]
- `heat_flux_abs` - Conductive heat flux magnitude (W/m^2)
State fields that are no output field:
- `k_xx` - Thermal conductivity xx (W/(m K))
- `k_yy` - Thermal conductivity yy (W/(m K))
- `k_zz` - Thermal conductivity zz (W/(m K))

### Source slots

- `volumetric_power` (W/m^3): Field Q: each transfer replaces it (PML ring ignored) with the sum of the heating couplings (em_heat_joule, currents_heat_joule, fluid_heat_convection).

### Feature `heat.temperature` - Temperature

Fixed temperature (Dirichlet): outer faces at the face (half-cell conductance 2 k / dx); on object perimeters the boundary cells inside the object are held, the value on their faces toward the free cells (the window edge is no perimeter: select the outer face; conformal_boundaries: on the drawn outline). On cells held by two features the later one wins; held cells ignore heat_flux / convection (validation warns on possible overlaps). Anchors a steady solve.

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, at least 1, outer faces and object perimeters; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result none

Params:
- `temperature` [K] (default 293.15; > 0; may use t) - Temperature
  Held on the selected outer faces or in the boundary cells inside the selected objects; follows reuse_build. A value of t: outer faces only (validation error for objects).

### Feature `heat.heat_flux` - Heat flux

Prescribed heat flux. Outer faces: a Neumann condition; object perimeters: flux * perimeter length / cell area into the boundary cells inside the object (true perimeter length to ~2 %; conformal_boundaries: per cut-cell chord of the drawn outline). Does not anchor a steady solve.

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, at least 1, outer faces and object perimeters; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result none

Params:
- `flux` [W/m^2] (default 10000; may use t) - Inward heat flux
  > 0 heats the domain or the object, < 0 extracts heat. Typical 1e3-1e6 (sunlight ~1e3).

### Feature `heat.convection` - Convective cooling

Convective loss h (T - T_ext) per area. Outer faces: a Robin condition in series with the half cell; object perimeters: the boundary cells inside the object lose h * perimeter length / cell area * (T - T_ext) (true perimeter length to ~2 %; conformal_boundaries: h L / (1 + h delta / k_n) per cut-cell chord L at distance delta). Anchors a steady solve when h > 0.

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, at least 1, outer faces and object perimeters; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result none

Params:
- `h` [W/(m^2 K)] (default 10; >= 0) - Heat transfer coefficient
  Loss h (T - T_ext) per area; h = 0 does not anchor a steady solve. Still air 5-25, forced air 10-200, water 500-10000.
- `T_ext` [K] (default 293.15; > 0) - Ambient temperature
  Temperature of the surrounding fluid.

### Feature `heat.radiation` - Surface-to-ambient radiation

Grey-body loss eps sigma (T^4 - T_amb^4) per area from the boundary cells of the selected outer faces and object perimeters (staircase weights, also under conformal_boundaries), at the boundary cell temperature (error ~ h_r dx / (2 k), h_r = 4 eps sigma T^3 ~ 5 W/(m^2 K) at 300 K). Adds to the face condition (with convection both act). Linearised: a steady solve re-solves until the radiating temperatures change by < 1e-7 relative (at most 50 solves, then a run warning), a transient step uses its start temperature. Anchors a steady solve when eps > 0. No view factors or surface-to-surface exchange.

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, at least 1, outer faces and object perimeters; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result none

Params:
- `emissivity` [1] (default 0.9; [0, 1]) - Surface emissivity
  Hemispherical grey-body eps: oxidised metals and most dielectrics 0.8-0.95, silicon ~0.6, polished metals 0.02-0.1.
- `T_amb` [K] (default 293.15; > 0) - Ambient temperature
  Temperature of the enclosing surroundings (e.g. vacuum chamber walls).

### Feature `heat.symmetry` - Symmetry

Even mirror plane on outer faces: the face stays insulated (the solve is unchanged) and becomes a model mirror plane: fields unfold T even across it (Results.field(unfold=True)), field derived integrals reaching it count twice, max / min include the image. A heat source on the plane is half the source of the unfolded model; a plane held at T_face is a temperature face instead. Errors: another heat face feature on the same face, the x_lo axis of geometry axisymmetric, a polar / spherical domain, an EM physics whose mirror bc is not symmetric / antisymmetric there, parity_sectors.

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, at least 1, outer faces only; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result none

Params: none

### Feature `heat.heat_source` - Heat source

Adds Q to Q_ext on the selected cells (sources add; the coupled slot Q is separate). A steady solve ignores it on cells that neither conduct nor lose heat.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result none

Params:
- `Q` [W/m^3] (default 1e+12; may use x, y, t) - Power density
  2D: Q times the area is the power per m of depth. Must be finite on the selected cells. x, y (3D: z) or t, not both; follows reuse_build.

### Feature `heat.point_heat_source` - Point heat source

P deposited in the cell containing each point (on a cell edge: the cell on its +x / +y side; triangles: the mesh node; tetrahedra: the exact point load). Points outside the physical domain are an error.

- Category source; selection point entities, object kinds point, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result none

Params:
- `P` [W/m, W axisymmetric, W 3d] (default 1; may use t) - Power
  Planar 2D: a line source along z, Q_ext += P / cell area in the cell containing the point; its temperature grows as the cell shrinks (logarithmic singularity). Axisymmetric: the ring's total power (on the axis cell a point source); 3D: a point source. 1D: per the 1D total (slab W/m^2 although the unit reads W/m; cylinder W/m; sphere W). Follows reuse_build.

### Feature `heat.fixed_temperature_domain` - Fixed temperature (domain)

Holds every selected cell at the temperature (heat flows in or out freely), the value on their faces toward the free cells (half-cell conductance 2 k / dx of the free neighbour, whatever the held cells' own k, so a k = 0 sink conducts; conformal_boundaries: on the drawn edge); heat_flux_abs reads 0 inside. Anchors a steady solve.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result none

Params:
- `temperature` [K] (default 293.15; > 0) - Temperature
  Held in every selected cell.

### Feature `heat.out_of_plane_convection` - Out-of-plane convection

Convective loss through the top / bottom faces of a thin slab (2D membrane or chip layer): volumetric loss h * sides / thickness * (T - T_ext) on the selected cells (also when axisymmetric). Anchors a steady solve when h > 0.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result none

Params:
- `h` [W/(m^2 K)] (default 10; >= 0) - Heat transfer coefficient
  Loss h (T - T_ext) per area; h = 0 does not anchor a steady solve. Still air 5-25, forced air 10-200, water 500-10000.
- `T_ext` [K] (default 293.15; > 0) - Ambient temperature
  Temperature of the surrounding fluid.
- `thickness` [m] (default 1e-06; > 0) - Layer thickness
  Out-of-plane (z) thickness of the slab; the loss scales as 1 / thickness.
- `sides` (int; default 2; [1, 2]) - Cooled sides
  Cooled slab faces: 1 (the other insulated) or 2 (top and bottom).

### Feature `heat.initial_temperature` - Initial temperature

Temperature of the selected cells at t = 0 for transient heat; a steady solve uses it only as the starting guess and for cells that neither conduct nor lose heat (validation info).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result none

Params:
- `temperature` [K] (default 293.15; > 0) - Temperature
  At t = 0; other cells start at T0.

### Feature `heat.temperature_probe` - Temperature probe

Temperature (K) of the cell containing the point after every heat solve: time_dependent every heat step; stationary and the frequency-domain background stage one per fixed-point iteration, all at t = 0.

- Category probe; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; result kind `timeseries`

Params: none

### Feature `heat.thermorefractive_noise` - Thermorefractive noise

One-sided PSD of X = integral w(x, y) g(z) exp(-j q0 z) dT dV over the selected cells (thermal_noise study only; elsewhere the result stays empty): S_X(f) = 4 k_B T0^2 integral dq/2pi |g~(q - q0)|^2 Re sum conj(w) u dA, (j 2 pi f rho cp + k_zz q^2 - div k grad) u = w on the heat window. Assumes uniform T0, a z-invariant cross-section and isobaric (entropy) fluctuations only (no pressure / Brillouin part; dndT the measured isobaric coefficient). Held cells and Dirichlet faces do not fluctuate; insulated faces act as mirrors. An em mirror face lies on the window edge (keep the heat face there insulated) and doubles the result. Every selected cell with w != 0 needs rho and cp > 0 (validation and run error). mode_pair: modes normalised to 1 W, so S is in (power fraction) / Hz and |X|^2 the scattered power per incident power; a heterodyne beat with local oscillator P_LO carries 4 P_LO P_in S. illumination: S in W/Hz, the scattered field as solved (static mean scattering excluded). expression: S in (w K m^3)^2 / Hz. Result xy over the study frequencies: series psd (all cells) and psd_db; with several materials also psd_<material> (self term; psd_other for cells in no material), psd_cross = psd - sum of the self terms (may be negative, integral 0) and psd_<material>_db (a colliding material name is a run error). Extra keys: variance (exact integral of psd: k_B T0^2 integral |w g|^2 / (rho cp) dV), contribution_variances (per material), static_variance (the never-relaxing q = 0 part of a region without temperature anchor, a delta at f = 0), band_fraction (share of variance - static_variance inside the solved band), axial_wavenumber,mirror_factor, axial_norm (integral |g|^2 dz [m]); mode_pair / illumination also wavelength, collected_mode, collected_n_eff, collected_te_fraction (and incident_mode). Cost: one host SuperLU of the window per frequency, axial sample and collected mode.

- Category monitor; selection domain entities, at least 1; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `weighting` (default "mode_pair"; mode_pair | illumination | expression) - Weighting
  mode_pair: X = amplitude scattered into collected_mode per incident amplitude (1 W modes of mode_physics, Lorentz reciprocity): w = omega eps0 / 4 sum_i 2 n_i dndT_i E_inc,i E_partner,i, the partner travelling against the collected direction (backward collection of a forward mode: |E_t|^2 - |E_z|^2; forward collection of the same mode: |E|^2, X = phase noise in rad), q0 = |beta_inc +- beta_coll|, n_i = sqrt(Re eps_ii). illumination: E_inc = the field [V/m] of illumination_physics (e.g. a gaussian_beam from the top), X in W^0.5, q0 = beta_coll, S in W/Hz (scales with the source amplitude squared). expression: w = weight, q0 = axial_wavenumber.
- `illumination_physics` (ref: physics name; nullable; visible when weighting in (illumination)) - Illumination physics. Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.illumination_physics`
- `mode_physics` (ref: physics name; nullable; visible when weighting in (mode_pair, illumination)) - Mode physics. Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.mode_physics`
- `incident_selection` (default "collected"; collected | te | tm | number; visible when weighting in (mode_pair)) - Incident mode. Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.incident_selection`
- `incident_mode` (int; default 1; >= 1; visible when incident_selection in (number)) - Incident mode number
  em_modes rank (1 = highest Re n_eff), <= n_modes of mode_physics.
- `incident_direction` (default "forward"; forward | backward; visible when weighting in (mode_pair)) - Incident direction
  backward: E_z sign flipped, beta -> -beta.
- `collected_selection` (default "te"; te | tm | te_and_tm | number; visible when weighting in (mode_pair, illumination)) - Collected mode. Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.collected_selection`
- `collected_mode` (int; default 1; >= 1; visible when collected_selection in (number)) - Collected mode number
  em_modes rank (1 = highest Re n_eff), <= n_modes of mode_physics.
- `collected_direction` (default "backward"; forward | backward; visible when weighting in (mode_pair, illumination)) - Collected direction. Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.collected_direction`
- `weight` [1/(K m^3)] (default 1; may use x, y; visible when weighting in (expression)) - Weighting function
  w(x, y) at the cell centres: X = integral w dT dV (per unit z length times the axial profile), in units of w times K m^3.
- `axial_wavenumber` [1/m] (default 0; >= 0; visible when weighting in (expression)) - Axial wavenumber
  q0 of the weighting phase exp(-j q0 z) along z; 0 = uniform.
- `axial_profile` (default "uniform"; uniform | gaussian) - Axial profile. Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.axial_profile`
- `interaction_length` [m] (default 0.0001; > 0; visible when axial_profile in (uniform)) - Interaction length
  L of the uniform profile; the PSD scales with L.
- `waist` [m] (default 1e-05; > 0; visible when axial_profile in (gaussian)) - Spot radius
  w0 of g(z) = exp(-z^2 / w0^2); integral |g|^2 dz = w0 sqrt(pi / 2).
- `axial_points` (int; default 8; [1, 64]; visible when axial_profile in (gaussian)) - Axial samples
  Gauss-Hermite nodes of the q integral, one factorisation per frequency each (equal |q| merged: q0 = 0 halves the cost). 6-12 typical.

### Feature `heat.particle_noise` - Diffusing particle scattering

Scattering spectrum of dilute particles (e.g. proteins) diffusing in the liquid on the selected cells (thermal_noise study only; independent of the heat materials): one-sided PSD of X = integral w(x, y) g(z) exp(-j q0 z) dc dV, dc the Poisson number-density fluctuation (<dc dc'> = n0 delta, n0 = c N_A). S_X(f) = 4 n0 integral dq/2pi |g~(q - q0)|^2 Re sum conj(w) u dA, (j 2 pi f + D q^2 - div D grad) u = w on the selected cells, which the particles cannot leave. w = the thermorefractive_noise weighting with dndT_i -> dn/dc * M / N_A (first Born / dipole, isotropic polarisability). Lineshape about D (q0^2 + 1/d^2) / (2 pi), d the evanescent decay length (BSA, q0 = beta: ~1 kHz). The coherent mean signal is not part of S. Not modelled: hindered diffusion near walls, binding, particle interactions. Result and extra keys as thermorefractive_noise plus series psd_single = psd / (n0 V_s) (one particle in the sensing volume V_s = (integral |w g|^2 dV)^2 / integral |w g|^4 dV) and keys bound_signal_max (|w|^2 of one particle bound at the strongest cell, W or power fraction) at (bound_signal_x, bound_signal_y), sensing_volume, particles_in_sensing_volume, index_increment [m^3], number_density. Cost: one host SuperLU of the selected cells per frequency and axial sample.

- Category monitor; selection domain entities, at least 1; result kind `xy`

Params:
- `weighting` (default "illumination"; illumination | mode_pair) - Weighting
  As thermorefractive_noise with dndT_i -> dn/dc * M / N_A: illumination S in W/Hz, mode_pair S in 1/Hz.
- `illumination_physics` (ref: physics name; nullable; visible when weighting in (illumination)) - Illumination physics. Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.illumination_physics`
- `mode_physics` (ref: physics name; nullable; visible when weighting in (mode_pair, illumination)) - Mode physics. Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.mode_physics`
- `incident_selection` (default "collected"; collected | te | tm | number; visible when weighting in (mode_pair)) - Incident mode. Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.incident_selection`
- `incident_mode` (int; default 1; >= 1; visible when incident_selection in (number)) - Incident mode number
  em_modes rank (1 = highest Re n_eff), <= n_modes of mode_physics.
- `incident_direction` (default "forward"; forward | backward; visible when weighting in (mode_pair)) - Incident direction
  backward: E_z sign flipped, beta -> -beta.
- `collected_selection` (default "te"; te | tm | te_and_tm | number; visible when weighting in (mode_pair, illumination)) - Collected mode. Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.collected_selection`
- `collected_mode` (int; default 1; >= 1; visible when collected_selection in (number)) - Collected mode number
  em_modes rank (1 = highest Re n_eff), <= n_modes of mode_physics.
- `collected_direction` (default "backward"; forward | backward; visible when weighting in (mode_pair, illumination)) - Collected direction. Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.collected_direction`
- `refractive_increment` [m^3/kg] (default 0.000185; > 0) - Refractive index increment
  dn/dc in the liquid (1 mL/g = 1e-3 m^3/kg); proteins ~1.85e-4. With molar_mass: the index increment per particle dn/dc * M / N_A [m^3] (excess polarisability alpha / eps0 = 2 n_liquid times it).
- `molar_mass` [kg/mol] (default 66.5; > 0) - Molar mass
  M (kg/mol = kDa); BSA 66.5.
- `diffusivity` [m^2/s] (default 5.9e-11; > 0) - Diffusion coefficient
  Translational D in the liquid (Stokes-Einstein k_B T / (6 pi eta R_h)); BSA in water at 20-25 C: 5.9e-11 to 6.1e-11.
- `concentration` [mol/m^3] (default 1e-06; > 0) - Concentration
  Mean c (1 nM = 1e-6 mol/m^3); n0 = c N_A. The PSD scales with c, psd_single does not.
- `axial_profile` (default "uniform"; uniform | gaussian) - Axial profile. Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.axial_profile`
- `interaction_length` [m] (default 0.0001; > 0; visible when axial_profile in (uniform)) - Interaction length
  L of the uniform profile; the PSD scales with L.
- `waist` [m] (default 1e-05; > 0; visible when axial_profile in (gaussian)) - Spot radius
  w0 of g(z) = exp(-z^2 / w0^2); integral |g|^2 dz = w0 sqrt(pi / 2).
- `axial_points` (int; default 8; [1, 64]; visible when axial_profile in (gaussian)) - Axial samples
  Gauss-Hermite nodes of the q integral, one factorisation per frequency each (equal |q| merged: q0 = 0 halves the cost). 6-12 typical.

## Physics type `laminar_flow` - Laminar Flow (2D)

2D incompressible laminar flow per unit z length: D2Q9 lattice Boltzmann (TRT collision with the magic parameter 3/16, He-Luo incompressible equilibrium, Guo forcing) on the window, which needs a uniform mesh of square cells (no PML; outputs edge-extended into an EM PML ring). Solid cells (no viscosity) are no-slip halfway bounce-back walls (solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries: interpolated Bouzidi bounce-back at the drawn wall position); unreferenced outer faces are fixed no-slip walls. Steady flow is exact for Poiseuille channels, second-order otherwise; valid at lattice Mach < 0.2 and laminar Reynolds numbers. A steady solve needs ~ L^2 lattice steps (L = longest window axis in cells; a 500-cell axis ~1e6), each one GPU kernel (cpu backend: the numba twin when installed, else the far slower numpy twin; half_storage GPU only). pressure is gauge pressure. Heat: fluid_heat_convection; buoyancy is a field_transfer of heat T into body_force_y.

- Default instance name `fluid`; studies stationary, time_dependent (default {"type": "stationary"})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor; refinement indicator fields u_x, u_y; dispersion poles not used
- Features: wall, slip_wall, inlet_velocity, pressure, periodic, body_force, initial_velocity, flow_probe

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `time_mode` (default "stationary"; stationary | transient) - Time dependence
  stationary: each solve marches the lattice to a steady state (re-solved only when a material, force or face changed; dt_limit inf); transient: one or more lattice steps per runner step (dt_limit = dt_lbm), only in a time_dependent study (other studies solve the steady state). Transient flow cannot share a time_dependent study with an FDTD wave physics (step far below dt_lbm: validation error), nor with elastic_waves when the acoustic step gives the least viscous fluid tau < 1/2 + 1e-3 (3 nu dt / dx^2, e.g. water on 10 um cells; validation error, a warning below 1/2 + 0.02).
- `relaxation_time` [1] (default 1; (0.5, 5]) - Lattice relaxation time
  TRT tau+ of the most viscous fluid: dt_lbm = (tau - 1/2) dx^2 / (3 nu_max), nu = viscosity / rho; other fluids get tau = 1/2 + 3 nu dt_lbm / dx^2. The lattice Mach number sqrt(3) u dt_lbm / dx must stay small (validation warns above 0.2 for numeric inlet velocities; the run warns above 0.2, fails above 0.7): lower tau for fast flow, raise it (up to ~2) to reach a steady state in fewer steps. Steady results do not depend on tau (weakly with conformal_boundaries: interpolated walls).
- `tolerance` [1] (default 1e-06; > 0) - Steady-state tolerance
  A steady march stops when the remaining velocity change, extrapolated from the geometric decay between checks (rate r: change * r / (1 - r)), is <= tolerance * peak lattice speed on two checks in a row, or when the change stops decreasing below 1e-5 of the peak (float32 noise floor ~1e-7..1e-6: a smaller tolerance stops there). Error ~ tolerance.
- `max_steps` (int; default 0; >= 0) - Lattice step limit
  Per steady march; 0 = auto: 30 decay times L^2 / (pi^2 nu_lat) of the slowest diffusive mode (L = longest window axis in cells, doubled on an axis with exactly one slip / pressure face such as a free-surface film, halved on a periodic axis; nu_lat the smallest lattice viscosity), at least 10 of the largest check intervals (checks start every max(100, 3.5 L) steps, doubling while one sees < 5 % of a decay). A march hitting the limit keeps its result and logs a warning.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `viscosity` [Pa s] (>= 0; nullable) - Dynamic viscosity
  Dynamic viscosity mu. Cells with viscosity > 0 are fluid (they also need rho); unset or 0 = a solid no-slip obstacle. May follow state fields (e.g. water 2.414e-5 * 10**(247.8 / (heat_T - 140)); a stationary study iterates). Typical: water 1.0e-3 (20 C), air 1.81e-5, glycerol 1.4, silicone oil 1e-2.
- `rho` [kg/m^3] (>= 0; nullable) - Density
  Mass density. Heat: transient heat capacity rho*cp (unset = 0: no heat capacity, those cells follow their neighbours; validation warns when heat is transient). Laminar flow: required on fluid cells (kinematic viscosity viscosity / rho, inertia, pressure scale). Typical: silica 2200, silicon 2329, water 998, air 1.2.

### Fields

Output fields (primary u_abs; [state] = also a state field):
- `u_abs` - Flow speed |u| (m/s) [state]
- `u_x` - Velocity x (m/s) [state]
- `u_y` - Velocity y (m/s) [state]
- `pressure` - Pressure (Pa) [state]
- `vorticity` - Vorticity (1/s)
- `body_force_x` - Coupled body force x (N/m^3)
- `body_force_y` - Coupled body force y (N/m^3)
- `viscosity` - Dynamic viscosity (Pa s)

### Source slots

- `body_force_x` (N/m^3): Coupled force density along x (e.g. buoyancy), added to the body_force features; replaced by each transfer.
- `body_force_y` (N/m^3): Coupled force density along y, e.g. Boussinesq buoyancy +rho g beta (T - T0) from heat T by field_transfer (g = 9.81, gravity along -y: warm fluid is pushed along +y); replaced by each transfer.

### Feature `laminar_flow.wall` - Wall

No-slip halfway bounce-back (the wall sits on the face), moving along itself at tangential_velocity. A later boundary feature on the same face wins (validation warning).

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, at least 1, outer faces only; requires a uniform mesh (see mesh); result none

Params:
- `tangential_velocity` [m/s] (default 0; may use x, y, t) - Wall velocity
  Along the wall: +x on y_lo / y_hi, +y on x_lo / x_hi (a lid-driven cavity); x, y at the centres of the face cells. Stationary flow re-marches to a steady state after each change in t.

### Feature `laminar_flow.slip_wall` - Slip wall (symmetry)

Free slip (specular reflection of the populations): zero normal velocity and shear stress, a symmetry plane.

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, at least 1, outer faces only; requires a uniform mesh (see mesh); result none

Params: none

### Feature `laminar_flow.inlet_velocity` - Velocity inlet

Moving-wall bounce-back with the face-normal velocity (solid cells along the face stay solid). Combine with a pressure face elsewhere (validation warns: without one inflow and outflow must balance exactly).

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, at least 1, outer faces only; requires a uniform mesh (see mesh); result none

Params:
- `velocity` [m/s] (default 0.001; may use x, y, t) - Inflow velocity
  Normal velocity into the domain (< 0 outflow); with profile 'parabolic' the mean over each run of fluid cells along the face; x, y at the centres of the face cells. Typical microfluidics 1e-4 - 1e-2. Stationary flow re-marches to a steady state after each change in t.
- `profile` (default "uniform"; uniform | parabolic) - Profile
  uniform: the value per cell; parabolic: the value times the discrete Poiseuille shape s (w - s) of each run of fluid cells along the face, mean 1 (peak 1.5 x the value).

### Feature `laminar_flow.pressure` - Pressure

Anti-bounce-back with the boundary cell velocity: an open inlet or outlet. A model without a pressure face keeps a zero mean pressure.

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, at least 1, outer faces only; requires a uniform mesh (see mesh); result none

Params:
- `pressure` [Pa] (default 0; may use x, y, t) - Pressure
  Gauge pressure (0 at an open outlet); x, y at the centres of the face cells. Stationary flow re-marches to a steady state after each change in t.

### Feature `laminar_flow.periodic` - Periodic pair

Both faces of one axis (['x_lo', 'x_hi'] or ['y_lo', 'y_hi']); the lattice wraps around. Drive such a channel with a body_force. Only the flow is periodic (other physics keep their own face conditions).

- Category boundary_condition; selection boundary entities, exactly 2, outer faces only; requires a uniform mesh (see mesh); result none

Params: none

### Feature `laminar_flow.body_force` - Body force

Force density on the selected cells (several add; solid cells ignore it), held in the solver state body_force_x_ext / _y_ext, separate from the coupled slots body_force_x / _y (output fields). The same feature as the solid_mechanics body_force.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params:
- `f_x` [N/m^3] (default 0; may use x, y, t) - Body force x
  Guo forcing; a periodic channel pressure gradient dp/dx is f_x = -dp/dx (an oscillating one, e.g. F cos(omega t), gives Womersley flow). Stationary flow re-marches to a steady state after each change in t.
- `f_y` [N/m^3] (default 0; may use x, y, t) - Body force y
  E.g. gravity -rho g = -9.79e3 for water (a hydrostatic pressure gradient builds up against it). Stationary flow re-marches to a steady state after each change in t.

### Feature `laminar_flow.initial_velocity` - Initial values

Transient flow: the populations of the selected fluid cells start at the equilibrium of (u_x, u_y, pressure) instead of rest (a later feature wins its cells; solid cells stay at rest). Keep the velocity divergence free: a divergent start relaxes through sound waves. Stationary flow only starts its first steady march from it.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; result none

Params:
- `u_x` [m/s] (default 0; may use x, y) - Initial velocity x
  At the cell centres, e.g. the Taylor-Green vortex U sin(k x) cos(k y).
- `u_y` [m/s] (default 0; may use x, y) - Initial velocity y
  At the cell centres.
- `pressure` [Pa] (default 0; may use x, y) - Initial pressure
  Gauge pressure; 0 is fine for slow flow (an inconsistent start only launches weak sound waves that the viscosity damps).

### Feature `laminar_flow.flow_probe` - Flow probe

The cell containing the point: stationary flow once per steady solve and every stationary iteration (t = 0); transient flow after every runner step, at its end time.

- Category probe; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; result kind `timeseries`

Params:
- `component` (default "u_abs"; u_abs | u_x | u_y | pressure) - Quantity
  u_abs = |u|, u_x, u_y [m/s] or pressure [Pa].

## Physics type `magnetic_fields_ac` - Magnetic Fields, AC (2D)

2D quasi-static time-harmonic magnetic fields (eddy currents): curl(nu curl A) + j omega sigma_dc A = J, nu = 1 / (mu0 (mu_dc - j mu_dc_loss)), phasors exp(+j omega t) of peak amplitude; planar A_z or axisymmetric psi = r A_phi as in magnetostatics (setting geometry). B from the complex face fluxes; J_conduction = sigma_dc E, E = -j omega A (+ v of solid conductors); q_eddy, q_magnetic and w_mag are time averages. Outer faces default to magnetic insulation. No remanence (a permanent magnet is static: magnetostatics). Tensor mesh: one complex host SuperLU factorisation (scipy required); an operator change (sigma_dc(heat_T), mu_dc) first tries GMRES preconditioned with the old factor. A time-dependent study re-solves only when a material, a source or a held value changed. Fields are edge-extended into an EM PML ring. Triangle mesh: complex elements (setting discretization) for planar A_z or axisymmetric A_phi (not psi), same features, scalars and results; state fields per element (A at the centroid, element means of B and the densities; plots show A, B on the nodes); a solid conductor touching the axis is a run error (v / r singular). There Automatic is a double cuDSS LDL^T on the gpu backend with nvmath-python (an operator change refactorises on the kept analysis; a cuDSS refusal falls back to host SuperLU with a warning), else host SuperLU.

- Default instance name `magnetic`; studies stationary, time_dependent (default {"type": "stationary"})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields B_abs; dispersion poles not used
- Features: magnetic_insulation, symmetry, external_field, fixed_potential, current_source, coil, probe

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (default "planar"; planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry. Help: shared `magnetic_fields_ac.geometry`
- `frequency` [Hz] (default 50; > 0) - Frequency
  omega = 2 pi f. One frequency per build: sweep it with a parameter (each value refactorises; a reused sweep build (reuse_build) follows a parameters-only value and keeps the factor plan). Skin depth delta = sqrt(2 / (omega mu0 mu_dc sigma_dc)): copper 9.3 mm at 50 Hz, 0.66 mm at 10 kHz, 66 um at 1 MHz; resolve delta with >= 3 cells near conductor surfaces. Quasi-static: no displacement current (sizes << c / f).
- `discretization` (default "quadratic"; quadratic | linear) - Discretization. Help: shared `electric_currents.discretization`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `mu_dc` [1] (> 0; nullable; writes mu_dc_xx, mu_dc_yy) - Static relative permeability. Help: shared `magnetic_fields_ac.mu_dc`
- `mu_dc_xx` [1] (> 0; nullable) - Static relative permeability along x
  Overrides mu_dc along x (axisymmetric: r).
- `mu_dc_yy` [1] (> 0; nullable) - Static relative permeability along y
  Overrides mu_dc along y (axisymmetric: z).
- `mu_dc_loss` [1] (>= 0; nullable) - Magnetic loss (imaginary permeability)
  mu = mu_dc - j mu_dc_loss (exp(+j omega t)); unset = 0. Dissipates q_magnetic = omega Im(nu) |B|^2 / 2, nu = 1 / (mu0 mu). Dispersive (tabulated mu', mu''): an expression of the swept frequency parameter. Typical: soft ferrite mu_dc 2000, mu_dc_loss 10 - 200 (rising with f); Metglas ~1e4 / 1e3 at 100 kHz.
- `sigma_dc` [S/m] (>= 0; nullable; writes sigma_dc_xx, sigma_dc_yy) - Static conductivity
  Sets sigma_dc_xx and _yy (component entries override it; they must be equal, else a run error); unset = 0: no induced current. Carries the eddy and solid-conductor currents; in stranded coils only the wire conductivity of the coil resistance. The electric_currents arrays: a sigma_dc(heat_T) expression reaches both. Copper 5.8e7, aluminium 3.8e7, stainless steel 1.4e6, electrical steel 2e6 (laminations: the stack value or lower), sea water 4.8.
- `sigma_dc_xx` [S/m] (>= 0; nullable) - Static conductivity along x
  Overrides sigma_dc for this axis; must equal sigma_dc_yy.
- `sigma_dc_yy` [S/m] (>= 0; nullable) - Static conductivity along y
  Overrides sigma_dc for this axis; must equal sigma_dc_xx.

Output fields (primary B_abs; [state] = also a state field):
- `B_abs` - Magnetic flux density amplitude (T) [state]

- `B_y_re` - Magnetic flux density y (axisymmetric: z), real part (T) [state]
- `B_y_im` - Magnetic flux density y (axisymmetric: z), imaginary part (T) [state]
- `A_abs` - Magnetic vector potential amplitude (T m) [state]
- `A_re` - Magnetic vector potential (z; axisymmetric: phi), real part (T m) [state]
- `A_im` - Magnetic vector potential (z; axisymmetric: phi), imaginary part (T m) [state]
- `J_total_abs` - Total current density amplitude (A/m^2) [state]
- `J_total_re` - Total current density, real part (A/m^2) [state]
- `J_total_im` - Total current density, imaginary part (A/m^2) [state]
- `J_conduction_re` - Conduction current density (eddy and solid conductors), real part (A/m^2) [state]
- `J_conduction_im` - Conduction current density (eddy and solid conductors), imaginary part (A/m^2) [state]
- `q_eddy` - Ohmic loss density (time average) (W/m^3) [state]
- `q_magnetic` - Magnetic loss density (time average) (W/m^3) [state]

- `J_applied_im` - Applied current density, imaginary part (A/m^2) [state]

- `mu_dc_yy` - Static relative permeability yy (1) [state]
- `sigma_dc_xx` - Static conductivity (S/m) [state]

Scalar outputs: energy: time-averaged magnetic energy (1/4) Re(A^H K A) of the free cells; eddy_loss: time-averaged ohmic loss, the integral of q_eddy = sigma_dc |E|^2 / 2 over the conducting cells (stranded coils excluded); magnetic_loss: (omega / 2) Im(A^H K A), the mu_dc_loss dissipation (the integral of q_magnetic only approximately at material interfaces); planar per m (J/m, W/m), axisymmetric whole rings (J, W); per enabled coil <coil>_current_re, <coil>_current_im, <coil>_voltage_re, <coil>_voltage_im, <coil>_resistance, <coil>_inductance, <coil>_power as its table result.

### Feature `magnetic_fields_ac.coil` - Coil or conductor

Coil or conductor carrying a time-harmonic current (param conductor). Go / return pairs: two coils at +I / -I (or phase 180). Result 'table': one row [feature, current_re, current_im, voltage_re, voltage_im, resistance, inductance, power] of the latest solve (also scalars <feature>_<key>): the complex current and loop voltage (stranded: R_dc I + j omega flux linkage), Z = V / I: resistance Re Z, inductance Im Z / omega, power Re(V I*) / 2; planar per m of length (A, V/m, Ohm/m, H/m, W/m), axisymmetric whole rings (A, V, Ohm, H, W). With several conductors each Z includes the mutual terms (series +I / -I: the resistances and inductances add to the loop values).

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result kind `table`

Params:
- `conductor` (default "stranded"; stranded | solid) - Conductor
  'stranded': many thin turns, uniform J = turns I / area, no eddy currents (the cells' sigma_dc only sets the coil resistance); 'solid': one massive conductor (cells need sigma_dc > 0), J = sigma_dc (v - j omega A) / r with the applied field v uniform over it, skin and proximity effects included.
- `drive` (default "current"; current | voltage; visible when conductor in (solid)) - Drive
  'current': one circuit row, the solve finds v; 'voltage': the solve finds the current. Stranded coils are current-driven.
- `current` [A] (default 1; visible when conductor in (stranded) or drive in (current)) - Current amplitude
  Peak, per turn (solid: total), > 0 along +z (axisymmetric: counter-clockwise seen from +z).
- `voltage` [V/m, V axisymmetric] (default 0.001; visible when drive in (voltage)) - Voltage amplitude
  Peak loop voltage: planar v (per m of length), axisymmetric around the ring (v = voltage / (2 pi r)).
- `phase` [deg] (default 0) - Phase
  Of the current or voltage phasor; held potentials and the external field are at phase 0.
- `turns` [1] (int; default 1; >= 1; visible when conductor in (stranded)) - Turns
  Spread over the selected cross-section.
- `fill_factor` [1] (default 1; (0, 1]; visible when conductor in (stranded)) - Copper fill factor
  Conducting share of the cross-section; coil resistance = turns^2 / (fill_factor area^2) times the sum of (path length / sigma_dc) area over its cells (0 where sigma_dc is unset: an ideal winding).

## Physics type `magnetostatics` - Magnetostatics (2D)

2D magnetostatics, finite volumes (Jacobi-PCG): -div(nu grad A) = J, nu = 1 / (mu0 mu_dc); planar A_z of currents J_z (c_xx = nu_yy, c_yy = nu_xx: B_y = -dA/dx sees mu_yy), axisymmetric psi = r A_phi (setting geometry). B = curl A (planar B_x = dA/dy, B_y = -dA/dx; axisymmetric B_r = -(1/r) dpsi/dz, B_z = (1/r) dpsi/dr) and H = nu (B - B_r) from the face fluxes averaged to the cell centres; w_mag = (nu_xx B_x^2 + nu_yy B_y^2) / 2. Outer faces default to magnetic insulation. mu_dc may depend on x, y and state fields (a stationary study iterates); saturation_polarization or bh_curve materials follow an anhysteretic B-H curve (settings nonlinear_*; study summary nonlinear_iterations; an unconverged loop warns). A time-dependent study re-solves only when mu_dc, remanence, a source or a held value changed. Fields are edge-extended into an EM PML ring. Triangle mesh: elements (setting discretization) for planar A_z or axisymmetric A_phi itself (not psi): B = curl A at quadrature points, H = diag(nu) (B - B_r) (no xx / yy swap), saturating materials isotropic by Newton; state fields per element (A at the centroid, B / H / w_mag element means; plots average B, H to the nodes).

- Default instance name `magnetic`; studies stationary, time_dependent (default {"type": "stationary"})
- Backends gpu, cpu; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields B_abs; dispersion poles not used
- Features: magnetic_insulation, symmetry, external_field, fixed_potential, current_source, coil, probe

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (default "planar"; planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry. Help: shared `magnetic_fields_ac.geometry`
- `discretization` (default "quadratic"; quadratic | linear) - Discretization. Help: shared `electric_currents.discretization`
- `nonlinear_tolerance` [1] (default 1e-06; > 0) - Saturation iteration tolerance. Help: shared `magnetostatics.nonlinear_tolerance`
- `nonlinear_max_iterations` (int; default 100; >= 1) - Saturation iteration limit. Help: shared `magnetostatics.nonlinear_max_iterations`
- `nonlinear_method` (default "auto"; auto | anderson | picard | newton) - Saturation iteration method. Help: shared `magnetostatics.nonlinear_method`
- `nonlinear_relaxation` [1] (default 0.5; [0.015625, 1]) - Saturation iteration damping. Help: shared `magnetostatics.nonlinear_relaxation`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `mu_dc` [1] (> 0; nullable; writes mu_dc_xx, mu_dc_yy) - Static relative permeability. Help: shared `magnetic_fields_ac.mu_dc`
- `mu_dc_xx` [1] (> 0; nullable) - Static relative permeability along x
  Overrides mu_dc along x (axisymmetric: r).
- `mu_dc_yy` [1] (> 0; nullable) - Static relative permeability along y
  Overrides mu_dc along y (axisymmetric: z).
- `remanence_x` [T] (nullable) - Remanence along x
  Remanent flux density B_r along x of a permanent magnet: H = (B - B_r) / (mu0 mu_dc), entered as face sources at the magnet boundary (exact for a uniformly magnetised region). Typical: NdFeB 1.2 - 1.4 T with mu_dc 1.05, SmCo 1.0 T, ferrite 0.4 T with mu_dc 1.1. Unset = 0. Axisymmetric on a tensor mesh: validation error (magnetise along z with remanence_y); triangles allow it.
- `remanence_y` [T] (nullable) - Remanence along y
  Remanent flux density B_r along y (axisymmetric: along the axis z) of a permanent magnet: H = (B - B_r) / (mu0 mu_dc), entered as face sources at the magnet boundary (exact for a uniformly magnetised region). Typical: NdFeB 1.2 - 1.4 T with mu_dc 1.05, SmCo 1.0 T, ferrite 0.4 T with mu_dc 1.1. Unset = 0.
- `saturation_polarization` [T] (> 0; nullable) - Saturation polarisation
  Saturation polarisation J_s of an anhysteretic B-H curve (magnetostatics only): Frohlich-Kennelly B = mu0 H + J_s a H / (1 + a H), a = mu0 (mu_dc - 1) / J_s (initial permeability mu_dc, B -> mu0 H + J_s), no hysteresis. Tensor mesh: per axis with mu_dc_xx / mu_dc_yy at the cell-centre |B|, a fixed point on ln of the secant reluctivity nu = H(|B|) / |B| (settings nonlinear_*); energy and coil inductances are then secant values. Triangle mesh: isotropic (mu_dc_xx must equal mu_dc_yy: validation error), H = nu(|B|) B per quadrature point, Newton. Unset = linear; mu_dc <= 1 stays linear. Not with a remanence in the same material (validation error); ignored by magnetic_fields_ac. Typical: iron 2.15, electrical steel 2.0, Metglas 0.6 - 1.6, Mn-Zn ferrite 0.4 - 0.5, NiFe (mu-metal) 0.8.
- `bh_curve` (table; columns H [A/m], B [T]; >= 2 rows, every column strictly increasing; >= 0; nullable; no x, y; no fields; writes no array) - B-H curve. Help: shared `magnetostatics.bh_curve`

### Fields

Output fields (primary B_abs; [state] = also a state field):
- `B_abs` - Magnetic flux density magnitude (T) [state]
- `B_x` - Magnetic flux density x (axisymmetric: r) (T) [state]
- `B_y` - Magnetic flux density y (axisymmetric: z) (T) [state]
- `A` - Magnetic vector potential (z; axisymmetric: phi) (T m) [state]
- `H_x` - Magnetic field x (axisymmetric: r) (A/m) [state]
- `H_y` - Magnetic field y (axisymmetric: z) (A/m) [state]
- `w_mag` - Magnetic energy density (J/m^3) [state]
- `J_coupled` - Coupled current density (A/m^2) [state]
- `J_applied` - Applied current density (A/m^2) [state]
- `mu_dc_xx` - Static relative permeability xx (1) [state]
- `mu_dc_yy` - Static relative permeability yy (1) [state]

Scalar outputs: energy: field energy of the free cells, (1/2) A^T K A = integral of B^2 / (2 mu0 mu_dc) (J/m planar, J axisymmetric; with remanence the energy of B alone, not the co-energy; held cells and the external-field ring excluded, held-free faces count their free half cell; saturating: the secant value at the converged nu; triangle mesh: the integral of H dB over the elements outside fixed_potential regions); <coil>_flux_linkage (Wb/m, Wb) and <coil>_inductance (H/m, H) of every enabled coil, as its table result.

### Source slots

- `current_density` (A/m^2): J_z (axisymmetric J_phi; field J_coupled), added to the current_source and coil features (field J_applied); each transfer replaces it.

### Feature `magnetostatics.current_source` - Current density

Applied current density on the selected cells, added to field J_applied (sources and coils add; the coupled slot current_density, field J_coupled, is separate): planar J_z (> 0 along +z: B circles counter-clockwise), axisymmetric J_phi (> 0 counter-clockwise seen from +z: B_z > 0 inside).

Params:

### Feature `magnetostatics.coil` - Coil

Stranded coil: J = turns current / area uniform over the selected cells (area = their cross-section; no skin or proximity effects: use the solid conductors of magnetic_fields_ac). A planar coil without a return is a net current per m of depth returning through the insulation faces: model a go / return pair as two coils with opposite currents. Result 'table': one row [feature, current, turns, flux_linkage, inductance] of the latest solve (also scalars <feature>_flux_linkage / _inductance): flux_linkage = turns / area * integral of A over the coil (axisymmetric 2 pi psi: the flux through each turn), Wb/m planar or Wb; inductance = flux_linkage / current, H/m or H (nan at zero current). Series coils at +I / -I: their inductances add to the loop inductance 2 W / I^2 (W the energy scalar); with several currents a coil's value includes the mutual flux.

- Category domain_condition; selection domain entities, at least 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result kind `table`

Params:
- `current` [A] (default 1) - Current
  Per turn, > 0 along +z (axisymmetric: counter-clockwise seen from +z); a reused sweep build (reuse_build) follows it (tensor meshes).
- `turns` [1] (int; default 1; >= 1) - Turns
  Spread over the selected cross-section.

- Category probe; selection point entities, object kinds point, exactly 1; mesh kinds tensor, triangles; result kind `timeseries`

Params: none

## Physics type `magnetostatics_3d` - Magnetostatics (3D)

3D magnetostatics by the reduced scalar potential, finite volumes (7-point stencil): H = T - grad phi_m (T the coil fields), B = mu0 mu_dc H + B_r, div B = 0, solved for u = mu0 phi_m with per-axis mu_dc (no cross terms) and face drive w = mu0 T + B_r / mu_dc, so the face flux is B (accurate also in high-mu cores); B averaged from the face fluxes to the cell centres, H = (B - B_r) / (mu0 mu_dc) per axis, w_mag = sum of B^2 / (2 mu0 mu_dc) per axis (not B . H / 2 in magnets), J = curl T. Outer faces default to magnetic insulation. Saturating materials (isotropic) run a fixed point on ln of the secant permeability, one assembly and warm-started solve per iteration (settings nonlinear_*; no 'newton'); field mu_eff shows the assembled permeability. No Lorentz force yet, no eddy currents. Linear solver pcg (Automatic: multigrid). A time-dependent study re-solves only when mu_dc, a saturation or a remanence changed. Fields are edge-extended into an EM PML shell. Tetrahedron mesh (3D Cartesian): phi_m elements (setting discretization) on affine tetrahedra, sparse direct solver (Automatic: cuDSS on the gpu backend with nvmath-python, else host SuperLU; one factorisation per saturation iteration); B, H, w_mag, J and mu_eff are element means; field derived values are not available there yet (use probes and the coil table).
