## Study type `frequency_domain` - Frequency domain

Time-harmonic solves (exp(+j omega t), omega = 2 pi c / wavelength) of every harmonic physics once per wavelength, in list order; the study wavelengths override the wavelength setting (em_modes: n_modes modes per wavelength, its mode_number mode in the snapshot, mode_dispersion results versus wavelength; em_fdfd_conical at a fixed k_z). Time-domain types (em_fdtd_*: harmonic FDTD) instead run one pulse after the background solve with a running DFT of the whole window at every wavelength until the field energy falls below auto_shutoff of its peak (or max_duration), divided by the spectrum of their shared source waveform (every source of one such physics: the same gaussian or ricker waveform, wavelength and bandwidth): the phasor response to a unit source at phase 0, as FDFD gives it (fields <component>_re / _im / _abs / _phase, e_abs_harmonic, e_intensity_harmonic, absorbed_power_harmonic; ez / hz: the out-of-plane component, stored by default ez_abs / hz_abs; em_fdtd_3d: ex, ey, ez at the cell centres, stored by default e_abs_harmonic; em_fdtd_bor: see its type); their monitors keep their own unnormalised pulse spectra. Memory: 8 (ez) / 24 (hz, 3D) B per window cell and wavelength. Background physics iterate to a stationary fixed point (max_iterations, tolerance), then every coupling into the harmonic physics (and material properties of background fields such as T) applies once, so every wavelength sees the same background. Coupled wavelength scan (an enabled coupling or material property reads a harmonic physics, e.g. em_heat_joule from FDFD; every physics must then support stationary: no em_modes or time-domain type): each wavelength is a stationary fixed point of every physics (max_iterations, tolerance, relaxation), warm-started from the previous one in list order: ascending scans blue to red (the thermal triangle of a red-shifting ring), descending red to blue (hysteresis); a wavelength that does not converge warns and the scan continues; summary fixed_point over all wavelengths (converged = all, iterations and relative_change the largest) and wavelength_fixed_points [{wavelength, converged, iterations, relative_change, tolerance}]; a cancel inside a wavelength leaves its monitors at the last iterate. Default stored fields include <field>_re / _im (|field|^2 per wavelength). The last wavelength stays the live state; feature results hold every wavelength (sorted by wavelength; snapshot labels keep the solve order).

- Needs a physics that steps in time: no; background study stationary; coupled points; StudySpec.adaptation allowed

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `wavelength_start` [m] (default 1.5e-06; > 0) - Start wavelength
  Range used when wavelengths is null or empty: n_wavelengths wavelengths from wavelength_start to wavelength_stop, in that order; they override the wavelength setting of every FDFD physics. Typically 0.4e-6 to 2e-6.
- `wavelength_stop` [m] (default 1.6e-06; > 0) - Stop wavelength
  Must exceed wavelength_start (equal allowed with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 11; >= 1) - Number of wavelengths
  Spaced linearly in wavelength (not frequency); 1 solves the centre. Each costs one assembly, factorisation and solve per FDFD physics (harmonic FDTD: one DFT update per sample and 8 / 24 B of GPU memory per window cell).
- `wavelengths` [m] (float_list; > 0; nullable) - Wavelength list
  Vacuum wavelengths solved in list order; a non-empty list overrides the range.
- `auto_shutoff` [1] (default 0.0001; (0, 1]) - Pulse shutoff level
  em_fdtd_* only (harmonic FDTD): the pulse ends once t > 2 t0 and the EM energy over the window (checked ~10 times per wall second) is at most auto_shutoff times its running peak, or at max_duration. The truncated ring-down errs the harmonic fields by roughly sqrt(auto_shutoff) times the ring-down share (more for slowly decaying resonances); 1e-6 for percent-level comparisons.
- `max_duration` [s] (default 2e-12; > 0) - Maximum pulse duration
  em_fdtd_* only: upper bound of the pulse time; ending before auto_shutoff logs a warning (high-Q resonances: raise it). Typical 1e-12 to 1e-11 s.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; >= 1) - Maximum coupling iterations. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.max_iterations`
- `tolerance` [1] (default 0.0001; > 0) - Relative tolerance. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.tolerance`
- `relaxation` [1] (default 1; > 0) - Coupling relaxation. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; >= 0) - Coupling acceleration depth. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.anderson_depth`
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` [Hz] (default 5; >= 0) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the GUI live field frames; 0 disables them. Never changes results (headless api.run sets 0).
- `parity_sectors` (bool; default false) - Parity sectors. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.parity_sectors`

## Study type `frequency_response` - Frequency response

Driven time-harmonic response (exp(+j omega t), omega = 2 pi f) at a list of frequencies (the EM frequency_domain study takes wavelengths) of every frequency-response physics (solid_mechanics, solid_mechanics_3d, membrane or pressure_acoustics; solid_mechanics 2D: planar plane strain / plane stress or axisymmetric, not generalized plane strain or guided modes; solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra; pressure_acoustics: -div(grad p / rho) - omega^2 p / (rho c^2) = j omega q on triangles / tetrahedra). Solids: (K (1 + j eta) - omega^2 M) u = f, consistent mass of rho (every solid cell needs rho > 0), eta = mechanical_loss_factor, piezoelectric: the coupled potential with eps (1 - j dielectric_loss_tangent); every load, prescribed displacement, electrode voltage and floating charge is a complex drive amplitude (phase 0); one complex symmetric factor per frequency (2D: host SuperLU outside the solver roles, counters in the summary; solid_mechanics_3d: its 'linear' sparse_direct solver, SuperLU or cuDSS LDL^T with the plan reused). With stress_stiffening the initial_stress is first relaxed by a static solve (loads stay the drive) and its K_sigma joins K (real, no loss). A free body is allowed (regular at f > 0). membrane: the pressure_load / line_force / point_force phasors, one complex factor per frequency on its 'linear' sparse_direct solver. Results: the admittance feature (Y = I / V of an electrode versus f, Butterworth-Van Dyke fit); snapshots labelled "f = <Hz> Hz" holding the real parts (phase 0), u_abs = |u|, u_x_im / u_y_im (/ u_z_im) the imaginary parts (triangles / tetrahedra; store them through stored_fields); the last frequency stays live. Triangles / tetrahedra: frequency_probe records the complex displacement per frequency (u_x_re, u_x_im, u_x_abs, u_x_phase, ...), every support result becomes a table of its complex reaction per frequency (F_x_re, F_x_im, ...); solid_probe samples and electrode tables stay empty; membrane: field_probe, port and mode_projection records per frequency. Background physics run first (their couplings into the solved physics apply once); couplings reading a solved physics: validation error; StudySpec.solved_physics restricts the solved physics. ticks = frequencies; summary response_frequencies (+ frequency_sweep with a reduced sweep). parity_sectors: membrane symmetry / antisymmetry faces are mirror planes too.

- Needs a physics that steps in time: no; background study stationary

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `frequency_start` [Hz] (default 1e+06; > 0) - Start frequency
  Range used when frequencies is empty.
- `frequency_stop` [Hz] (default 2e+06; > 0) - Stop frequency
  Must exceed frequency_start (equal allowed with n_frequencies = 1).
- `n_frequencies` (int; default 101; >= 1) - Number of frequencies
  Both ends included, spaced as log_spacing selects (1 = the arithmetic or geometric mean). Each costs one complex factorisation per solved physics; resolve a resonance of quality factor Q at f0 with a step well below f0 / Q.
- `log_spacing` (bool; default false) - Logarithmic spacing
  false: evenly in f (a resonance sweep); true: evenly in log f (a spectrum over decades).
- `frequencies` [Hz] (float_list; > 0; nullable) - Frequency list
  Solved in this order; a non-empty list overrides the range. Feature results (admittance) are sorted by frequency.
- `snapshots` (default "all"; all | last | none) - Stored snapshots
  Which frequencies keep a snapshot: 'all' one each, 'last' the last solved one (also after a cancel), 'none'. A snapshot is ~1 MB per field for a large window, so hundreds of frequencies may keep only the last. Feature records per frequency and the live last-frequency state are the same for every choice; with 'last' / 'none' fields are formed for the last frequency only (the live view is not refreshed during the sweep).
- `sweep_method` (default "direct"; direct | adaptive | modal) - Sweep method
  'direct': one complex factorisation per frequency. 'adaptive' (asymptotic waveform evaluation): a reduced model trained on the list: factorisations at the ends and the middle, each adding the solution and rom_moments frequency derivatives to a Galerkin basis, then one more at the frequency of the largest estimated residual until it is <= rom_tolerance or rom_max_points; every listed frequency is then a small dense solve (use a fine list). Pays off for a few to tens of resonances in the window; hundreds of modes need as many basis vectors (keep 'direct'). 'modal': the modal_count eigenmodes nearest the band centre (membrane: its 'eigen' solver; solids and pressure_acoustics: a host shift-invert of K, M) plus the direct solution at the centre (static correction); exact for a uniform loss_factor once every mode is in the basis. Both end with one verification factorisation at the worst frequency; summary frequency_sweep {method, physics: {name: {basis_size, factorizations, expansion_frequencies [Hz], max_residual, worst_frequency [Hz], verified_error, converged, warnings, ...}}}. Records come from the reduced coordinates, fields only for the stored snapshots. Types: membrane (not with ports), solid_mechanics and solid_mechanics_3d (modal: not piezoelectric), pressure_acoustics (background_pressure_field or a damping boundary: adaptive only, one snapshot per expansion, no derivatives).
- `rom_tolerance` (default 1e-06; > 0; visible when sweep_method in (adaptive, modal)) - Reduced model tolerance
  Largest estimated relative residual ||b - A x|| / ||b|| over the list ('adaptive': training stops below it; 'modal': a warning above it). Near a resonance of quality factor Q the error can be ~Q times the residual: for Q = 1e4 use 1e-8 or below; the summary reports the true worst error.
- `rom_moments` (int; default 4; [0, 20]; visible when sweep_method in (adaptive)) - Derivatives per expansion
  Frequency derivatives per expansion frequency (back-solves on its factor): each factorisation adds rom_moments + 1 basis vectors.
- `rom_max_points` (int; default 40; >= 1; visible when sweep_method in (adaptive)) - Most expansion frequencies
  Expansion frequencies (factorisations, verification not counted) at most; reaching it without rom_tolerance warns.
- `modal_count` (int; default 20; >= 1; visible when sweep_method in (modal)) - Number of modes
  Eigenmodes nearest the band centre ((min + max) / 2 of the list); take every resonance of the band plus a margin on either side.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; >= 1) - Maximum coupling iterations. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.max_iterations`
- `tolerance` [1] (default 0.0001; > 0) - Relative tolerance. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.tolerance`
- `relaxation` [1] (default 1; > 0) - Coupling relaxation. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; >= 0) - Coupling acceleration depth. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.anderson_depth`
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` [Hz] (default 5; >= 0) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the GUI live field frames; 0 disables them. Never changes results (headless api.run sets 0).
- `parity_sectors` (bool; default false) - Parity sectors. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.parity_sectors`

## Study type `mode_analysis` - Mode analysis

Every mode physics (em_modes) computes n_modes modes at its wavelength setting (xy = the cross-section, propagation along z). Background physics iterate to a stationary fixed point (max_iterations, tolerance), then every coupling into the mode physics (and material properties of background fields such as T) applies once; couplings or material properties reading a mode physics: validation error. Snapshots per mode number k in the em_modes rank order (descending Re(beta^2)); n_eff complex when lossy; several em_modes physics: names and values joined; mirror faces add the parity ("mode k [x_lo symmetric]: ..."). Afterwards each em_modes physics shows its mode_number mode; ticks = the mode snapshots. n_eff versus a parameter: a sweep with a derived value of mode_table; versus wavelength: frequency_domain.

- Needs a physics that steps in time: no; background study stationary; StudySpec.adaptation allowed

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; >= 1) - Maximum coupling iterations. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.max_iterations`
- `tolerance` [1] (default 0.0001; > 0) - Relative tolerance. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.tolerance`
- `relaxation` [1] (default 1; > 0) - Coupling relaxation. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; >= 0) - Coupling acceleration depth. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.anderson_depth`
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` [Hz] (default 5; >= 0) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the GUI live field frames; 0 disables them. Never changes results (headless api.run sets 0).
- `parity_sectors` (bool; default false) - Parity sectors. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.parity_sectors`

## Study type `nonlinear_frequency_domain` - Nonlinear frequency domain

Cascaded frequency-domain nonlinear optics (em_fdfd_nonlinear): its harmonic channels are solved together, not one wavelength after the other as in frequency_domain. Undepleted: each channel one FDFD solve in rank order (inputs, then the channels generated from them, each driven by the nonlinear polarisation of the lower ranks); pump_depleted: sweeps (picard) or Newton steps (newton) over all channels until self-consistent (a log line per sweep / step with its residual; not converged within max_iterations: a warning, the last iterate is stored and the snapshot labels end in "(not converged)"); cancel between channel solves. Background physics iterate to a stationary fixed point, then their couplings into the nonlinear physics apply once. Solution feedback: a coupling from a nonlinear physics into a background physics (em_heat_joule into heat: linear, two-photon and free-carrier absorption of every channel) alternates background and nonlinear solves (pump_depleted warm-started) up to feedback_rounds, a log line per round, summary feedback {couplings, rounds, converged, relative_change, tolerance, history} (None without feedback); couplings between nonlinear physics and material properties reading one are validation errors. The run log lists the mixing terms and each channel solve. One snapshot per channel in solve order (default stored field the primary e_abs), labelled "channel <name>: lambda = <nm> nm" (several nonlinear physics: their name first, the others NaN); afterwards each shows its first input channel. ticks = n_channels; summary nonlinear_solve = {physics: {mode, order (channel names in solve order), channel_solves, sweeps, converged, residual, tolerance, residual_history, continuation_steps, method ('picard' | 'newton', '' undepleted), gmres_iterations, backtracks}}. Spectra (a QPM tuning curve, SHG versus pump wavelength) and power curves: parameter sweeps over the poling period, input wavelength or source amplitude, with derived values of channel monitors or the power_exchange_<channel> scalars.

- Needs a physics that steps in time: no; background study stationary; solution feedback

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; >= 1) - Maximum coupling iterations. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.max_iterations`
- `tolerance` [1] (default 0.0001; > 0) - Relative tolerance. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.tolerance`
- `relaxation` [1] (default 1; > 0) - Coupling relaxation. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; >= 0) - Coupling acceleration depth. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.anderson_depth`
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` [Hz] (default 5; >= 0) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the GUI live field frames; 0 disables them. Never changes results (headless api.run sets 0).
- `feedback_rounds` (int; default 20; >= 1) - Feedback rounds
  Used when an enabled coupling reads a physics the study solves and writes a background physics (e.g. em_heat_joule from em_fdfd_nonlinear into heat): rounds of background solve (feedback couplings applied first) and study solve, until every primary field of these physics changes by at most the tolerance between rounds; a warning when not reached or when the change stops decreasing for 3 rounds (from round 4); the last round is kept; no relaxation. Without a coupling back into the study physics one background solve follows the study solve. Typically 5-20.

## Study type `optimization` - Optimization

Density-based topology optimisation over the design_region features: maximises J = the sum of weight * quantity of every adjoint_objective of every physics (weight -1 minimises), each physics at its own wavelength setting (several physics of one polarisation at different wavelengths share the permittivity arrays: one design region serves a broadband objective). Densities rho in [0, 1] are filtered, projected and mapped to eps (see design_region). scipy L-BFGS-B with bounds [0, 1] minimises -J / |J0| (J0 = J of the initial design); each evaluation writes the densities, solves every physics (scipy_splu reuses the previous factor as a GMRES preconditioner while the design changes little) and takes dJ/d eps from one transposed solve (eps_sensitivity). Stops at max_iterations, the tolerance or 5 x max_iterations evaluations, per continuation stage (iterations count on across stages, objective_initial is J at the first stage beta). Snapshots: the initial design (iteration 0) and every accepted iteration, labelled "iteration k: J = <value> W/m" (em_eme: no unit, a power fraction), plus "final: J = ..." when the last evaluated state differs; default stored fields include "<physics>.design_density"; afterwards the physics hold the returned design. Each design_region result is J and its grayness versus iteration; summary optimization {iterations, evaluations, design_cells, objective_initial, objective_final, continuation_stages, message}; ticks = iterations. Physics: em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz / em_fdfd_nonlinear / em_eme only; no couplings or state-dependent material properties. The gradient is exact for the discrete model except on source, port and objective lines (keep design regions off them); sigma_e, poles and mu_r of design cells are not optimised. em_fdfd_nonlinear: design_region writes eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy; objectives of its channels; the adjoint is one transposed solve per channel in reverse order (undepleted) or the transposed fixed point by GMRES (pump_depleted; no free carriers, and iteration_method newton with a chi3 medium); chi2 / chi3 tensors and poling stay fixed. em_eme (polarization ez or hz, section_tolerance 0): design_region (ez: eps_r; hz: eps_xx, eps_yy) and port power fraction objectives (unit 1); each evaluation re-solves the changed sections, dJ/d eps from the cascade adjoint (exact for n_modes 0).

- Needs a physics that steps in time: no

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `max_iterations` (int; default 20; [1, 10000]) - Maximum iterations
  L-BFGS-B iterations per continuation stage; each needs one or more evaluations (at most 5 x max_iterations in all), one evaluation = per FDFD physics one assembly, one solve and one transposed (adjoint) solve. Typical 20-200.
- `continuation_stages` [1] (int; default 1; [1, 20]) - Sharpening stages
  Beta continuation of the design_region projection: stage s (1 .. n) runs L-BFGS-B with projection_beta x beta_growth^(s - n), so the last uses the design_region value. 1 = none; projection_beta 0 regions stay unprojected. Typical 3-5 with a final beta 8-32.
- `beta_growth` [1] (default 2; > 1) - Sharpening growth
  Projection beta factor between consecutive continuation stages; typical 1.5-2.
- `tolerance` [1] (default 1e-05; >= 0) - Relative tolerance
  L-BFGS-B ftol on f = -J / |J0|: stop once an iteration lowers f by at most tolerance * max(|f|, 1); 0 runs all max_iterations. Typical 1e-4 to 1e-6.
- `live_update_hz` [Hz] (default 5; >= 0) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the GUI live field frames; 0 disables them. Never changes results (headless api.run sets 0).

## Study type `optomechanics` - Optomechanics

Vacuum optomechanical coupling g0 between optical and mechanical eigenmodes of one model: every solid_mechanics (or solid_mechanics_3d) physics with an optomechanical_coupling feature is mechanical, the physics those features name are optical (em_modes: cross-section modes at its wavelength setting; em_fdfd_ez / _hz: n_optical_resonances in-plane resonances near its wavelength setting; em_fdfd_bor on triangles: resonances of its azimuthal order(s), paired with an axisymmetric solid on triangles or a 3D solid on tetrahedra); every other physics runs as a stationary background physics first (an FDFD physics no feature names too), its couplings into the solved physics applied once; couplings or material properties reading a solid_mechanics, em_modes or em_fdfd_* physics are a validation error. Order: background, optical solves (the first coupling's optical mode is shown), the vibration modes of each solid (consistent mass, supports held at 0, prestressed only with stress_stiffening, which the tensor-mesh solid does not offer; a coupling with scattering backward makes the solid solve its guided 2.5D modes at k_z = 2 Re beta of that optical mode), the g0 table of every coupling, then one snapshot per mechanical mode labelled "mechanical mode k: f = <Hz> Hz, g0 / 2 pi = <Hz> Hz" (the first coupling's g0); default stored fields are the primary fields (mode shape, optical intensity); the solid field om_integrand (this study only) maps the moving-boundary g_om density of the shown mode; mode 1 stays shown, the optical physics keeps its selected mode. ticks = the mechanical snapshots, summary n_resonances.

- Needs a physics that steps in time: no; background study stationary

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `n_mechanical_modes` (int; default 6; [1, 100]) - Number of vibration modes
  Per solid with an optomechanical_coupling: the n + 4 eigenvalues omega^2 nearest (2 pi target_frequency)^2 (0 = the lowest), ranked by |omega - omega_target|; one g0 row and one snapshot each. 4-20 typical.
- `n_optical_resonances` (int; default 4; [1, 100]) - Number of optical resonances
  em_fdfd_ez / _hz / _bor optics only: resonances near its wavelength setting (eigenfrequency study rules; em_fdfd_bor per azimuthal order); optical_mode picks one. em_modes solves its n_modes modes.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; >= 1) - Maximum coupling iterations. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.max_iterations`
- `tolerance` [1] (default 0.0001; > 0) - Relative tolerance. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.tolerance`
- `relaxation` [1] (default 1; > 0) - Coupling relaxation. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; >= 0) - Coupling acceleration depth. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.anderson_depth`
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` [Hz] (default 5; >= 0) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the GUI live field frames; 0 disables them. Never changes results (headless api.run sets 0).

## Study type `stationary` - Stationary

Steady solve of every physics at t = 0; coupled physics repeat until the primary fields reach a fixed point (tolerance) or max_iterations. FDFD and em_eme types solve at their wavelength setting; with heat every iteration re-solves them at the latest temperature and hands their absorbed power to heat. EM FDTD: use time_dependent; em_modes: mode_analysis.

- Needs a physics that steps in time: no; StudySpec.adaptation allowed

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; >= 1) - Maximum coupling iterations
  Gauss-Seidel iterations over the physics of a coupling loop (model order, each coupling applied once its sources are solved); sinks (feeding no coupling back) are solved once afterwards; no loop = a single pass. Typically 10-50. Warns when the tolerance is not reached; stops early with a warning when the change has not decreased for 3 iterations (from iteration 4); non-finite fields fail the run.
- `tolerance` [1] (default 0.0001; > 0) - Relative tolerance
  Converged when every primary field of the loop physics changes by at most this fraction of its range max|f| (heat T as its rise T - T0). The remaining error is about change * g / (1 - g) for loop gain g (at g = 0.9, 1e-4 means ~1e-3); with anderson_depth about the change. Typically 1e-4.
- `relaxation` [1] (default 1; > 0) - Coupling relaxation. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; >= 0) - Coupling acceleration depth
  Anderson acceleration of the loop-back couplings (Walker-Ni, depth m, mixing parameter = relaxation): before each sweep every loop-back value becomes the least-squares combination of the last m iterates and changes (host float64, ~3 m + 3 copies per value); 0 = plain relaxation. A monotone loop of gain g needs ~ln(tolerance)/ln(g) Picard iterations (~120 at g = 0.9, 1e-6), far fewer accelerated. It can converge to fixed points Picard cannot reach (an unstable bistable branch, an unphysical one past a runaway), so it is opt-in. Typically 3-5.
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` [Hz] (default 5; >= 0) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the GUI live field frames; 0 disables them. Never changes results (headless api.run sets 0).
- `parity_sectors` (bool; default false) - Parity sectors. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.parity_sectors`

## Study type `thermal_noise` - Thermal noise

Thermorefractive noise of a z-invariant cross-section (fluctuation-dissipation theorem, Levin-type direct approach). Every heat physics (planar 2D, never CG-solved here, no temperature anchor needed) computes the one-sided PSD of X = integral w(x, y) g(z) exp(-j q0 z) dT dV of each thermorefractive_noise feature: S_X(f) = 4 k_B T0^2 integral dq/2pi |g~(q - q0)|^2 Re sum conj(w) u dA, where (j omega rho cp + k_zz q^2 - div k grad) u = w on the heat window (k, boundary conditions, held cells and losses as in a steady solve: held temperatures are ideal reservoirs that do not fluctuate, insulated faces are mirrors), one host SuperLU factorisation per (frequency, axial sample), or GPU line-block batches (the heat shifted solver: sparse_direct by default, or line_block). The temperature is uniform T0 (the heat T0 setting; a heated background is not supported). Every em_modes physics is solved first (its modes give the mode-pair weightings). particle_noise features solve the same way for dilute particles diffusing in a liquid (4 n0 instead of 4 k_B T0^2, diffusivity instead of k / rho cp). Couplings reading heat or em_modes: validation error. Results: one xy result per feature (psd versus frequency) with the exact total variance (sum rule k_B T0^2 integral |w|^2 / (rho cp) dV), its never-relaxing static part and the share of the rest inside the band; one snapshot per mode number after the mode solve (as in mode_analysis) and a final one labelled "thermal noise"; ticks = factorisations; summary noise_frequencies.

- Needs a physics that steps in time: no; background study stationary

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `frequency_start` [Hz] (default 1000; > 0) - Start frequency
  Range used when frequencies is empty. Below the slowest thermal relaxation rate the spectrum is flat. At q_z = 0 the mean temperature of an insulated region never relaxes: that share is the static_variance of the result, outside every band. Typical 1e2-1e4.
- `frequency_stop` [Hz] (default 1e+09; > 0) - Stop frequency
  Must exceed frequency_start. Above the fastest relaxation rate D q^2 / (2 pi) of the weighting the spectrum falls as 1/f^2 (water, q = 1.5e7 1/m: about 5 MHz). Typical 1e9-1e11.
- `n_frequencies` (int; default 31; >= 1) - Number of frequencies
  Both ends included, spaced as log_spacing selects (1 = the geometric or arithmetic mean). Each costs one sparse factorisation per axial sample of every thermorefractive_noise feature.
- `log_spacing` (bool; default true) - Logarithmic spacing
  true: evenly in log f (spectra spanning decades); false: evenly in f.
- `frequencies` [Hz] (float_list; > 0; nullable) - Frequency list
  Solved and reported in ascending order; a non-empty list overrides the range.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; >= 1) - Maximum coupling iterations. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.max_iterations`
- `tolerance` [1] (default 0.0001; > 0) - Relative tolerance. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.tolerance`
- `relaxation` [1] (default 1; > 0) - Coupling relaxation. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; >= 0) - Coupling acceleration depth. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.anderson_depth`
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` [Hz] (default 5; >= 0) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the GUI live field frames; 0 disables them. Never changes results (headless api.run sets 0).

## Study type `time_dependent` - Time dependent

Advances every physics in ticks of dt_sync, the smallest dt_limit of the physics (EM: its Courant step); a physics with every = n steps on every n-th tick over n * dt_sync. Couplings apply after every tick at their own every and are flushed at the end of the run, also on cancel.

- Needs a physics that steps in time: yes

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `duration` [s] (default 1e-13; > 0) - Duration
  The run stops at the tick nearest the duration. EM: typically 100-1000 fs, the pulse (2*t0 = 9/(pi*bandwidth*f0); ricker 8/f0) plus transit and ring-down (validation warns when it ends before the longest pulse, plus the domain diagonal * n_max / C0 with a flux, DFT, mode or far-field monitor); transient heat: ms to s.
- `output_interval` [s] (default 0; >= 0) - Output interval
  Between snapshots of the stored fields, from t = 0; 0 = n_snapshots evenly spaced. Intermediate snapshots stop past 1 GB; the final state is always stored.
- `n_snapshots` (int; default 20; >= 1) - Number of snapshots
  With output_interval 0: snapshots at t = 0, duration / (n_snapshots - 1), ..., the final state (1 = final only). Headless self-test runs store only the final state unless the model sets output_interval or n_snapshots (selftest examples: unless an analytic curve reads a snapshot).
- `live_update_hz` [Hz] (default 5; >= 0) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the GUI live field frames; 0 disables them. Never changes results (headless api.run sets 0).
- `parity_sectors` (bool; default false) - Parity sectors. Help: shared `eigenfrequency.parity_sectors`

## Templates

Worked examples that validate without errors (selftest templates_validate): modifying the closest one is the most reliable way to write a valid model. api.template(key) returns one as a ModelSpec, python -m open_sol template KEY FILE writes its model file.

Their model JSON is in api_templates.md beside this file (its Contents gives each template's line range; also describe('templates')). One line per template: key - label: description, then the physics types it uses (their feature types in parentheses), couplings, solver types and study.

- `dielectric_cylinder` - Dielectric cylinder: EM: a 550 nm gaussian point source scatters off a glass cylinder; field probe and transmitted flux spectrum. Uses physics em_fdtd_ez (point_source, field_probe, flux_monitor); study time_dependent.
- `gold_nanodisk` - Gold nanodisk: EM: TFSF plane wave on a Drude gold disk (uniform 2 nm mesh); near-field DFT and far-field pattern, 400-900 nm. Uses physics em_fdtd_ez (plane_wave_tfsf, dft_monitor, far_field); study time_dependent.
- `joule_heating` - Joule heating: EM + heat: a CW gaussian beam heats a gold disk in silica; Joule and thermo-optic couplings, 293.15 K walls. Uses physics em_fdtd_ez (gaussian_beam), heat (temperature, temperature_probe); couplings em_heat_joule, heat_em_thermo_optic; study time_dependent.
- `transient_heat_sink` - Transient heat sink: Heat (transient): a heater in a silicon block, convection on top, fixed temperature at the bottom. Uses physics heat (heat_source, convection, temperature, temperature_probe); study time_dependent.
- `nonlinear_conduction` - Nonlinear conduction: Heat (stationary): temperature-dependent conductivity k_300*(300/T)**1.3 around a heated core. Uses physics heat (heat_source, temperature); study stationary.
- `photoacoustic_disc` - Photoacoustic disc: elastic_waves (time_dependent): a 1 mm absorbing disc in water heated by a 100 ns pulse (heat_pulse_source, Grueneisen 0.2): the thermoelastic pressure (initial p0 = Grueneisen x absorbed energy density, ~35 kPa) leaves the disc as an N-shaped pulse recorded by a pressure probe 2 mm away. Uses physics elastic_waves (heat_pulse_source, field_probe); study time_dependent.
- `rigid_disk_scattering` - Rigid disk scattering (pressure acoustics): Axisymmetric pressure_acoustics: a thin rigid disk in a plane wave (scattered-field background, PMLs), the mean pressure on its top and bottom faces from k a = 0.05 to 0.3 (log sweep); the low-frequency pressure difference is (8 / 3 pi) k a p0. Uses physics pressure_acoustics (background_pressure_field, rigid_obstacle, surface_pressure); study frequency_response.
- `fresnel_interface` - Fresnel interface: EM: a 1 um gaussian pulse crosses a vacuum / glass (eps_r = 4) interface in a y-periodic strip; flux spectrum 0.9-1.1 um behind it (8/9 of a vacuum run). Uses physics em_fdtd_ez (line_source, flux_monitor); study time_dependent.
- `gold_nanodisk_hz` - Gold nanodisk (in-plane electric field): EM (H_z polarisation): TFSF plane wave with in-plane E on a Drude gold disk (uniform 2 nm mesh, 200 fs); near-field DFT of |E|^2 shows the particle plasmon, plus the far-field pattern, 400-900 nm. Uses physics em_fdtd_hz (plane_wave_tfsf, dft_monitor, far_field); study time_dependent.
- `directional_coupler` - Directional coupler (in-plane electric field): EM (H_z polarisation): two 0.3 um silicon strips in silica with a 4 um long, 0.2 um gap coupling section and cosine S-bends (uniform 20 nm mesh); a 1.55 um gaussian mode source in strip A and mode monitors give the through, cross and reflected power fractions (|S|^2) and phases, 1.45-1.65 um. Uses physics em_fdtd_hz (mode_monitor, mode_source); study time_dependent.
- `fd_joule_heating` - Joule heating of a gold nanowire (frequency domain): EM (FDFD, E_z) + heat, stationary study: a 530 nm gaussian beam heats a 30 nm gold nanowire in water by about 9 K; Joule and thermo-optic couplings, convection on the outer faces, max T and the absorbed power. Uses physics em_fdfd_ez (gaussian_beam), heat (convection, temperature_probe); couplings em_heat_joule, heat_em_thermo_optic; study stationary.
- `effective_index_rib_waveguide` - Rib waveguide (effective index 2.5D): EM (FDFD, H_z): top view of a 0.5 um silicon rib (220 nm rib on a 90 nm slab, silica above and below) collapsed by the effective-index method (effective_index features); a 1.55 um mode source and a mode monitor give the lateral mode index and transmission. Uses physics em_fdfd_hz (effective_index, mode_source, mode_monitor); study stationary.
- `disk_resonator_eigenmodes` - Disk resonator eigenmodes: EM FDFD (E_z), eigenfrequency study: the whispering-gallery resonances of a silicon disk (eps_r 12.11, radius r_disk = 1 um) in air nearest 1.55 um (6 resonances; each mode is a near-degenerate pair on the staircase disk), with wavelength, Q and field shape per resonance; derived lambda_1 and Q_1 of the nearest one. The same modes as the FDTD disk_resonator template (ring-down), without a source or a long run. Uses physics em_fdfd_ez (resonance_table); study eigenfrequency.
- `cylinder_harmonic_fdtd` - Dielectric cylinder, time-domain spectrum: EM FDTD (E_z) in a frequency_domain study (harmonic FDTD): one plane-wave pulse (TFSF box, 1 um, bandwidth 0.5) scatters off a dielectric cylinder (eps_r 4, radius r_cyl = 0.3 um) and gives the complex E_z phasor of every study wavelength 0.85-1.2 um (8 values, one snapshot each) from a single time-domain run; switch the physics to em_fdfd_ez for the same maps by one frequency-domain solve per wavelength. Uses physics em_fdtd_ez (plane_wave_tfsf); study frequency_domain.
- `waveguide_bend_optimization` - Waveguide bend optimization: EM FDFD (E_z) at 1.55 um, optimization study: a 0.28 um silicon strip in silica turns by 90 degrees inside a 1.2 x 1.2 um design region (density from silica to silicon, filter radius 80 nm, tanh projection reaching beta 8 by a continuation over 3 stages: beta 2, 4, 8, at most 25 L-BFGS-B iterations each). Objective: the mode 1 power leaving along +y (mode_power_positive). The design_density field is stored per iteration; the design_region result shows J and the grayness versus iteration. Uses physics em_fdfd_ez (mode_source, adjoint_objective, design_region); study optimization.
- `disk_resonator` - Disk resonator ring-down: EM (E_z): a 1.55 um gaussian pulse (bandwidth 0.2) from a line current inside a silicon disk (eps_r 12.11, radius 1 um) in air excites its whispering-gallery modes; a resonance_monitor near the rim lists their wavelengths, Q and amplitudes over 1.45-1.65 um from the 2 ps ring-down. Uses physics em_fdtd_ez (point_source, resonance_monitor); study time_dependent.
- `bloch_band_diagram` - Photonic crystal band diagram: EM (E_z): one unit cell of a square lattice of dielectric rods (eps_r 8.9, r = 0.2 a, a = 0.5 um), Bloch-periodic with bloch_kx = k_fraction 2 pi / a swept over 0-0.5 (Gamma-X); a point-source pulse and a resonance finder per k give the band frequencies (TM gap ~1.14-1.56 um). Uses physics em_fdtd_ez (point_source, resonance_monitor); study time_dependent.
- `fdfd_band_diagram` - Photonic crystal band diagram (frequency domain): EM (FDFD, E_z): the rod unit cell of bloch_band_diagram (eps_r 8.9, r = 0.2 a, a = 0.5 um), Bloch-periodic with bloch_kx = k_fraction 2 pi / a swept over 0-0.5 (Gamma-X); an eigenfrequency study per k lists the 6 band frequencies nearest 1.2 um (resonance_table), without time stepping or a resonance fit. Uses physics em_fdfd_ez (resonance_table); study eigenfrequency.
- `nonlinear_silicon_slab` - Nonlinear silicon slab: EM (E_z): a 1.55 um gaussian pulse of 1 GV/m peak crosses a 2 um silicon slab with Kerr (n2 6e-18 m^2/W), two-photon absorption (beta 8e-12 m/W) and TPA free carriers (lifetime 1 ns, FCA 1.45e-21 m^2, dn/dN -1.35e-27 m^3) in a y-periodic strip; transmitted flux spectrum, probe trace and the carrier_density map. Uses physics em_fdtd_ez (line_source, nonlinear_medium, flux_monitor, field_probe); study time_dependent.
- `phase_change_gst_switch` - GST phase-change switch: EM (E_z, frequency domain at 1.55 um) + transient heat, time dependent: a cw line source (3 MV/m) heats a 100 nm GST-225 film on 0.5 um of silica over a 293 K heat sink; em_heat_joule feeds the absorbed power to heat, heat_em_phase_change crystallises the film from its temperature history (more absorbing as it crystallises), and the FDFD re-solves after every heat step; crystallinity and T maps, film temperature and crystallinity traces. Uses physics em_fdfd_ez (line_source, phase_change_medium), heat (temperature, temperature_probe); couplings em_heat_joule, heat_em_phase_change; study time_dependent.
- `strip_waveguide_modes` - Strip waveguide modes: EM cross-section modes, mode_analysis: a 500 x 220 nm silicon strip in silica at 1.55 um (20 nm mesh, CPML on every side); mode table of 4 modes (n_eff, loss, TE fraction, effective area), derived n_eff_1 and te_fraction_1 (quasi-TE0: n_eff ~2.4, te_fraction ~1). Uses physics em_modes (mode_table); study mode_analysis.
- `thermo_optic_phase_shifter` - Thermo-optic phase shifter: Heat + EM cross-section modes, mode_analysis with a sweep over P_heater (0, 10, 20 W/m): a gold heater 1 um above a 500 x 220 nm silicon strip in silica, substrate face at 293.15 K; steady heat, heat_em_thermo_optic, then the modes on the heated permittivity; derived n_eff_1 (dn_eff ~5e-4 at 20 W/m: ~2 rad per mm) and T_core. Uses physics heat (temperature, heat_source), em_modes (mode_table); couplings heat_em_thermo_optic; study mode_analysis.
- `pn_phase_shifter_depletion` - PN phase shifter (prescribed carriers): EM cross-section modes, mode_analysis with a sweep over the reverse bias V_R (0, 2, 4 V): a 500 x 220 nm silicon rib on a 90 nm slab in silica with a lateral pn junction at its centre (N_A = N_D = 5e17 cm^-3). The carrier densities are prescribed by the depletion approximation in closed form (none inside the depletion width W(V_R), the doping outside) and enter eps_r / sigma_e of silicon through the Soref-Bennett plasma dispersion at 1.55 um; derived n_eff_1 and loss_1 (dB/cm) per bias (dn_eff ~1e-4 between 0 and 4 V). Uses physics em_modes (mode_table); study mode_analysis.
- `pn_phase_shifter_electrostatics` - PN phase shifter (electrostatics): Electrostatics + EM cross-section modes, mode_analysis with a sweep over V_R (0, 2, 4 V): the rib of 'pn_phase_shifter_depletion', but the electrostatics solves V of the depletion-approximation space charge between slab contacts at 0 V and V_bi + V_R, and the carriers follow V by Boltzmann statistics (n = N_D exp((V - V_bi - V_R) / V_T), p = N_A exp(-V / V_T), clamped at the doping): smooth depletion edges and the 2D field of the rib, read by eps_r / sigma_e (Soref-Bennett) as state-dependent materials; derived n_eff_1 and loss_1. Uses physics electrostatics (terminal, charge_density), em_modes (mode_table); study mode_analysis.
- `microdisk_bor_eigenmodes` - Microdisk whispering-gallery modes (axisymmetric): EM body-of-revolution FDFD, eigenfrequency study: the whispering-gallery resonances of azimuthal order m = 15 of a silicon microdisk (eps_r 12.11, radius r_disk = 1.5 um, 240 nm thick) in air nearest 1.55 um, solved on the (r, z) half plane above its equatorial plane (pmc mirror on z_lo: quasi-TE modes, E in the disk plane), cpml on r_hi and z_hi, 20 nm mesh. Wavelength, Q (radiation into the PML) and field per resonance; derived lambda_1 and Q_1. A full 3D answer at 2D cost; list several orders in azimuthal_orders (e.g. 14, 15, 16) for the free spectral range. Uses physics em_fdfd_bor (resonance_table); study eigenfrequency.
- `dipole_radiation_3d` - Dipole radiation (3D): em_fdtd_3d: a z-oriented electric dipole (1e-12 A m, gaussian pulse at 1 um) in a 1.2 um vacuum cube with CPML on all six faces; a flux box around it gives the radiated cw power, analytically eta0 k^2 (I l)^2 / (12 pi). Uses physics em_fdtd_3d (dipole_source, flux_box); study time_dependent.
- `photonic_crystal_slab_bands_3d` - Photonic crystal slab band diagram (3D): em_fdtd_3d: one unit cell of a square lattice of air holes (a = 0.5 um, r = 0.3 a) in a 0.275 um eps 12 slab with vacuum and CPML above and below, x / y periodic with bloch_kx = k_fraction 2 pi / a swept over 0-0.5 (Gamma-X); an in-plane dipole on the mid-plane and a resonance finder per k give the TE-like band frequencies and Q (guided below the light line, leaky above it). Uses physics em_fdtd_3d (dipole_source, resonance_monitor); study time_dependent.
- `pec_box_eigenmodes_3d` - PEC box cavity with a silicon cube: eigenmodes (3D): em_fdfd_3d: a 1.0 x 0.8 x 0.6 um vacuum box with pec walls on all six faces and a 0.3 um eps 12 cube at its centre; the eigenfrequency study finds the 4 resonances nearest 1.4 um (resonance table: wavelength, Q = inf for this lossless closed cavity) and their mode shapes on 40 nm cells (10 per wavelength in silicon). Uses physics em_fdfd_3d (resonance_table); study eigenfrequency.
- `nanobeam_mirror_cell_bands_3d` - Nanobeam mirror cell band diagram (3D, frequency domain): em_fdfd_3d: one mirror cell of a silicon nanobeam photonic crystal in D2O (period a = 394.3 nm, hole d = 279.3 nm along y through a 595.2 x 220 nm beam, n 3.47 / 1.32), quarter cross-section (x_lo antisymmetric = PEC plane, y_lo symmetric = PMC plane: the TE-like sector), 300 nm D2O and 8 CPML cells on x_hi / y_hi, z periodic with bloch_kz = k_fraction 2 pi / a swept over 0.4-0.5 (guided, below the D2O light line); an eigenfrequency study per k lists the 4 bands nearest 1.496 um (resonance_table). At k_fraction 0.5 the dielectric (longer wavelength) and air band edges bound the TE-like gap that should contain 1.496 um; set a and d to a taper cell to follow the band-edge grading. a / 16 cells (24.6 nm) with subpixel smoothing, ~4e4 unknowns per k (one host factor each, minutes); more padding mainly raises the guided-band Q (the evanescent tail reaches the CPML). Uses physics em_fdfd_3d (resonance_table); study eigenfrequency.
- `linear_taper_eme` - Linear taper (EME): EME, stationary: a 10 um linear taper from a 0.5 um to a 2 um wide guide (eps 4 in silica, ez, 1.55 um, 25 nm mesh, cpml on y, pec x faces); eme_ports with the fundamental incident from x_lo, the section table, derived T1 = transmission into the fundamental of the wide guide, and eme_length_sweep: T1 versus the taper length from 2.5 to 40 um, re-cascaded from the one solve. Uses physics em_eme (eme_ports, eme_section_table, eme_length_sweep); study stationary.
- `mmi_1x2_eme` - 1 x 2 MMI splitter (EME): EME, stationary, ez at 1.55 um: a centre-fed 1 x 2 multimode interference splitter (eps 4 in silica, 25 nm mesh, cpml on y, pec x faces): a 1 um input guide, a 3 um wide MMI section of length L_mmi (parameter, 7.3 um = 3 L_pi / 8 for the two-fold symmetric image, L_pi = 4 n_r W_e^2 / (3 lambda) with the effective width W_e ~ 3.36 um) and two 1 um output guides centred at +-0.75 um. The output port modes are the supermodes of the guide pair, so T1 (symmetric supermode) is the power split equally into both outputs and the antisymmetric one stays ~0 by symmetry. Beat-length check: the section table lists n_eff_1 / n_eff_2 of the MMI section (its two lowest, even and odd modes), and L_pi = lambda / (2 (n_eff_1 - n_eff_2)) of those modes is exact for the EME, which propagates every section mode with its own beta; set L_mmi = 3 L_pi / 8 from it to tune the splitter. Uses physics em_eme (eme_ports, eme_section_table); study stationary.
- `thermo_optic_phase_shifter_eme_3d` - Thermo-optic phase shifter (EME 3D): Heat + em_eme_3d, stationary: a 0.5 x 0.2 um silicon strip in silica running 20 um along z, a 1.5 x 0.2 um heater region 1 um above it from z = 5 to 15 um dissipating P_heater (parameter, 1 mW), the substrate face y_lo at 293.15 K; steady heat, heat_em_thermo_optic, then the EME of the heated guide (pec transverse walls of the 4 x 3 um box, 50 nm cells, 10 modes, section_tolerance 1e-4: heated layers within about 1 K of a section's first layer merge into it, a staircase of a few percent of the phase shift). The transmission row of the eme_ports table gives the phase of S21 (sweep P_heater to get the phase shift, about 0.1 rad per mW here); derived T1 and the mean core temperature. Uses physics heat (temperature, heat_source), em_eme_3d (eme_ports, eme_section_table); couplings heat_em_thermo_optic; solvers pcg; study stationary.
- `heated_microchannel` - Heated microchannel: Laminar flow + heat, stationary: water flows (parabolic inflow, mean U_in = 2 mm/s) through a 20 um channel in a silica chip past a 60 x 6 um heater (Q_heater, ~7 W/m) 10 um above it; fluid_heat_convection carries the heat downstream; derived T_max, T_outlet (mean water temperature at the outlet) and U_max. Uses physics laminar_flow (inlet_velocity, pressure), heat (temperature, heat_source); couplings fluid_heat_convection; study stationary.
- `heated_slab` - Heated slab: Heat (stationary): a 1 mm slab with a uniform 1e+09 W/m^3 source between two 300 K walls; peak rise Q L^2 / (8 k) = 62.5 K. Uses physics heat (temperature, heat_source); study stationary.
- `heated_chip_3d` - Heated chip (3D): Heat (stationary, 3D): a 1 x 1 x 0.5 mm silicon block (k = 130 W/(m*K)) on a 300 K heat sink (z_lo) with a 0.4 mm square chip dissipating 0.8 W in its top 50 um, convection on z_hi; derived value T_max. Uses physics heat (temperature, convection, heat_source); study stationary.
- `waveguide_thermal_noise` - Waveguide thermal noise: thermal_noise study of a 480 x 220 nm silicon strip in silica (library materials) at 1550 nm: em_modes on the half cross-section (x_lo antisymmetric mirror through the strip centre, quasi-TE family; em CPML on the other faces) and heat with the substrate sink T = 293.15 K on y_lo (2 um below the strip), other faces insulated. One thermorefractive_noise feature on all cells (mode_pair: the quasi-TE mode backscattered into itself, q0 = 2 beta, uniform over 1 mm): psd in 1/Hz (backscattered power per incident power per Hz) with the silica and silicon self terms and their cross term. 29 log-spaced frequencies 1000..1e+10 Hz, uniform 20 nm mesh; derived values n_eff_1 and the PSD at 1 MHz. Uses physics em_modes, heat (temperature, thermorefractive_noise); study thermal_noise.
- `flux_concentrator_needle` - Flux-concentrator needle: Magnetostatics, axisymmetric, stationary sweep: a Metglas needle (r = 31 um, l = 15 mm, mu_dc 1e5) in a uniform axial field B_ext = 1e-4 T concentrates the flux at its tip; derived B_sensor (mean |B| over a 31 um disc a gap below the tip) and gain = B_sensor / B_ext (EF = 20 log10(gain) dB), swept over gap = 25 .. 400 um. Uses physics magnetostatics (external_field); solvers pcg; study stationary.
- `iron_c_core_saturation` - Iron C-core saturation: Magnetostatics on a triangle mesh, planar, stationary sweep: an iron C-core (80 x 60 mm, 10 mm limbs, mu_dc 4000, saturation_polarization 1.8 T) with a gap_width = 2 mm air gap in its right limb, driven by a 200-turn coil around the left limb (go and return sides as two coil features); I_coil swept 0.5 .. 32 A. Derived B_gap = mean |B| in the gap against the ideal mu0 N I / g (analytic curve, valid below the knee: the core reluctance takes ~3 %); Newton (nonlinear_method auto) solves the saturation. Uses physics magnetostatics (coil); study stationary.
- `busbar_proximity` - Busbar pair, proximity effect: Magnetic fields AC, planar, stationary sweep over the frequency f = 50 Hz .. 20 kHz: two copper bars 10 x 2 mm (wide faces 2 mm apart) carry +I and -I (solid conductors, prescribed current 100 A): the current crowds onto the facing surfaces. Derived R_loop, L_loop (per m of length) and the loss P per m. Uses physics magnetic_fields_ac (coil); study stationary.
- `flux_concentrator_needle_ac` - Flux-concentrator needle, AC: Magnetic fields AC, axisymmetric, stationary sweep over the frequency f = 10 Hz .. 30 kHz: the flux_concentrator_needle model (Metglas needle r = 31 um, l = 15 mm, mu_dc 1e5, applied axial field amplitude B_ext = 1e-4 T) with the needle conductivity sigma_needle = 7e5 S/m and magnetic loss mu_dc_loss = loss_tangent mu_dc: eddy currents screen the needle once the skin depth falls below its radius (~1 kHz), so the gain = B_sensor / B_ext (mean |B| over a 31 um disc a gap = 100 um below the tip; EF = 20 log10(gain) dB) drops with frequency. Uses physics magnetic_fields_ac (external_field); study stationary.
- `needle_3d` - Flux concentrator needle (3D): Magnetostatics (3D, stationary): a 15 mm x 125 um x 25 um Metglas needle (mu_dc 1e5) along z in a uniform axial field B_ext (external_field, 10 x 10 x 35 mm window held at the applied potential), the geometry of Carey et al. 2026 on coarse 25 um cells around the needle and its lower tip (graded by 1.3 to 1 mm, by 1.5 to 2 mm outside). Derived values: gain_h50 = mean |B| / B_ext over a sensor box 50 um below the tip and EF_h50 = 20 log10(gain) against the prolate-spheroid estimate (Eq. 2 with m = l / sqrt(w t)); line curve B_axis: |B| on the needle axis below the tip against Eq. 2. The converged, paper-matched run is experiments/Ben_flux/needle_3d_scalar_potential. Uses physics magnetostatics_3d (external_field); study stationary.
- `heated_chip_stress_3d` - Heated chip stress (3D): Heat + solid mechanics 3D, stationary: a 1 x 1 x 0.5 mm silicon block on a 300 K heat sink (z_lo, also clamped) with a 0.4 mm square chip dissipating 0.8 W in its top 50 um, convection on z_hi; heat_solid_thermal_strain hands the temperature rise to the solid; derived T_max, von_mises_max, u_z_max. Uses physics heat (temperature, convection, heat_source), solid_mechanics_3d (fixed); couplings heat_solid_thermal_strain; study stationary.
- `solid_bloch_band_diagram_3d` - Phononic nanobeam band diagram (3D): Solid mechanics 3D on builtin tetrahedra: one unit cell (a = 0.5 um) of a free-standing silicon nanobeam (0.25 x 0.25 um core) with a 0.75 um wide wing over the middle half of the period, periodic along x with bloch_kx = k_fraction 2 pi / a swept over 0-0.5 (Gamma-X); an eigenfrequency study per k lists the 8 bands nearest 4 GHz (resonance_table; target > 0 drops the rigid modes at Gamma). The bands per k form the band diagram; gaps between them are the phononic band gaps of the corrugation. mode_shapes keeps every mode on the beam surface per k (View in browser on the canvas showing a solid field, or show <run dir> --html: animated modes beside the band diagram). Uses physics solid_mechanics_3d (resonance_table, mode_shapes); study eigenfrequency.
- `heated_waveguide_stress` - Heated waveguide stress: Heat + solid mechanics (plane strain), stationary: cross-section of a 0.48 x 0.22 um silicon waveguide in silica under a 2 x 0.2 um gold heater (P_heater = 20 W/m), substrate y_lo held at 293.15 K and clamped, rollers on the sides; heat_solid_thermal_strain hands the temperature rise (~5 K at the core) to the solid; derived T_core, stress_xx_core, stress_yy_core, von_mises_max. Uses physics heat (heat_source, temperature, convection), solid_mechanics (fixed, roller); couplings heat_solid_thermal_strain; study stationary.
- `silicon_beam_thermoelastic_damping` - Silicon beam thermoelastic damping: Solid mechanics (plane stress), eigenfrequency: half of a simply supported library-silicon beam (h = 2 um, L = 80 um, mirror roller at mid-span), its symmetric flexural modes with a resonance table and the thermoelastic_damping table (Q_TED per mode, T0 293.15 K); derived f_1 (1.19 MHz) and Q_ted_1 (1.3e5: far below the Debye peak, omega tau ~0.04; the 3rd and 5th flexural modes at 10.7 / 29 MHz reach 1.7e4 / 1.0e4, the peak Delta / 2 ~ 1e-4 sits near omega tau = 1; a lower k_beam or a thicker beam moves the fundamental towards it). Uses physics solid_mechanics (displacement, roller, resonance_table, thermoelastic_damping); study eigenfrequency.
- `solid_bloch_band_diagram` - Phononic crystal band diagram (2D): Solid mechanics (2D, plane strain) on a quadratic triangle mesh: one unit cell (a = 1 um) of a square lattice of circular holes (radius 0.35 a) in silicon, periodic along x and y with bloch_kx = k_fraction pi / a swept over 0-1 (Gamma-X) and bloch_ky 0; an eigenfrequency study per k lists the 8 bands nearest 1 GHz (resonance_table; the target > 0 drops the two rigid translations at Gamma). The bands per k form the in-plane band diagram; gaps between them are the phononic band gaps of the lattice. Uses physics solid_mechanics (resonance_table); study eigenfrequency.
- `silicon_ring_breathing_g0` - Silicon ring breathing g0: Optomechanics study: quasi-TE0 mode (em_modes, 1.55 um, group index) and the lowest in-plane vibration modes of a suspended 450 x 220 nm silicon strip (quarter domain with mirrors and rollers), optomechanical_coupling table of g0 / 2 pi (moving boundary, photoelastic, total) for a ring of R = 10 um (length 2 pi R). Uses physics em_modes (mode_table), solid_mechanics (roller, optomechanical_coupling); study optomechanics.
- `silicon_disk_wgm_g0` - Silicon disk breathing g0: Optomechanics study: in-plane whispering-gallery resonance (em_fdfd_hz eigen-solve near 1.55 um, quarter domain with mirrors) and the vibration modes of a 2D silicon disk of R = 1.5 um in air (plane strain, rollers on the mirror faces), optomechanical_coupling table of g0 / 2 pi (moving boundary, photoelastic, total) for a 220 nm thick disk (length). Uses physics em_fdfd_hz, solid_mechanics (roller, optomechanical_coupling); study optomechanics.
- `silicon_nitride_membrane_modes` - Silicon nitride membrane modes: A 1 x 0.7 mm silicon nitride membrane (50 nm film at 1 GPa stress: tension 50 N/m, areal density 1.55e-4 kg/m^2) clamped on its frame: the six lowest drum modes on quadratic triangles, f_mn = (c / 2) sqrt((m / a)^2 + (n / b)^2) with c = sqrt(T / rho_s) = 568 m/s (f_11 = 495 kHz), listed by the resonance table. Uses physics membrane (clamped, resonance_table); study eigenfrequency.
- `ppln_slab_shg` - PPLN slab waveguide SHG (QPM tuning curve): Nonlinear FDFD (undepleted): a 1550 nm mode pumps a periodically poled z-cut lithium niobate slab in silica; sweep of the poling period over the QPM peak, forward second-harmonic mode power vs the coupled-mode sinc^2 curve. Uses physics em_fdfd_nonlinear (harmonic_channel, chi2_medium, mode_source, mode_monitor); study nonlinear_frequency_domain.
- `gaas_disk_shg` - GaAs disk SHG (mixed polarisation): Nonlinear FDFD (undepleted): an H_z plane wave at 1550 nm on a GaAs disk generates an E_z second harmonic through d14; sweep of the crystal angle (90 degree period), SH far field. Uses physics em_fdfd_nonlinear (harmonic_channel, chi2_medium, plane_wave_tfsf, far_field); study nonlinear_frequency_domain.
- `silicon_thg_waveguide` - Silicon slab waveguide THG (absorbing silicon): Nonlinear FDFD (undepleted chi3): a guided pump mode in a silicon slab waveguide generates the third harmonic in dispersive, absorbing silicon; sweep of the pump wavelength, forward and backward third-harmonic power. Uses physics em_fdfd_nonlinear (harmonic_channel, chi3_medium, mode_source, mode_monitor, flux_monitor); study nonlinear_frequency_domain.
- `shg_saturation_tanh` - Pump-depleted SHG saturation (tanh^2): Nonlinear FDFD (pump depleted, Newton-Krylov): phase-matched second-harmonic generation in a periodic strip with the pump amplitude swept into saturation; SH and depleted pump amplitudes against the coupled-mode tanh and sech curves. Uses physics em_fdfd_nonlinear (harmonic_channel, chi2_medium, line_source, field_probe); study nonlinear_frequency_domain.
- `silicon_fwm_waveguide` - Silicon waveguide FWM with TPA and free carriers: Nonlinear FDFD (pump depleted, Newton-Krylov): degenerate four-wave mixing in a silicon slab waveguide with two-photon and free-carrier absorption; sweep of the pump power, idler conversion and the nonlinear losses. Uses physics em_fdfd_nonlinear (harmonic_channel, chi3_medium, mode_source, mode_monitor); study nonlinear_frequency_domain.
- `gold_ridge_surface_shg` - Gold ridge surface SHG: Nonlinear FDFD (undepleted, surface chi2): an in-plane polarised 1550 nm plane wave on a gold ridge generates second harmonic at the metal surface; sweep of the ridge width, SH power and far field. Uses physics em_fdfd_nonlinear (harmonic_channel, surface_chi2, plane_wave_tfsf, far_field); study nonlinear_frequency_domain.
- `graphene_thg_grating` - Graphene on a nitride grating: THG: Nonlinear FDFD (undepleted, sigma3 sheet): third harmonic of graphene on a silicon nitride grating; pump wavelength sweep across the guided-mode resonance, TH power up and down. Uses physics em_fdfd_nonlinear (harmonic_channel, conducting_sheet, sheet_nonlinearity, line_source, flux_monitor); study nonlinear_frequency_domain.
- `shg_metasurface_optimization` - Inverse-designed SHG metasurface: em_fdfd_nonlinear (E_z channels p at 1.55 um and sh = 2 p, undepleted cascade), optimization study: a y-periodic 0.5 um cell with a 0.3 um z-cut lithium niobate film (d33 25 pm/V, eps 4.58) on silica, pumped at normal incidence by a 1e7 V/m line source in air. A 0.8 um design layer on the film (density from air to silicon nitride, eps 1 .. 4, filter radius 60 nm, tanh projection reaching beta 8 over 3 continuation stages, at most 30 L-BFGS-B iterations each) is shaped to maximise the second-harmonic flux transmitted into the silica (adjoint_objective of channel sh): the layer focuses and phase-matches the pump in the film. The design_density field is stored per iteration; the design_region result shows J and the grayness versus iteration. 2D: powers per unit length in z. Uses physics em_fdfd_nonlinear (harmonic_channel, chi2_medium, line_source, adjoint_objective, design_region); study optimization.
- `thermo_optic_heater` - Thermo-optic heater: Electric currents + heat + EM FDFD (E_z), stationary: a gold strip heater (1 x 8.8 um, V_heater = 0.02 V, sigma_dc(T)) 1.52 um beside a 0.48 um silicon slab waveguide in silica; Joule heating (~2 kW/m), out-of-plane sink (7e5 W/(m^2 K) through 1 um: heater rise ~60-80 K, waveguide ~20 K), thermo-optic phase of the guided mode (~0.1 rad, mode_monitor phase_positive); derived P_heater, T_max, T_waveguide. Uses physics em_fdfd_ez (mode_source, mode_monitor), heat (out_of_plane_convection, temperature_probe), electric_currents (terminal); couplings currents_heat_joule, heat_em_thermo_optic; study stationary.
- `silicon_pn_photodiode` - Silicon pin photodiode: drift_diffusion, stationary: a lateral p+ / i / n+ silicon diode (4 x 0.2 um, 10 nm cells) reverse-biased by V_reverse = 1 V, with a uniform generation G_light = 1e27 1/(m^3 s) in the 2 um intrinsic absorber (photocurrent ~ q G A = 6.4e-5 A/m, read from the contact tables); derived R_total. Uses physics drift_diffusion (doping, ohmic_contact, generation); study stationary.
- `induction_billet` - Induction heating of a billet: Magnetic fields AC + heat, axisymmetric, time-dependent: a 20-turn coil carrying I = 300 A peak at f = 1 kHz heats an aluminium billet (r = 20 mm, 60 mm tall) by eddy currents in its skin (delta ~2.7 mm); the eddy loss feeds transient heat for 20 s through magnetic_heat_induction. Probes record the surface and core temperature; derived the eddy loss P [W], the coil resistance and inductance and the hottest billet temperature. Uses physics magnetic_fields_ac (coil), heat (temperature, temperature_probe); couplings magnetic_heat_induction; study time_dependent.
- `yz_ln_saw_idt` - SAW from an IDT on YZ lithium niobate: Electrostatics + elastic_waves with electrostatics_acoustics_piezo (time_dependent): a 5-pair interdigital transducer (period 20 um, two driven terminals at +1 / -1 V, gaussian at f = v_R / period = 174 MHz, bandwidth 0.2) on a YZ lithium niobate substrate (a crystal entry, euler_deg 0, 90, 90: propagation along crystal Z, surface normal Y) launches surface acoustic waves; vy probes on the surface 100 and 200 um from the IDT. The literature Rayleigh velocity is ~3488 m/s (free surface); the coupling is two-way (bound charge: piezoelectric stiffening included, one electrostatics solve per acoustic step) and the in-plane c26 = c14 is stepped, so the remaining deviation is mesh dispersion (~20 cells per SAW wavelength) and the crystal data. Uses physics elastic_waves (field_probe), electrostatics (terminal); couplings electrostatics_acoustics_piezo; study time_dependent.
- `tfln_acousto_optic_modulator` - Thin-film lithium niobate acousto-optic modulator: Elastic_waves + electrostatics + EM FDFD (H_z), time_dependent, in the sagittal plane: a 3-pair interdigital transducer (period 4.4 um, terminals at +V_drive / -V_drive, cw at f = 3400 m/s / period = 773 MHz) on a 1 um Y-cut lithium niobate film (crystal entry, euler_deg 0, 90, 90: SAW along crystal Z, surface normal Y; eps_xx = n_e^2, eps_r = n_o^2) on silica launches a surface acoustic wave (two-way piezoelectric coupling) along the film, which also guides 1.55 um TM light along x: a mode_source (mode 1) left of the IDT, mode_monitors of modes 1 and 2 near the right end. acoustics_em_acousto_optic (rotated photoelastic tensor: the diagonal rows and the eps_xy row of the shear and normal strains) and electrostatics_em_pockels (clamped r of the IDT field and of the SAW piezoelectric field, r51 into eps_xy) feed the optics, which re-solves every 100 acoustic steps on the frozen state (stroboscopic snapshots). The period aims at TM0 -> TM1 phase matching, period = lambda / (n_eff,1 - n_eff,2), from slab estimates (n_eff ~2.08 / ~1.73); the template is not tuned by a run: read n_eff of both monitors and the SAW speed from the surface vy probe, then adjust the finger geometry and the frequency. Derived values: through_fraction and converted_fraction (mode 2) of the last solve. Not modelled: metal of the fingers in the optics (vacuum there), eps_xy in the port modes (they follow the strained diagonal eps of their line), acoustic and optical loss. Cost: ~6000 acoustic steps, each with an electrostatics solve, and ~60 sparse direct solves. Uses physics elastic_waves (field_probe), electrostatics (terminal), em_fdfd_hz (mode_source, mode_monitor); couplings electrostatics_acoustics_piezo, acoustics_em_acousto_optic, electrostatics_em_pockels; study time_dependent.
- `ln_phase_modulator` - Lithium niobate phase modulator: Electrostatics + EM FDFD (H_z) with the Pockels coupling, stationary, sweep over V_bias (0, 50, 100 V): an x-cut lithium niobate slab waveguide (1 um, along y, optic axis along x) in silica between two 10 um electrodes (terminals at +V_bias/2 and -V_bias/2, 3 um gap; pec_domain in the EM); derived phase (mode_monitor phase_positive) and E_x_core per value. Uniform-field estimate E = V / gap: V_pi L = lambda gap / (n_e^3 r33) = 1.5 V cm, 0.20 rad at 100 V; the silica gap (eps_dc 3.9 against 28 in the core) takes most of the voltage, so expect ~5x less (series estimate E = V / (w + (gap - w) 28 / 3.9)). Uses physics em_fdfd_hz (mode_source, mode_monitor, pec_domain), electrostatics (terminal); couplings electrostatics_em_pockels; study stationary.

## Results, reports and files

The user runs the commands; every command writes report files, which agents read instead of terminal output: check.json, summary.json, log.txt and figures/*.png. Arrays stay in results.npz for further processing.

Registered selftest cases are not listed here: describe('selftests') (python -m open_sol describe selftests) gives each name, label and what it checks, python -m open_sol selftest --list the names.

### Command line

- Run the commands from the folder that contains the open_sol package (python -m open_sol ...).
- describe [topic] [--out FILE | --update-reference] [--json]: this reference, or one topic, on stdout or into FILE; --update-reference rewrites api_reference.md and api_templates.md next to the package (full text only: no topic, no --json).
- template KEY [FILE] [--force]: write the template KEY (see Templates) as a model JSON file, default ./KEY.json; an existing file is overwritten only with --force.
- check MODEL.json [--out DIR] [--set NAME=EXPR ...] [--backend auto|gpu|cpu] [--max-wall-time S] [--json]: CPU-only validation, mesh, memory and run-time estimates, time step and step count -> check.json; --max-wall-time S warns when even the shortest estimated run time exceeds S seconds.
- profile [--backend gpu|cpu] [--quick]: measure this machine for the run-time estimates (~30 s, --quick ~5 s with coarser curves) -> time_profiles/time_profile_<backend>.json next to the package (OPEN_SOL_PROFILE_DIR overrides the folder); default every available backend (cpu, and gpu when a CUDA device answers); prints each task's wall time and the stored profile's.
- run MODEL.json [--out DIR] [--figures] [--max-wall-time S] [--no-arrays] [--set NAME=EXPR ...] [--backend auto|gpu|cpu] [--json]: build and run on the model's backend (GPU or CPU) -> summary.json, log.txt, results.npz (not with --no-arrays), model.json (the model as given) and figures/*.png (with --figures: <key>.png per saved field and feature result, derived_<plot>.png per derived curve plot, <result>_vs_<column or row>.png per table x_column of its curves, curve_<name>.png per line curve, scene_3d.png for a 3D model: perspective picture of the objects with the first saved field on the x, y and z cut planes through the window middle); --max-wall-time stops cleanly with status timeout and partial results.
- show PATH [--out DIR] [--figures] [--series NAME] [--html [FILE]] [--what NAME] [--fields LIST] [--no-geometry] [--set NAME=EXPR ...] [--backend auto|gpu|cpu] [--json]: outline and check counts of a model file, or the summary of a results directory (--figures re-renders its figures into <out>/figures/*.png, by default the run directory's figures/, a sweep also its sweep_*.png overlays; --series NAME draws only that series of xy results and sweep overlays; a 3D run directory draws scene_3d.png with its saved cut planes: the mid-height z cut and the stored cuts of the last snapshot) -> show.json. A 3D model file with --figures gets <out>/figures/scene_3d.png, the objects only (CPU, no run; api.scene_figure). --html [FILE] (results directory) writes the self-contained web page of --what NAME (Results.export_html: a field, a dft_fields or a mode_shapes result; default the only mode_shapes result) to <out>/<model stem>_<what>.html (_modes.html without --what; a field page carries the model objects, shown or hidden on the page, unless --no-geometry; a mode page takes the kept stress / strain, --fields stress,strain | stress | strain | none choosing them); exit 1 when there is nothing to show.
- --set NAME=EXPR (repeatable) replaces the expression of the model parameter NAME for this command only (the file is not changed; run records it in model.json), e.g. --set P_in=2e3 --set "w=450*nm"; an unknown NAME is a model error at the parameters node. --backend (check, run, show) overrides the model's solver_defaults.backend for this command only (run records it in model.json).
- mesh-study [PART ...] [--out DIR] [--case CASE ...] [--fine] [--force | --retry-failed] [--max-cells N] [--max-wall-time S]: the mesh study (parts per_physics, audit, prototypes (CPU), accuracy, pcg, line_block (GPU), analyse; default all, in this order) -> DIR (default ./mesh_study_out) records/, runs/, tables/, figures/ and mesh_study_report.json; recorded variants are skipped unless --force (all) or --retry-failed (those that did not complete); --max-cells skips larger variants (default 2e7); exit 1 when a part raised.
- selftest [NAME ...] [--heavy | --all] [--out DIR] [--reset] [--json] [--list]: the built-in checks, then the registered analytic cases (the named ones, heavy or not; else the non-heavy ones, with --heavy only the heavy ones, with --all every one) -> selftest_report_light.json, selftest_report_heavy.json (--all: both) or selftest_report_named.json (names given), plus one <case>/<run>/ run directory per run; a run rewrites only its own report files. A case is heavy when it took >= 5 s (--list marks them). --all (no NAMEs) runs everything: every case with its gpu runs and variants (with a usable GPU), then the --examples run (each example once, on its own backend) -> also selftest_report_analytic.json and examples/ run directories; exit 1 unless the cases and the examples passed.
- Reuse: <out>/selftest_cache.json keeps per case / example its last passing record (example: also no_tolerance), the hashes of the package code units that run depended on (each top-level function and class with methods, and each file's module-level code incl. data classes, compared without comments and docstrings: the units that ran, those they name, and the module-level code of every file touched) and the environment (Python, numpy, scipy, cupy, backends, device); an unnamed case or example whose units, model file and environment are unchanged is not rerun: its stored record enters the report with reused true, reused_from [time], and is not printed. --reset reruns every selected one; named ones always rerun. Run under a debugger or coverage tracer nothing is traced and nothing new is cached. The cache also keeps the last run time of every case / example.
- Output: per phase (the cases, each examples run) one line with the number to run and the number cached; per run test a start line "i/n  ~T left  name  (last T)" (i over every phase of the call, T left = the summed last run times of it and every later test, "+ k untimed" for those never timed) and a result line (PASS / FAIL / ERROR / NOTOL, error and tolerance or worst error / tolerance, wall seconds), plus the message of a test that did not pass.
- selftest --examples [NAME ...] [--out DIR] [--reset] [--json]: instead of the cases, run every examples/**/*.json of a repository checkout that has a derived value with a reference or an analytic curve on its own backend (NAMEs: only these, relative path with or without .json, or stem), two lines per example (Output) -> selftest_report_analytic.json plus one examples/<path>/ run directory each (no arrays, no figures); exit 1 when an example fails a tolerance or does not complete.
- check, run, show and selftest write their report files in every case, also when a build or run fails; --json also prints the report on stdout.
- Default --out: check and run '<model dir>/<model stem>_out/'; show of a model file the same, of a results directory that directory; selftest './selftest_out'. Directories are created as needed; files are overwritten.

### Exit codes

- 0: success (check without errors, run completed, every selftest passed, describe / template / show done).
- 1: model errors (check), a run status other than completed, a failed or erroring selftest, an incomplete documentation table (describe).
- 2: usage errors: bad arguments, a missing model file, an unknown describe topic, template key or selftest name, an existing template FILE without --force.

### JSON files

- UTF-8 with ASCII escapes, indent 2. Non-finite floats are the strings "nan", "inf" and "-inf"; tuples become lists; node paths are lists of strings.
- Issue record: {level (error | warning | info), path [...], node (the path label, e.g. "feature em/source"), message}.

### check.json

- {open_sol_version, status (ok | warnings | errors), model {title, file (null for a spec not read from a file)}, n_errors, n_warnings, n_infos, issues [issue records], mesh, mesh_error, meshes, transfers, study, memory_estimate, time_estimate, solvers}.
- time_estimate: the run-time estimate on this machine's stored profile (CLI profile; seconds_low / seconds_guess / seconds_high, its items), also given as an info issue at ("study",); null without a profile or an estimate (the info says why). Its build: the same keys for building every run (build stages, upload, triangle meshing: a mesh that does not change between sweep values is made once), null when it fails; the build log line "Build estimate" compares it with the measured stage times.
- meshes [{name, kind, mode, shape ([nx, ny] or [nx, ny, nz], null for triangles or without an estimate), elements (triangles: estimated count, else null), cells, dx_min, dx_max, max_ratio (resolved), physics (names on it), used, gpu_bytes, host_bytes (its share of memory_estimate, null without one), error (its estimate failure or null)}] per MeshSpec; transfers [{coupling, source_mesh, target_mesh, kind (interpolate | conservative), nnz, bytes}] of the couplings across meshes.
- solvers {physics: {role: {type, solver (the solver node, null = Automatic), backend, precision, settings}} of the roles the study uses, or null when they do not resolve (see the issues)}, or null when the model does not load.
- mesh = the first used mesh: {nx, ny, nz (1 in 2D), name, kind, n_cells, dx_min, dx_max, dt, npml_sides, uniform, note, wavelength_min, wavelength_source, auto_rule, custom_axes, line_blocks, line_block_hint} (triangles: nx / ny null plus n_elements, n_nodes, n_edges, pml_widths; counts include the PML cells; auto mode: auto_rule wavelength / physics / uniform_flow, the resolved wavelength_min in m and its source, "mesh" for the setting or the physics name, else null and ""; custom_axes = the axes whose cells come from MeshSpec.axes edges / segments; line_blocks {block axis: [n_blocks, block_size]} of the window cells for the line_block solver, a block along x = one grid row, and line_block_hint its cost n_blocks * block_size^3 per block axis with the cheaper one; both empty in 3D), or null with mesh_error giving the reason.
- study {type, dt_estimate (s or null: the smallest of the mesh Courant dt and the time_step of every time-stepping physics), n_steps (round(duration / dt_estimate) when the study has a duration, else null), n_sweep_values (1 without a sweep), total_steps (n_steps * n_sweep_values, or null), n_wavelengths (frequency_domain: the number of wavelengths solved per sweep value, else null)}.
- memory_estimate {gpu_steady (bytes of GPU pool memory the build keeps), gpu_build_peak (bytes at the build high-water mark), gpu_run (bytes the study adds while it runs: run_items kept once allocated, e.g. harmonic FDTD accumulators, growing point traces, plus largest_phase: the transient_items of one phase, e.g. one solve or one adjoint, freed when it ends; phases never overlap), gpu_peak (max of gpu_build_peak and gpu_steady + gpu_run), gpu_external (cuDSS direct-solver factors alive through the run, outside the pool: a fill-in rule), external_transient_items [{phase, label, bytes}] (factors alive only in that transient phase, a factor once per phase it lives in), external_extra (the largest factorisation peak on top), external_peak (gpu_external + the largest phase of external_transient_items + external_extra), device_peak (max of gpu_build_peak and gpu_steady + run_items + the largest phase of its transient_items plus the factors alive in it, + gpu_external + external_extra: checked against the GPU budget), host (bytes of CPU factorisations and analyses: a fill-in heuristic), items / host_items / run_items / external_items [{label, bytes}] and transient_items [{phase, label, bytes}] largest first, largest_phase {phase, bytes} or null, budget (the check memory_budget argument in bytes, or null), host_budget (the check host_budget argument: available host RAM in bytes, or null)}, or null when the mesh or the estimate fails. CPU estimates counted per physics and feature type (approximate; summary.json compares gpu_steady and gpu_build_peak with the measured build); validation errors when device_peak exceeds a known GPU budget or host exceeds the available host RAM (a run: both always; CLI check: the host RAM), warns above 80 % of either; without a host budget it warns above 8 GiB of host memory.

### summary.json

- open_sol_version, status (completed | partial | timeout | cancelled | failed), message, model {title, file, study_type}, wall_time (s).
