- build {nx, ny, nz (1 in 2D), n_cells, dt, dx_min, dx_max, npml_sides, build_seconds, gpu_bytes, session_gpu_bytes, gpu_breakdown [[build stage, bytes]] (pool use added by each stage; "build temporaries freed" is negative), stage_seconds [[build stage, wall s]] (validation + estimates first; also the "Build time by stage" log line), gpu_peak_bytes (build high-water mark of the pool), gpu_budget, gpu_estimate}, or null when no build succeeded. gpu_estimate is null or {gpu_steady, gpu_build_peak, gpu_run, gpu_external, external_extra, external_peak, host, items / run_items / external_items [[label, bytes]], transient_items / external_transient_items [[phase, label, bytes]], steady_deviation, peak_deviation (measured / estimated - 1), peak_unseen_bytes (free pool blocks stranded before the build by arrays of open Results: build temporaries placed there do not raise the pool mark, so an estimate up to this far above gpu_peak_bytes has deviation 0)}; a deviation above 25 % is also a warning.
- build_seconds_total (s: every build of the study summed: sweep values, refinement levels, parity sectors; one build: build.build_seconds) or null; study_seconds (s: the study runs on the built sessions, without build and post-processing; summed over sweep values, refinement levels and parity sectors) or null; time_check (null without a machine profile) the run-time estimate against the runs, merged over sweep values / levels / sectors with item labels "<run>: <item>"; solvers {physics: {roles {role: {type, solver (the solver node, null = Automatic), backend, precision, settings (the resolved solver settings), counters}}, counters}} of the last run, how each result was computed: role counters pcg {solves, cg_iterations, unconverged_solves} (linear: heat, electric_currents, electrostatics, magnetostatics, solid_mechanics, solid_mechanics_3d), sparse_direct {back_end, factorizations, factor_seconds, recycled_solves, gmres_iterations} (linear: em_fdfd_*, em_fdfd_nonlinear, drift_diffusion, magnetic_fields_ac; shifted: heat in a thermal_noise study), line_block {batches, shifts, refinement_sweeps, rejected_shifts (re-solved by SuperLU), kept_factors, factor_solves, rejected_factor_solves, batched_operators, worst_accepted_residual} (shifted: heat thermal noise, em_fdfd_bor, em_modes; linear: em_fdfd_ez / _hz), arpack_shift_invert {eigen_solves, eigen_factorizations, operator_applications (group-index solves included), eigen_unconverged, eigen_seconds} (eigen: em_modes, em_fdfd_* in an eigenfrequency study), block_eigen {eigen_solves, eigen_iterations, eigen_single_iterations, eigen_double_iterations, operator_applications, mass_applications, preconditioner_applications, eigen_seconds, eigen_unconverged, eigen_dense_solves, eigen_block_size, eigen_last_residual} (eigen: solid_mechanics_3d on brick meshes, opt-in), explicit_kernels {} (stepper); the physics' own counters (loops and solves outside a role) em_fdfd_* {solves}; em_fdfd_nonlinear {channels, sweeps, solves}; magnetic_fields_ac {solves}; em_modes {solves, modes_found, solve_seconds, line_block_fallbacks with a line_block shifted node}; drift_diffusion {newton_iterations, chord_steps (Newton iterations solved on the last factorised Jacobian), continuation_steps, cold_starts, rejected_predictions (continuation steps whose secant prediction did not converge), solve_seconds}; laminar_flow {lattice_steps, solves}; a damped nonlinear loop (electric_currents / electrostatics nonlinear electrolyte, magnetostatics saturation) {nonlinear_runs, nonlinear_iterations, nonlinear_unconverged; the electrolyte also diagonal_refreshes; the tensor saturation loop also kept_preconditioner_solves (solves on a kept multigrid hierarchy or direct factor), kept_preconditioner_fallbacks (of those, rebuilt and repeated) and with a direct factor kept_factor_cg_iterations} once it ran; physics with neither are left out (ticks counts the steps of time-stepped ones).
- ticks and tick_unit, what one tick is (time_dependent: runner ticks, step; stationary and optimization: iterations, iteration; frequency_domain: wavelengths solved, wavelength; mode_analysis: mode snapshots, mode; eigenfrequency and optomechanics: resonance snapshots, resonance; thermal_noise: factorisations, factorisation; nonlinear_frequency_domain: channel snapshots, channel; frequency_response: frequencies solved, frequency), t_end (s; 0 in studies without time steps), warnings [text], errors [text], issues [issue records of a failed build], traceback (text).
- memory {pool_used, pool_reserved, device_free, device_total, budget, other, host_available (available host RAM, null when unknown), build_gpu_bytes, session_gpu_bytes} in bytes, or null: pool_used and gpu_bytes are process-wide, session_gpu_bytes is the share of this build. failed_build_memory: null, or of the last failed build {breakdown [[build stage, bytes]], total_bytes, peak_bytes, budget, failed_owner (the stage that raised), estimate}.
- derived {name: value}; derived_reference {name: reference} and derived_error {name: relative error} of the derived values with a reference; sweep null or {parameter, values, derived {name: [value per sweep value]}, reference {name: [reference per sweep value]} and error {name: [relative error per sweep value]} (derived values with a reference; a failed value keeps its reference), results [{"physics.feature": digest} per sweep value], failed [{index, value, message} per value whose build or run failed], converged [true | false | null per sweep value: fixed_point.converged, null for a failed value or no fixed point], curve_error {name: [curve_error record per sweep value]} of the analytic curves on a feature result, derived_series [derived_series record or null per sweep value], builds (model builds of the sweep: 1 with SweepSpec.reuse_build, else one per value), with SweepSpec.keep_fields also snapshot_times [[s] per value] and snapshot_labels [[text or null] per value] of the kept snapshots (results.npz sweep_snapshot)}.
- derived_series null or {kind xy, x [time s or wavelength m per stored snapshot, in record order], x_label Time | Wavelength, x_unit, y_label, series {name: [value per point]}, series_units}: every derived value without a source evaluated on the live state at each snapshot of a time_dependent or frequency_domain run (also once the 1 GB snapshot limit stops storing fields; NaN and one warning where it fails), null below 2 points; parity-sector runs give null.
- wavelength_fixed_points (frequency_domain coupled wavelength scan only) [{wavelength, converged, iterations, relative_change, tolerance} per solved wavelength with a fixed-point loop]; fixed_point then holds converged = all of them, the largest iterations and relative_change.
- run_memory null or {measured_bytes (pool high-water mark of the run since its build), estimated_bytes (gpu_steady + gpu_run of the estimate), unseen_bytes (as peak_unseen_bytes of the build), deviation (measured / estimated - 1)}; external_memory null or the same record of the cuDSS factors outside the pool (measured_bytes: high-water mark of the live factors since the build started, a plan counting its peak estimate; estimated_bytes: the estimate's external_peak; null when neither side has any); parameters {name: value} of the built session (a sweep: the value the run ended on) or null; sweep_index (0-based) of the sweep value that top-level derived, fields and results belong to, or null.
- Study-specific keys, present only when that study ran: optimization {iterations, evaluations, design_cells, objective_initial, objective_final, continuation_stages, message} (optimization); noise_frequencies [Hz] (thermal_noise, empty unless completed); n_modes (mode_analysis: mode snapshots); n_resonances (eigenfrequency, optomechanics: resonance snapshots); response_frequencies [Hz] (frequency_response: the solved ones in solve order) and frequency_sweep {method, physics: {name: reduced-model info}} (frequency_response with sweep_method adaptive / modal; see that setting); n_channels (channel snapshots), nonlinear_solve {physics: {mode, order, channel_solves, sweeps, converged, residual, tolerance, residual_history, continuation_steps, method, gmres_iterations, backtracks}} and feedback (solution-feedback record or absent) (nonlinear_frequency_domain).
- convergence (StudySpec.adaptation; also convergence.json, Results.convergence()) {target, method, tolerance, max_levels, growth, max_cells, anisotropic, meshes [refined], levels [{level, cells {mesh: cells incl. padding}, window_cells {mesh: n}, n_cells, refined_cells (window cells of the refined meshes), value (target), relative_change, derived {name: value}, study_seconds, gpu_steady (estimate, bytes), status}], richardson null or {cells, values, levels, order_cells q, order (q x dimensions), dimensions, extrapolated, error_estimate, relative_error_estimate, coefficient C} of v = v_inf + C N^-q over the last three levels, richardson_note, converged, stop_reason (converged | max_levels | max_cells | memory | no_refinement | not_finite | cancelled | failed), message, adapted_meshes [MeshSpec objects of the last level]}; fields, results and derived are the last computed level's, ticks and study_seconds sum the levels; StudySpec.adaptation keep_levels adds the earlier levels' snapshots labelled 'level k: ...'.
- estimation (StudySpec.estimation) {method, parameters [names], initial / lower / upper (null = unbounded) / fitted {name: value}, standard_errors {name: value} or null, correlation [[...]] or null, rank, reduced_chi_square, statistics_note, absolute_sigma, cost (0.5 sum r^2 at the best point), cost_initial, best_evaluation, evaluations, max_evaluations, targets [{derived, measured, sigma, model, residual}], curves [{source, n_points, rms_residual, max_abs_residual}], history {evaluation [k], cost [per evaluation], parameters {name: [value per evaluation]}}, live_is_best, converged, stop_reason (converged | max_evaluations | not_finite | failed | cancelled), message}; fields, results and derived are those of the best-point run (a cancelled search: the last run), ticks = evaluations (tick_unit evaluation), study_seconds sums every run.
- parity_sectors null or (study setting parity_sectors) {faces [mirror faces], labels [sector label per run, the model's own signs last], status [per sector], combined (derived holds the quadratic-total combination), derived {name: [value per sector]}, results [{"physics.feature": digest} per sector], combined_results {"physics.feature": digest} (Results.sector_result(..., combined=True)), snapshot_sectors [sector label per snapshot, "" for a combined one]}; derived, fields and results of the summary are then the combination (derived) and the last sector (fields, results); ticks and study_seconds sum the sectors. With a parameter sweep: this block is the last value's, sweep derived holds the combined values per sweep value, sweep results the last sector's results per value and sweep sector_derived [{name: [value per sector]} per sweep value].
- curve_error {name: {max, rms, n_points}} of every analytic curve, evaluated at the simulated samples (a feature result: its t / iteration, wavelength, angle (far field: every wavelength, both normalised to their peak), x or table x_column; a line: the containing-cell profile points, the analytic at the sampled cell centres; sweep: the swept values against its series quantity) on the finite points: max = max |simulated - analytic| / ptp(analytic) (the analytic range: an absolute temperature against its rise; max |analytic| for a flat curve, absolute when that is 0), rms likewise; target sweep: |simulated - analytic| / |analytic| per swept value (curves spanning decades). A curve that cannot be compared (series fft or ratio, series "" with several candidates, no result) has max and rms NaN, n_points 0 and a note.
- derived_curves {name: {plot, label, unit, x_label, x_unit, x [abscissa values], y [values], with a reference also y_reference and curve_error {max, rms, n_points (, note)}} or {plot, error}} of every derived curve over the final results (a sweep: its last value).
- fixed_point {converged, iterations, relative_change, tolerance} of the coupled stationary loop (stationary; frequency_domain: the background solve, a coupled wavelength scan: over all wavelengths), or null (time_dependent, or no physics loop: a single pass). A run that did not converge keeps status completed (partial for a sweep with failed values) and says so in message; its derived values and results are those of the last iteration.
- stored_fields ["physics.component"], field_meshes {"physics.component": name of the mesh the field lives on}, meshes [{name, kind (tensor | triangles), shape (cells incl. padding, null on triangles), elements (triangles, else null), cells, window_cells, dx_min, dx_max (m: physical cell lengths, element edges), physics [names], ledger [[build stage, bytes] of the build memory ledger lines of this mesh]} per built mesh], stored_cuts [[axis, cell-centre position m] of the 3D stored cut planes every snapshot holds], fields {key: field digest}, results {"physics.feature": result digest, or {kind, error}}, snapshot_times [s], snapshot_labels [text or null per snapshot: "lambda = <nm> nm" for frequency_domain, "mode <k>: n_eff = <value>" for mode_analysis, "resonance <k>: lambda = <nm> nm, Q = <value>" for eigenfrequency (solid mechanics: "resonance <k>: f = <value> Hz"; optomechanics: "mechanical mode <k>: f = <value> Hz, g0 / 2 pi = <value> Hz"; mirror faces add the parity: "mode <k> [x_lo symmetric]: ..."), "iteration <k>: J = <value>" per accepted iteration and "final: J = <value>" for optimization, the mode labels then "thermal noise" for thermal_noise, "channel <name>: lambda = <nm> nm" for nonlinear_frequency_domain, "f = <value> Hz" for frequency_response, null for time snapshots; parity sectors: "<label> [<sector>]" and the combined ones], live_snapshot (index of the snapshot holding the state Results.field reads when that is not the last: resonance 1 of eigenfrequency / optomechanics, mode_index of mode_analysis; else null), snapshot_solutions (per snapshot the physics whose every field and 3D cut the live GUI session renders from a kept solution; empty lists headless), wavelengths [m] (frequency_domain only: the solved list in solve order, one snapshot each: shorter than requested after a cancel or timeout), harmonic_pulse (frequency_domain only: null without an em_fdtd_* physics, else {steps, simulated_time [s], stop_reason decayed | max_duration | cancelled, final_energy_ratio (window field energy / its peak at the end), source_end [s]} of the harmonic FDTD pulse), files {summary, log, arrays (results.npz or null), meshes (meshes.npz or null), model (model.json or null), figures ["figures/<name>.png"]}.
- status failed: see message (an out-of-GPU-memory failure says so and names the budget and the remedies), issues, errors and traceback; timeout: max_wall_time was reached and the results are partial; partial: a sweep finished but some values failed (message "k/n sweep values failed ...", sweep.failed; their derived values are NaN and their results empty).
- A digest that cannot be computed is {error: "Type: message"}. A partial sweep whose last value failed keeps the sweep table but has empty fields and results.
- When writing the report itself fails, the status is failed (exit 1) and summary.json holds only open_sol_version, status, message ("post-run failure: Type: message; the study ended <its status>"), errors, traceback and files; when even that cannot be written, Results.summary() holds it with files null and the reason in errors.

### show.json

- {open_sol_version, kind (model | results), path, outline, check, summary}: outline (model: title, description, parameters with their evaluated value, domain, geometry, selections, materials, physics with features, couplings, mesh, solvers, solver_defaults, study, derived_values, analytic_curves, derived_curves) or null, check {n_errors, n_warnings, n_infos} (model) or null, summary (results: the summary.json content, or {error: "Type: message"} with exit code 1 when the directory cannot be loaded) or null.

### selftest_report_<subset>.json

- {open_sol_version, passed (bool), n_cases, n_passed, n_failed, n_error (cases with status error, not in n_failed), subset (light | heavy | named: which registered cases the file holds), n_skipped (registered cases not in it), n_reused, reused [case names whose stored record was reused, counted as passed], wall_time, device {device_id, name, kind (gpu | cpu), device_total, device_free, budget} [bytes] or null, warnings [text], cases [{name, label, description, status (passed | failed | error), measured, expected, error, tolerance, details, message, wall_time, vram_deviation, vram_part, vram_verdict, vram_max_bytes, count_deviation, count_item, runs {run name: {status, wall_time, message, out_dir, timing, vram, counts}}, variants (cases with variants only) {variant name: {status (passed | failed | error | skipped), backend, precision, measured, expected, error, tolerance, details, message, wall_time, runs}}}]}.
- A variant repeats the case's runs on another backend and / or solver precision (run directories <case>/variant_<name>/<run>/) and judges the same check against its own tolerance; a failed or erroring variant fails the case, a gpu variant without a usable GPU is skipped.
- timing {build_seconds (summary build_seconds_total), study_seconds, output_seconds (run() after the study: summary, host copies, files), n_cells, ticks, cell_ticks_per_second (time_dependent: n_cells * ticks / study_seconds, else null), solvers} from the run summary, or null when the run raised: a performance baseline, comparable only between reports of one machine (the first run of an engine in a process also loads its compiled kernels); the solvers counters are machine-independent.
- vram (gpu runs with a memory estimate, else null) {kept, build_peak, run, external: {measured_bytes, estimated_bytes, deviation (measured / estimated - 1), verdict, beyond_floor (differ by more than 1 MiB)} or null, deviation, part, verdict, beyond_floor}: kept / build_peak from the summary build ledger, run = summary run_memory, external = summary external_memory. The estimate counts the big arrays held at the same time, so it sits just below the measured bytes: verdict over (it books more than was held: the estimator misreads the solver), unaccounted (more than 25 % held beyond it: an array no item lists, or memory the code could free) or empty; deviation / part / verdict = the worst part (one with a verdict first, then one beyond the floor, then the largest |deviation|). counts (null without a run-time estimate or counted items) {deviation, item}: the time_check item (predicted count with a summary counter, e.g. CG iterations) whose measured / predicted - 1 is the largest, signed, and its label (0 and null when none is off by more than one). vram_deviation, vram_part, vram_verdict, count_deviation / count_item (case and example records) = the worst / largest over its runs (null without one), vram_max_bytes the largest measured_bytes of any vram part over its runs: the memory estimators / time recipes to update (CLI: "vram -40% max 1200 MB  counts +200% (item)" after the time split; - = the estimate books too much, + = more held than estimated).
- A case passes when its error is finite and error <= tolerance; a run that does not complete fails its case, and an exception in the comparison makes it an error.
- An interrupted selftest writes the cases already run (passed false, a warning says so); a failing progress callback is dropped with a warning.
- Built-in cases, run first: templates_validate (every template validates without errors), examples_validate (every examples/**/*.json of a repository checkout loads and validates without errors), api_reference_current (api_reference.md and api_templates.md equal the text describe generates), import_contracts (every package import keeps the layering rules of model/import_contracts.py) and structure_index_current (the repository module index equals the text generated from the module docstrings); they run in the light, heavy and all subsets and appear in each of their report files; a named run (names) runs only the built-ins it names.
- A selftest --all run writes the light and the heavy file from one run (wall_time, device and warnings are the whole run's), then the examples file; api.selftest returns the combined dict with subset all, report_files [names] and examples {passed, n_examples, n_passed, n_failed, n_error, n_no_tolerance, n_skipped_backend, n_reused, wall_time, warnings}; its passed also needs the examples run.
- Before a report file (this one or an examples file) is overwritten, its timing summary goes to <file stem>_prev.json {source, written (file time), open_sol_version, subset, passed, counts, n_reused, wall_time, device, cases {case name or example path: {status, wall_time, reused}}}: the previous run to compare run times with (a reused case keeps its stored wall_time; compare --reset runs).

### selftest_report_analytic.json

- Only examples with a derived value with a reference or an analytic curve are selftest examples (the others are not run or listed; naming one is a usage error); each runs once, on its own backend (solver_defaults.backend).
- {open_sol_version, passed (no failed or erroring example), n_examples, n_passed, n_failed, n_error, n_no_tolerance, n_skipped_backend, skipped_backend [example paths setting backend gpu, not run without a usable GPU], n_reused, reused [example paths whose stored record was reused], wall_time, device, warnings, ranking [{example, kind (derived | curve), name, error, tolerance, ratio, flags}] of the entries with a tolerance by ratio = error / tolerance (non-finite first, then descending), without_tolerance [the same rows] by error, examples [...], report_files [its own file name; [] without out_dir]}.
- Example: {example (path under examples/), title, status (passed | failed | error | no_tolerance), run_status, message, wall_time, out_dir, worst_ratio, flags, backend (the run's; null when the file did not load), timing, vram, counts, vram_deviation, vram_part, vram_verdict, vram_max_bytes, count_deviation, count_item (as a selftest run / case), derived [{kind, name, value, reference, error, tolerance, ratio, flags (+ per_value_error in a sweep)}], curves [{kind, name, target, series, error (the curve_error max; a sweep: the worst value), rms, n_points, tolerance, ratio, flags, note (+ per_value_error)}]}. A sweep derived value: value / reference lists per value, error the worst value.
- Flags: over_tolerance, nonfinite, not_compared (curve without simulated counterpart), suspicious_exact (error < 1e-9 for a simulated quantity with a non-zero reference: the reference likely reads the result), sweep_not_converging (the sweep changes the mesh dx, auto mode points_per_wavelength, and the error at the finest mesh is not below the one at the coarsest; not when every error is below 1e-9). An entry with a tolerance fails on over_tolerance, nonfinite or not_compared; error: the run did not complete (failed, partial, timeout) or raised.

### Digests

- field: {physics, component, label, unit, shape [nx, ny], min, max, mean (area-weighted over the cell areas), abs_max, abs_max_at [x, y] (cell centre of the largest |value|, m), n_nonfinite, time, time_label}; statistics over the finite cells, null when none is finite.
- timeseries: {kind, component, unit, n_samples, t_start, t_stop, min, max, final}.
- flux_spectrum: {kind, unit (of power: a.u. or W/m), n_wavelengths, wavelength_min, wavelength_max, power_min, power_max, wavelength_at_max}; power statistics over the finite values.
- dft_fields: {kind, quantity, shape, n_wavelengths, wavelengths, intensity_max [max per wavelength of the intensity of the monitor quantity (|E_z|^2 or |E_x|^2 + |E_y|^2)] or null}.
- far_field: {kind, quantity, unit, n_wavelengths, n_angles, wavelengths, power_max [per wavelength: the largest finite power], angle_at_max_deg [per wavelength]}.
- xy: {kind, x_label, x_unit, n_points, x_min, x_max, series {name: {unit, min, max, x_at_max}}}; statistics over the finite values only (NaN marks a value that could not be computed).
- table: {kind, columns, units, n_rows, rows [the first 50 rows]}.
- mode_shapes: {kind, n_nodes, n_triangles, n_resonances, frequencies [Hz per mode, resonance order], bloch_k [rad/m per axis]}.
- Values that cannot be computed (empty arrays, no finite value) are null.

### results.npz

- np.savez archive, read with np.load(path, allow_pickle=False); written unless run --no-arrays (save_arrays=False).
- field/<physics>.<component>/values (float32 (nx, ny) window cells), .../x_edges and .../y_edges (float64 cell edges, m).
- result/<physics>.<feature>/<key> for every numeric array value of >= 1 dimension, and result/<physics>.<feature>/<key>/<name> for every such array inside a dict value (one level, e.g. the xy series/<name>; loading rebuilds the dict, whose other entries stay in the metadata); a dft_fields result adds intensity_all, float64 (n_f, mx, my) = the intensity of the monitor quantity (|E_z|^2 or |E_x|^2 + |E_y|^2) at every wavelength.
- sweep/<index>/<physics>.<feature>/<key> (and .../<key>/<name>) per sweep value, sector/<index>/... alike per parity sector; sweep_snapshot/<value index>/<snapshot index>/... as snapshot/<index>/... per kept snapshot of a keep_fields sweep (metadata sweep_snapshots [[snapshot entry] per value]); snapshot/<index>/<physics>.<component>/values per snapshot (snapshots are saved only here), plus .../x_centers and .../y_centers (float64 cell centres, m) when the values sit on the native window cells (native polar / spherical cells also .../mapped_x and .../mapped_y, the float64 drawing-plane centres); without them the values are nearest-cell resampled on uniform pixels over extent; 3D models add snapshot/<index>/cut<c>/<physics>.<component>/... per stored cut and snapshot/<index>/segment/<curve name>/distance, values, centre_x, centre_y, centre_z (float64) per 3D-segment line curve.
- metadata: 0-d unicode JSON string (json.loads(str(npz['metadata']))) {format (open_sol.results), version (1), fields {key: {physics, component, info {name, label, unit, signed, cmap, primary}, time, time_label, plane, mesh}}, results {key: non-array entries (table rows included)}, sweep_results [...], sector_results [...], sector_combined_results {key: ...} (arrays under sector_combined/<key>/), snapshots [{time, label, fields {key: {extent, info, time_label, native_shape ([nx, ny] window cells when resampled, else null), plane, axes (names of the value axes), unfolded (already mirrored over the mirror faces: parity-sector snapshots), mesh}}, cuts [fields per stored cut], segments {curve name: {physics, component, start, end, info, time_label}}}]}; plane ["z", cut height in m] of a 3D model, else null; mesh = the name of the mesh the field lives on (fields of a triangle mesh are saved as their raster over the window); tuples come back as lists, non-finite floats outside arrays as "nan", "inf", "-inf".

### meshes.npz

- The meshes the fields live on, written with results.npz: <mesh>/x_edges, <mesh>/y_edges (3D: + z_edges) = float64 window cell edges of a tensor mesh in Domain coordinates (m; polar / spherical windows: logical r - radius_min [m] and angle - angle_min [rad]), or <mesh>/points (float64 (n, 2) m), <mesh>/triangles (int32 (k, 3)) and <mesh>/pml_faces (uint8 per element, bits x_lo 1, x_hi 2, y_lo 4, y_hi 8; 0 inside the window) of a triangle mesh, or <mesh>/points (float64 (n, 3) m) and <mesh>/tets (int32 (k, 4)) of a tetrahedron mesh; metadata {format (open_sol.meshes), version (1), meshes {name: {kind}}}.

### log.txt

- One line per event, '[<elapsed s>] [<level>] <message>': log events, the build (Built, or BuildFailed with its issues and traceback), sweep steps, the end of the study (finished or failed), the time-out and GPU memory leak warnings; warnings at Results.close() are appended.

### Python API (open_sol.api, re-exported by open_sol)

- describe(topic=None, as_dict=False) -> this reference as text (templates as an index; describe('templates') has their JSON), or as a dict; template(key) -> ModelSpec; load(path) -> ModelSpec; save(spec, path).
- spec arguments may be a ModelSpec (copied), a dict (ModelSpec.from_dict) or a model file path; invalid content is a model error, an unreadable file raises OSError.
- parameters={name: expression string or number} (check and run) overrides parameter expressions of the spec copy (numbers stored as repr(float); run records them in model.json); an unknown name is an error issue at ("parameters",) (run without out_dir: KeyError listing the known names).
- check(spec, out_dir=None, parameters=None, memory_budget=None, host_budget=None, backend=None, max_wall_time=None) -> the check.json dict (also written with out_dir); memory_budget [bytes] (e.g. a run summary build.gpu_budget) adds the GPU memory check, host_budget [bytes] (e.g. open_sol.core.host_memory.available_bytes()) the host RAM check (an estimate over a budget on size-based element counts: check builds the triangle / tetrahedron meshes first and reports on their counts, as a build judges); backend ('auto' | 'gpu' | 'cpu') overrides solver_defaults.backend; max_wall_time [s] adds a warning when even the shortest estimated run time exceeds it.
- profile_machine(backend=None, quick=False, progress=print) -> {key, date, quick, text, path}: measures and stores the machine profile of the run-time estimates (CLI profile; backend None = the default backend).
- scene_figure(spec, path, parameters=None, highlight=(), z_stretch=1.0, view=None) -> path: CPU-only perspective picture of a 3D model (.png / .pdf / .svg by the suffix; ValueError in 2D) as the GUI 3D preview draws it: translucent objects in their material colours, points / lines as markers, highlight = entity names drawn in the highlight colour, z_stretch scales the box height only (thin layers), view = (elevation, azimuth) in degrees; objects that do not resolve are left out with a RuntimeWarning.
- run(spec, out_dir=None, max_wall_time=None, progress=None, figures=False, save_arrays=True, parameters=None, backend=None, snapshots=True) -> Results: blocking, runs on the calling thread on the model's backend (backend 'auto' | 'gpu' | 'cpu' overrides solver_defaults.backend, kept in model.json); snapshots=False stores only the final state (time_dependent: output_interval 0, n_snapshots 1; model.json keeps the model's values); progress(event) receives every event except live frames. With out_dir it always writes summary.json and log.txt and never raises (except KeyboardInterrupt); without out_dir a failed build re-raises its exception (ModelError with .issues), a failed run raises RunError(message, traceback), and a timeout returns normally. progress=True prints to stdout through ProgressPrinter(stream=None, period=2.0) (the CLI printer: build, log and sweep lines, Progress lines at most every period s). Events, in open_sol.api: LogEvent(level, message), SweepStep(index (0-based), count, parameter, value), Built(summary: BuildSummary with nx, ny, n_cells, dt, build_seconds, ...), BuildFailed(message, traceback, issues, out_of_memory, build_memory), StudyStarted(), Progress(fraction, t, t_end [s], tick, wall_elapsed, ticks_per_second, message, tick_unit 'step' | 'iteration' | 'wavelength' | 'mode solve' | 'eigen solve' | 'factorisation' | 'channel solve', stages (stage names of the run in order, e.g. Background solve, Wavelength solves), stage_index (0-based), stage_fraction, stage_elapsed [s]; fraction and wall_elapsed cover the whole run, each stage an equal share), SweepValueDone(index, count, parameter, value, sweep: a copy of the study sweep table so far, after each computed or failed sweep value), StudyFinished(summary dict), StudyFailed(message, traceback, out_of_memory, session_live, build_memory). build_memory: the build ledger record (summary.json failed_build_memory layout) or null.
- Results: status, spec, out_dir, session (live only), build_summary, log, is_live; summary() -> dict; field_names(), result_names(); convergence() -> copy of the mesh refinement report of a StudySpec.adaptation run (KeyError without one); save(path, save_arrays=True); close(copy_to_host=True); Results.load(path).
- Results.field(name, physics=None, plane=None, unfold=False, native=False) -> FieldData: values float32 (nx, ny) on the native window cells, x_centers / y_centers float64 in m, extent, info, time, plane, axes. unfold=True mirrors over the model's x / y mirror faces (ValueError for a field without a parity). 3D: plane=(axis, position [m]) picks the cut normal to axis 'x' | 'y' | 'z' (values along axes ('y', 'z') / ('x', 'z') / ('x', 'y')), live only; default and saved fields the mid-height z cut. Polar / spherical domains: a containing-cell image over the sector's box, NaN outside, native_shape set; native=True (live only) gives the window cells instead: axes ('r', 'phi' | 'theta'), x_centers = r in m, y_centers = the angle in rad, extent (r_min, r_max, angle_min, angle_max), mapped_centres = the drawing-plane (x, y) centres in m, float64 (nx, ny) each.
- Results.volume(name, physics=None, max_bytes=2**30) -> VolumeData of a 3D field (values float32 (wx, wy, wz) on the window cells, centres (x, y, z) float64 in m, info, time; live only, ValueError above max_bytes); export_volume(name, path, physics=None, max_bytes=2**30) -> its .npz (values, x_centers, y_centers, z_centers, metadata kind volume).
- Results.result(physics, feature, **options) or result('physics.feature', **options) -> result dict (dft_fields: freq_index=i adds freq_index and intensity); figure(what, path, title='', freq_index=None, series=None) -> PNG path of a field (physics.component or a unique component) or a feature result (physics.feature; series: only that series of an xy result); derived_curves() -> [(plot, xy result or None, {curve name: error text})] of the derived curves over the final results.
- Results.scene_figure(path, field=None, physics=None, planes=None, z_stretch=1.0, view=None) -> path of a 3D run: the api scene_figure picture of its model (built parameters) with field on cut planes in one colour scale, the objects then as edges only (live: planes [(axis, position [m])], default an x, y and z cut through the structure as export_html; closed / loaded: the saved mid-height z cut plus the stored cuts of a last snapshot at the same time).
- Results.export_html(path, what=None, physics=None, title=None, geometry=True, planes=None, figure=None, fields=None, max_bytes=None) -> the written .html path: a self-contained web page (no network, WebGL2; PNG and video export), live, closed or loaded alike; other result kinds raise ValueError.
  - what = a field ('physics.component' or a unique component; physics narrows it): every stored snapshot holding it is a frame (time snapshots play, labelled ones get a slider; a '<base>_re' / '_im' pair is animated over one period, Re / Im[A exp(j wt)]), else the current / saved state. 2D: a map (2D Cartesian flow / current / potential / magnetostatic / heat pages can add particles or arrows of the in-plane vector; 2D solid_mechanics / membrane fields drawn on the deformed body). 3D: cut planes (live: an x, y and z cut at a mirror plane of its physics, else through the objects that do not span the window, else the window middle; snapshots and closed / loaded runs: the mid-height z cut and stored_cuts); planes [(axis, position m)]: the live state on exactly those planes, a snapshot its held cut nearest each, ValueError in 2D or for an axis no snapshot holds when not live; live Cartesian 3D Results also put the whole field on the page, up to 60 kept GUI snapshots.
  - what = a dft_fields result 'physics.feature': its intensity map per frequency.
  - what = a mode_shapes result (None = the only one): the complex mode shapes animated on the solid surface beside the band diagram (a sweep: every successful value, abscissa k a / 2 pi of the Bloch wavenumber, else the swept parameter), coloured by displacement or, with the kept stress / strain, stress, strain and energy measures; fields = a list of 'stress' / 'strain' (None = every kept one, ValueError for one not kept); max_bytes: viz.mode_player.ModePageTooLarge (a ValueError with .sizes per group) when the mode data would pass it, nothing written; fields / max_bytes on another page: ValueError.
  - geometry (field and 2D dft_fields pages): the model objects at the built parameters (ValueError without the model spec: pass geometry=False); mirror planes add the mirror images. Large data is thinned (named in the page subtitle).
  - figure (field and dft_fields pages): {setting: value} the page's Plot settings panel opens with (its Copy settings gives this dict; None / missing = automatic; ValueError on a mode_shapes page, for an unknown key, a value outside its choices / range or min >= max): font_size (px, 6 - 40, default 11), title_size (px, 8 - 72, default 26), title 'top_left' | 'top_center' | 'top_right' | 'off', color_min / color_max (field unit; a signed field with one of them stays symmetric about 0), x_min / x_max / y_min / y_max / z_min / z_max (axis limits in m; not along the normal of a single plane), colorbar 'bottom_right' | 'bottom_left' | 'top_right' | 'top_left' | 'right' | 'left' | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'off', colorbar_length (fraction of the view side, 0.1 - 1), horizontal_axis 'bottom' | 'top', vertical_axis 'left' | 'right', scale_bar 'off' | 'on' (default 'on': a true-length bar on a face-on map in place of the axes), scale_bar_length (m, > 0; default a round length near a fifth of the view), scale_bar_color 'auto' | 'white' | 'black', legend_color 'auto' | 'white' | 'black', background 'theme' | 'white', export_scale 1 | 2 | 4 (PNG pixels per screen pixel).
- Stored states (live, closed and loaded alike): snapshots() -> [(time, label, [physics.component keys])] (frequency_domain: one per wavelength, field() holds only the last); snapshot_field(index, name, physics=None, plane=None) -> FieldData of one snapshot, float32 on the native window cells (x_centers / y_centers set, graded meshes included) up to 250,000 window cells, else nearest-cell resampled on a uniform grid over extent (x_centers None, native_shape set); 3D: plane None = the mid-height z cut, (axis, position [m]) = the StudySpec.stored_cuts plane on that axis nearest position, an int = that stored cut; sweep_result(physics, feature) or sweep_result('physics.feature') -> [result dict, or None for a failed value] in summary()['sweep']['values'] order; sweep_xy(physics, feature=None, column='frequency', sort=True) -> 'xy' result of a per-value 'table' result vs the swept parameter, series '<column>_<k>' = the k-th smallest value of that column per sweep value (sort=False: the k-th row), NaN where missing (e.g. the bands of a resonance_monitor over a Bloch k sweep); sweep() -> copy of the sweep table {parameter, values, derived, reference, error, converged, failed, derived_series}; sweep_field(index, name, snapshot=-1, physics=None, plane=None) -> FieldData of a kept snapshot of sweep value index (keep_fields; snapshot / name / plane as snapshot_field); sweep_figure(quantity, path, series=None, title='') -> PNG of a sweep: quantity 'physics.feature' = one curve of that result per swept value (legend '<parameter> = <value>'; series picks an xy series or a flux_spectrum power / power_per_cw; far fields in dB at their first wavelength), 'derived' = every derived value vs the swept parameter, 'derived_series:<name>' = that derived value along the study axis per swept value (run --figures writes figures/sweep_derived.png, sweep_<key>.png and sweep_series_<name>.png of a sweep, derived_series.png of a run with a derived series); sector_result(physics, feature) -> [result dict or None per parity sector] in summary()['parity_sectors']['labels'] order (combine quadratic totals, e.g. flux power, with open_sol.core.mirror.combine_sector_totals, far-field patterns per angle with open_sol.core.mirror.combine_sector_far_fields: the mean of the complex amplitude_re / amplitude_im of the far_field results, power = |mean|^2; a sweep: the last value's sectors); sector_result(physics, feature, combined=True) -> the stored result of the drawn source alone (driven studies where every sector ran: far_field combined per angle, flux_spectrum power / power_per_cw as quadratic totals when its line / plane / box reaches every mirror plane, i.e. mirror_factor = 2^k; entry combined_sectors = 2^k), KeyError otherwise.
- Non-finite numbers in summary() derived, derived_reference, derived_error, sweep derived / reference / error, curve_error max / rms (sweep too) and fixed_point relative_change, in table rows and in the scalar entries of result dicts (e.g. resonance_monitor start_time) are floats in every state (Results.load converts the JSON strings back); digest statistics stay "nan" / "inf" strings.
- export_field(field_data, path) and export_result(result, path) (open_sol, from open_sol.io) write a FieldData / result dict as .npz or .csv (field metadata: plane of a 3D cut, axes, resampled / native_shape; a native polar / spherical field adds x_mapped / y_mapped arrays (.npz) or x / y columns after r and the angle (.csv)); export_volume(volume_data, path) a VolumeData as .npz only.
- A live Results holds the GPU session: close() (or a with block) copies the stored fields and feature results to host memory and frees the GPU (copy_to_host=False skips the host copy); a closed or loaded Results is CPU-only (saved fields and results only; result() options other than freq_index raise ValueError). Close it before the next run: r = run(...) in a loop keeps the old session on the GPU while the next one builds (run warns while earlier Results are live); use "with run(spec) as r:" instead.
- selftest(out_dir=None, names=None, progress=None, heavy=False, reset=False) -> the selftest report dict (+ report_files: the files written to out_dir); heavy False runs the light registered cases, True the heavy ones (>= 5 s each), None everything (all cases, then selftest_examples with backend cpu and gpu; progress also gets the example records); names overrides it. With out_dir, unchanged passing cases are reused from out_dir/selftest_cache.json (CLI selftest Reuse); reset=True reruns them. progress(dict) gets events and records: {event: begin, phase, n_run, n_reused, n_total} per phase, {event: start, index, n_total, name, last_wall_time (s or None), remaining (s, summed last run times of it and every later test), n_untimed, time_estimate ({seconds_low, seconds_guess, seconds_high (build + study + output), phases {build, study, output: the same keys}, n_runs, n_estimated, message, not_estimated} of its runs on the stored machine profile, or None)} before each test, then its case / example record (time_estimate: {before, n_checked_runs, split {total, build, study, output, other: {seconds, estimate}, study_work_at_build}}: study estimated at the runs' measured counts, its counter-timed work done at build (e.g. a factorisation in finalize; study_work_at_build s) moved from build to study seconds, build / output the guesses before, other (checks, run set-up) never estimated; {event: skipped, name, message} for a case this machine cannot run).
- selftest_examples(out_dir=None, names=None, progress=None, reset=False) (open_sol.api) -> the selftest_report_analytic.json dict (written with out_dir; each example once, on its own backend, examples/ run directories); progress gets the events of selftest and each example record; reuse and reset as selftest.
- save_session_run(directory, spec, session, build_summary, study_summary, log_entries, model_file=None, save_arrays=True) -> directory: writes the run directory run(out_dir=) would of a live session its caller built and ran (the GUI worker); the session stays open; log_entries = [(clock text, level, message)].
- export_session_html(path, what, spec, session, build_summary, study_summary, log_entries, model_file=None, physics=None, geometry=True, planes=None, figure=None, fields=None, max_bytes=None) -> the written path: Results.export_html of such a live session (the GUI View in browser buttons, canvas and Results Field tab: planes = the shown 3D cut); the session stays open.
- Never mix api.run with the GUI worker in one process.

### GPU memory

- Runs use a GPU memory budget (cupy pool limit), recomputed at the start of every run, of at most 90% of the device memory and at most the free memory plus the blocks already cached by the cupy pool, minus 512 MiB headroom; when that leaves nothing the run fails before building (an error at model). Running out of it fails the run cleanly: status failed, with a message naming the budget and the remedies (fewer cells, smaller DFT / far-field boxes or fewer n_wavelengths, closing other GPU programs).
- A derived value that runs out of GPU memory becomes NaN plus a warning.

### Regenerating this reference

- After a registry or template change regenerate api_reference.md and api_templates.md with: python -m open_sol describe --update-reference. selftest (api_reference_current) fails while either file differs from the generated text.

### Result kinds (Results.result and Session.feature_result dicts)

#### Result kind `timeseries`

Produced by: elastic_waves.field_probe, electric_currents.potential_probe, electrostatics.potential_probe, em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium, em_fdfd_hz.phase_change_medium, em_fdtd_3d.field_probe, em_fdtd_bor.field_probe, em_fdtd_ez.phase_change_medium, em_fdtd_ez.field_probe, em_fdtd_hz.phase_change_medium, em_fdtd_hz.field_probe, heat.temperature_probe, laminar_flow.flow_probe, magnetic_fields_ac.probe, magnetostatics.probe, magnetostatics_3d.probe, solid_mechanics.solid_probe, solid_mechanics_3d.solid_probe

- `kind`: 'timeseries', str
- `t`: sample times, float64 (n,), s
- `values`: sampled field values, float32 (n,), in 'unit'
- `component`: name of the sampled field component, str
- `unit`: unit of 'values', str

#### Result kind `flux_spectrum`

Produced by: em_fdfd_bor.flux_monitor, em_fdfd_conical.flux_monitor, em_fdfd_ez.flux_monitor, em_fdfd_hz.flux_monitor, em_fdfd_nonlinear.flux_monitor, em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane, em_fdtd_3d.flux_box, em_fdtd_bor.flux_monitor, em_fdtd_ez.flux_monitor, em_fdtd_hz.flux_monitor

- `kind`: 'flux_spectrum', str
- `frequency`: monitored frequencies, float64 (n_f,), Hz
- `wavelength`: vacuum wavelengths c / frequency, float64 (n_f,), m
- `power`: power through the line per unit z length, float64 (n_f,), in 'unit'; > 0 toward +x (vertical line) or +y (horizontal line); em_fdtd_3d: through the plane (> 0 toward +normal) or out of the box, and power_per_cw in W
- `unit`: unit of power, str: 'a.u.' (em_fdtd_*: dt-weighted spectra, compare runs by ratios) or 'W/m' (em_fdfd_*: time-averaged power per unit z length)
- `power_per_cw`: em_fdtd_* only, when every source shares one waveform: power / (2 abs(S(omega))^2), the cw power comparable with em_fdfd_* power, float64 (n_f,), W/m; NaN where the source spectrum S is too weak (see the feature description)

#### Result kind `dft_fields`

Produced by: em_fdtd_3d.dft_plane, em_fdtd_ez.dft_monitor, em_fdtd_hz.dft_monitor

- `kind`: 'dft_fields', str
- `frequency`: monitored frequencies, float64 (n_f,), Hz
- `wavelength`: vacuum wavelengths c / frequency, float64 (n_f,), m
- `x_centers`: x of the recorded cell centres (every box cell, or every downsample-th), float64 (mx,), m
- `y_centers`: y of the recorded cell centres, float64 (my,), m
- `extent`: box edges (x0, x1, y0, y1), 4 floats, m
- `shape`: recorded cell counts (mx, my), 2 ints, cells
- `downsample`: recording stride in cells along x and y (1 = every box cell), int
- `quantity`: monitor quantity that intensity holds, str: 'abs(E_z)^2' (em_fdtd_ez) or 'abs(E_x)^2 + abs(E_y)^2' (em_fdtd_hz, E_x and E_y averaged to the cell centres)
- `intensity_per_cw_factor`: only when every source shares one waveform: 1 / abs(S(omega))^2 per frequency, float64 (n_f,), 1/s^2; intensity times its freq_index entry is the cw intensity in (V/m)^2; NaN where the source spectrum S is too weak
- `freq_index`: only with the option freq_index: the chosen frequency index (0-based), int
- `intensity`: only with the option freq_index: abs(E(omega))^2 of the monitor quantity (see quantity) at that frequency, float64 (mx, my), a.u.
- `hz_intensity`: em_fdtd_hz only, with the option freq_index on a live Results (closed and loaded Results lack it): abs(H_z)^2 at that frequency, float64 (mx, my), a.u.

#### Result kind `far_field`

Produced by: em_fdfd_bor.far_field, em_fdfd_ez.far_field, em_fdfd_hz.far_field, em_fdfd_nonlinear.far_field, em_fdtd_3d.far_field, em_fdtd_bor.far_field, em_fdtd_ez.far_field, em_fdtd_hz.far_field

- `kind`: 'far_field', str
- `frequency`: monitored frequencies, float64 (n_f,), Hz
- `wavelength`: vacuum wavelengths c / frequency, float64 (n_f,), m
- `quantity`: far-field quantity that power is proportional to, str: 'abs(E_z)^2' (em_fdtd_ez, em_fdfd_ez) or 'abs(eta0 H_z)^2' (em_fdtd_hz, em_fdfd_hz)
- `angles`: observation angles counter-clockwise from +x, float64 (n_angles,), rad
- `power`: radiated power per unit z length and angle, rho quantity / (2 eta0) at rho -> inf, float64 (n_f, n_angles), in 'unit'; its integral over the angle is the power through a closed flux box
- `unit`: unit of power, str: 'a.u.' (em_fdtd_*: dt-weighted spectra without the 1/2, as their flux_spectrum) or 'W/(m rad)' (em_fdfd_*)

#### Result kind `xy`

Produced by: em_eme.eme_length_sweep, em_eme.adjoint_objective, em_eme.design_region, em_eme_3d.eme_length_sweep, em_eme_3d.adjoint_objective, em_fdfd_bor.field_probe, em_fdfd_bor.mode_monitor, em_fdfd_conical.field_probe, em_fdfd_ez.field_probe, em_fdfd_ez.mode_monitor, em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective, em_fdfd_ez.design_region, em_fdfd_hz.field_probe, em_fdfd_hz.mode_monitor, em_fdfd_hz.adjoint_objective, em_fdfd_hz.design_region, em_fdfd_nonlinear.design_region, em_fdfd_nonlinear.field_probe, em_fdfd_nonlinear.mode_monitor, em_fdfd_nonlinear.adjoint_objective, em_fdfd_sphere.plane_wave, em_fdfd_sphere.dipole_source, em_fdfd_sphere.field_probe, em_fdtd_3d.mode_monitor, em_fdtd_bor.mode_monitor, em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor, em_fdtd_hz.mode_monitor, em_modes.mode_dispersion, em_modes.shg_overlap, heat.thermorefractive_noise, heat.particle_noise, membrane.field_probe, membrane.port, membrane.mode_projection, pressure_acoustics.frequency_probe, pressure_acoustics.surface_pressure, solid_mechanics.frequency_probe, solid_mechanics.admittance, solid_mechanics_3d.frequency_probe, solid_mechanics_3d.admittance

- `kind`: 'xy', str; the producing feature may add further keys, listed in its description
- `x`: abscissa shared by every series, float64 (n,), in x_unit
- `x_label`: name of the abscissa, str
- `x_unit`: unit of x, str ('1' = dimensionless, '' = none)
- `y_label`: name of the plotted quantity (y axis), str

#### Result kind `mode_shapes`

Produced by: solid_mechanics_3d.mode_shapes

- `kind`: 'mode_shapes', str
- `nodes`: surface node positions, float64 (n, 3), m: the vertices (and, quadratic elements, edge midpoints) of the boundary faces of the solid, numbered compactly
- `triangles`: surface triangles, int32 (m, 3), indices into nodes, counter-clockwise seen from outside the solid (quadratic elements: each face split into 4 at its edge midpoints)
- `resonance_number`: 1-based resonance of each mode, int32 (r,), in the resonance_table row order
- `frequency`: Re f of each mode, float64 (r,), Hz
- `q_factor`: quality factor Re f / (2 Im f) of each mode, float64 (r,), 1; NaN for an undamped mode
- `displacement_re`: real part of the complex nodal displacement, float32 (r, n, 3) (components x, y, z), m, as the solver normalises the mode
- `displacement_im`: imaginary part of the same, float32 (r, n, 3), m (0 for a real mode)
- `bloch_k`: Bloch wavenumber per axis (x, y, z) of the solve, float64 (3,), rad/m; 0 off the periodic axes
- `periodic`: 1 per Bloch-periodic axis, else 0, int8 (3,)
- `period`: cell length L per axis (the mesh extent), float64 (3,), m
- `phase_convention`: Bloch phase and time convention of the displacement, str, e.g. 'u(x + L) = u(x) exp(-j k L), time exp(+j omega t)'
- `unit`: unit of nodes and the displacement, str ('m')
- `density`: mass density at each node (mean over the solid elements around it), float64 (n,), kg/m^3
- `stress_re`: mode_shapes fields 'stress' / 'stress_strain' only: real part of the complex modal stress at the nodes, float32 (r, n, 6) (components xx, yy, zz, xy, xz, yz), Pa, in the normalisation and phase of the displacement
- `stress_im`: imaginary part of the same, float32 (r, n, 6), Pa
- `strain_re`: mode_shapes fields 'stress_strain' only: real part of the complex strain, float32 (r, n, 6) (xx, yy, zz, xy, xz, yz; tensor shear strain), 1
- `strain_im`: imaginary part of the same, float32 (r, n, 6), 1
- `potential_re`: piezoelectric with fields 'stress' / 'stress_strain' only: real part of the complex electric potential at the nodes, float32 (r, n), V
- `potential_im`: imaginary part of the same, float32 (r, n), V
